Peanut Butter loved jelly again, and the strange pairings ended. Cupid Pig put her arrows away and waited for the next Valentine's Day.

On Wednesday, he went on a field trip. On Thursday, recess was fun, and on Friday, he looked forward to a big kickball game. On the bus ride home, Simon heard germs talk to him. Simon rested all weekend, drank lots of fluids, and by Monday he felt good again and was ready to go back to school.

The class walked through town and gave gifts to people like the police lady, the garbage man, the librarian, the dentist, the grocer, the vet, the barber, the bookseller, the doctor, and the bank teller. At last he found the baker’s shop and gave her the thank-you card. The baker fixed his legs with chocolate and gave him boots. The gingerbread man hurried back to school and helped give the teacher a big thank-you poem and gift.

By dinner, Jeremy was no longer felt like an enemy. Dad served the pie, but the boy stopped Jeremy from eating it. Then he saw Dad already eating it. The pie was delicious, and Jeremy became a friend.

Fletcher climbed up and held the last leaf tight, but it came off and he carried it to the den. In the morning, he found the tree covered with shining icicles and hugged it before going to breakfast.

Each time, he did something different from the other sheep.
He ran with the dogs
instead of standing with the sheep.
He would not share his wool,
and he even rode the spinning wheel,
dyed himself instead of the yarn,
and put his head in the loom to weave his forelock.

that Wilbur was not following the way sheep should act.
Grandpa always answered,
“Don’t worry,”
and repeated that the others still held on to their wool all night long.

and told him he must follow the flock
and do everything like the other sheep.
Wilbur thought all night,
and after that he taught everyone to do the same unusual things he had done.
Then Mom and Pop worried because everyone looked and acted like Wilbur,
and they could not find him.

summary_text: Many years ago, Bagheera the Panther found a lost man cub named Mowgli in the jungle of India. He took him to a family of wolves, and Mother Wolf agreed to raise him. Mowgli grew up with the wolf cubs and became friends with the elephants too. Bagheera watched over him from far away because the jungle had many dangers. He once saved Mowgli from a crafty snake. But the tiger Shere Khan hated humans and wanted to kill Mowgli. Bagheera and Rama, Mowgli’s wolf father, decided Mowgli must go to the man village. Mowgli did not want to leave, so he ran into the jungle. There he met Baloo the bear, then was taken by King Louie and the monkeys. Bagheera and Baloo rescued him, and after a fight with Shere Khan, Mowgli used fire to scare the tiger away. In the end, Mowgli saw a girl at the water hole, followed her to the man village, and went there to live.

The people danced and celebrated into the night because they had found freedom.

summary_text: Laura traveled across the giant Prairie in a covered wagon with her paw, ma, big sister Mary, little sister Carrie, and their bulldog Jack. They were looking for a place to build a house. One morning Laura and Mary woke before the sun, ate cornmeal mush, and helped ma wash the dishes. Then paw drove the wagon until he stopped and said this was the place for their house. Paw and ma unloaded the wagon while Laura, Mary, and Jack watched. Paw then drove away to bring back logs from the creek bottom. Laura felt frightened without the wagon, but she helped ma while Mary watched baby Carrie. For many days paw hauled logs and made piles for the house and stable. When there were enough logs, paw and ma began building the house together. Later paw met Mr. Edwards, who lived across the creek. Mr. Edwards came to help finish the house, and he and paw worked fast, cut a door and windows, and then stayed for supper. That night paw played his fiddle, Mr. Edwards danced, and the family sang under the big moon.

Julius says he is Black and explains that people sometimes make stories about race that are not true, like saying one race is better than another. He also says people can think they are better for other reasons, such as having more money, going to a certain school, or being a boy or a girl. Julius asks the listener to touch the bones under their skin and notice that everyone has the same hard bones underneath. He says that if people took off their skin and hair, they would look alike. By the end, Julius says that race is not all a person is, and he asks the listener to share something about themselves that cannot be seen just by looking.

summary_text: On Valentine's Day, all the animals on Farmer Jake's Farm traded cards and treats. Turkey got a card from a secret admirer and wanted to make secret Valentines for his pals too. He dressed as a cat and tried to give Rooster a card, but Rooster saw that it was Turkey. Then Turkey dressed as a dog to surprise Horse, but Horse knew it was him. Next, Turkey dressed as a toad for Cow, but Cow found out too. Cow, Horse, Rooster, Sheep, and Pig still liked the Valentines, and they helped Turkey keep trying. Turkey dressed as an owl and helped deliver cards to Sheep and Pig in the barn, but they still knew it was him. Turkey felt sad that his surprises were not secret. Then he found one more idea: pizza for the Valentine's dance. He delivered the pizza unseen, and everyone loved the surprise.

summary_text: The child wanted a puppy just for himself, so he traded his baseball mitt for one. His baby sister liked the puppy right away, and Mom and Dad were surprised. They said he could keep the puppy if he took care of him himself. So the child feeds the puppy every morning, puts on the leash, and takes him for walks. He teaches the puppy to heel, sit, stay, play dead, roll over, and fetch. The puppy still needs practice, but he learns many things. The puppy also helps around the house. He is a good guard dog, brings in the paper for Dad, and stays with the child while he does homework. When the puppy gets dirty, the child gives him a bath and dries him off. Then they get ready for bed together.

summary_text: Simon the squirrel bounces around under his tree and looks for acorns to save for winter. He gathers nuts, but when his friends start playing, he joins them and says he will collect the nuts another day. The warm autumn days pass, and a chilly wind begins to blow, but Simon does not stop to prepare. Then winter comes quickly. Snow falls, the ground gets covered, and Simon realizes he does not have enough food. He feels cold, scared, and alone, and he calls for help. A blue feathered bird and wise friend Olly come to him. Olly helps Simon calm down, breathe, and look around. Simon learns he can be strong. He digs in the snow, finds the buried acorns, and carries them home. In the end, Simon has enough food for winter and feels proud.

summary_text: Millie makes mistakes all the time. She spills milk, uses too much toothpaste and glue, spells banana wrong, and runs too fast. Millie wants to be a top athlete, so she signs up for a hurdle race. At the race, she runs fast but forgets to jump, so she breaks the hurdles one by one. Her mom cheers from the side. Millie finally jumps, but she falls on her face and then on her bum. When she jumps very high to avoid the hurdles, she crashes into a tree and gets stuck with some cats. Millie calms herself and looks for a way down. She uses her shoelaces and branches to make a long stick and reaches a kite, then comes down safely with the cats. At home, Millie says she will try to be the best athlete ever. She practices jumping again and again. Her family also practices their own goals. On race day, Millie jumps over the hurdles, keeps going after one mistake, and wins the race. She learns that practice helps and mistakes can be useful.

summary_text: Bentley the hippo was thinking about a big space adventure when something mushy hit his head. It was a banana, and Bentley asked who threw it. Toby came to meet Bentley for ice cream, and soon Jackson the monkey appeared. Jackson said he was sharing, but he kept throwing bananas. Bentley and Toby walked toward the ice cream cart, and Bentley told Toby about his space dream. Then they heard soft whimpering near a bush and found Jackson. Jackson was guarding his bananas and had forgotten his ice cream. He threw another banana, and Bentley and Toby told him they liked bananas, but not when they were thrown. They shared their ice cream with Jackson instead. Jackson learned about sharing, and he gave a banana to each friend. Bentley made banana splits, and all three friends enjoyed the treats and talked about going on a space adventure together.

summary_text: Gerald was not seen one day, and his friend asked what happened to his trunk. Gerald said, “I Broke My Trunk.” He began a long, crazy story. First, he was playing with Hippo and wanted to lift Hippo onto his trunk. Then Rhino came and wanted a turn, so Gerald lifted both Hippo and Rhino. After that, Hippo’s big sister came too, and she wanted to play her piano. Gerald lifted two hippos, one rhino, and a piano, and that was very heavy. Still, that was not how he broke his trunk. Gerald said he was proud and ran to tell his very best friend, but he tripped and fell. That was when he broke his trunk. His friend laughed and said it was a funny story. Then Piggy asked what happened to his snow, and Piggy and Gerald both said they had hurt their noses. In the end, they lay in bed and decided to read.

summary_text: Pinkalicious was ready to be Pinker Girl for Halloween in Pinkville. In the morning, the lights would not turn on, and the radio was silent. Peter and her parents learned that a big storm had caused a power outage. The mayor said the electric company was trying to fix it, but if the lights were still out by evening, no one could go trick-or-treating. Pinkalicious and Peter were upset. Pinkalicious put on her Pink Girl costume and had an idea. With Mommy, she went to town hall and asked the mayor not to cancel Halloween. She said the children could still celebrate safely if they used pink lanterns and flashlights. The mayor liked the idea and announced a Halloween party in Pinkville Park. That night, everyone came with lights, costumes, and candy. They danced, listened to a ghost story, and had fun. Pinkalicious got candy and said it was the sweetest Halloween ever.

summary_text: A bare brown tree has magic. When someone taps it, a leaf appears. Tapping again makes more leaves grow, and then many more leaves cover the tree. Rubbing the tree makes it warm, and little flower buds appear. Touching and counting them shows seven buds. Soon the buds turn into flowers. Then the tree is jiggled, and the flower petals fall down. The petals are brushed away, and a kiss is blown to the tree. After the tree is shaken, all the apples fall off. Knocking on the trunk changes the leaves to yellow. A little squirrel is then seen eating an apple. Next, a whooshing breeze is blown, and then clapping brings snow and icicles. After counting to ten and opening eyes, the magic begins again with green leaves.

Another child agrees and says macaroni would be better, but later says she does not really like macaroni and cheese. The group talks about how messy both choices would be. Next, they choose between walking on stilts for a year or using a pogo stick everywhere. Ryan picks the pogo stick because stilts would make him hit his head on doorways. Stephen and another child also talk about the fun of bouncing, but Stephen says stilts would make him look taller. Then they choose between being in the ocean in a row boat or in the desert with a skateboard. The children give different answers, saying the desert feels easier to handle, while the ocean could be scary. Finally, they choose between a laugh that sounds like an air horn or a wailing siren, and they debate which sound would be funnier or more annoying.

summary_text: On a tiny island at the edge of the world, a lighthouse stands on a high rock and sends its light to the sea. A new keeper arrives to take the place of the old one. He polishes the lens, fills the oil, trims the wick, winds the clockwork, paints the rooms, writes in the log book, and listens to the wind. He drinks tea, fishes for cod, and writes letters to his wife. Soon the tender brings supplies and his wife comes too. He shows her the round rooms, and they set the table for two. Then thick fog comes, and a bell rings to warn ships. One dark night, a boat crashes on the rocks, and the keeper pulls three sailors from the water and wraps them in blankets.

summary_text: Deep in the Australian bush, two possums lived together. Their names were Hush and Grandma Poss. Grandma Poss could do bush magic. She made wombats blue, cucuras pink, dingo smile, and emus shrink. Her best magic made Hush invisible so snakes could not see her. But one day Hush said she wanted to know what she looked like, so she asked Grandma Poss to make her visible again. Grandma Poss looked in all her magic books, but she could not find that spell. The next day, she remembered that the magic had something to do with food, so they left the bush and traveled across Australia. They ate many foods, but Hush stayed invisible. In Darwin they ate a Vegemite sandwich and Hush got a tail. In Perth, pavlova made her legs and body appear. In Tasmania, a lamington made her visible from head to tail. After that, Hush stayed visible, and once a year she ate those foods again to keep it that way.

summary_text: On a cold winter morning, Dexter ran downstairs to eat his mom’s bacon and cheese bread pudding, but his twin sister Leah got the first bite again. Later, when Mama and Papa were busy cooking for a big dinner, Dexter and Leah helped in the kitchen. Papa found out they had no eggs, so he sent the twins to Ms. Marvis’s house to get some. At Ms. Marvis’s home, Dexter noticed it felt very quiet and lonely. On the way back, he and Leah talked about how their house was always full of people, and they asked their parents to invite Ms. Marvis to dinner. That night, Ms. Marvis shared stories about living in Poland and making punchki, jelly donuts made in winter. The next day, Papa used her recipe, and the twins helped make punchki to give to Ms. Marvis. They later built a snow family in her yard, and Ms. Marvis wrote a thank-you letter saying their kindness made her feel special.

summary_text: Funny bunny PJ was sad because he did not like being a bunny. His mother made him eat cooked carrots every day, and he had many brothers and sisters. His ears were very big. One day PJ left home. He said he wanted to be a bear, so he lived with the bears. But the bears slept for the winter, and PJ could not sleep. Then he tried being a bird and liked it for a while. After that, he tried being a beaver, but beavers worked too hard for him. PJ went to live with the pigs, but the pigs only sat in mud. He tried being a moose, then a possum, then a skunk, but he did not like those lives either. At last PJ said he wanted to be a bunny again and hurried home. His family was happy to see him, and PJ was happy too. He ate his carrots, played with his brothers and sisters, and liked being a bunny again.

Outside, he found Duck, Sheep, Pig, and Cow having a loud fight. Duck said Cow would not share toys. Sheep said Pig took her ball. Cow and Duck teased each other, and everyone shouted. Nick asked them to stop and told them to show kindness. He explained that kindness means doing nice things, helping others, sharing, waiting your turn, and being grateful. The animals listened and began to talk about kind things they had done, like helping family, teachers, neighbors, and older people. They apologized for being rude and mean. By the end of the day, the animals were polite and kind, and Nick was glad he had helped his friends.

summary_text: Spot helps children get ready for online learning. Spot tells them to wear comfortable, appropriate clothes, not pajamas, and to eat before class so their stomachs do not grumble. He reminds children to join early, check the computer, camera, and microphone, and be ready to listen, watch, and raise a hand when they want to speak.

summary_text: A girl was new at school. She wanted to make good friends, so she used the golden rule and treated her classmates the way she liked to be treated. She was helpful, loving, fair, and kind. She shared, took turns, solved problems with words, and gave sweet hugs. Most children liked her, but one kid did not. This kid teased her and acted rude. The girl tried to be a friend, but the teasing made her feel sad. She saw that this was not a true friend, because a friend should not make someone feel small. So she made a boundary. She said she would play if the kid was kind, but if not, she would play with other true friends. She also said the kid could join again when they were ready to be nice. She learned to stand up for herself, stay respectful, and ask a trusted adult for help when needed.

summary_text: Finn was in a horrible mood, and Grandpa wanted to talk with him. Finn said Grandpa would not understand, but Grandpa asked him to go for a walk. Finn agreed, though he said he would stay under here. Grandpa promised to remember to think of what was beneath. As they walked into the forest, Grandpa showed Finn how there are things under the parts we can see, like tree roots under the ground and the water under a boat. He said that sometimes things that look still can have a lot happening below. Grandpa also said that some things are a mystery, like a nest or a baby on the way. He explained that beneath what is outside, there can be growing, changing, or hidden feelings inside plants, animals, and people. Finn listened and began to want to know more. Grandpa said everyone is more than what you see, and sometimes the person who seems not to understand knows exactly how you feel. At the end, they walked home, climbed the hill, and looked at the stars.

summary_text: Laura lived in a little log house in the big woods of Wisconsin with Paw, Ma, Mary, Carrie, and Jack. One day Paw said that after the crops were planted, the family would go to town. Laura and Mary were very excited. They tried to play going to town, but they did not know what a town was like. Then Paw said, "We'll go to town tomorrow." That night Ma bathed Laura and Mary and wrapped their wet hair in rags so it would be curly in the morning. They put on their best dresses and rode in the wagon with Paw and Ma. In town, Laura saw many houses and people. They went into the store, where Laura saw cloth, boots, tools, and candy. The storekeeper gave Laura and Mary each a candy heart. Then the family had a picnic by the lake and rode home tired. Paw sang, "There's no place like home."

summary_text: One December afternoon, a toy bear in a big store woke up and heard a boy and his mother talking about Christmas gifts. The boy wanted a fire engine, not the bear. Later, a girl wanted a Piper doll, not the bear. The bear felt sad because he had no name and no clothes, and he wondered how he could ever be on a Christmas list. At night, he climbed down from his shelf and looked for something special to wear before he went to see Santa. He tried hats, shoes, and baby clothes, but nothing fit. Then he followed a sign with Santa’s picture and found the North Pole, Santa’s workshop, and some elf clothes. The clothes fit him, so he put them on and waited in Santa’s chair. In the morning, Santa found him, gave him the name Corduroy, and sent him back to the toy department. Soon a little girl saw him, said he was the bear she had always wanted, and Corduroy smiled because he had found a home.

She hurts her knee and her teddy bear flies away. She goes to the doctor, who puts smelly medicine on her knee and bandages it. The princess cries for her mom while she waits to get better.

summary_text: On Saturday, Fergus and his baby brother Dink looked for treasures at the beach. They waited for 15 minutes, but no one came for it, so they made it part of their treasure pile and named it Dave. Fergus did not want to go into the water because he thought there was murky ickiness there. Later, Fergus went to get ice cream. After that, Fergus and Dink kept looking for more treasures and found another one.

They followed it to the barn, stopped Swiper when he tried to swipe, and then found all three piggies inside. Mommy Pig hugged her babies, and the piggies gave Dora and Boots apples to say thank you.

summary_text: A square had four equal sides and four matching corners, and it was happy. On Wednesday, it was shredded in strips, so it became a park. On Thursday, it was shattered, so it became a bridge. On Friday, it was snipped into ribbons, so it became a river. On Saturday, it was crumpled and ripped and wrinkled, so it became a mountain. On Sunday, the square waited and waited for something else to happen, but nothing did. Its sides felt confining and its corners felt rigid and cramped. Then it changed into a window that looked out on the mountain, the river, the bridge, the park, the garden, and the fountain.

After they left, the witch planted another pumpkin seed.

summary_text: One night, Owl went down to the seashore and sat on a large rock. The sky was dark, and then a small tip of the moon came up over the sea. Owl watched as the moon climbed higher and became a full, round moon. He looked at it for a long time and said that if he was looking at the moon, the moon must be looking back at him, so they must be good friends. Owl told the moon he would come back again, but first he had to go home. When he walked home, he saw that the moon was following him. He asked the moon to stay over the sea, then over the trees, and not come home with him. Owl said goodbye and climbed a hill. The moon went behind clouds and disappeared. Owl felt sad. At home, he put on his pajamas and got into bed. Then the moon came out again and filled his room with silver light. Owl saw the moon in his window and said it had followed him all the way home. He felt happy and was not sad anymore.

summary_text: Piglet wanted to paint the things he loved most in the wood, so he asked Pooh, Rabbit, Kanga, Roo, Tigger, and Eeyore to sit for portraits. He set up his studio outside in the sunshine and began with Pooh, but Pooh kept thinking about honey and food, and his tummy would not stay still. Then Piglet tried Rabbit, but Rabbit remembered his garden and hurried away to work. Tigger could not stop bouncing, and Kanga and Roo arrived just as Tigger bounced off into the wood. At last Piglet painted Eeyore, who stayed still. Piglet then thought of a new idea. He painted his friends doing what they always do best, like Pooh following bees, Rabbit working in his garden, and Tigger bouncing. When he showed the paintings, his friends looked carefully and thanked him. Piglet said everyone is good at something different, and his paintings helped him remember how lucky he was to have such wonderful friends.

summary_text: Jack and his mother were very poor, and they had only one cow. Jack’s mother told him to sell the cow and bring back the money. On the way, Jack met a man who had no money, but he offered Jack five magic beans for the cow. Jack took the beans home, but his mother was angry and threw them out of the window. The next day, Jack saw a giant bean stalk growing up to the sky. He climbed it and found a giant castle. A giant woman hid him in a cupboard when her giant husband came home. The giant counted his money and fell asleep. Jack took the money and climbed down to his mother. Jack climbed the bean stalk two more times. Each time, the giant brought something special: a Magic Hen that laid golden eggs, and then a magic Harp that played music. Jack took them too. At last, Jack ran down the bean stalk, his mother cut it down, and the giant was gone. Jack and his mother were no longer poor.

summary_text: A tree grew in a busy city plaza below two tall towers. It gave people shade, gave birds a place to rest, and was one of the first trees to blossom each year, showing that spring was coming. The tree liked city sounds, rain on concrete, and watching people pass by. One day, something terrible happened in the plaza, and the tree was left alone in dark, hot, close air. Weeks later, people found it and took it to a quiet nursery in a park. There, the tree was cared for all winter, and its leaves grew back. Birds visited it, and a dove built a nest in its branches. After many years, the tree was taken back downtown. It saw that the old towers were gone, and a new plaza had a forest with three empty spaces. Two were for the fallen towers, and one was for the tree. The tree stayed there and kept blossoming each spring.

This time Sludge comes to the can, and Nate sees that Sludge is the one taking the garbage. Nate gives Sludge a bone and dog food, and the case is over.

summary_text: A king kept many wild beasts in his menagerie, and the most feared one was Iron John, a wild man covered in gray hair. One day the king’s youngest son, Walter, lost his golden ball in Iron John’s cage. Iron John said he would return it only if Walter freed him. Walter found the hidden key under his mother’s pillow, opened the cage, and Iron John escaped with him into the forest. There, Iron John made Walter guard a spring and warned him not to let anything fall into it. Walter watched the spring for years and grew up there. But three times he made mistakes: a hair turned to gold, then his finger became gold, and finally all his hair turned gold. Iron John then sent him away with a golden horn and told him to seek work. Walter became a garden servant named Walter-in-the-Mud, later rode in gold to a ball and a tournament, defeated enemies in battle, and was finally healed by Elsa’s tears. He married Elsa and went with her to Iron John’s land.

summary_text: The story is about an egg who says he is a very good egg. He helps by carrying groceries, watering plants, changing tires, and painting houses. Long ago, he lived in a store with eleven other eggs in a carton. Their names were Meg, Peg, Greg, Clay, Shell, Shelly, Sheldon, Shelby, Eggbert, Frank, and other Frank. The other eggs did not follow rules. They stayed up too late, ate sugary cereal, cried, and broke things on purpose. The main egg tried to fix their behavior and keep peace, but he became tired and stressed. One morning, he saw cracks in his shell and learned from his doctor that pressure was hurting him. He decided to leave the carton and go on his own. On the road, he spent time walking, reading, floating in a river, writing in a journal, breathing, and painting. Slowly, his shell healed. Then he went back home, and the other eggs were happy to see him. He understood that the other eggs did not need to be perfect, and he did not need to be perfect either.

summary_text: On New Year’s Eve, a poor little girl walked through the cold city streets selling flowers and matches. She had lost her slippers, so her feet were bare and frozen. No one bought anything from her, and she was very hungry and tired. Afraid to go home because her father would beat her, she sat in a corner out of the wind. To warm her hands, she struck a match. In the bright flame, she saw a warm stove, then a table with roast goose and desserts, then a beautiful Christmas tree with candles and toys. Each time the match went out, the vision disappeared. When she lit another match, she saw her kind grandmother. The girl struck many matches to keep her there, and grandmother took her into the light. In the morning, the girl was found dead, frozen to death, with burned matches in her hand.

summary_text: The first day of school was coming, and Max, Millie, and the animals on Farmer Jake’s Farm were very excited. Turkey and his pals practiced writing names, counting corn kernels, reading stories, and playing recess games so they could be ready. But when the big day came, they were told they could not ride the bus because critters were not allowed at school. Turkey wanted to go anyway. The animals tried many disguises to sneak him in. First, Turkey dressed like a backpack, but Max sent him away. Then he looked like a book, but the teacher found him. After that, he dressed like a soccer ball for recess, but Millie saw him. Next, he dressed like a lunch lady in the cafeteria, but he was sent out again. At last, the principal announced special Farm Day visitors. Turkey and his pals sang for the class, and the children cheered. The teacher let them stay as special Farm guests for the afternoon.

summary_text: Arnold climbs high into his apple tree, and it is his secret place. In spring, he watches buds grow into apple blossoms. He sees bees gather nectar, and he makes a swing, a blossom wreath, and a flower arrangement with his family. In summer, the tree has big green leaves. Arnold builds a tree house, rests in the shade, and watches tiny apples grow bigger. He even juggles some green apples. In fall, the tree has red apples and golden leaves. Arnold gathers leaves for his tree house and picks apples into a basket. He and his family make apple pies and fresh cider from the apples. On Halloween, Arnold decorates some of the biggest apples. In winter, snow falls. Arnold hangs popcorn and berries for the birds, builds a snow fort, and makes a snowman. When the snow melts, spring comes again.

summary_text: Arfi is a dog who wants a home. He writes letters to many places on Butternut Street and asks, “Can I be your dog?” First he writes to the Yellow House, but the Honeywells say they already have a cat and cannot take a dog. Then Arfi writes to the Butcher Lady, Veronica Shank, but she says a dog once made meatballs go missing, so she says no. Arfi also writes to Fire Station Number Five, but the station says the fire dog job is already filled. Next he asks the Junkyard Guy, who tells him to get lost. Arfi writes to the last house on Butternut Street, but the letter is returned because nobody lives there. Arfi is sad and back in his box when it starts raining. Then a letter arrives from Mitzi Whipple, the letter carrier. She asks Arfi to be her person, and Arfi happily says yes. He finally has a friend and a home.

summary_text: A girl and her best friend do many things together. One day the girl decides to make the most magnificent thing. She hires an assistant, gathers supplies, and starts working. She tinkerers, hammers, measures, saws, glues, twists, and paints, while her assistant helps by pouncing, growling, chewing, circling, and tugging. But each time they finish, the thing is wrong. It is square, round, fuzzy, long, short, rough, smooth, big, small, and even smells like stinky cheese, but it is still not magnificent. The girl gets angrier and works faster until she hurts her finger and shouts that she quits. Her assistant takes her for a walk. As they walk, she sees that some parts of her wrong things are actually good. By the end of the trail, she knows how to make it right. She works carefully again, and this time she makes the most magnificent thing.

summary_text: Herbert Halwe was known as Halfway Herbert because he did many things only halfway. He brushed only part of his teeth, did half his homework, answered only half the test questions, ate only part of his meals, and listened only halfway to his soccer coach. One day, Herbert tried to ride his bike with only one shoe tied. His shoelace got caught in the wheel, and he crashed into his dad’s car. His bike bent, his leg hurt, and the car got dented. When his dad asked what happened, Herbert told only half the truth. Then Mr. Rug, the next door neighbor, called and said he saw the crash. Herbert’s dad explained that half the truth is a whole lie and that Jesus wants people to follow him with their whole hearts. Herbert prayed for help, and God gave him the Holy Spirit. After that, Herbert finished things, listened well, and obeyed better.

summary_text: Penelope Rex is a little T-Rex who feels nervous about starting school. She asks what her classmates will be like and worries about leaving home and her mommy. Her mom gives her a backpack with ponies on it, and her dad packs 300 tuna sandwiches and apple juice in a pony lunchbox. On the first day, Penelope is surprised to see that her classmates are children. She eats them because she thinks children are delicious. Mrs. Noodleman tells her, “We don’t eat our classmates!” and makes Penelope spit them out. Penelope feels sad because her classmates are dirty, scared, and do not want to play with her. At home, her dad asks if she ate her classmates and tells her that children are the same on the inside, but they should not be eaten. The next day Penelope tries again, but she keeps eating classmates until they run away from her. Then she meets Walter the goldfish and asks him to be her friend. After she learns what it feels like to be someone’s snack, she stops eating children. Penelope and the other children play together, have lunch together, and become friends.

summary_text: Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter lived with their mother in a sand-bank under a big fir-tree. One morning Mrs. Rabbit told them not to go into Mr. McGregor’s garden, because their father had an accident there. She went to the baker’s and bought bread and currant buns. Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail went to gather blackberries, but Peter went into Mr. McGregor’s garden. He ate lettuces, beans, radishes, and parsley. Then Mr. McGregor saw him and ran after him. Peter lost his shoes, got caught in a gooseberry net, and left his jacket behind. He hid in the tool-shed, jumped into a can, sneezed, and ran out a window. At last he found the gate, escaped home, and flopped down tired and wet. His mother gave him chamomile tea and put him to bed, while the other little rabbits had bread and milk and blackberries.

summary_text: The Loupin Lady lives in a small house by the sea. Long ago, she was a little girl named Alice. Her grandfather was an artist who made ship figureheads and painted pictures. Alice helped him and listened to his stories about faraway places. She said she would travel, live by the sea when she was old, and do something to make the world more beautiful. When she grew up, she left home and worked in a library in another city. People called her Miss Rumpus. She traveled to a tropical island, climbed mountains, crossed jungles and deserts, and made friends in many places. At last she hurt her back and came to live by the sea. There she planted loupin flowers in her rocky garden. The wind and birds spread the seeds, and soon flowers grew everywhere. Miss Rumpus planted more seeds all over the land, and the flowers spread even farther. Now people call her the Loupin Lady.

He stole tracks and planned a bank robbery, but his getaway car was too slow. He was caught and put in jail. Billy cried, and later his mother came to get him.

Hoot told Peep that owls say only “who,” and he said “who” can mean hello, goodbye, good morning, and good night. But Hoot forgot that owls never shout. Peep listened for a while, then flew away when Hoot would not listen to her. Hoot thought Peep would not listen to his wisdom, and Peep thought Hoot did not believe in singing about mystery and magic. After Peep left, Hoot missed her songs. He heard Peep’s sweet voice on the wind and learned that little sisters have their own owl wisdom. Hoot asked Peep to teach him her song. Soon Hoot and Peep sang together in their own special ways, and the night felt perfect.

George and his friends had solved the mystery and had proof for everyone.

Amelia Bedelia and Mr. Rogers’s cousin Uncle Lou go to Grace’s cookie jar bakery to help run the shop while Grace is away. They read Grace’s recipes and follow them carefully, even when the instructions sound strange. Amelia Bedelia cuts chocolate chips in half, makes 12 pound cakes, pinches salt, and helps make smart cookies and different kinds of cheesecake. When one cake falls, they use a spare cake and later make a crumb cake. Grace calls to say Amelia Bedelia should bring one last cake to the bake-off the next day. At home, Amelia Bedelia bakes a special sheet cake that looks like a bed. At the contest, Chef du Jour tastes it and gives her first prize.

summary_text: Each Monday at dawn, Mrs. Nelly McNaught brings out a barrel and does a big wash. She works all morning. When the sun is high, she hangs the wash on the clothesline to dry. She hangs dresses, shirts, underwear, nightgowns, skirts, stockings, shoes, paper, the news, the dog, and his dish and bone. She gets a wrong number and hangs up the phone. She also hangs a hat, an old wedding gown, two sleepy bats, a lamp, a large Christmas wreath, and Grandpa McNauch’s removable teeth. She hangs a kite by the tip of its tail. When the postman comes, she hangs up the mail. She keeps hanging things until everything in sight is hung up, even the turkey she is roasting that night. By dusk, she has hung up the last of her wash. Then she takes off her apron, lets down her hair, and hangs herself up in a comfortable chair.

summary_text: A wolf went around town huffing and puffing and blowing houses down. Three little pigs got tired of being scared, so they went to ninja school. Pig one learned Aikido, but he got bored and quit. Pig two learned jiu-jitsu and wanted to fight the wolf right away. Pig three studied karate very hard. She practiced cartwheels, crescent kicks, crane moves, blocks, and board breaking. One day, the wolf came to Pig one’s straw house and tried to scare him. Pig one tried to fight back, but he missed. The wolf chased the pigs to Pig two’s house and blew the door down. Pig two kicked, but the wolf got away. Then they ran to Pig three. Pig three bowed, warned the wolf, and showed strong ninja moves. She split a stack of bricks, and the wolf got scared and ran away. The pigs were happy and went back to school to keep learning.

On Father's Day, Dad loves both pictures and puts them straight on the fridge.

summary_text: A little train rumbled over the tracks. She was happy and carried toy animals, dolls, a clown, good food, and lollipops for the boys and girls on the other side of the mountain. Then the train stopped. Her wheels would not turn. The little clown asked a shiny new engine to help, but he said no and steamed away. Next, a big strong engine came, but he also said no. Then an old rusty engine came, but he was too tired and said he could not pull the train. The dolls and toys felt sad. At last, a very little blue engine came. She said, “I think I can! I think I can!” She hitched herself to the train and pulled hard. Slowly the train moved up the mountain. The blue engine kept going until they reached the top. Everyone shouted, “Hooray!” The children on the other side would now get their toys and food.

summary_text: On the night before Father’s Day, Dad rides his bike while Mom, Mike, and the narrator clean the garage. Then Mom brings out his shiny car. Dad is surprised and happy. The family gets inside and takes a long Sunday ride. Dad thanks them for the best Father’s Day.

Mrs. Wimpy Dimple later explained that Splat could not promise things he could not keep. She told him to look for something he could change. He wondered if it had all been a dream.

The family then shared a thankful feast, and Runt warned that they still were not safe from holiday dinners.

He stayed with Peggy and Paul, visited the mice, and still helped keep Hazel away from the pantry.

summary_text: Three bears lived in a house in the woods. Papa Bear was big, Mama Bear was middle-sized, and Baby Bear was wee little. One morning, Mama Bear made porridge and put it in three bowls. The porridge was too hot, so the bears went for a walk. While they were away, Goldilocks came to the house. She tasted each bowl. Papa Bear’s porridge was too hot, Mama Bear’s was too cold, and Baby Bear’s was just right, so she ate it all. Then she sat in three chairs. Papa Bear’s chair was too hard, Mama Bear’s was too soft, and Baby Bear’s chair was just right, but it broke. Goldilocks went upstairs and tried three beds. Baby Bear’s bed was just right, so she fell asleep. When the bears came home, they saw the porridge was eaten, the chair was broken, and Goldilocks was in Baby Bear’s bed. Goldilocks woke up, saw the bears, and ran away.

Mama reminded them that Thanksgiving is for giving thanks. On Thanksgiving Day, the family gave thanks for their meal and for home, family, and friends.

summary_text: Zoe woke up in the morning when the sun was shining and the birds were singing. She and her mom had a whole day together, and they went many places. First they went to the library, where Miss Foster said there should be no loud talking or yelling. Zoe asked, “Really? Never?” and Mom said, “Not here.” Then they went to the park, where Mr Jones said no walking on the grass. Mom said, “But here—run wild, my child!” Next they visited Grandma, who said no wet shoes, but Mom said they could splash in the rain. Zoe went to school for painting day, and her friend said paint goes on paper, not on you. Later, at a store, they were told no children could play there, but Mom said, “But here—play!” Then Zoe had a playdate with Ada and made a couch fort. At bedtime, Mom tucked Zoe in and said there were no more adventures today.

Grandpa asks Finn to take a walk.
Finn agrees
but stays under a covering.
Grandpa says he will think about what is beneath things.
In the forest, Grandpa talks about trees.
Some parts are above the ground,
and other parts grow below it.
They look at a still boat,
and Grandpa says that much may be moving beneath the quiet water.
Grandpa sees something digging
and thinks she may become a mother.
He explains that beneath something solid may be something hollow,
and beneath something falling apart, something new may begin.
He says people are more than what we see.
Beneath actions are explanations,
and beneath differences may be sameness.
Grandpa also says that someone who seems unable to understand may know exactly how another person feels.
At the top of a hill, Finn sees the stars
and smiles.
Finn says he will remember to think about what is beneath.

summary_text: Panda wants to find the perfect hug. He looks in the magic mailbox and gets a magnifying glass. He uses it to search for hugs that are too small, too tight, too scary, or too strange. He thinks about a bug, a boa constrictor, a grizzly, a snail, and a jellyfish. None of these hugs feels just right. He keeps looking and wonders if the perfect hug is far away in space or hiding close by. More things arrive from the magic mailbox, including a stuffed panda, and Panda keeps trying to find a hug that fits him well. At the end, Panda learns the secret: a hug takes two. If you hug me, then I’ll hug you. The story ends with Panda finding that the perfect hug is shared.

summary_text: Winter covered Sodor with snow, and the tracks were slippery. Henry was the only engine to make all his deliveries on time. Thomas said Henry must have lucky trucks, so Henry felt happy and thought he would always be useful. The next morning, his trucks were gone because Edward needed them to carry coal to the villages. The Fat Controller sent Henry to collect presents for children. Henry slipped on Gordon’s icy hill, met logs blocking the track, and waited for Rocky to clear them. At last, Henry found Edward and his trucks, but he crashed into them and broke them. Henry was sad, but he remembered the children needed their presents. He went to the airport without his trucks, collected the presents, and delivered them all around Sodor. The children cheered when he arrived. Henry learned that his trucks were not lucky after all. He was lucky because he could still help the children.

summary_text: Max wore his wolf suit and made mischief. His mother called him wild thing, and Max said he would eat her up. So she sent him to bed without supper. That night, a forest grew in Max’s room. It grew into vines, trees, and an ocean. Max sailed on a private boat to where the wild things are. The wild things roared, showed their claws, and rolled their eyes. Max said, “Be still,” and looked at them without blinking. They were frightened and made Max king of all wild things. Max said, “Let the wild rumpus start!” Then he sent the wild things to bed without their supper. After that, Max felt lonely and wanted to be where someone loved him best. He smelled good things to eat from far away and left being king. The wild things begged him to stay, but Max said no. He sailed back home through night and day and found his hot supper waiting in his room.

summary_text: Allan was a very scary alligator. Every day he polished his scales, sharpened his nails, and brushed his big teeth. Then he went into the jungle and scared the frogs, monkeys, and parrots. Allan loved being scary. At night he went back to the swamp, did his crossword, and took out his false teeth. He kept his false teeth in a secret place, and no one knew about them. One morning Barry the beaver saw Allan and got very frightened. Barry hid behind a bush, and Allan’s false teeth fell out. When Allan woke up, his teeth were gone. He went into the jungle anyway, but without his teeth he was not very scary. Allan went home feeling sad and cried until the next morning. Then the jungle animals came to his swamp and brought back his teeth. They told Allan to stop scaring them. Allan agreed, and after that he became Allan the Gardener, Allan the Hairdresser, Snappy Cuts, and Allan the Dentist. Sometimes he even let Barry borrow his teeth.

summary_text: The story tells about 13 American women who did not give up when people said they could not do big things. Harriet Tubman was born into slavery, but she escaped and led her family, friends, and strangers to freedom. Helen Keller was blind, and some people did not think she could learn, but she learned to read, write, and speak. Clara Limi worked in a factory with terrible conditions and helped workers get better treatment. Nellie Bly became a reporter and told the truth about how people were treated, even when it was risky. Virginia Apgar became a doctor and made the Apgar score for newborn babies. These women kept going even when others tried to stop them.

summary_text: The old Grinch climbed to the roof with empty bags. He slid down the chimney and came into the Who house. He looked at the little Who stockings and said they would be the first things to go. Then he took all the presents, like bicycles, roller skates, drums, tricycles, checkerboards, darts, popcorn, and plums. He stuffed the bags and sent them up the chimney. Next he went to the ice box and took the Who feast, the pudding, the roast beast, and even the last can of hash. He put the food up the chimney too. Then he grabbed the Christmas tree and started to push it away. At that moment he heard a small sound and saw little Cindy Lhoo, who was not more than two. She asked why he was taking the tree. The Grinch told a lie and said he would fix the tree in his workshop and bring it back. Cindy Lhoo believed him, and he sent her back to bed with a drink.

summary_text: A good egg lives in a store carton with many other eggs: Meg, Peg, Greg, Clegg, shell, Shelley, Sheldon, Shelby, Eggbert, Frank, and other Frank. Bluey and Bingo remind each other that they are not forgettable. Then Bluey sees bunny footprints. The girls follow them to Dad’s study and move the yoga ball. There, they find that the Easter Bunny did remember them.

The child cries until Mom hugs them and says it may be at Grandma’s house. Grandma arrives with the truck, and the child is happy because the monster truck is safe.

summary_text: The story tells about seeds and how they begin their lives. A seed is sleepy and stays tucked inside a flower, a cone, or under the soil. Many seeds wait through one or two seasons until spring, and some wait much longer. Seeds can be hidden inside fruits, or they can be naked on cones. Seeds also come in many sizes, from tiny orchid seeds to very large cocoa dimer palm seeds. Seeds are adventurous and travel far by wind, ocean water, shoestrings, or animals. They are inventive and look for a place with sunlight, soil, and water. A seed is generous because it carries a seed coat and food for the baby plant. When a seed gets rain and warmth, it drinks water, sends roots down, and grows toward the sun. Then the seed wakes up and becomes a plant, like a sunflower or a dandelion.

They like different things, but most of all they like each other. Horse and Unicorn become friends, and their friendship is better than pink cupcakes.

summary_text: Ruth Bader Ginsburg grew up in Brooklyn, New York, in a busy neighborhood with many immigrant families. Her mother, Celia, took her to the library and showed her books about girls and women who did important things. Ruth also saw unfair signs like “No dogs or Jews allowed,” and she remembered the hurt of prejudice. In school, she disagreed when teachers made her write with her right hand instead of her left. She also wanted to take shop class like the boys, but girls had to take sewing and cooking. Ruth loved opera and did well in many subjects. In high school she was a strong student, but her mother died just before graduation. Later Ruth went to college, married Marty Ginsberg, and went to law school with him. She studied hard, became a lawyer and teacher, and fought in court for equal rights for women and others.

summary_text: Ruth Bader Ginsburg grew up in Brooklyn, New York, in a Jewish immigrant neighborhood where girls were expected to marry, not make their mark on the world. Her mother disagreed and took her to the library, where Ruth read about girls and women like Nancy Drew, Amelia Earhart, and Athena. Ruth also saw prejudice firsthand, including signs that said Jews were not allowed in some places. In school, she protested being forced to write with her right hand, and she objected to girls having to take sewing and cooking instead of shop. After high school, she went to college, met Martin Ginsberg, and they married, went to law school, and had a daughter, Jane. Ruth graduated near the top of her class, but many employers would not hire her because she was a woman, a mother, and Jewish. She kept going, became a lawyer and professor, later a Supreme Court justice, and used dissents to fight unfair treatment and support equality for women and others.

summary_text: In the village of La Paz, everyone and everything sang all day long. The dogs barked, mothers sang, engines hummed, and fountains made music. The village was so noisy that people could not hear, sleep, or think. They fired the mayor and then voted for Don Pepe, who promised peace and quiet. After he won, new laws told people not to sing in public, then not to sing at home, and then not to sing at all. Soon La Paz became completely silent. Some people left, some learned to hum, and others were glad to rest. Seven quiet years passed. Then a merry gallito and his family came to a mango tree. The next morning the rooster sang, but the mayor said singing was not allowed. Don Pepe tried to stop him by cutting down the tree, taking away his hen and chicks, putting him in a cage, and covering him with a blanket. Still, the gallito kept singing. At last, the village gathered to listen, and the rooster said a song lives on as long as someone sings it.

summary_text: After Michael and his family moved to Falconer Road, he explored the garage behind the house and found it to be dark, dirty, and unsafe. Mr Stone, the estate agent, had tried to make the place sound better by telling them to use their “mind’s eye,” but Michael could only think about the old man, Ernie Myers, who had lived there before and died alone. The house and garden were in bad shape, but Michael’s parents bought it anyway and started cleaning while worrying about the baby. One Sunday, Michael went back to the garage with a torch. He saw broken furniture, dust, cobwebs, and rubbish everywhere. His mother warned him to stay out because it was dangerous. Later, when he went in again, he found an even deeper mess and finally saw a strange little creature sitting behind the tea chests. Michael thought it was dead, but it spoke to him. That was the beginning of Michael’s discovery that the garage held something extraordinary.

summary_text: One winter morning, a new girl named Maya came to Chloe’s classroom with the principal. Maya wore old, ragged clothes and broken shoes, and she looked shy. Miss Albert placed Maya in the empty seat next to Chloe. Maya smiled at Chloe, but Chloe did not smile back and moved away. For many days, Chloe, Kendra, and Sophie ignored Maya at school and at lunch. Maya tried to show them her birthday jacks, cards, Pickup Sticks, a doll, and a jump rope, but they always said no. As the weather grew warmer, Maya came one day in a pretty dress and fancy shoes, but the other girls laughed because they were secondhand. Soon after that, Maya stopped coming to school. In class, Miss Albert taught the students about kindness by dropping a stone into water and showing how ripples spread. Chloe could not think of any kind thing she had done. Later, Miss Albert said Maya’s family had moved away. Chloe went home, threw stones into the pond, and thought about all the kind words and actions she had not given Maya.

summary_text: Otis was a friendly little tractor who worked on the farm with his farmer every day. After work, he liked to play on the hills, by the mud pond, and near the haystacks. At night, he slept in his little stall in the barn. One night, the farmer brought home a baby calf. The calf cried for her mother, but Otis’s soft putt-putt sound helped her fall asleep. Soon, the calf followed Otis everywhere. They played together and sat under the apple tree. Then the farmer got a big yellow tractor and moved Otis out of his stall. The big tractor made loud noises, and the calf did not like him. Later, the calf got stuck in the mud pond. The farmhands, the big tractor, and the fire truck could not help. Then Otis came, circled the pond, and freed the calf. Everyone was happy, and Otis and the calf stayed best friends.

summary_text: One day, a lion walked into the library and went to sleep in the story corner. The library workers did not know what to do because there were no rules about lions. The lion listened quietly during Story Hour, but he roared sadly when the children had to leave. Miss Merryweather said he could return if he stayed quiet. The lion came early each day and helped by dusting books, licking envelopes, and helping children reach high shelves. Everyone loved him, but Mr. McBee thought lions did not belong in libraries. One day, Miss Merryweather hurt her arm and needed help. The lion roared to get Mr. McBee, so he broke the rules and left. The lion stayed away until Mr. McBee told him about a new rule allowing roaring to help an injured friend. Then Mr. McBee told Miss Merryweather that the lion was back, and she happily ran to see him.

summary_text: After helping Moana restore the heart of Te Fiti, Maui was delighted to have his magical fishhook back. The hook made him feel unstoppable because it let him change shape and fight monsters. Maui flew as a hawk across the bright sky, then landed on a green island to rest. While exploring, he decided to go fishing. He built a canoe from a sturdy tree and paddled far from shore. Maui dropped his hook deep into the cold sea and waited. Soon, something pulled hard on the line. Using all his strength, Maui hauled it upward. A rocky point appeared, followed by a whole mountain. His hook had caught a hidden island. Maui pulled up more of it, revealing valleys, waterfalls, forests, and a curving beach. He admired the beautiful island and imagined Moana and her people discovering it. Then he freed his hook and sailed away, eager to fish up more islands for voyagers to find.

In the morning, William saw happy families and a gift from the night gardener. Later, the leaves changed, fell, and the topiary disappeared, but the town and William were changed by what had happened.

summary_text: Mr. Hatch was a quiet man who lived alone and did the same things every day. He walked to the shoelace factory, ate lunch by himself, bought a turkey wing, read the paper, and went to bed early. One Valentine’s Day, he found a package on his porch. Inside was a heart-shaped box of candy and a card that said, “Somebody loves you.” Mr. Hatch was surprised and happy. He laughed, danced, and put on a tie and aftershave. After that, he began smiling and talking to people. He shared candy at work, helped Mr. Smith at the newsstand, and found little Melanie Todd when she was lost. He baked brownies, and the neighborhood children came to his house for a picnic. Later, Mr. Goober the postman said the valentine had been delivered to the wrong house. Mr. Hatch gave back the box and card and felt sad again. But the next Saturday, everyone in the neighborhood came to his house with hearts, candy, streamers, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.”

summary_text: Jule Anne got clean new clothes from her mother. She put on a new shirt and new pants, then sat under the apple tree. A mud puddle hid in the tree and jumped on her head. Jule Anne ran inside and told her mother, and her mother washed her in a tub and cleaned her ears, eyes, and mouth. Then Jule Anne put on more clean clothes and sat in the sandbox. Another mud puddle hid on the house and jumped on her, and this time mud got in her nose too. Her mother washed her again and cleaned her nose. Jule Anne put on fresh clothes, found a yellow raincoat, and went outside. She called to the mud puddle, but nothing happened. When she took off the raincoat, the mud puddle came out from behind the doghouse and jumped on her again. Her mother washed her once more. At last, Jule Anne put on clean clothes, took smelly yellow soap, and called the mud puddle into the backyard. She threw both bars of soap at it, and the mud puddle ran away and never came back.

The fox said a big lake was ahead and helped him cross. The fox told him to climb higher and higher, then flipped him into the air and ate him.

summary_text: It is a brand new school year, and the child is excited because the class should be full of old best friends. The tummy feels bubbly and full of happy feelings. The happy bubbles pop, the insides feel squished, and even smiling feels hard. The child remembers what Mom and Grandpa might say: take a deep breath, be a little brave, and find a smile somewhere. The child also remembers that the best BFF is always me. Then the child thinks about different kinds of new friends, like a smiley friend, a sporty ninja, a funny bunny, a quiet book friend, and a talker who listens. Soon the happy bubbles come back, because there is a whole class of new mates and a playground full of friends waiting. The child feels ready for the best year ever.

summary_text: Long ago, luck was easy to find in Ireland because the leprechauns made it. Then the big folk came, and the leprechaun king worried they would take all the luck. The leprechauns used golden nets to sweep up the luck and store it in an oak chest. But they took too much, and Ireland became unlucky. Hens laid no eggs, cows gave no milk, and potatoes rotted. A woman named Fiona knew the leprechauns had the luck, so she bought a cow and chickens and planted potatoes. Each day she showed milk, eggs, and potatoes to her neighbors, and people thought she had lots of luck. The leprechaun king brought Fiona to his throne room and tested her with shells, a harp, and chess. Fiona lost each test and said she had no luck. Then she wished for a hole in the chest. Luck spilled out, and Fiona returned home as luck flowed freely in Ireland again.

Splat whispered to Seymour, and the door opened. Mrs. Wimpy Dimple changed the chalkboard and wrote, "Cats don't chase mice." Splat went home happy and said he had friends.

summary_text: One happy gray stone lived in a pile with many other stones. He waited while the other stones were picked for different jobs, and he hoped he would have a purpose too. At last, he was chosen and placed on a desk beside a big cup. He thought he might help, but he was only a paperweight. Then bright scribbles came by and made art on the paper. The paper stack got taller and taller, and the scribbles cried because they had used all the paper. Stone did not want them to be sad, so he rolled down and asked if they could use red, yellow, and blue. The scribbles liked his idea and painted on him. More stones came, and soon Stone was picked again. He became a small gift that could brighten someone’s day. After that, scribble stones traveled everywhere and helped many people feel happy.

summary_text: King Mufasa was proud of his son, Simba. Simba had a guardian bird named Zazu. His best friend was Nala, a young lioness. One day, Simba went deep in the jungle and met two new friends: Timone, a mircat, and Pumba, a war dog. Timone said, “Hakuna Matata. No worries.” Simba stayed with them and lived an easy life in the jungle. As Simba grew into a handsome lion, he looked up at the stars and thought about his old home. He remembered that he should be king there. Then Nala found Simba, and they played and romped like old times. Nala told Simba, “Come back home, Simba.” After that, Simba returned home and became the new king. He also had a little cub of his own.

summary_text: A cow on a farm made an unusual sound: “Oink!” The cows that went “Moo” laughed at her, and the other animals laughed too. The cow felt very sad. One day, she met a pig that made another unusual sound: “Moo!” The pigs and the other animals laughed at the pig, so the pig felt sad too. The cow had an idea. She made loud “Oink” sounds, and the pig listened carefully. The pig tried again and again until she could oink. Then the pig taught the cow to moo. Other animals laughed, but the cow listened and practiced. At last, the cow could moo. The cow and the pig were happy because each could make both sounds. They were the only animals on the farm who could do both, so they had the last laugh.

On the way home, the family learned that Alice and Eliza Jane had also won ribbons. Father said the Wilder family had done itself proud.

summary_text: In a pumpkin patch, a little pumpkin named Spooky was born. He was not round like the other pumpkins. He was square, and the other pumpkins teased him because he could not roll. Spooky wished he could be like them. Then Halloween was almost here, and a big storm came. The wind tossed the round pumpkins around and broke their vines. Spooky stayed safe because he was square. When the fence broke, three pumpkins rolled into the bay. Spooky tipped and flipped until he fit in the gap and stopped the pumpkins from going farther. The pumpkins shouted hooray. After the storm, the farmer saw Spooky holding the broken fence. He knew Spooky had saved the day. The next year, the farmer planted Spookley’s seeds, and many pumpkins grew in many shapes and colors. Every Halloween, people come to see the special pumpkins and remember not to judge by how something looks.

summary_text: One warm day, a little cricket was born from a tiny egg. A big cricket said, “Welcome,” and rubbed his wings together. The little cricket tried to answer, but no sound came out. A locust, a praying mantis, a worm, a spittle bug, a cicada, a bumblebee, a dragonfly, and mosquitoes all said hello in their own ways. Then he saw another cricket, and she was quiet too. He rubbed his wings together one more time, and this time he made a beautiful chirping sound. She heard it and said, “Thank you.”

Soon they heard giggling inside a trap. There was a tiny leprechaun in green clothes, holding something shiny and golden. Tim and Morin walked up to him and stared right into his eyes. Then they asked him to tell them where the gold was.

summary_text: Tony Sar loved to make things move. When he was a little boy, his father asked him to feed the chickens every morning. Tony tied ropes and pulleys from the chicken coop to his bedroom window so he could open the coop door without leaving bed. In the morning, he pulled the rope, the chickens ate, and his father was so impressed that Tony never had to do the chore again. When Tony grew up, he moved to London and began making marionettes out of wood, cloth, and strings. His puppets moved so well that people thought they were real. Later, in New York City, Macy’s asked him to create holiday window puppets and then help with a parade. Tony made new puppets and floats, and the first Macy’s parade was a big success. When the animals scared children, Tony made larger balloons from rubberized silk and filled them with helium. On Thanksgiving Day, the giant puppets rose into the sky and marched through New York City, starting the famous Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

summary_text: One day in the jungle of N, Horton the Elephant heard a tiny cry. He looked around and saw only a small Speck of dust blowing in the air. Horton guessed that a tiny person might be on the Speck, so he gently lifted it with his trunk and put it on a soft clover. The Sour Kangaroo and her child laughed at Horton, but Horton carried the clover away to keep the small people safe. The Wickersham brothers took the clover and gave it to a black-bottomed eagle named Vlad Vladikoff, who flew away with it. Horton chased the eagle for a long time until Vlad dropped the clover into a huge field of clovers. Horton searched and searched until he found Whoville again. The mayor told Horton that the Whos needed to make more noise to prove they were there. The Whos all shouted together, and the smallest one, Jojo, added one more sound. Then everyone could hear them, and Horton was glad they were safe.

Oscar was a small, funny-shaped dog. The other dogs teased him and called him names, and even Oscar’s mother did this when the dogs went to obedience school. Oscar felt upset, but on Halloween he thought about costumes and trick-or-treating instead. When he got home, his mother had made him a big hot dog bun costume with mustard. Oscar did not want to hurt her feelings, so he wore it.

That night, the dogs met on the Block in scary costumes. When Oscar arrived, they laughed at his costume and ran off to trick-or-treat. Oscar’s costume slowed him down, and he got no treats. Later, the dogs saw a monster near a graveyard and jumped into a pond. Oscar looked carefully and saw that the “monster” was really two hory cats. The cats ran away, and Oscar swam to the dogs. His costume helped as a life raft, and he carried them back to shore. The dogs shared their treats with Oscar and called him hero sandwich.

On Halloween, Oscar thought about trick-or-treating and scary costumes instead of the teasing. When he got home from obedience school, he found that his mother had made him a costume: a giant hot dog bun with mustard, meant for him to fit in the middle. Oscar did not want to hurt her feelings, so he wore it. The dogs on the Block showed off their costumes, and when Oscar arrived, they laughed at how silly he looked. During trick-or-treating, his costume slowed him down, so the other dogs got to the houses first and took all the treats. Later, a scary monster appeared near a graveyard, but Oscar saw that it was really two cats. The dogs were embarrassed, and Oscar rescued them by using his costume as a life raft. After that, the dogs shared their treats with him and called him hero sandwich.

summary_text: Mikey was excited because he was about to turn four. He told his mom that all of his friends would come, there would be many presents, a big cake, and a perfect party. His mom said the party was not complete until he chose what to eat. Mikey thought about pizza, burgers, hot dogs, pork, fried rice, pasta, dumplings, and other foods. He asked his granny and Nona about birthday food, and he remembered food from cousins’ parties too. Soon he felt confused and rushed to the park. There, his friend Sophia asked what was wrong. Mikey said he could not choose a dish for his party tomorrow. Sophia reminded him that his mom was Italian and his dad was Chinese, so he could choose both. Mikey understood and went home. He told his mom he wanted fried rice and marinara sauce. The next day, his mom cooked the dish, his friends helped, and everyone loved the meal. The party ended with everyone saying, “Different is good.”

summary_text: Anil loved hearing stories about a far away village with green wheat fields and coconut palms. One day he asked who was telling the story, and his grandfather, D, began to speak. Later Anil wanted to know if the power could return again, but there was no Roy at home. So Anil made the dough himself. He mixed flour, salt, and water, rolled the Roy, cooked them on the Tava pan, and stacked them high. D ate the Roy, licked his fingers, flexed his muscles, and the power came back. Anil and D went outside to find more adventures.

In 1863 he became president and signed a paper saying all the slaves would be free. Susan B. Anthony wanted girls to vote too. She tried to vote and got arrested. She kept speaking for fairness, and in 1920 women in America got the right to vote.

summary_text: The narrator refuses to leave Marlborough Court, the condemned housing project that has been his home for years. He lives alone with his spaniel, Poppy, and believes the council should not force him out simply because the estate is being demolished for a new intersection. Another resident, Mr. Malqueenie, also stays behind, but the two men do not get along. Strange events begin: a football appears outside the narrator’s door, every door in the estate seems to rattle, and horrifying faces appear on Mr. Malqueenie’s window. Soon Mr. Malqueenie dies, and Poppy disappears. The narrator follows Poppy’s yelps into an empty flat, where he discovers millions of cockroaches covering the floor, walls, and ceiling. Terrified, he leaves the estate. He sees his belongings being burned, then turns back, determined not to be bullied. Before he can return, a vehicle hits him. Later, he sees that the new intersection is completely gridlocked, so the project has not improved the city as promised.

summary_text: Edward feels unhappy about his neck because he thinks it is too long, bendy, narrow, and strange. He tries to hide it with scarves, bow ties, trees, shrubs, ditches, and even the river, but nothing helps. He looks at other animals, like a zebra, elephant, and lion, and wishes his neck looked better. His mother tells him he should be proud of it, but Edward still does not like it. One evening, he meets Cyrus, who has a short neck and says he wishes he had Edward’s neck because it would help him do more things. Cyrus explains that he has spent seven days on a hill watching a banana ripen, but he cannot reach it. Edward uses his long neck to grab the banana for him. Cyrus is grateful and says Edward’s neck is impressive. Edward then says Cyrus’s neck is elegant too, and both of them feel better about their necks by the end.

summary_text: Jasper Rabbit was having trouble at school. He failed math and spelling, and only art went well. Then he found a purple crayon that was pointy, perfect, and seemed happy to see him. He got an A+ and a sticker. Later, the crayon helped him with math, and the answers seemed easy. Jasper saw strange purple words appear, like “Jasper and crayon forever” and “Who needs math when you have Bunny Ball Three?” He tried to hide the crayon, but his poster became a purple masterpiece. Jasper felt scared, so he put the crayon in a box, broke it, melted it, and threw it away. But it kept coming back, helping him with quizzes and even showing him a mural of his future. Finally, Jasper threw it in the toilet. After that, he studied on his own, got a C+, and felt free. The crayon floated away, and then Elliot Pelican found it.

summary_text: A narrator dreams of “you,” and then the two are together. They carry gifts in a backpack and cross a bridge that is like the universe. They say goodbye, “Adios corazon,” and reach the other side. There, they cannot go back, and they become immigrant migrants. The sky and the land welcome them with words they do not know. They do not understand many things and feel afraid to speak. They make many mistakes. Then they become caminantes, walking thousands and thousands of steps across the land. One day, they find a new place that is strange and surprising. In that place, they do not need to speak. They only need to trust, and they do. Books become their language, their home, and their lives. They learn to read, speak, write, and make their voices heard. In the end, they are stories, two languages, lucha, resilience, hope, and dreamers, “sonyadores of the world.”

Trixie helped put the laundry in the machine and put money in too. Then they left. A little later, Trixie realized something. She turned to her daddy and said, “Aggle flaggle klabble.” Daddy answered, “That’s right. We’re going home.” Trixie said more words, but Daddy told her not to get fussy. Trixie cried and went boneless because she was unhappy. When they got home, Mommy opened the door and asked, “Where’s Knuffle Bunny?” The family ran back down the block, through the park, past the school, and to the laundromat. Daddy looked and looked, but Knuffle Bunny was not there. Then Daddy decided to look harder.

summary_text: On Christmas Eve, long ago, a boy from Finmark was traveling to Oslo with his ice bear. He saw smoke from a hut and went toward it because he was cold and hungry. Inside the hut, Kyrie was warming food on the fire. There was sausage, fish, buns, cakes, porridge, and apple cider. Kyrie had been afraid because trolls had come in past years and eaten the Christmas meal. Her father had gone up the mountain to watch for them. The boy came inside, and the ice bear slept under the stove. Soon they heard knocking at the door and more loud banging. The boy pushed a chest in front of the door and locked the windows. Then the trolls broke in through the cellar trapdoor. They ate the food and made a big mess. A little troll woke the ice bear by poking his nose with sausage. The bear chased the trolls away. Later, Kyrie's father came home, and they all ate porridge. One year later, a little troll saw Kyrie and asked about the sleeping cat, and Kyrie said it had grown into a big cat with seven kittens, so the troll ran away.

summary_text: Jean-Michel grows up in Brooklyn and dreams of becoming a famous artist. At home, he draws all day at a table covered with pencils and papers. Later, Matilde becomes ill and cannot stay at home. Jean-Michel keeps visiting her and shows her his artwork, telling her it will one day be in a museum.

summary_text: A troll lived under a bridge in mud and trash. He was very hungry and waited for animals to cross above him. One day he heard clip-clop sounds and climbed up to stop a little goat. The goat said his name was Billy Goat Gruff and told the troll he was too small to eat. He also said his big brother would come later and would be bigger and tastier. The troll let him pass. Then the second Billy Goat Gruff came. He said the same thing, and again the troll let him cross after hearing about the bigger brother. At last, the third Billy Goat Gruff arrived. The troll tried to threaten him, but the big goat lowered his horns and rammed the troll. The troll flew off the bridge and down the waterfalls. The three goats went to the grassy ridge and stayed there eating grass.

summary_text: There was once a good shoemaker who became very poor. He and his wife had only enough leather to make one last pair of shoes. The shoemaker planned to cut the leather at night and sew the shoes in the morning. But when they came to the workshop, they found two finished shoes on the table. A dandy gentleman came to the shop, tried the shoes on, and paid double. The shoemaker bought leather for more shoes. Again, each night, he cut the leather, and each morning the shoes were finished. Soon the shoes were famous, and the shoemaker and his wife were no longer poor. Near Christmas, they stayed up and watched. At midnight, two tiny elves came in and made the shoes. The next day the couple made warm clothes and shoes for the elves. That night the elves found the gifts, put them on, danced, sang, and ran away. After that, they were never seen again, and the shoemaker and his wife lived happily.

summary_text: On her birthday, Carmela rode her scooter with her big brother through their town. They passed the greenhouses, the Laundromat, the bodega, the pharmacy, and other busy places. Carmela wore her birthday bracelets, and they jingled as she moved. Her brother did not want her to follow him, and he kept telling her she was annoying. Carmela found a dandelion and wanted to make a wish, but she did not know what to wish for. She helped her brother with the laundry and kept imagining many things, like candy, her mom in a hotel bed, and her dad getting his papers fixed. Then her brother went into a friend’s house, and Carmela sat on the curb. She thought about turning him into animals and looked at the dandelion again. On the way home, she fell and crushed the dandelion. Her brother helped her, then took her to an abandoned farmhouse near the sea. He told her to close her eyes and make her wish. When she opened them, she saw white spores floating in the air like wishes. He said not to tell the wish, and Carmela took off her bracelets and went home with him.

Rosco then told Nigel not to play with Odie, but Nigel also said this was not kind. Nigel went to play with Odie and the other chickens. Next, Rosco told Nugget not to play with Jasmine because Jasmine sang too much. Nugget told him to be kind and maybe sing with Jasmine. Rosco was soon alone because he had been bossy. He remembered that the other chickens had once been kind to him when he was new. Rosco went to say sorry. The chickens forgave him and let him play with them. Rosco thanked them for showing him how to be kind.

summary_text: Rosco was a rooster who did not like to wait. One morning, Joey practiced crowing before the sun came up. Rosco heard Joey and told him his crow was wrong and too slow to learn. Gracita heard Rosco being unkind. She told him that love is patient and kind, and that being patient means waiting without getting upset. Rosco said he did not like waiting. Later, the farm dogs, Leila and Piper, chased a soccer ball. Rosco wanted to play right away, but Piper and Ilila told him he had to wait his turn. At 3:00, Farmer John brought grain for the chickens, and Rosco pushed to get food first. Chaita told him to wait. Rosco then saw he had not been patient. He said sorry to Piper, Lila, and Joey. Joey kept practicing and finally crowed right. Everyone cheered for him. That night, Rosco began to rush the hens into the coupe, but he stopped and said they could take their time while he waited patiently.

summary_text: Poe was a pilot who fought against the evil First Order. One day, Leia gave Poe a special mission. Poe and his droid, BB-8, had to find a man named Lor San Teca on the planet Jakku. When the First Order troopers landed, Poe told Lor to hide and gave the map to BB-8 so the First Order would not get it. The troopers captured Poe and took him to Kylo Ren. Poe called FN-2187 Finn, and they flew back toward Jakku to find BB-8.
