summary_text: Jamie oor lived in Ireland and was very lazy. His wife, Eileene, planted, watered, and weeded the potatoes, but Jamie would not help dig them up. One day Eileene hurt her back and had to stay in bed. Jamie became worried because there would be no potatoes for winter. At midnight he went to church, but on the hill he heard singing and tapping. He found a leprechaun making fairy shoes. Jamie grabbed him and asked for a pot of gold, but the leprechaun offered a wish instead. Jamie wished for the biggest potato in the world. The leprechaun gave him a seed. Jamie planted it, and a huge potato grew so big it pushed up the garden and part of the cottage. The villagers came, helped dig it out, and shared the potato. In spring Jamie kept one potato eye, but the villagers promised to give him food if he did not plant it again.

She travels through Muffin Meadow, Black Coffee Cave, Bacon Bridge, and Hash Brown Hill, stopping for a quick picnic on the way. When she reaches the peaceful top of Pancake Peak, a noisy group of creatures appears. The packrat Fitz, the Havalina Lewis, and the porcupine Violet are stranded. They ask Julia to help them get back down the mountain. Julia does not like this change, but she helps them return safely to the base of Pancake Peak. The friends rest for a sunny picnic at Hash Brown Hill, and Fitz shares snacks from his pack so he can carry it again. They keep going, but Bacon Bridge is broken. Then they enter Black Coffee Cave, where Julia loses her headlamp and flashlight. Lewis uses his strong nose to lead them toward Muffin Meadow. Violet warns them about a trap and protects the group from danger. At the end, Julia reaches home in time for dinner and eats with her new friends.

summary_text: Eugene loved the aquarium on Saturday. She watched the glittery fish and, most of all, the sharks. She pretended to swim like them and wanted to know what it would be like to live under the sea. In the summer, her mother took her to the beach in Atlantic City, and Eugene dove into the water. She imagined sharks, sea stars, and ocean currents, and she saw sharks as beautiful. Since the sharks were only in her mind, she decided to learn all she could about them. Eugene read books about whale sharks, nurse sharks, tiger sharks, and lemon sharks. She joined the Queens County aquarium society and filled her notebooks with shark drawings and facts. Her mother also gave her a small aquarium, and Eugene kept fish and snails in her room. As she grew older, people told her to stop thinking about sharks, but Eugene studied zoology, became a scientist, found new fish, saw a wild shark, and later trained sharks. In the end, she proved sharks are smart and should be protected and loved.

summary_text: Sylvester Duncan lived with his mother and father in Oatsdale. He liked to collect pebbles. One rainy day he found a bright red pebble that was round like a marble. When he wished for the rain to stop, it stopped right away. He then learned the pebble was magic. He made rain come back, then wished the sunshine back and even made a wart disappear. Happy and excited, he started home to show his parents. On Strawberry Hill, he saw a hungry lion. He got scared and said, “I wish I were a rock,” and he turned into a rock. The magic pebble fell beside him, and he could not touch it. Back home, his parents searched for him for a long time, but they could not find him. Seasons changed, and Sylvester stayed a rock on the hill. One May day, his parents had a picnic there. His mother sat on him, and his father picked up the red pebble and put it on the rock. Sylvester wished to be himself again, and he changed back. His parents hugged him, and they took the pebble home and locked it in a safe.

summary_text: Mr. Small has a little Auto. It is red and shiny, and he keeps it in the garage at the end of the driveway. One day he oils it, pumps up the rubber tires, and fills the radiator with water. Then he gets ready for a drive. He steps on the starter, the engine begins to hum, and the little Auto backs out of the garage and goes chug chug down the driveway and road. Mr. Small toots the horn and scares the ducks and chickens. A small dog follows, but soon falls behind. The little Auto goes fast, passes a horse and buggy, and goes uphill and downhill until it comes to town. Mr. Small drives on the right side of the street, waits at a stop sign, stops at a filling station for 5 gallons of gas, and later waits by a trolley car. He parks to buy a newspaper, then starts home. A red light makes him stop, rain makes him put up the top, and a flat tire makes him jack up the car and put on the spare. When the sun comes out, he washes and polishes the little Auto and puts it back in the garage, shining like new.

summary_text: Melvin did not like disappointment. If his cookie had fewer chocolate chips, if he lost a turn in a game, or if he did not get the backpack he wanted, he wanted to throw a fit. At school, his teacher had a rule: "you get what you get and you don't throw a fit." This meant Melvin had to stay calm when he got crayons instead of markers, when he was last in line, or when his napkin was pink instead of green. Melvin thought he could still throw a fit at home. But one night, when it was his turn to choose the movie, he picked Dinosaur Rumble, and his sister wanted to watch a pony movie called Trouble. Melvin told her the rule. Then his family said the same words to him about cookies, games, and backpacks. Melvin wanted to cry and shout, but he did not. He learned the rule was for home too.

summary_text: The story explains that there is a peaceful spot and an anxiety spot. The anxiety spot shows up when someone feels worried, nervous, anxious, or scared. It can grow bigger when a child tries something new, like playing soccer for the first time or taking a test. When this happens, the story says to answer the worry with, “I can do this.” Small anxiety spots can sometimes help keep a child safe, but big worries can make it hard to enjoy good things. The story also says anxiety can cause a tummy ache or sweating. To help keep anxiety from growing, children should eat healthy foods, get enough rest, and use music, drawing, or writing to share their worries. If anxiety grows fast, the story teaches a trick: imagine gray spots on the fingers and a green spot on the palm, say, “I can do this. I can be calm,” then take a deep breath and blow the worry away.

summary_text: A poor raccoon wants pizza very much, but he does not know how to ask politely. Someone says pizza is wonderful and suggests a secret pizza party at the raccoon’s house. The pizza party is kept secret so it can feel special. The raccoon is told to call the pizza man and ask for the best pizza pie. Then the raccoon worries that the delivery guy may know him from posters and chase him with a broom. He tries to act calm and follows a sneaky route past the broom factory, the broom Enthusiast Club, and the raccoon sniffing broom Bots. But the bots are there, so he runs fast. At last, the raccoon and the others make it home, block the doors, and open the pizza box. They have a secret pizza party and try to stay quiet, but the pizza makes them so happy that they forget to be secret.

summary_text: One night, Monica looked out her window and saw the moon. It looked very close, and Monica wanted to play with it. She stretched her arms, but she could not reach it. Monica asked Papa to get the moon for her. Papa took a very long ladder and carried it to a very high mountain. He put the ladder on the mountain and climbed up and up until he reached the moon. Papa told the moon that Monica wanted to play with it. The moon said it got a little smaller every night. When it was just the right size, Papa could take it. The moon became smaller and smaller, and Papa brought it down to Monica. Monica jumped and danced with the moon. She hugged it and threw it in the air. Then the moon got smaller and smaller until it disappeared. Later, Monica saw a thin moon again, and each night it grew bigger.

The child does not want to play because it all feels like too much. Later, the child asks for a gentle hug and feels brave. The child learns to say what is needed, like quiet time, a dark place, a soft shirt, and personal space. With deep breaths and a held hand, the child feels thankful and calm.

summary_text: Jamie O'Rourke was the laziest man in Ireland, and he would not dig the potatoes. His wife, Eileen, did the planting, watering, and weeding, but then she hurt her back and had to stay in bed. Jamie worried that there would be no food for winter, so he went to church at night. On the way, he found a leprechaun making fairy boots. Jamie caught him and asked for a pot of gold. The leprechaun offered a wish instead, and Jamie wished for the biggest potato in the world. Jamie planted the seed, and a giant potato grew so big that it pushed up the garden shed and part of the cottage. The villagers came to see it and helped dig it out. The potato blocked the road, so everyone cut it up and shared it. All winter they ate the potato, and in spring the villagers promised to help Jamie and Eileen always have food if he did not plant another giant potato.

summary_text: On a sunny day in the highlands, Princess Merida looked for Angus, her horse and best friend. She found him near a very high bridge, where he was helping the stable master carry stones. Angus became frightened, so Merida hugged him and calmed him down. Then Merida and Angus rode into the hills and went farther from home than they had before. Later, they found an old road that led into a dark, misty wood. Merida wanted to go home, but she saw a big shadow and heard a twig snap. Angus got scared and ran fast into the fog. Merida saw that the shadow was only an old tree. Angus kept racing toward a cliff, and Merida could not stop him. She saw a ledge far across a ravine and told Angus to jump. Angus trusted Merida, leaped across, and landed safely. Then they ran back to the castle and went home safe together.

Then the engines worked together to clear the tracks and bring the Christmas tree back to Tidmouth station. People waved and cheered. The tree was decorated just in time, and the Christmas party began.

The next day, snow covered the yard, and Sir Topham Hat said Thomas had done the right thing. On Boxing Day, Thomas, James, and Henry gave children free rides and gifts, and Thomas was very happy.

summary_text: Molly and Gill were walking to school when they saw a spider web. Gill found a spider and named him Charlie. Molly asked about spiders, and Gill said spiders wait for flies in their webs and then eat them. Molly and Gill said they could come back later. At school, Mr. Grouper told the class they would be in a bug parade. The children got costumes and joined the parade. Charlie watched from his new web. There were marching ants, a ladybug on a float, a bubble puppy dressed as a grasshopper, and a dragonfly flying around. Molly and Gill learned that spiders are not insects; they are arachnids. Then the wind blew hard and some big bug balloons flew away. One fly balloon headed toward Charlie’s web. Molly and Gill used ropes to make a giant web and caught the balloon. Charlie and his web stayed safe, and Charlie made a heart of silk for his friends.

summary_text: Almanso lived with his father, mother, brother Royal, and sisters Eliza Jane and Alice in the New York State countryside. One morning, the family rode to the county fair. Father brought the girls’ pickles, preserves, jellies, and Alice’s woolwork. Almanso’s pumpkin had already gone in a wagon because it was too big for the buggy. At the fair, mother, Royal, and the girls went to help in the church building, and Almanso went with father to the animal sheds. He saw big horses, cattle, hogs, sheep, and then a mule that scared him when it roared at him. Later, Almanso ate a very big dinner in the crowded church dining room. After that, the judges looked at the pumpkins and gave Almanso’s pumpkin a blue ribbon. Almanso and father walked around the fair and watched the contests. On the way home, they learned that Alice, Eliza Jane, and the family’s foods had won prizes too, and Almanso felt very proud.

Chief Bogo arrests Bellweather, and Judy and Nick keep working together to keep Zootopia safe.

summary_text: Nikki wanted new mittens made of wool as white as snow. His grandmother Baba did not want to make white mittens at first because she said they could be lost in the snow. Nikki wanted them, so Baba made them. She told him she would look to see if he was safe and sound when he came home, and then she would look to see if he still had his Snow White mittens. Nikki went outside, and soon one mitten dropped in the snow. A mole found it and crawled inside. Then a snowshoe rabbit came by and squeezed in too. A hedgehog, an owl, a badger, a fox, and a great bear all came to live in the mitten as well. The mitten stretched, but Baba's knitting held. Then a tiny mouse climbed in. The mouse tickled the bear, and the bear sneezed. The sneeze sent the mitten and the animals flying apart. Nikki saw the mitten in the sky and ran to get it. When he got home, Baba saw that he was safe and still had his mittens.

summary_text: On the night before Christmas, Olaf looked around the house while Elsa slept in her bed and Anna snored softly. The stockings were hung by the chimney, and the night was quiet. Then Olaf heard a loud clatter outside. He went to the window and saw the bright moon, snowy air, and a flying sled in the sky. Kristoff was riding with Sven, and they called out names like a Christmas song as the sled flew toward the castle. Olaf watched as the sled went over the wall and up to the roof. Soon he heard thumping on the roof and then a bump in the chimney. A man in black boots and red pants came out of the fireplace with a fluffy white beard and kind eyes. He carried a big bag of gifts for Anna, Sven, Kristoff, Elsa, and Olaf's friends. Olaf tugged on his coat, said his name, and told him he liked warm hugs. The man laughed, hugged Olaf, and then climbed back up the chimney. Before he left, he said, Merry Christmas to all and to all a good night.

summary_text: Abigail is eight years old and has trouble reading in school. She works in the blue group, where the books and activities seem less exciting than those in the yellow and green groups. Her mother explains that dyslexia means learning differently. Abigail can think in pictures, notice hidden possibilities, use her senses, and imagine many things. When her brother Josh calls her a superhero too, she feels less alone and begins to see dyslexia as a powerful way to understand the world.

summary_text: One wonderful day, Jim pansy woke up and thought everything was wrong. The sun was too bright, the sky was too blue, and the bananas were too sweet. Jim did not know what was happening. Norman from next door said Jim might be grumpy, but Jim said he was not. On his walk, Jim met Marabou, then lemur, then snake. Norman kept saying Jim was grumpy, and the others pointed out Jim’s hunched body, bunched eyebrows, and frown. Jim tried to fix these things by loosening up, raising his brow, and smiling, but he still did not feel happy inside. Many animals asked Jim to sing, swing, roll, stroll, lie in the grass, stomp, take a bath, hug, laugh, nap, eat, jump, sit in the sun, and dance. Jim did none of it. He shouted, stormed off, and felt sorry. Then Jim found Norman again. Norman was grumpy too because he had danced with porcupine and got hurt. Jim asked if Norman was okay, and Norman said he would feel better soon. Jim said he was still grumpy too, and Norman said it was a wonderful day to be grumpy. Jim agreed and felt a little better.

Scout took these foods home and made a dish with bun, ketchup, pickles, bacon, patty, mustard, and bun. The meal was good, but something was still missing. Scout visited Dr. Ham, and together they made tomato, onion, and lettuce. Scout added them to the dish, and it became perfect. The dinosaurs loved it, and the dish was named the hamburger.

summary_text: Ebenezer Scrooge is a wealthy but miserly man who dislikes Christmas and treats his clerk, Bob Cratchit, harshly. On Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his dead friend Marley, followed by the ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. The first ghost shows Scrooge his lonely childhood and the moments when he chose wealth over love. The second shows Bob’s poor but loving family, including Tiny Tim, and the difficult lives of working people. The final ghost shows Tiny Tim dying and a lonely grave marked with Scrooge’s own name. Frightened, Scrooge realizes he can change. On Christmas morning, he buys a turkey and gifts for the Cratchit family. He promises to become a better employer, pay Bob well, and use his wealth to help sick and poor people. Scrooge changes from a miser into a generous and kind man.

People have walked on the Moon, leaving footprints and objects behind. The Moon says it is always with Earth, day and night.

summary_text: In 1844, thirteen-year-old Hansen Gregory left his family farm in Maine to work at sea. He became a cook’s assistant, climbed high into ship rigging, learned to steer by the sun and stars, and eventually became captain of a fast clipper ship. He even rescued seven sailors from a freezing sea. The story of his famous pastry began on June 22, 1847. Hansen and the cook were making fried cakes for hungry sailors. The cakes were crisp outside but greasy and raw in the middle, so sailors called them “sinkers.” Hansen used a pepper-can lid to cut holes in the dough before frying it. The new ring-shaped cakes were sweet, brown, and cooked all the way through. Hansen’s mother sold them to sailors, and the idea spread around the world. Later, sailors told exciting legends about how he invented donuts, but Captain Gregory said the holes made them well done and prevented indigestion.

But Grandma was busy and full of surprises. Her house was filled with books, fish charts, fishing poles, and a half-finished bear carving. She gave Nikki chores like stacking firewood, cleaning gutters, and fixing the truck. Then she taught Nikki to fish for bluegills near the lily pads. Nikki did not catch anything at first and thought the river had no fish. The next day, while waiting on the dock, Nikki found an old raft floating toward her with drawings of animals on it. Grandma helped her use the raft, and many birds and animals came close. Nikki began to draw what she saw. She spent the summer exploring, swimming, and learning about the river. On her last day, she helped a deer fawn stuck in mud, drew it on the raft, and Grandma painted over the drawing so Nikki would always be part of the river.

During the war in 1812, he ran through the night to warn families about danger. He later moved to Indiana, and in 1845 he became sick in a snowstorm and died in a cabin. People still told stories about him after he was gone.

Finally, a kind old woman offered her plain lima beans. Camila admitted she really loved lima beans, ate them, and the stripes disappeared. After that, she ate lima beans whenever she wanted and never got stripes again.

Nancy learns that making something together can become a special heirloom. On Christmas morning, the tree is magnificent, joyous, sparkly, and splendiferous.

summary_text: Old Bifana lived alone in a small house in Italy. She was grumpy and did not invite people inside, but she swept her house, steps, and path every day. One night, a bright star woke her. The next morning, three kings and a great procession came by. They were searching for a baby king in Bethlehem. A boy told Bifana that the baby would change the world and that the kings were bringing gifts. Bifana decided to go too. She baked cakes, cookies, and candies, and packed them in a basket. She also brought her broom. However, she stopped to sweep before leaving, so the procession went ahead. Bifana ran after it, but her old legs grew tired. Angels then filled the sky and announced that the new king had been born. Bifana never found the baby, but she still searches. Every January 6, she visits sleeping children, leaves gifts, and sweeps their rooms, hoping one of them might be the baby king.

summary_text: When the sun slips down, bats wake up and fly out of their barn, cave, and rafter. They call to each other and say the moon is perfect for bats at the beach. Soon they pack buckets, towels, blankets, books, and other things, then fly over the dark trees to the ocean. They land on warm sand and set up their blankets. The bats play games, bury friends in sand, make sand caves, and race on the waves. At lunchtime, they eat beetles, ants, milkweed bugs, crickets, moths, and other bug treats. Later, their stomachs hurt, so they go to the snack bar for dessert. The old bats sing bat songs while the little bats rest. Then the sky turns purple and the sun begins to come up. The bats say goodbye, pack their things, and fly home before day. They curl up in their home and dream about the moon weather.

The prince fell from the tower and became blind. Years later, he found the girl. Her tears healed his eyes, and he took her to his kingdom. They lived happily together.

Mayor Humdinger gave them the trophy, and Mayor Goodway gave it to Ryder and the Paw Patrol.

Milo wins and learns that not giving up is the secret ingredient.

summary_text: The Little Red Caboose always came last on the train. First came the big black engine, then the boxcars, oil cars, coal cars, and flat cars. Boys and girls waved at the engine and listened to the other cars go click, but they often turned away before the Little Red Caboose arrived. The little red caboose felt sad and wished he were a box car, a coal car, an oil car, a flat car, or even the big black engine. One day the train went up a long, tall mountain. The train got slower and slower, and it looked like it might slide back. The Little Red Caboose saw this and slammed on his brakes. He held tight to the tracks and stopped the train from slipping down. Then two big black engines pushed from behind and helped the train reach the top. Everyone cheered, and the other cars said the children saved their biggest waves for the Little Red Caboose because he saved the train.

A baker told Ember to come inside and help in the bakery. Ember washed, pushed dough, and used his small flame to light the stove. He watched the dough change into golden bread. In the end, Ember learned that baking gold was better than taking it, and sharing it was best of all.

summary_text: Once a year, wishes float through the sky, and a lucky rabbit catches three. He does not know what to wish for, so he asks his friends. Mouse wishes to fly because the world feels big and Mouse feels small. Fox wishes to write stories that people admire and that offer knowledge, hope, and inspiration. Bear wishes for a boat so Bear can explore the open sea. Rabbit thinks about each wish and realizes that his friends’ wishes could help them. He uses all three wishes for Mouse, Fox, and Bear, leaving none for himself. Then his friends explain that Rabbit’s kindness helped them feel important and inspired. Mouse says Rabbit will guide him home, Fox begins writing wonderful stories, and Bear invites Rabbit on an adventure in his new boat. Rabbit’s selfless choice brings his friends joy and gives them chances to share their talents together.

summary_text: Marjorie loved growing seeds into gardens, knitting cozy creations, and watching her favorite baking show. She wanted a friend who enjoyed those things too, because she missed Granny, who had shared her interests. One day, Marjorie saw a sign for a senior group at the community center. Although children were not allowed, she disguised herself with flour, glasses, scarves, perfume, and her mother’s cardigan. Inside, Arthur welcomed her. She learned knitting from Patrick, gardening from Betty, and a stew recipe from Jill. When the group began dancing, Marjorie tried to leave, but she eventually joined the cha-cha-cha. Her disguise slipped off while she danced, and everyone discovered she was a child. Marjorie apologized and explained that she only wanted friends. Arthur told her that people may look old on the outside but still feel like children inside. The group welcomed Marjorie, and she became their youngest member.

In the end, they say they are best friends and play spies and build a castle, adding flags, towers, arches, windows, stairs, a gatehouse, and a drawbridge until it is perfect.

summary_text: Mary lived in Nazareth. An angel came from God and told her she would have a baby boy named Jesus. Mary was afraid, but the angel said not to fear. Mary said she was the servant of the Lord. Later, Mary and Joseph had to travel to Bethlehem to be counted. Bethlehem was very crowded, so they stayed in a stable at an inn. There Mary had her baby. She wrapped baby Jesus in clothes and laid him in a manger. Shepherds were watching their sheep when an angel told them the good news that Christ the Lord was born. More angels sang, “Glory to God peace on Earth.” The shepherds hurried to Bethlehem and saw Mary, Joseph, and baby Jesus. They told everyone what they had seen. Then three wise men came from the East, followed a star, and found Jesus. They bowed down and gave him gifts. God warned them in a dream not to go back to King Herod, so they went home another way. An angel told Joseph to take Mary and Jesus to Egypt. They stayed there until Herod died, then returned to Nazareth, where Jesus grew up.

summary_text: Tommy was excited for the first big race at school. He wanted to win and stand on the top of the podium. summary_text: Deep under the blue sea lived the Sea King and his six daughters. The youngest princess was the prettiest, and she loved her garden, her grandmother, and hearing stories about the world above the water. When each sister turned fifteen, she went to the surface and came back with tales of the sky, the sunset, the stars, and the icebergs. At last the little mermaid turned fifteen too. She rose to the surface and saw a large ship with music, lanterns, and fireworks. On the ship she saw a handsome young prince. Soon a storm broke the ship apart, and the little mermaid found the prince floating in the water. She carried him to shore and watched a girl from a convent help him. The prince never knew the little mermaid saved him, and she became very sad. She later went to the sea witch, gave up her voice, and got legs. She lived with the prince, but he married the convent girl. In the end, the little mermaid threw away the knife her sisters gave her and became light in the dawn sky.

Red Riding Hood promised never to leave the forest path again.

summary_text:
On a snowy mountain, Gertie was the littlest yak in the herd. She had curly wool and grippy hooves, but she wished she were bigger, with tallness, huge hooves, and humongous horns. Her mother told her that yaks come in different sizes and that it was good to be small for now. Gertie still wanted to grow right away, so she ate many vegetables, climbed mountains, ran, hopped, skipped, and read books, hoping to become large. But no growing happened, and she felt upset.

Then the herd heard that another yak was stuck on a steep cliff ledge. Mommy yak said the herd could not reach him because their hooves were too heavy and their horns were too wide, but Gertie was small and grippy, so she was the only one who could help. Gertie climbed quickly to the ledge, where a small yak was shivering. She told him to hold on, let him climb onto her back, and carried him safely home. The herd cheered, and her mother hugged her and said Gertie had bigness inside. Gertie then felt happy being the right size for herself.

summary_text: Mr. Fish and his friends are playing happily at the ocean park. A bully shark comes and tells them to move. Mr. Fish feels scared, and the happy park does not feel happy anymore. Mr. Fish's friends stand together beside him, so nobody feels scared. Soon, the friends are laughing and playing again. They take turns, show empathy, and remember to be kind, be fair, and speak up when something goes wrong.

summary_text: Miss Spider sat alone and drank tea while she looked at the sky and the leaves. She wished for friends to stay with her so she could give them cakes and tea. First, two beetles, Ike and May, came out of the woodwork, but they were scared and ran away. Then three fireflies came inside at night and flew away when they saw her web. Four bumblebees would not stop for tea. Five bugs peered from the shadows, but Miss Spider found they belonged to a broom. Six ants came in with two rubber bugs, but they would not drink her tea. Seven butterflies were there too, but Miss Spider did not see them. Eight places were set at the tea table, but no guests stayed. Nine moths saw a thunderstorm, and they flew away when Miss Spider came down with a tray. Miss Spider cried because she was still all alone. Then a wet moth could not fly, so she gave him a cloth, tea, and pie. When his wings were dry, she helped him fly away. He told Ike, and Ike told May, and soon many insects came to tea. Miss Spider was no longer alone.

summary_text: High in the mountains lived three billy goats named Baby Gruff, Middle Gruff, and Big Gruff. During the cold winter, they ate dry thistles and brambles. When the snow melted, they went down to a valley where fresh green grass grew across a stone bridge. A hungry troll lived under the bridge and wanted to eat anyone who crossed. Baby Gruff crossed first. He told the troll that Middle Gruff was bigger and tastier, so the troll let him pass. Middle Gruff did the same and said Big Gruff was fatter and yummier. When Big Gruff came, the troll tried to gobble him up. Big Gruff pointed his strong horns at the troll and butted him into the rushing river. The troll was swept far away. The three goats ate green grass all summer and never saw the silly troll again.

summary_text: Matthew met Goldilocks on the way, and she invited him in for lunch. They shared a large bowl of oatmeal until they were full. After saying goodbye, Matthew returned to the castle. On the way, a vicious wolf chased him, so he hid in the hut of the three small pigs. The wolf tried to blow the house down, but he was too tired and failed. Matthew then reached a bridge, where a grumpy old troll jumped out and said he would eat him. Before the troll could do anything, a large billy goat knocked him into the lake. Matthew thanked his new friends and kept going. He ran past a race where a dozing hare and a tortoise were competing, and he finished first. Then a giant beanstalk appeared, and Matthew climbed it to the top of the castle. He could not open the door, so he went in through a window and saw a harp and a goose that laid golden eggs. After opening a mysterious door, he found a magician and a book called The Magic Story. The wizard sent Matthew home, and Matthew disappeared and was reunited with his family. When he read the book again, it shone, and he vanished once more.

summary_text: Mr. and Mrs. Mallard flew over many places looking for a home. Mrs. Mallard said no to places with foxes or turtles, so they kept going until they came to Boston. The ducks crossed safely, reached the Public Garden, and met Mr. Mallard at the pond. They stayed on the island, ate peanuts, and slept there at night.

summary_text: Kia was a little girl in southern Africa. Her mother died, and her father took Kia to work with the cows. Kia learned how to care for cows and grew strong. Later, her father married a new woman who had a daughter. The stepmother did not like Kia and gave most of the food to her own daughter. Kia became very thin and hungry. One day, by the lake, a shining purple fish came up and asked why she was crying. Kia told the fish her sad story. The fish took her to a watery world with green grass, fat cows, fruit trees, cream, and honey. Kia ate there, then returned home full. She went every day, and the fish sang, “KIA KIA, please be brave.”

summary_text: In southern Africa, a man and woman had a baby girl named Kia, which means flower. Kia’s mother became ill and died, so Kia lived with her father and helped him herd cows. She learned many things about the cows and grew tall and strong. After ten years, her father married another woman so Kia could have a mother again. The new wife came with her own daughter, but she was cruel to Kia and gave most of the food to her own child. Kia grew thin and hungry. One day at the lake, a shining purple fish spoke to her and took her to a watery world with fruit trees, fat cows, cream, and honey. Kia ate there each day, and the fish sang, “When I'm gone, KIA KIA, do not cry. Please be brave.” When the stepmother found out, she had the fish killed and cooked. Kia buried the bones by her mother’s grave, and a purple flower grew there with a feast beside it. The king saw the flower, later found Kia with a matching sandal, and married her.

summary_text: Mr. Fish sent off for flyers and chose a perfect place for his first vacation. He packed his bags and sang that he was ready for adventure away from home. He started early, but soon he saw a flashing orange sign. An array offered him a local map, and Mr. Fish thanked them and kept going. He went around a roundabout and stayed on his way. Then he became hungry. An eel told him about a diner on the next street, and Mr. Fish found it and ate there. After that, a crab saw that his luggage was overflowing and helped him fix it at a rest stop. At the lodge, Mr. Fish unpacked, but then he saw that he had forgotten his snoozy snuggly. He felt sad and wanted to go home. Then he remembered a loving message from far away, fell asleep, and woke up ready to keep going. He had more fun, saw more sights, and met new friends. At the end, he knew that bumps and detours are part of a trip, and he was glad to be back home.

Mr. Fish felt happy, and he swam with his class, saying they were smart, could learn, and belonged.

summary_text: Deep in the ocean, Mr. Fish and his pals were playing at the park on a warm, gentle day. They laughed and felt happy. Then a shark came along and made mean noises. Then the friends were no longer scared, and they played together again. The park filled with happy play, and they remembered to be kind, be fair, and speak up when something goes wrong.

summary_text: On a warm day in the ocean park, Mr. Fish and his friends were laughing and playing. Then a shark came swimming in and told them to move aside. He realized that words can make a difference and that his voice was strong too. He turned back, faced the shark, and spoke up. He told the shark that his actions were mean and that he needed to leave until he could be respectful. The friends stood together, and the park became happy again.

summary_text: Wilson Bentley, also called Willie, was born in 1865 on a farm in Jericho, Vermont, where heavy snow was common. He loved snow more than anything and spent his happiest days watching snowflakes land on mittens, barns, and fields. His mother taught him at home, gave him books, and later gave him an old microscope. Willie used it to study flowers, raindrops, grass, and especially snow. While other children played in the snow, he caught single snowflakes and learned that each crystal had six branches and that no two were exactly alike. He tried drawing snow crystals for three winters, but they melted too soon. Then, at age 16, he read about a camera with a microscope and wanted to photograph snowflakes. His parents bought the expensive camera, but the first pictures failed. Willie kept trying, learned new methods, and finally made clear photographs. He shared them with others, gave talks, and became known as the snowflake man. He later published Snow Crystals, worked until the end of his life, and died after walking home in a blizzard.

summary_text: Wahoo Cray lives with his father, Mickey, who works with wild animals. After a frozen iguana falls from a palm tree and injures Mickey, he stays on the couch with headaches and double vision. The show’s assistant, Raven Stark, visits and signs them up to provide animals. She wants Alice, their huge alligator, and Beulah, a large Burmese python. Wahoo explains that Alice once bit off his thumb when he was showing off. Raven says the program is committed to making its dangerous adventures seem real. Mickey and Wahoo do not yet know how much trouble the job will bring.

summary_text: On December 31st, Pooh turned the page on his calendar and found there were no more months. Piglet felt sad, and Tigger checked his own calendar too. It had no more months either. Then Pooh finished the poem and said goodbye to August, September, October, November, and December. After that, the friends heard happy sounds from Rabbit’s house. Inside, Rabbit, Eeyore, Christopher Robin, Kangaroo, and Owl were making noise with balloons, streamers, a horn, a bell, and a drum. The friends thought there were no more months, but Christopher Robin said there would be a new year with new months and new calendars for everyone. The friends were glad and celebrated the New Year together.

summary_text: Princess Gigi lives in the kingdom of the African Sky, where she can sing to wild dogs, make the wind play, and dance with the Tall Grass. But she cannot make the water come closer or run clearer. One early morning, her mother wakes her before sunrise, and they must go to the well to collect water. Gigi feels tired and thirsty, but she and her mother place empty pots on their heads and begin their long walk, singing as they go. Halfway there, they stop at a giant kite tree and eat sweet Shea nuts. When they reach the well, they hear water running, see their friends, and wait while the pots are filled. On the way home, the walk feels harder because the pots are heavy and their bodies are tired. At home, the family boils water, washes clothes, and cooks food. Gigi drinks, sings, dances, and hears her mother say they will journey again tomorrow.

Owl opened the door, but no one was there, only snow and wind. After it happened again, Owl thought the poor old winter was knocking and wanted to be kind. Owl made a new fire, the house became warm again, the snow melted, and the pea soup turned soft once more.

Al cried that he would never sleep. He jumped on the bed, and the bed came falling down. Then he ran downstairs and sat in a chair near the fire. He decided to leave the bumps on the bed and sleep there instead.

summary_text: One night, Al went down to the seashore and sat on a big rock. The sky was dark. Soon a small piece of the moon came up over the sea, and then the whole round moon shone brightly. Al watched it for a long time and said that if he looked at the moon, the moon must be looking back at him too. He said he would come again, but then he had to go home. As Al walked along the path, he looked up and saw the moon following him. He told the moon to stay over the sea, but it kept coming. He climbed a hill and shouted, “Goodbye, moon!” Then the moon went behind some clouds and disappeared. Al felt sad, went home, put on his pajamas, and got into bed. Soon the moon came back from behind the clouds and filled the room with silver light. Al saw the moon through the window and felt happy again.

summary_text: One night Al went down to the seashore and sat on a large rock in the dark. A small tip of the moon rose over the sea, and Al watched it climb higher until the full moon was shining. He stayed on the rock for a long time and spoke to the moon as if it were a friend. Al said he would come back later, but first he had to go home. When he walked down the path, the moon seemed to follow him. Al kept telling the moon that it should stay over the sea, but it continued to come along over the trees. He climbed a hill and shouted, “Goodbye, moon!” Then the moon moved behind some clouds and disappeared. Al felt sad as he went home, put on his pajamas, and got into bed. Later, the room filled with silver light when the moon came out again and shone through the window. Al saw that the moon had followed him home after all, and he was no longer sad.

summary_text: George Washington was born in 1732 in a simple Virginia farmhouse. As a boy, he liked fishing, boating, watching ships, and riding horses. He learned to read and write in school and practiced his handwriting by copying rules. When he was 11, his father died, and George helped his mother run the farm and care for his younger sister and brothers. He found his father’s surveying tools and used them to measure land, and he liked surveying. When he was 16, he got a job surveying land in the Virginia wilderness. In 1753, he joined the Virginia army and went to the Ohio valley to warn the French to leave English land. In 1754, the French and Indian War began, and George led Virginia soldiers. He later married Martha Custis and moved to Mount Vernon. In 1775, the war between England and the American colonies began, and George was chosen to lead the Continental Army. After eight hard years, the colonies won. George later became the first president in 1789, was re-elected in 1792, and died in 1799 at Mount Vernon.

summary_text: Borreguita was a little lamb who lived on a farm at the foot of a mountain. One day her master tied her to a stake in a field of red clover. While she ate, a coyote came and said he would eat her. Borreguita told him she was still too thin, and he should come back when she was fat. The coyote agreed and left. Later he returned, but Borreguita tricked him again. She told him about cheese, and at night she led him to the pond. He saw a round shape in the water and thought it was cheese, but it was only a reflection. When he jumped in, the image broke and he got wet, while Borreguita escaped. The next day she fooled him again by pretending to hold up a mountain under a rock ledge. Coyote helped by holding it up with his own feet, and Borreguita ran away. At last, Borreguita tricked him one more time and knocked him back, so Coyote never bothered her again.

summary_text: Rocket loved to play outside. He chased leaves, chewed sticks, and listened to birds sing. Every fall morning, he rested under his favorite tree. One day, a little yellow bird surprised him and called him her student. She showed him a sign and invited him to class. Rocket did not know how to read, but he stayed. The bird read a story about an unlucky dog named Buster who lost his favorite bone. Rocket listened closely and wanted to know the end. The next morning, he came back early. The bird gave him a name tag and taught him letters, sounds, and words. Each day he learned more, and each afternoon she read stories. When the weather turned cold, she flew away and told him not to forget that words are built one letter at a time. Rocket practiced all winter. When spring returned, the bird came back. Rocket learned more words, read more stories, and heard the story of Buster finding his bone.

summary_text: Rosa Parks grew up in America at a time when black people were treated unfairly. As a child, she was small and often sick, but she learned to stand up for herself. When she was 11, a boy on rollerskates shoved her, and she pushed him back. His mother yelled because Rosa was black, but Rosa stayed calm and told the truth. At school, Rosa saw that black children had a small old wooden school with one room, few books, and only five months of school. White children had a new brick school with many books, a playground, and nine months of school. Black children had to walk, while white children rode buses. Later, Rosa worked with the NAACP and fought for fair laws. She would not use separate water fountains or elevators. Then, at age 42, she was told to give up her bus seat. She stayed seated, was arrested, and her action helped start the Montgomery bus boycott. After 381 days, the bus rules changed, and people could no longer be separated by skin color.

summary_text: Lucida lived with her parents, Paco, and Lupe in a Mexican mountain village. She helped care for their home, her younger siblings, and Pepito, the family burro. Near Christmas, Padre Alvarez asked Lucida’s mother to weave a new blanket for the baby Jesus in the Christmas procession. Lucida helped dye the wool and weave the colorful blanket. Then her mother became sick and had to leave with Papa. Lucida tried to finish the blanket, but the yarn tangled, so she believed she had ruined her family’s gift. On Christmas Eve, Lucida hid while the villagers carried candles and gifts to the church. An old woman told her that any gift given with love would be beautiful. Lucida gathered green weeds and placed them near the manger. The weeds suddenly grew red, star-shaped flowers. Everyone saw their beauty. In Mexico, people called the flowers la flor de noche buena, or the flower of the holy night—the poinsettia.

summary_text: Mr. Jelly was frightened of almost everything. He lived alone in a wood, far from other people. One morning, a leaf brushed his window, and he thought his house was falling down. At breakfast, crackling cornflakes sounded like guns, so he hid under the table. During a walk, a worm frightened him, and he climbed a tree because he thought it was a snake. In a field, a sleeping tramp snored. Mr. Jelly thought the sound came from a huge lion and fainted. The kind tramp helped him and shared a secret: when something is frightening, count to ten. On the way home, Mr. Jelly stepped on a twig and then had a leaf fall on him. Each time, he counted to ten and saw that nothing dangerous had happened. After that, Mr. Jelly became much braver and rarely hid or trembled anymore.

Two men came and said they hid a package of jewels there. Pluto woke up, grabbed the package, and Mickey found him. The police caught the thieves, and Mickey got the reward. Pluto got a new collar and a bone.

That night, Penelope went downstairs, said sorry, and the family made room for him. With training and family outings, Mittens became less trouble, and Penelope loved him.

summary_text: Big Bear walked through the autumn woods while the wind blew all around him. First, leaves flew off the trees when Bear sneezed. Bear said the wind did not do it, and he tried to nail the leaves back with a hammer and tacks. Then he came to an apple tree. When he sneezed again, the branches shook and the apples fell to the ground. Bear put the apples back on the branch. After that, Bear went to the lake and saw twenty geese. When he sneezed, the geese flew away with loud honks and flapping wings. The wind kept saying it did these things because it was fall. At last, the wind told Bear that it whips leaves off trees, drops apples, scares geese south, and makes Bear sneeze. Bear listened and went to his den. The door slammed shut, and Bear hid in bed and turned out the light.

summary_text: A donkey worked for many years on a farmer’s land, but he wanted to leave and see the world. The farmer was unhappy, yet he let the donkey go when he saw how sad he was. The donkey walked toward Bremen, where he hoped to become a street musician. On the road, he met an old dog, a sad cat, and a rooster, and each one wanted to leave home too. The donkey invited them to join him, saying they could make music in Bremen. As evening came, they found a house with food inside. They made a tall stack at the window and played loud music to scare the people away. The family ran off, and the four friends ate the supper and slept in the house. Later, an uncle came to check the house, but the cat, dog, donkey, and rooster frightened him away too. After that, the family stayed away, and the animals lived happily in the house.

summary_text: One dark night in 1851, Harriet Tubman hid outside a cabin and whistled “Go Down Moses” to call enslaved people to freedom. As a conductor on the Underground Railroad, she led ten people away from slavery. They followed the North Star, but clouds covered it, so Harriet used the lessons Daddy Ben had taught her. She felt the bark of a tree to find north because moss grew on the north side. The story then goes back to Harriet’s childhood. She was born Aramenta Ross, called Minty, and grew up enslaved on a Maryland tobacco plantation. She worked hard, had little food, and was not allowed to learn to read. When she was a teenager, a weight thrown at a runaway struck her, and after that she often fell asleep without warning. Daddy Ben taught her how to hide, find safe plants, and follow the North Star. Later Harriet escaped, crossed into Pennsylvania, and became free in Philadelphia. After that, she returned many times to lead others to freedom.

summary_text: The story visits many special days around the world. People bake treats, light lights, and wait for bright nights. Other celebrations include a king’s golden parade, Carnival with feathers, samba, dancers, and floats, and Midsomar, when people make flower crowns and picnic. Families welcome spring, celebrate freedom at Passover, share yams at the New Yam Festival, and welcome the new year at Novi God. Ramadan ends with prayers and a three-day feast. On the Day of the Dead, families make altars and light candles. At Devali, tiny lamps show that good conquers all. The story ends by saying everyone can come together on a special day.

summary_text: Jasper Rabbit needed new underwear on Thursday, and his mom took him to the underwear store. She bought plain white packages, but Jasper saw creepy underwear and wanted them instead. Mom thought they were too creepy, but Jasper said he was a big rabbit now, so she bought one pair. That night, Jasper wore them to bed. The underwear glowed green, and Jasper got scared. He changed into plain white underwear and hid the creepy pair in the laundry hamper. The next morning, the creepy underwear were on him again. Jasper threw them away, but they came back from his drawer, so he mailed them to China. The next day they returned again with chopsticks. Jasper used his mom’s sewing scissors, then later dug a deep hole at Creek hanger Hill and buried them. After that, he found plain white underwear in his drawer, and at last he was not scared.

In the end, the child learned that great art can begin with a scribble, and a unicorn can make art too.

summary_text: Trixie went with her daddy on an errand. They walked down the block, through the park, past the school, and into the laundromat. Trixie helped put the laundry into the machine and put the money in, too. Then they went home. After a little while, Trixie found that Kuffle Bunny was gone. She said, "Agle flaggle clubb," and her daddy said they were going home. Trixie said more upset words and cried and balled. Her daddy got unhappy, too. When they got home, Trixie’s mommy opened the door and asked, "Where's Kuffle Bunny?" Then the whole family ran back down the block, through the park, past the school, and into the laundromat. Daddy looked and looked for Kuffle Bunny, but he could not find him. Then Daddy looked harder, and they found Kuffle Bunny. Those were the first words Trixie ever said.

The room had toys, books, and maps, but no beds for naps. The children colored, painted, played Simon Says, tumbled, skipped, stood on their heads, and sang silly songs. Soon, each child had a friend. Then the parents came to say goodbye, and many were sad and crying. Miss Sunrise gave them one last hug and sent them away. At the door, the children waved and said, “Don’t cry Mom and Dad kindergarten is cool.”

summary_text: There was a tawny, scrawny lion who was always hungry. He chased monkeys, kangaroos, zebras, bears, camels, and elephants, but he never got fat. The other animals were afraid of him and talked to him from far away. Then a fat little rabbit came by, and the big animals asked him to talk to the lion. The rabbit went close and counted the lion’s ribs. He said the lion looked too scrawny, so he should come to the rabbit’s house for supper. The rabbit said there would be carrot stew with his five sisters and four brothers. The lion went with him. On the way, the rabbit stopped to pick berries, mushrooms, and herbs, and then he caught fish. At the house, nine rabbits were cooking stew. They gave the lion stew and berries until he was full and fat. After that, he did not want to hunt anymore. He kept visiting the rabbits for supper instead.

He returned every day for carrot stew instead of hunting, and the animals were glad. When they asked the rabbit what he had said, he answered that they had forgotten to talk because they had such a good time.

summary_text: Lucas is an ordinary boy who loves sweets and his toy, Teddy. One day, he is in a bad mood and teases his friend Lisa because she wears glasses. Lisa cries, and Lucas feels sorry. His mother explains that hurting feelings is wrong and that kindness means using gentle words, showing respect, helping people, and doing good deeds. Lucas thinks about her words and decides to be kind. The next morning, he thanks his mother, puts away his toys, makes his bed, and invites a new boy to sit beside him. At school, he helps the boy and shares his crayons. Lucas apologizes to Lisa, and she says it is okay. After school, he waits patiently, helps find a ball, and picks up rubbish. He helps an old lady, covers his sleeping dad, and helps his sister. Lucas learns that kindness makes his heart happy and that anyone can learn to be kind.

summary_text: One day it rained hearts, and Cornelia Augusta caught one heart, then another, and many more. She thought it must be close to Valentine's Day, so she began making valentines. She looked at each heart and chose the best ones for her friends. She found seven hearts that looked alike and strung them together with a needle and thread. She took one special heart, pasted it on paper, and glued a white, soft cotton ball on it. She knew right away who that card was for. Then she used the biggest heart to make more cards by drawing circles and cutting them out. The smaller hearts were arranged on paper, painted with many colors, and folded in half. Cornelia Augusta put stamps on all the valentines and mailed them. After that, it never rained hearts again where she lived, but each next year she found other ways to make valentines.

summary_text: Louise was a cat who lived at the fire station after a big rescue long ago. He liked to go visiting in the fire truck and was often given leftovers. One night, after too much catnip and too many sardines, he took a wrong turn. He climbed a wall and saw Tabitha, a pretty cat behind a thick glass door. Louise and Tabitha looked at each other and fell in love from far away. Tabitha’s owner, Sho, was not happy. The next morning, Louise brought Tabitha a bouquet made of sardine tins, twine, and feathers. The next day he brought mice. After that he brought pigeons. Then he brought balloons, which was hard for a cat to do. Every day, Louise and Tabitha kept staring at each other until Sho chased Louise away. After that, Louise asked his friends for advice over a bowl of cream.

summary_text: Corduroy was a bear in the toy department of a big store. He waited every day for someone to take him home, but no one wanted a small bear in green overalls. Then one morning, a little girl named Lisa saw him and wanted him, but her mother said no because he was missing a button on one shoulder strap. That night, after the store closed, Corduroy climbed down from his shelf to look for the button. He rode an escalator, went to the furniture floor, and found a button on a mattress. When he pulled it, he fell and made a loud crash. The night watchman heard the noise, found Corduroy, and put him back on the toy shelf. In the morning, Lisa returned. She had saved money in her piggy bank and bought Corduroy. She carried him home, and in her room she sewed on a new button. Lisa said she wanted a friend, and Corduroy said he did too.

summary_text: Once, people and Outside belonged together, with nothing between them. But now, even when people are outdoors, they sometimes feel as if they are still inside and forget Outside is there. Outside gently reminds them. Sunlight flashes at the window, sunsets and shadows come inside, and chirps, rustles, and taps on the roof make songs. Outside brings special smells, including sun-baked, fresh, and mysterious smells. Outside feeds people with sun, rain, and seeds, which become warm bread and berries. It cuddles people in soft cotton clothes and holds them in wooden chairs that were once trees. People feel Outside in their cats and dogs. Outside also shows when it is time to rest and when it is time to begin again. Sometimes a spider, a bug, or a snail comes inside. Even rivers come inside before rushing back to the sea. Outside says, “I miss you,” and waits for an answer.

One night, when a black cat named Midnight comes to the house, Karen gets scared and thinks the witch is near. Later, Karen believes she sees Mrs. Porter and Midnight flying away on a broomstick. The next day she keeps watching the house and thinks a witch meeting will happen there at midnight. She and her friend Hani make up a plan to stop the witches, but they later learn the meeting is really the Sunnybrook Gardeners Club. Karen has to apologize and write a note, but she still thinks Mrs. Porter is a witch.

summary_text: Camelli returns to his village in Kenya after a long time away. The children see him first, and the Messi people greet him warmly. He finds his mother, but he cannot stay because he must go back to New York, where he is studying to be a doctor. Before he leaves, he tells the elders and the tribe one story. He tells them about September 11 in New York City, when tall buildings were hit by terrible fires and smoke, and more than 3,000 people died. The Messi listen in silence and feel sad for the people who suffered. An elder asks what they can do to help. Camelli says, “The cow is life,” and offers his only cow as a gift. The tribe blesses the cow and sends word to the United States Embassy in Nairobi. Later, an American diplomat arrives and sees a big ceremony. The Messi give 14 blessed cows to America as a sign of comfort and peace.

summary_text: A hare boasted to the other animals that he was very fast and that the tortoise was very slow. One day, he laughed at the tortoise and said he could never win a race. The tortoise said he could beat the hare, so they chose a race to the foot of the mountain. The squirrel said, “Ready!” The mouse said, “Set!” The raccoon said, “Go!” The hare ran far ahead right away. The tortoise moved slowly but steadily. The hare looked back and saw the tortoise was far behind. He stopped to eat carrots and lettuce and talk with friends. Then he lay down in a pumpkin patch and went to sleep. While he slept, the tortoise kept going and passed him. At last, the tortoise crossed the finish line before the hare woke up and ran back. The story says, “Slow and steady wins the race.”

summary_text: One night, Geppetto, a kind wood carver, wished that his puppet, Pinocchio, could become a real boy. There, lazy boys changed into donkeys. Pinocchio and Jiminy Cricket escaped and learned that Geppetto was trapped inside a giant whale named Monstro. Because Pinocchio had been brave, truthful, and unselfish, the Blue Fairy made him a real boy.

summary_text: Parley Elementary had a lunchroom that was very loud and crowded. Students could not find places to sit, and they wrote to Mrs. Mench, the principal, asking for help. Mrs. Mench thought for a while, then made changes that made the lunchroom even worse. First, she put science projects in the room, so there was less space. Then she moved classroom pets there, and the lunchroom filled with snakes, tarantulas, hamsters, and worms. After that, she brought sports teams inside because it was too hot to practice outdoors. Balls flew, whistles blew, and the room became messy and smelly. The students kept sending notes because they were unhappy. At last, when the heat wave ended, Mrs. Mench moved the sports teams back outside, returned the animals to their classrooms, and put the science projects in the hallways. Then the students had a quiet, roomy lunch and thanked her with chocolate and notes.

Then Bunny says there is a problem: tomorrow is Groundhog Day, and if Groundhog sees his shadow, he will go back into his hole for six more weeks and miss the party. Moose and his friends make a plan to stop that from happening. Squirrel wants to change the calendar, and Porcupine says he will blindfold Groundhog. But the animals argue all night and do not notice morning coming. Groundhog wakes up, sees his shadow, and goes back into his hole. Moose asks why, and the friends learn that Groundhog is afraid of shadows. They show him dancing leaf shadows, cloud shadows, silhouettes, and shadow puppets. Groundhog enjoys them all. At the end, he still goes back to his warm hole, but he gives the others a nose kiss and they call it Ground Hug Day.

When the work was done, they went home and said good job to the boy.

summary_text: In a twinkling forest, a cheerful skeleton named Skellyy loved moonlit walks, soft music, and his three best friends: Willow, Hazel, and Tany, who were friendly witches. In the woods, strange things moved, a bush puffed pink smoke, and Skellyy sneezed and spun around. When the smoke cleared, he found that he was lost. They flew through the woods and found Skellyy on a mossy rock. They took him home, and that night they made Moon Perry muffins instead and ate them under the stars.

summary_text: On Christmas Eve, Bluey’s family is at the Heeler house after dinner, and everyone is waiting for Santa. Bluey is very excited because presents are already under the tree. Muffin wonders how Santa gets in without a chimney, and Bluey says he might use the veranda. Then Bingo jumps out and says, “Let’s play Veranda Santa!” The kids decide Dad will be Veranda Santa, and they all go to bed and pretend to sleep. Dad tiptoes across the veranda and leaves presents under the pillows. In the morning, the children are happy with their gifts, but Bluey does not want to accept Bingo’s sorry when she takes the pencil case. Later Bluey becomes Veranda Santa and tells the others they get no presents because they peeked. After the family says sorry, Bluey accepts it. Then Socks helps Bingo, but Bluey gets upset when Socks bites and does not say sorry. Mom and Dad explain that Bluey should say sorry too, and Bluey finally apologizes to Socks. At the end, the family plays Veranda Santa one more time.

summary_text: Donald Duck took pizzas out of the oven when Huey, Dewey, and Louie came into the kitchen. Donald had made different pizzas: pineapple and sardines for himself, pepperoni for Daisy, and sausage for the boys. He told them not to touch the pizzas and went to get Daisy. While they were gone, a shaggy brown bear came to the house. He smelled the pizzas, crawled through the open window, and ate Donald’s pineapple and sardine pizza because it was just right for him. Then he sat on the couch, tried Daisy’s chair, and finally rocked in Donald’s favorite rocker until it tipped over. After that, he went upstairs, tried the boys’ beds, and fell asleep in Donald’s bed. When Donald, Daisy, and the boys came back, they saw the eaten pizzas and the mess. Donald followed the clues upstairs and found the sleeping bear. Soon Charlie from Charlie’s Pizza arrived, said the bear was his pet, and took him home. Charlie then gave Donald and the others three big hot pizzas as a reward.

summary_text: The book says it has no story and tells the reader there will be no elves, pirates, frogs, dogs in cars, rockets, or other wild things. The pages talk back and ask how a book can have no story. Page six says it is the book with no story and decides what happens. The book keeps saying there will be no pictures, no thrills, and no happy ending. Then the other pages ask why it will not tell a story. They try to help by making up a silly opening about Prince Porkchop Lover and Princess Sleeping Pickle, but the book stops them. The pages and reader give the book a big hug, and then they shake it three times. After that, words start coming out. The book first tells a small story about itself, then begins to imagine more stories with polar bears, pirates, elves, and flying adventures. In the end, the book becomes full of stories and says to imagine a story, a poem, or a play, and never think you have nothing to say.

summary_text: The people of Squawk Valley wanted a turkey for their Thanksgiving feast, but no turkey could be found. They were worried they might have to eat shredded wheat instead. Ebenezer Beezer had an idea. The people would hold an arts and crafts fair with turkey as the theme. They made turkey pictures and statues from potatoes, clay, rope, oatmeal, paper, and soap. They put posters in the forest to invite a turkey to pose. Pete, a proud, clever, hungry turkey, saw the signs and volunteered. The people hired him. On Thanksgiving Day, Pete judged all the turkey artwork. There were turkey creations everywhere, so Pete hid among them. When the people searched, Pete was gone. They found a note saying he had taken his modeling fee. The oatmeal turkey was missing too. The people had no real turkey, so they ate shredded wheat. They learned that a plump, perky turkey can be very clever.

summary_text: The child says, “This is my body. It belongs to me.” The child learns the names of body parts like belly button, vulva, butt, elbows, penis, and nipples. The child says, “I am the boss of my body,” and talks about doing things that feel good. Grown-ups still make some choices to keep the child safe and healthy, like putting on helmets. Sometimes the child does not like these choices and feels upset. It feels better when grown-ups ask first or explain what is happening. The story says everyone is different, and some people like hugs while others do not. Asking if something is okay is called asking for consent. When someone says yes, it means consent. When someone says no, or shows no in many ways, we must listen and stop right away. People can change their mind, and their body choices matter.

summary_text: It was the Gingerbread Girl’s birthday. The little old man and woman gave her a box of animal crackers tied with a licorice ribbon. When she opened it, the lion, bear, elephant, gorilla, kangaroo, crocodile, and polar bear crackers jumped out and ran away. The Gingerbread Girl chased them while farmers, a cat, a mouse, sheep, children, chickens, and scouts watched or joined the noisy chase. Soon, the crackers reached the river, where the hungry fox waited. He promised to carry them across, but he planned to eat them. The Gingerbread Girl told the crackers that the fox had very sensitive ears. The crackers ran to his ears and made a huge, loud roar. The fox became frightened and ran away. The animal crackers returned home with the Gingerbread Girl, and everyone celebrated her birthday. That night, the tired crackers slept safely together.

summary_text: A small green chameleon sat on a shiny green leaf. When it moved to a brown tree, it turned brownish. On a red flower, it turned reddish. On yellow sand, it turned yellowish and was hard to see. When it was warm and had food, it turned sparkling green. When it was cold and hungry, it turned gray and dull. When the chameleon was hungry, it sat still and waited. Its eyes moved up, down, and sideways until it saw a fly. Then its long, sticky tongue shot out and caught the fly. That was its life. Then one day the chameleon saw a zoo it had never seen before. It saw many beautiful animals and wished it could be big, white, and like them. Its wish came true, but it was not happy. It wished to be like many animals. Then a fly flew by. The chameleon was hungry, but it was mixed up and could not catch it. It wished to be itself. That wish came true, and it caught the fly.

summary_text: The Rainbow Fish was the most beautiful fish in the sea, but he did not play with the other fish. A little blue fish asked for one shiny scale, but the Rainbow Fish said no and swam away. Then the other fish left him, and he was all alone. The Rainbow Fish asked the starfish for help. Then the little blue fish came back and asked for one scale. The Rainbow Fish gave him a tiny scale. The little blue fish was happy, and the Rainbow Fish felt happy too. Soon, the Rainbow Fish gave scales to all the fish. He had only one shining scale left, but he was the happiest fish in the sea because he had friends.

summary_text: Pigasso was a young pig who loved to paint, and Mootisse was a young bull who loved to paint big, bright pictures. Soon, many pigs and cows wanted to see their art, and both artists became famous. But too many visitors came, and Pigasso got tired of the noisy pig pen. Mootisse also got tired of the crowded cow town. They each found a quiet farm and moved there. Then they met as neighbors across the road. At first they were friendly, but soon they began to tease each other about their paintings. Pigasso called Mootisse a Mad Cow, and Mootisse called Pigasso an Art Hog. They got angry and painted their houses in a big art battle. After that, they built a tall fence between them. Later, they missed each other and painted on the fence. They laughed, took the fence down, and became great friends.

summary_text: A child wakes up and sees that Dad is full of puns. At breakfast, Dad says a quiet person should walk with sneakers on, then balances his plate on one leg and calls it a balanced breakfast. At school, his puns continue with space drawings and an apple sticker that says, “You’re awesome to the core.” After school, Dad jokes about a traffic jam caused by grapes, a spider’s web, bright homework, mushroom soup, a stuffed teddy bear, and a paused television. The child loves Dad but asks him to stop because some puns are confusing. Dad listens, and the family spends a quieter evening together. At bedtime, the child remembers Dad’s old jokes and realizes that some are funny. Then the child makes a dinosaur joke: a sleeping dinosaur becomes a dino snore. Dad is delighted, and they share a laugh before saying good night.

summary_text: A tiny sea snail lived on a black rock with other snails, but she dreamed of seeing the wide world. One night, a great grey-blue humpback whale came near the rock. The snail saw many wonderful things, but she felt very small. One day, speedboats frightened the whale, and he became stuck on the shore when the tide went away. The whale could not move on land. The snail crawled to a school and wrote, “Save the whale,” with her silvery trail. The children called the firemen, who dug a pool and kept the whale cool. When the tide came back, the whale returned safely to the sea. The snail had saved him, and later many snails sailed on the whale’s tail.

summary_text: Three monks named Hok, Lok, and Siew walked down a mountain road and talked about happiness. They came to a village where people were tired, scared, and did not trust one another. The villagers shut their windows and would not answer the monks’ knocks. Siew said they would show the village how to make stone soup. The monks made a fire, filled a pot with water, and put in three smooth stones. A little girl watched them and helped find the stones. When she told her mother, the mother gave the girl a bigger pot. Soon the other villagers came out to watch. The monks talked about salt, pepper, carrots, onions, and more. Each time, someone ran to get an ingredient and put it in the soup. At last, everyone shared rice, buns, tea, cakes, and more. They ate together, told stories, and let the monks sleep in their homes. In the morning, they said goodbye, and the villagers said sharing had made them richer.

The other child asks, “Can I try it?” The first child says no, but then agrees to let them try once. Soon, the children argue again, saying, “That’s my chair,” and repeating, “Mine!” One child tells the other to get up and go away. At last, both children say they are sorry. They decide to go play together, and the story ends with them saying, “Yeah, mine.”

summary_text: Phyllis was a groundhog who liked to wake up in February, go outside, and play in mud and water. Her mother and aunties often said, “That’s Phyllis.” In summer, Phyllis picked blackberries and said that when she grew up, she wanted to be Punxsutawney Phil. The others laughed because Phil was a fellow. One February morning, Phyllis woke early and felt that spring was coming early. She tried to wake Uncle Phil, but he kept sleeping. The other groundhogs said Phil Jr. or Pete should do the job, but Phyllis said she could do it. At last, they dumped snow on Uncle Phil and woke him up. Phyllis went with him outside and showed him the melting snow, running brook, singing chickadees, and warm spring air. Uncle Phil finally agreed that spring was coming early. Then he said he would retire and choose Phyllis to be the next Punxsutawney Phil.

On Valentine’s Day morning, Froggy gave his mother breakfast in bed and gave her the heart that said “I love you.” His mother gave him many candy kisses.

Max found Turkey, turned him in, and won the extra special prize. Everyone laughed, and Max got a chocolate bunny pizza with jelly bean topping.

summary_text: Captain Marvel and Miss Marvel are practicing together when an alarm calls them to Jersey City. A giant alien plant is breaking the city. It seems to be looking for something. The plant grabs Captain Marvel and pulls her underground. Miss Marvel asks Spectrum for help. They follow the vines and find Captain Marvel near the plant’s roots. When the plant attacks again, Miss Marvel suggests talking to it. Spectrum changes into light, and the plant finally communicates. They learn that it fell from space and needs special soil, water, and light that Earth cannot provide. Captain Marvel is proud of Miss Marvel for finding a peaceful answer. The Marvels decide to discover the plant’s home planet and prepare for their first mission into space.

Carla kept saying her food was different, creative, or unique. On Thursday and Friday, she brought even stranger sandwiches. By Monday, no one wanted to sit with her, so she ate alone.

Then Miss Pento announced a picnic. At the park, Buster forgot his lunch and got very hungry. Carla offered him some of her combo Delight sandwich. After that, many students brought unusual sandwiches of their own. The next day Carla finally ate a plain peanut butter and jelly sandwich, and everyone was surprised.

summary_text: In a small village, six Blind Men heard that a huge elephant had come to town. They had never met an elephant before, so they went to learn about it by touching it with their hands. The first man touched the side and said the elephant was like a wall. The second touched a tusk and said it was like a spear. The third touched the trunk and said it was like a snake. The fourth touched a leg and said it was like a tree. The fifth touched an ear and said it was like a fan. The sixth touched the tail and said it was like a rope. Soon they began to argue because each one thought only his answer was right. A wise old man came and told them they were all correct. He explained that each man had felt only one part of the elephant, so each description was only part of the whole. The Blind Men stopped arguing and understood that they had to listen to each other to see the full truth.

summary_text: A little house lived happily on a hill in the country. She watched the sun, moon, stars, flowers, trees, children, and the changing seasons. The man who built her said she would stay for many generations. As the years passed, roads, cars, buildings, trains, and city lights came closer. The quiet countryside became a busy city. The little house felt lonely, dirty, and sad. She could hardly see the sun, moon, or stars. One spring day, the great great granddaughter of the builder saw the little house and recognized her. Movers lifted the house onto wheels and carried her away from the city. They found a green hill with grass and apple trees. The house was placed there, repaired, painted pink, and lived in again. She was happy to see the seasons and stars once more. She never wanted to live in the city again.

summary_text: A told B, and B told C, that they would meet at the top of the coconut tree. Then D, E, F, and G joined in, and soon H, I, J, and K were climbing too. More letters kept coming, and the tree got crowded. L, M, N, O, P, and then Q, R, S, T, U, and still more W, X, Y, and Z rushed to the coconut tree. The letters piled up so high that everyone wondered if there would be enough room. The whole alphabet climbed together, and the adults came to help after the big pileup. Some letters got hurt or twisted, and others were tangled, looped, or bent. Then P, Q, R, S, and T appeared, followed by U, V, W, X, Y, and Z, and they wiggled free as the sun went down. At the end, the moon came out, A got out of bed, and said he would beat everyone to the top of the coconut tree again.

summary_text: Laura lived with her family and their bulldog Jack in a little log house in the snowy Wisconsin woods. Christmas was coming, so Ma baked bread, apple pie, and cookies. Laura and Mary helped make candy from hot molasses syrup poured into snow. The day before Christmas, Aunt Eliza, Uncle Peter, and their children arrived in a big bobsled. Everyone played in the snow, then hung stockings by the fireplace and went to bed. On Christmas morning, Laura found red mittens, peppermint candy, and a beautiful rag doll with button eyes and a calico dress. She named the doll Charlotte. Ma made pancake people for breakfast. Since it was too cold to play outside, the children ate candy, admired their mittens, and looked at pictures in Paw’s green book. Then the cousins went home through the woods. Laura held Charlotte, and everyone remembered what a happy Christmas it had been.

In the morning, Lisa came back with money from her piggy bank and took Corduroy home. She sewed on a button, and Corduroy found a home and a friend.

summary_text: A peaceful green spot explains that an anxiety spot appears when someone feels worried, nervous, anxious, or scared. It may ask questions like, “What if I am bad at soccer?” or “What if I fail?” Children can answer, “I can do this.” Small worries can sometimes protect us, but too many worries can cause a tummy ache, sweating, or missed fun. Healthy food, plenty of rest, drawing, music, and writing can help. The peaceful spot then teaches a calming trick. Children imagine gray worry spots on their fingers, draw a line toward the green spot in their palm, and say, “I can do this. I can be calm.” Then they take a deep breath and blow the worry away. They practice this on the first day of school and at a party. Each time they shrink the anxiety spot, their peaceful spot grows stronger.
