summary_text: The Highway Rat rode along the highway and stole food from travelers. He stopped a rabbit and took her clover. Then he stopped a squirrel and took his sack of nuts. Next he stopped some ants and took their green leaf. The animals grew thinner, but the Highway Rat grew very fat from eating their food. One day a duck met him on the road. The Rat said he wanted to eat her, but the duck said her sister had tasty food in a cave on the hill. The Rat followed her. When they reached the cave, the duck called out to her sister. The Rat heard a voice promising cakes and chocolates, so he ran into the cave. While he was inside, the duck took his horse and rode away. She returned to her friends, and they shared the food and had a happy feast. The Rat found his way out later and did not rob again. He got a job in a cake shop and swept the floor.

The word games continue: a monkey makes money, plants wear pants, and a farm is too far. The moon says moo, four wear fur, and a plate is late. Foxes are foes, yours is ours, and without Z, the children cannot sing their ABCs.

Wherever the child travels and whatever wonders they see, they will always belong with the person who loves them.

summary_text: In March, Worm writes in his diary about the three things Mom says he should remember: the Earth gives worms everything they need, digging tunnels helps the Earth breathe, and Daddy should not be bothered when he is eating the newspaper. Worm then tries to teach Spider how to dig, but Spider gets stuck and swallows dirt, so Worm gives up. Spider later says he will teach Worm to walk upside down, but Worm learns that worms cannot do that. In April and May, Worm has many small adventures. He hides in the ground during fishing season, spends a rainy day on the sidewalk, eats his homework when he forgets lunch, and sneaks up on children in the park. Grandpa teaches good manners, so Worm greets many ants in a long line. He also has a nightmare about giant birds, fights with Spider, and then makes Spider laugh by falling out of a tree. Later, Worm goes to a school dance, makes a macaroni necklace in art class, and eats it for dinner. He also argues with his older sister, but Mom reminds him to be kinder. By the end, Worm says being a worm has good and bad parts, but life is still full of adventure.

summary_text: A mommy pig, a Daddy Pig, and three little pigs lived at the edge of a beautiful forest. When it was time for the three little pigs to leave home, Daddy Pig warned them to watch out for the big bad wolf. The first little pig got tired and built a straw house. The second little pig built a house from sticks and branches. The third little pig kept walking until he found a nice place by a stream. He worked hard and built a strong brick house. Then the hungry big bad wolf found the first little pig and said, “Little pig, little pig, let me come in.” The pig said no, so the wolf huffed and puffed and blew the straw house down. The first pig ran to the stick house. The wolf blew that house down too, and the two pigs ran to the brick house. The wolf could not blow it down. He climbed down the chimney, landed in hot soup, burned his tail, and ran away. The three little pigs stayed safe in the brick house and lived happily ever after.

summary_text: Otis and the little calf liked to play Follow the Leader with all the Farm Friends. They marched around the apple tree, the barn, the hill, the pond, the cornfield, the meadow, and Mud Creek. Everyone played together except the bull. The bull lived alone in a pasture and scared the other animals. Otis once brought him a red apple and asked him to play, but the bull snorted, glared, and charged at the fence, so Otis stayed away from him after that. One day a storm came. The sky turned green, the wind stopped, and the farmer shouted that a tornado was coming. Otis opened the stalls and let the calf, pig, sheep, horse, and cow out of the barn. Then he heard the bull crying in his pen. Otis rushed back, broke the gate, and led the bull to Mud Creek. The animals hid there until the tornado passed. After the storm, the farm needed repairs, and the bull joined the other animals in Follow the Leader.

Chrysanthemums and daisies keep standing while the sunlight still warms them. Then the setting sun comes, and the evening grows longer. Shadows stretch across the streets. Clouds cover the sky like a soft blanket. Northstar shines on the darkest nights. Evergreens shake in the wind, and Silent Night comes. Frost and icicles decorate the windows and eaves, and snowflakes fall like a white curtain. At the end, autumn is gone, and winter arrives.

After the rain stopped, tall grasses grew, and the trees made fresh green leaves. The lion rested in the shade, dino lay in the cool mud, the baboons ate fruit, the zebras drank water, and the porcupine said the rain would come back again when it was time.

summary_text: Ellis the elephant wanted to learn how America became one nation from sea to shining sea. He learned that George Washington became the first president, and that Washington, D.C., was built as the nation's capital. The explorers faced cold weather, mountains, rivers, and a frightening grizzly bear. Their friends, the Nez Perce, taught them to make canoes. At last, they reached the Pacific Ocean and later returned home. Settlers moved west, new states joined the Union, and Robert Fulton invented the steamboat. Wagon trains carried pioneers toward new frontiers. Ellis saw how courage, freedom, and exploration helped America grow.

summary_text: Butterflies soar in the sunlight, and moths flutter under the moon and stars. They have lived on Earth since the time of the dinosaurs and are found on every continent except Antarctica. Butterflies and moths are closely related insects. Both can fly, both have antennae, and both are the only insects with scaly wings. They also begin life as wingless, wiggly caterpillars. Their life has four stages: egg, caterpillar, pupa, and adult. This change is called metamorphosis. A baby caterpillar hatches from an egg on a leaf and eats the host plant. As it grows, its hard skin does not grow with it, so it molts and sheds the old skin. Caterpillars spend their time eating and growing, but many predators want to eat them. Some hide with camouflage, some look poisonous, and some use stinky smells or scary tricks. Others spin silk to bungee jump away. When they are big enough, they become a pupa inside a chrysalis or cocoon. Inside, the body changes and a new body with wings is made. Then the adult butterfly or moth comes out and flies.

summary_text: On a very hot summer day, a popsicle melted fast and became a sad, sticky stick in a puddle. The stick cried and wondered where he belonged. Then Twig, a stick made of wood from a tall tree, talked to him and said he had once been part of a tree too. Twig and another friend, Brush, showed the stick that they had also started as plain sticks before they found new things to do. Twig drew a line, and Brush painted with red, yellow, and blue. Still, the stick felt upset and said he could only melt. Twig took him back to the puddle where he first changed, and there she saw a tiny stick house in the tree. A blue bird flew down, lifted the stick, and placed him in the last open space. The stick found his new place, made tree art, and learned he could have a fresh start.

summary_text: Kamala and Maya looked at the empty courtyard and wished for a playground. They told Mommy, and she said they should ask the landlord, the person who owns the building. Kamala wrote a letter, Maya drew a picture, and they went to ask him. The landlord said no. That night, the sisters asked the other children in the building, and the children also wanted a playground. Kamala wrote a longer letter, but the landlord said the project would cost too much. He said they could do it themselves if they wanted. The children asked their parents and neighbors for help. Most people said no, but Mr. Green said maybe he could find scrap lumber and sand. Soon the children built parts of the playground. Miss Lopez said maybe they could get an old tire for a teeter-totter. More maybes turned into yeses. They had a potluck, and later Miss Flores helped them find a slide. After a bake sale and a sidewalk sale, the slide arrived. Kamala and Maya rode it first, and the landlord said they did a good job.

Peter looked into Susie’s room and saw the cradle, the high chair, and his crib. They were painted pink for the baby. Peter felt upset and saw that his old chair had not been painted yet. He picked it up and ran to his room. He said, “Let’s run away, Willie!” Peter packed a shopping bag with cookies, dog biscuits, his blue chair, his toy crocodile, and a picture of him as a baby. Willie took his bone. They went outside and sat in front of the house, but Peter was too big to fit in his little chair. Then his mother called from the window and said they had something very special for lunch. Peter and Willie pretended not to hear. Soon Peter came up with an idea, and his mother knew he was home when she saw signs. Peter then sat in a grown-up chair with his father. He said, “Daddy, let’s paint the little chair pink for Suzie.” They did.

The story ends by warning that a monster might be under your bed trying on snazzy pants.

summary_text: Sylvian was visiting her grandmummy in Connecticut on Halloween. She put on her bonnet and went with Wiggy to the cornfield on the hill to find the biggest pumpkin for a pumpkin moonshine. The hill was steep, so they puffed like steam engines. In the field, Sylvie found a very large pumpkin, but she could not lift it, so she rolled it along like a snowball. When the pumpkin reached the sloping edge, it began to run away down the hill. It bumped over stones and bushes and rushed into the barnyard. The goats, hens, and geese were frightened, and the pumpkin hit Mr. Hemelscamp, who was carrying a pail of white wash. Sylvie helped him up and said sorry to the animals. Then she told Grandpop, who cut the top off the pumpkin, took out the seeds and pulp, and made a face in it. They put a candle inside and placed the pumpkin moonshine on the front gate post. Sylvie saved the seeds, planted them next spring, and many pumpkins grew.

summary_text: Alex sneaks out of his apartment at night with a backpack full of stories he plans to burn in the basement boiler. The elevator takes him to the wrong floor, where he hears a favorite horror movie coming from a stranger’s apartment. A woman named Natasha invites him inside with the promise of the movie, cookies, and pumpkin pie. Once Alex enters, the television and food disappear, the door vanishes, and Natasha reveals that she is a real witch. Alex wakes in a magical room connected to endless identical rooms. He cannot escape, and no one outside can hear him. A mysterious girl briefly tells him that Natasha likes stories. When Natasha returns, Alex tries to attack her but is stopped by magic. He saves himself by offering to tell a story from one of his night books. Natasha listens to “Lost Dog,” a frightening tale about a dog that appears before people die. She decides Alex’s stories are useful and locks him away until tomorrow, when his real work will begin.

summary_text: Little Edson Arantes do Nascimento grew up playing soccer on the streets of Bauru, Brazil. His friend P gave him the nickname Pelé. A coach helped him leave his shoe factory job and move to Santos. When the club saw the 15-year-old boy play, they were impressed. Pelé kept practicing, scored his first official goal, and soon became the season’s top scorer. With his first paycheck, he bought his parents a new house. At 16, he joined Brazil’s national team for the World Cup in Sweden, and Brazil won its first World Cup. Pelé later won two more World Cups, became a world legend, and helped bring people together through soccer.

Then they find a lunchbox and share the food inside. Spoiled milk and sour grapes make them sick, and a turkey sandwich shocks them. They rush back to the board and see the mess they made. Before dawn, they clean the room, wipe the sink, pick up trash, and wash the lunchbox. By morning, they are back on the board when the teacher returns.

summary_text: Amos was a little mouse who loved the ocean. He built a boat called the Rodent, filled it with food and tools, and sailed away to see the world. At first, he became seasick, but soon he enjoyed the waves, whales, and stars. One night, Amos fell into the sea and could not reach his boat. A whale named Boris found him and carried him safely home. During their week together, Amos and Boris became close friends and promised to help each other. Many years later, a terrible hurricane washed Boris onto the shore. The huge whale could not return to the water. Amos hurried away and came back with two elephants. The elephants pushed Boris into the sea while Amos gave directions. Boris was saved, and the friends said goodbye with happy, sad tears. They knew they might not meet again, but they would always remember each other.

summary_text: In a tall forest, autumn came and the air turned cool. Most animals had already stored food for winter, but Cyril the squirrel had not. He had spent the year playing and had no food in his hollow. Then he found one pine-cone with the last nuts of the season inside. Just then, Bruce, who always planned ahead, also wanted the pine-cone because he thought he was one short for his own stores. Cyril and Bruce raced after the cone as it fell from the tree and bounced over bushes and rocks. It landed in the water, and both squirrels followed. A bird swept in and carried the cone away. The squirrels almost fell over the edge, but Cyril grabbed a branch and pulled Bruce to safety. After that, Bruce saw how silly they had been. The two squirrels stopped fighting and began to gather food together, sharing and laughing as friends.

summary_text: One day, the little sister used the jump rope without asking, and the child got very angry. The child felt a tight throat, a fast heart, and heavy breathing, and then exploded with anger. Later, Positive Ninja came over, and they played pig. When the child started losing, the child got upset again. Positive Ninja said anger is normal, but the way you handle it matters. Positive Ninja showed the 1 + 3 + 10 strategy. First, say one word like “relax” or “breathe.” Then take three slow, deep breaths. Last, count to 10. Positive Ninja also said to use an “I am” statement, like “I’m mad at you for breaking my toy.” After that, the child went inside for chocolate cake and found that the sister had eaten the last slice. The child felt angry again, but remembered the strategy. The child said “Breathe,” took three deep breaths, counted to 10, and said, “I’m upset that there’s no more chocolate cake.” It worked.

summary_text: Winter came, and Anna needed a new coat because her old blue coat was too small. Her mother had once hoped to buy one after the war, but the stores were still empty and there was no money. So Anna's mother thought of a way to trade special things for what they needed. First, she and Anna went to a farmer and asked for wool from his sheep. The farmer said they must wait until spring, so Anna visited the sheep often, asked if their wool was growing, fed them hay, and gave them hugs. In spring, the farmer sheared the sheep, and Anna's mother traded a gold watch for the wool. Then they traded a lamp to an old woman for yarn, red lingan berries made the yarn red, and a weaver traded cloth for a garnet necklace. At last a tailor made the coat, and Anna wore it home. At Christmas, the helper trades were remembered, and everyone shared cake and joy.

summary_text: Winter came, and Anna needed a new coat because her old blue coat had become too small. Her mother had hoped to buy one after the war, but the stores were still empty, and there was little food and no money. Anna wore the finished coat home, and at Christmas the helpers came to celebrate with cake.

She asks God to help her grow into a loving, good, and gentle girl.

When he returns home, he is an honorary wolf.

summary_text: Long ago, dinosaurs lived everywhere. They had big teeth and long necks, and Tyrannosaurus Rex was the scariest. The story says cavemen first dreamed of underpants because they felt embarrassed without clothes. When T-Rex saw a pair of men's knickers, he did not want to eat the caveman. He wanted the underpants instead. T-Rex grabbed a furry pair, but they ripped, and he tripped when he tried to pull them on. Triceratops wore pants on every horn, but Stegosaurus snatched them, and the pants became torn. Woolly Mammoth's coat made Stegosaurus itchy, and Diplodocus was cross because his pants were itchy too. Soon there were not enough knickers. Pants flew everywhere, and the dinosaurs fought over them all night. The fighting became so wild that the dinosaurs were wiped out. The cavemen cheered the next day. The story ends by saying that pants and knickers save mankind and should be treated with care.

summary_text: The cookie examples teach many life lessons. Cooperating means adding the chips while someone else stirs. Being patient means waiting for the cookies to finish. Being honest means telling the truth about taking a cookie. Courage means taking a deep breath and telling the truth. The examples also show envy, loyalty, open-mindedness, regret, contentment, and wisdom.

Friends cheer outside, but the child still worries that a ghost may follow home.

After this happens many times, Mommy asks Lola to try just one bite of shrimp. Lola says she has never tried it before. She finally says she could try shrimp. Lola goes to the shoreline, dips her beak into the water, and picks up one very small shrimp. She eats it and says she loves yummy shrimp. Mommy and Poppy are happy because Lola did eat shrimp.

Rudolph later returned, helped save his family and Clarice from the monster, and Santa used Rudolph’s red nose to guide the sleigh.

summary_text: Goodly, Lovely, Angel, Neatly, and Perfect planned a birthday party for Tacky the penguin. They made cards, prepared food, and planned a surprise. The friends tried to serve the cake, but it was passed from penguin to penguin and finally dropped. Next, the dance queen Twinkle-Webs performed. She danced the wrong way, fell, and said her career was over. Tacky cheered her up by showing his funny flap-waddle dance. Twinkle-Webs joined him, and soon all the penguins danced together. The party became happy and fun. Tacky received an autograph and a kiss. Everyone hugged him because, although he was an odd bird, he was a nice penguin to have at a party.

summary_text: In a big house high on a hill lives a family: a mama, a papa, a boy, a girl, and a baby. On the mantle in The Parlor sits a snow globe that nobody notices anymore except baby. Inside the snow globe lives a tiny family with the same members, and they are having tea and crumb cake too. The little family loves the snow that covers their world all year. They build snowmen, skate on a pond, throw snowballs, and make snow angels. They wish someone would shake the snow globe hard so they could have a hill for sledding. The little children ask their papa for stories about the big snowstorms from long ago, and he tells them there used to be big storms, but now only a small flurry comes sometimes. One evening, a real blizzard begins outside. The big family goes sledding, but baby stays inside. Baby climbs to the mantle, sees the little baby, grabs the snow globe, and shakes it hard. The little family rushes outside to sled, and later everyone sleeps and dreams of the next snowstorm.

summary_text: On the far away island of Sal-a-Massan, Yertle the Turtle was king of a clean, warm pond where the turtles had plenty to eat. Yertle was not happy with his small kingdom. He wanted to see more and be higher than everyone else. So he ordered nine turtles to stand one on top of another and made a tall throne. Yertle climbed up and sat on it. From there, he could see far away and cried that he was king of cows, mules, houses, a blueberry bush, a cat, and more. Then a turtle named Mac, who was at the bottom, said his back, shoulders, and knees hurt. Yertle told him to be quiet and demanded even more turtles. Many turtles came and built the stack higher. Mac cried out again that the turtles were in pain and hungry. Yertle still wanted to go higher, but then Mac burped, the throne shook, and Yertle fell into the pond. After that, Yertle was no longer king, and the turtles were free.

summary_text: Clothes are made from many different things, and each kind is used for a special job. Jeans are made from cotton. At the end, the story says old clothes can be reused or recycled instead of thrown away.

summary_text: Doug the dog looked for a good place for Carl and Russell to camp. He found a clearing with trees and a pretty valley view. They set up tents, cooked dinner, and roasted marshmallows. Before bed, Russell found small paw prints. Doug promised to watch all night while Carl and Russell slept. First, Doug chased a squirrel and accidentally pulled down Russell’s tent. Then a bat surprised him, and he spilled the lemonade. Later, Doug heard scratching and saw a raccoon taking sausages from the picnic basket. Doug pulled one end of a sausage while the raccoon pulled the other. When Doug growled, the raccoon let go and ran away. Doug returned the sausages, even though they were dirty. He stayed awake until Carl came out and found him asleep. Carl thanked Doug and called him a good dog.

summary_text: Two very tall towers stood side by side in New York City. A young street performer named Philippe Petit saw them and wanted to walk on a wire between them. He had already walked on a rope in Paris, so he began a secret plan. One August evening, he and friends brought a heavy cable into the South Tower and carried it to the roof. At midnight, friends in the other tower shot a line across with an arrow, and Philippe used it to pull the real cable into place. The cable slipped once and nearly fell, but Philippe fixed it. By sunrise, he put on black clothes, took his balancing pole, and stepped onto the wire. People below stopped to watch, and police came to arrest him. Philippe walked, danced, and rested on the wire for almost an hour before returning to the roof and giving himself up.

summary_text: Finn, Emma, and Chess Greystone are three happy siblings who race home from school each day. Finn likes to be silly, Emma enjoys counting and studying unusual details, and Chess protects the younger children. One afternoon, their mother is acting strangely. She stands frozen beside her laptop while a news report describes three kidnapped children in Arizona. The kidnapped children have the same first and middle names, ages, and birthdays as the Greystone siblings. The children are Rocky, Michael, and Emma Castano. Finn jokes about clones and matching names, but their mother does not laugh. Emma explains that, although coincidences are possible, matching names and birthdays among two sets of siblings is extremely unlikely. Their mother finally hugs all three children and promises to do everything she can to keep them safe. However, her trembling voice makes them wonder whether she knows more than she has told them. The siblings are left with a frightening mystery about who the kidnapped children are and how their families are connected.

At the club’s last summer meeting, the girls gather at Claudia’s, where Mimi is recovering from a stroke and other club members arrive one by one. Chrissy leads the meeting, and they take a babysitting job for Mrs. Perkins. Marianne also opens a magazine and notices a photo of Cam Geary, which makes her act differently than usual. At the end of the meeting, the club talks about school starting again and how life is changing. Marianne also sees that Chrissy has moved to Watson’s house across town, so they will not be able to see each other the same way anymore. The chapter ends with the first day of eighth grade arriving.

She shows the stars and moon, whispers good night, and makes the darkness glow with fireflies. The child sleeps close to Mommy and dreams of her love.

summary_text: Maple, Namas, Quill, and Nucamas are in the garden, where they talk about crab apples, choke cherries, and wea chaman, the plant that grows with beans and squash. Quill asks for a story, so Nucamas tells the story of Keipanak, the time of harvest, which some people call the first Thanksgiving. A long time ago, a boat with white sails brought newcomers to the shore. Seagull warned that new people were coming. The newcomers entered an empty village, took food and seeds, and built homes there. They did not know how to care for the land, so they struggled through the winter and many families died. In spring, Fox saw that they were hungry and told the Three Sisters. The plants and animals agreed to help, so the First Peoples were sent to teach the newcomers. Tasquantum showed them how to grow wea chaman, beans, and squash. The harvest became full, and everyone shared a feast. Nucamas explains that many Americans call this thanksgiving, but many of their people call it a day of mourning.

summary_text: Fox and Hare were best friends who loved to jump, leap, and bounce. Fox could sniff things far away, and Hare could hear things far away. One day, Bird told them that winter was coming and that they would soon see snow. Fox and Hare went into the forest to learn what snow was like. Bear said snow was white. Caribou said snow was cold. Salmon said snow was fluffy, and Goose said snow was sparkly. Fox and Hare searched for these things, but they became tired and it grew dark. They slept beside a lake. While they slept, white, cold, fluffy, sparkly flakes fell from the sky. In the morning, Fox and Hare woke up and saw snow. Bear and Caribou found them, and everyone rolled and played in the snow. Then they followed Caribou home.

summary_text: On a little farm behind a cottage lived a big dog named Agnes and a small hen named Rosie. Agnes was strong, wise, and cozy, and she helped keep the chickens safe at night by locking them in their coop. Most hens lived in neat, same-as-every-day ways. They laid eggs in nesting boxes, pecked in straight lines, and slept in a row. Rosie was different. She laid eggs wherever she wanted, followed Agnes around, danced, caught bugs, and slept on a tree branch. After days of rain, Rosie danced so fast in the sunshine that she rolled into a muddy puddle. Agnes helped her up. Later, the other hens looked at Rosie and turned away, and Rosie felt alone. Agnes whispered that being different was not bad. That night, Agnes left the coop latch open by mistake. Foxes came to the farm, but Rosie woke the hens and led them to safety. Then Rosie, the hens, and Agnes howled like dogs, and the foxes ran away.

summary_text: On a little farm behind a cottage lived a big dog named Agnes and many hens. Agnes was strong, wise, and always helped keep the farm safe. Every night she locked the chickens in their coop so foxes could not get in. Most of the hens were tidy and did the same things every day, but Rosie, the smallest hen, was different. She laid eggs when she wanted, followed Agnes around, danced, howled like a dog, and slept in a tree instead of with the other hens. One sunny day Rosie danced so wildly that she rolled into a muddy puddle. Agnes helped her out and brought her back. The other hens stared at Rosie and turned away, so Rosie felt alone. Agnes told her, “not all who are different are lost losing yourself has the greater cost.” That night Agnes forgot to close the latch all the way. Two foxes came, but Rosie woke the hens, led them to safety, and howled like a dog until the foxes ran away. In the morning Rosie saw the hens moving and dancing as they pecked.

summary_text: Emily was a very serious girl who liked taking serious walks. She met Duck, who was playful and not serious. Emily asked about Duck’s socks, but Duck said ducks did not wear socks because he had cold feet. The next day, Duck wore a tie. Emily said ducks did not wear ties, but Duck had a big meeting. Then Duck wore a hat because he was late for the roundup. Emily tried not to laugh. The next day, Duck wore boots because he had fields to plow and crops to plant. Emily began to smile. Soon Duck wore underwear, and Emily said she had never seen a duck wearing underwear. Duck shouted about pants on the line and went away. Emily smiled, giggled, and laughed. At last, she met Duck again and asked what he was wearing. Duck laughed and said he was a duck. Emily and Duck laughed together and went off happily.

Bobby took her to his favorite spot on the rocks, and she gave him paper to make a paper airplane. Bobby flew it outside, and it soared high. By lunchtime, Miss Kirby looked normal again. Bobby was not scared anymore, and they said goodbye until Monday.

summary_text: Ping was a young duck who lived with his big family on a wise-eyed boat on the Yangtze River. Every morning they crossed a little bridge to the shore to look for food, and every evening they went back to the boat. Ping always tried not to be last, because the last duck got a spank on the back. One evening Ping was busy catching a little fish and did not hear the call. His family crossed the bridge without him. Ping hid in the grasses so he would not be last, but the boat sailed away in the dark. In the morning Ping was alone and swam down the river to find his family. He met strange fishing birds and ducked underwater. Then he found crumbs leading to a houseboat, where a boy grabbed him. The boy’s family took Ping onto the boat, but later the boy set him free. Ping swam back just as his family returned, and he was spanked for being last. At last he was home again.

When she learns the losers may be beheaded, she rushes to cook the messy mixture with garlic and herbs. It becomes a delicious pizza. Prince Drooper tastes it, and Paulina wins. She decides she does not want to marry him and opens a pizza palace instead. People love her pizzas and wave when she passes by.

summary_text: One autumn morning, Sandy Squirrel and Roland Rabbit walked to school. After heavy rain, the stream was too high, and they could not cross it. This made them upset because it had happened before. They decided to build a bridge for everyone. They found fallen trees and tried to move a log, but it slipped into the water, and they fell in too. Sandy and Roland thanked the beavers and kept their help secret. Later, the weasels came back and saw the bridge. Mr. Badger was amazed too. At school, the teacher said many children had not arrived because of the stream, and Sandy and Roland received a diploma for their efforts.

summary_text: A tree house begins with time, looking up, and imagining a home high in a tree. The tree might stand alone or grow among many trees, but it should be tall enough to see sunlight. The builder needs blueprints, a hammer, nails, a saw, and a hard hat. Next come stilts, a ladder, a box for flowers, and places for begonias, zinnias, slugs, and marigolds. A swing, rope, and a way to climb make the tree house fun. A bookshelf, snacks, a sleeping bag, warm socks, pillows, and a flashlight make it cozy. Friends can share squeezed hands, secrets, and whispers while the wind keeps them safe. If a whisper breaks, they can yell, and animals will answer with sounds. Everything needed for a tree house includes time, looking up, flowers, snacks, friends, and imagination.

summary_text: Beatrice lives in the village of Kiss Inga in western Uganda with her mother and five younger brothers and sisters. Before the goat came, she worked in the fields, helped with the younger children, and wished she could go to school like the children she saw sitting on benches under the jackfruit trees. Her mother then told her that their family was one of 12 village families to receive a goat. Beatrice helped build a shed and plant elephant grass and other plants for the goat to eat. When the goat arrived, Beatrice named her Disa Luck. Two weeks later, the goat gave birth to twins, which Beatrice named Melinda WA and Surprise. Beatrice fed the goat well, sold the extra milk, and saved the money. After enough money was saved, her mother said Beatrice could pay for school. The next week, Beatrice started school in her new uniform, and she went off with the goat beside her, ready for a new life.

summary_text: In a corner of the sea, a happy school of little fish lived together. They were all red, except one little fish named Swimmy, who was black and could swim faster than the others. One day a tuna fish came rushing through the water. The tuna was swift, fierce, and very hungry. In one gulp, he swallowed all the little red fish. Swimmy escaped. He swam away through the deep sea, feeling scared, lonely, and sad. Then he saw many wonderful sea creatures, and as he explored, he became happy again. He saw a rainbow jelly medusa, a lobster, strange fish, seaweed forests, and more. Soon he found another school of little red fish hiding in the shade of rocks and weeds. Swimmy asked them to swim and play, but they said they could not because they were afraid of being eaten. Swimmy told them they must think of something. After thinking, he said they should swim together like one big fish. He taught them to stay close, and he said he would be the eye. Then they swam together in the water and chased the big fish away.

summary_text: A child sets out on an epic quest to learn the truth about dragons. The child puts on a favorite cloak and sturdy boots and goes into a deep forest on a crisp day. The child follows a brook past gnarled groves, crunchy oak leaves, and tall trees. The child must be careful of hob goblins under mossy bridges and glowing Willow the Wisps that try to lead travelers away. The child finds a yellow cottage in a swamp and meets a wise woman. She serves a warm drink and says dragons are fearsome, fire breathing, and live deep underground with treasure. Then the child travels to another forest with green bamboo and misty mountains. The child follows nine-tailed fox footprints and, if lost, can ask the white rabbit on the moon for help. The child reaches an airy palace and another wise woman says dragons are majestic, live in the sky and rivers, and can bring rain and floods. In the end, the child learns both truths about dragons and that both journeys can be taken.

summary_text: Rosie Gray, a famous actress, moves with her agent Sheila to an isolated house in the Lake District. Rosie is frightened because a killer has murdered nine women and seems to be acting in her name. The killer has called her repeatedly, whispering, “Just for you.” Rosie hopes her boyfriend, Ritchie, will make her feel safer. When Ritchie arrives, he tells Sheila that another woman has been murdered. During a violent storm, the electricity fails, and a telephone rings inside a drinks cabinet, although the house has no phone. Someone then knocks heavily at the front door and walks around the house. Rosie and Sheila cannot find the portable phone. Sergeant Cooper arrives, warning that another murder has happened nearby and that the killer may be close. He takes Rosie outside. Sheila hears glass breaking upstairs and collapses when someone grabs her. Ritchie later breaks in through a window and reveals that no police officer has been checking the house. Then the hidden phone rings again.

summary_text: A bright yellow bus spent her days driving. Every morning, people climbed inside with pitterpatters and giggles. She carried them from one important place to another, and their happy sounds filled her with joy. Then a new driver took her along unfamiliar roads. Later, another driver left her in a quiet place in the city and never came back. Nobody climbed in, and the bus became empty and quiet. One cold night, some people came inside and huddled together. They returned every night with soft voices, making the bus happy again. A truck carried her across the city and countryside to a farm beside a river. Animals climbed in with clip-clops, but the farmer later took them away. The river rose, and soon swimmers came into the bus. They drifted around her, and even though she carried nobody anywhere, they filled her with joy.

Back in Troll Valley, Anna placed the crystal in Boulda’s hands, and it glowed brightly again. Boulda said they had worked together, and Kristoff said they did it because she was family too.

summary_text: Mrs. Bobbin, a dressmaker, finished a beautiful gown for the duchess, but she had a bad headache and felt too sick to carry it. Her daughter, Irene, wanted to help, so she tucked her mother into bed, gave her tea with lemon and honey, and packed the dress in a big box. summary_text: Frank was a frog who wanted to fly. He tried to jump and flap, but he only fell, and the other animals laughed. Frank felt sad. After that, Frank went home. He told his parents that birds were flying and he was holding on, but he said he could be a great swimmer. His parents were proud, and Frank joined his friends in the pond.

summary_text: Olal Lakota Native American runner talks about growing up on the Pine Ridge reservation in South Dakota, where his family lives in poverty but stays strong together. After his mother dies, his father tells him to step inside a circle and says he must dig deeper to heal. The boy works hard, runs from bullies, and learns from old news stories about Native athletes. He goes to Haskell Institute, where he is first told he is too small and too slow for track. During summers he trains with homemade weights and later breaks state records. At races, he sometimes feels weak and dizzy, and coach Coffen gives him honey before he runs. He earns a scholarship to the University of Kansas, but faces racism there too. Later, while serving in the Marines, he learns he has hypoglycemia and borderline diabetes. With a new diet and training, he qualifies for the 1964 Olympics in Tokyo. In the 10,000-meter race, he stays with the leaders, fights through pain, and wins the gold medal. Afterward, he receives honor, a new Lakota name, and plans a giveaway to share his blessings.

summary_text: Christmas was almost here, and the Bear family was busy. They had hung holly, bought presents, and caught a big Christmas salmon. Now they wanted their Christmas tree. They had many tree things ready, like bells, balls, beads, a Santa bear sled, and a bright star for the top. Papa Bear wanted a tree that was tall, full, and fat. They found one, but it was home to a skunk, squirrels, a grouse, chipmunks, and crows. Then they found another tree, and more animals lived there too. Papa still wanted the right tree. At last he saw a tiny snowbird family trimming a small twig tree. Papa understood Christmas better and did not chop that tree. Later the Bears went back for a tree, but the lot was sold out. Then the other animals had decorated the Bears’ house with all their tree things. On Christmas Eve, the real Christmas star shone in the sky.

summary_text: The day before Christmas, Santa was sick with a bad chill in the cold winter wind. He worried that Christmas might be cancelled, so he called Pete the Cat for help. At the very last minute, he reached the last house and finished the deliveries. summary_text: Tama works in the library at Minoka, a prison camp for Japanese Americans. She does not like the desert, the dust, the fences, or the guard towers, and she tries not to look at the guards. Every day, George comes to the library with books he returned the day before. Tama has been in Minoka for a year, and life there is hard. The weather is very hot in summer, very cold in winter, and muddy in spring and fall. Families live in single rooms and have no privacy. Tama keeps working because she loves books, even though she does not know when she will leave. The library gives her a small place of comfort, and George’s smile helps too. One day, Tama feels sad and cannot find the right word for all her feelings. George tells her there is a word: “human.” Later, Tama sees that George loves her. They marry, have a son in Minoka, and keep hoping for change and beauty.

summary_text: Bony Legs was a mean witch who lived deep in the woods in a hut on chicken feet. She had iron teeth and waited for children. Sasha lived nearby with her aunt. One morning, Sasha went to borrow a needle and thread. She carried bread and butter and some meat for lunch. On the way, she found the hut and went inside. At the gate, she used the butter to make the hinges quiet. She gave her bread to a hungry dog and her meat to a sad cat. Then she threw the comb and it grew into tall trees. Bony Legs could not get past them, so Sasha went home safely.

They do not have the light, stick, or rope anymore. They find a way out by going up a ladder, through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. Then they run home, safe at last.

summary_text: A tiny sea snail lived on a black rock with other snails. She looked at the sea and the ships and said she wanted to sail. The other snails told her to sit still and stay put. But the tiny snail wanted to travel, so she climbed onto the tail of a great big gray blue humpback whale. The whale sang to her about ice, coral caves, stars, and waves, and he carried her across the sea. They saw big waves, caves with fish and sharks, and a sky that was sometimes sunny and sometimes stormy. Then the whale lost his way. Fast boats scared him, and he swam too close to shore. The tide went out, and the whale was stuck on the sand. The tiny snail asked him to move, but he could not. She crawled to the school, where children saw her trail and called the firemen. The children helped keep the whale cool, the tide came back, and the whale and snail returned safely. Back on the rock, the snail told her tale, and many snails rode on the whale’s tail.

The other birds became worried too, and all five hurried to tell the king. Then they met Foxy Loxy. He said they should hide in his den while he went to tell the king. The birds followed him inside. In the den, Chicken Little sneezed from the dust and suddenly remembered that birds should stay away from foxes. The other birds agreed, and they all ran out of the den and never went back.

summary_text: Luna Muna was finishing a Solar System model when the bell rang. She loved science, space, baking, and contests, and she wanted to bring something special to the science class bake sale. Her mom suggested Cosmic cupcakes with fun space facts in the wrappers. The next day, the class worked on many science treats, like ladybug strawberries, a Jello ocean, volcano muffins, robot cookies, and more. Luna Muna then had a big idea. She made a space Cafe with many desserts instead of just one treat. She wore her space helmet and rushed to bake, but she moved too fast and made a huge mess of flour, sugar, icing, and batter. She felt upset, but her classmates helped her clean up. Together they finished the table just in time. Customers came, bought the treats, and learned space facts. The class raised enough money for a telescope, and Mrs. Bunson said it was the best bake sale ever.

summary_text: There was a bright yellow bus that drove children every morning. They climbed in with pitter-patter feet, giggles, shuffles, and clunks, and the yellow bus carried them from one important place to another. A new driver came and took the bus on new roads, but the children still climbed in every morning. Later, another driver took the bus into the city and left her parked in a quiet place. No one came for a long time, and the bus sat empty. One cold night, children climbed in again with soft rustles and bumps, and they huddled together inside. After that, a truck towed the yellow bus through the city, over a bridge, and into the country. It left her on a farm in a valley by a river. The bus heard farm sounds, then the farmer took the animals away. The farm became quiet. Later, the river rose, and swimmers came with swish-swoosh sounds.

summary_text: The lupine lady was once a little girl named Alice who lived in a city by the sea. She loved listening to her grandfather, an artist, tell stories about faraway places. Alice said she would grow up, travel, and someday live by the sea. Her grandfather told her she must do a third thing too: do something to make the world more beautiful. When Alice grew up, she left home and worked in a library in another city. People called her Miss Rumphius. She traveled to many places, including a tropical island, mountains, jungles, deserts, and the land of the lotus eaters. She met kind people, saw animals, and collected beautiful shells. At the land of the lotus eaters, she hurt her back and decided it was time to live by the sea again. There she planted lupine seeds, and the flowers grew and spread. Soon fields and roads were covered with blue, purple, and rose-colored lupines, and people called her the lupine lady.

summary_text: A lonely old woman and old man made a gingerbread girl after a fox caught their gingerbread boy. The girl woke up in the oven and ran away. She met farmers, a pig, an artist, a cow, three dogs, children, and teachers. Everyone chased her, but she sang that she was too fast to catch. At the river, the same fox offered to help her cross. The gingerbread girl carefully climbed onto his tail. When the fox swam into deep water, she moved to his head, tied his snout with her licorice hair, and made him turn around. She rode the fox back to the house while the crowd followed. Then she and the old couple made more gingerbread. The house was happy and no longer lonely. The gingerbread girl also taught the fox some manners with gingerbread crumbs.

summary_text: At Abuela’s house in Mexico, Areli loved Saturdays with family, sunshine, games of al escondite, and chasing chickens. On Sundays, she and Alex waited for the phone to ring so they could talk to Mamá and Papá in America. Mamá and Papá said they were trying to bring the children to live with them. But years passed, and they did not come back for birthdays, Día de los Muertos, or Navidad. One day Alex packed a suitcase and left for Nueva York first. Later, Areli started kindergarten and learned new things at school. Then Abuela told her that it was Areli’s turn to leave. Areli said goodbye to her cousins, friends, mountains, and chickens. A kind man took her to America. There, Mamá and Papá cried and hugged her, and Alex was happy to see her. New York was bigger and louder than Mexico, and Areli had to learn English and face teasing at school because she was born in Mexico and was not yet a citizen.

summary_text: At Abuela’s house in Mexico, Areli loved Saturdays with family, games, chickens, and her favorite supper of tortillas and pollo con frijoles. On Sundays, she waited for calls from Mamá and Papá in America. They said they wanted the family together, but they could not return to Mexico. Alex later left for Nueva York, and Areli stayed with Abuela. She started kindergarten, learned new things, and made friends. Then Abuela told her that she would also go to New York. Areli said goodbye to her home, her cousins, and her friends, and a kind man took her to America. There she reunited with Mamá, Papá, and Alex, but life was hard. She did not know English, other children teased her, and she learned she was not a citizen because she was born in Mexico. Still, she worked hard in school, learned more each year, visited Ellis Island, and began to understand that immigrants were part of America. In the end, she called Abuela and said she could do anything there someday.

summary_text: Peppa goes to Zoe Zebra’s house for her first sleepover. Rebecca Rabbit, Suzy Sheep, and Emily Elephant are there too. Each girl brings a special toy. Zoe’s baby twin sisters, Zuzu and Zaza, want to join them. Zoe says sleepovers are for big girls, but the twins cry, so the girls let them stay. The friends play the piano, but Mommy Zebra asks them to be quiet because Daddy Zebra must sleep. The girls get into their sleeping bags and plan a midnight feast. They quietly go to the kitchen and take fruit. The floor creaks, and Mommy Zebra wakes up. The girls tell a story about a fairy and a monster, but Emily makes a loud elephant noise. Daddy Zebra wakes up too. He finishes the story by singing quietly about a little star. His gentle song makes everyone fall asleep.

summary_text: Blue is bored at the playground because she has played on everything. McKenzie suggests going to the creek, and Dad says he will take the kids there. Blue feels unsure at first and almost stays behind, but McKenzie tells her to come along. Dad carries Bingo, and the group goes down the slope to the creek. Blue sees that the creek is very different from the playground. There are thorns, spiders, leeches, and bumpy ground with no steps. When they arrive, Dad shows them where he played as a kid. The kids rock hop across the water on pointy, wobbly, and slippery rocks. Blue starts to see that the creek is beautiful and fun. A dragonfly flies by, and Blue begins making boats, stacking stones, and building dams. She also joins Dad at Daddy Day Spa, where Bingo puts mud on Dad's face and Blue brings more mud. At the end, Blue knows the creek is beautiful.

summary_text: In Wonderland, Alice saw the White Rabbit hurrying by with his pocket watch, saying he was late for an important date. She followed him into a hollow tree, where she slid on slippery white pebbles and fell far down past cupboards, lamps, a rocking chair, clocks, and mirrors. When she landed, the White Rabbit was gone through a tiny door. Alice met strange talking animals, but they could not help her find him. She kept wandering until she came to a neat house with pink shutters, and the White Rabbit came out. He called Alice “Marianne” and told her to get his gloves. Alice looked for them, but when she returned, he had gone again. After that, she met Tweedledee and Tweedledum, the Mad Hatter and the March Hare at a tea party, the Cheshire Cat, and Jabberwock. The Cheshire Cat told her about a shortcut, which led her to gardeners painting roses red for the Queen of Hearts. When the Queen arrived with the White Rabbit as trumpeter, Alice stood up to her and then ran home to the riverbank, glad to leave Wonderland behind.

summary_text: Angelina Ballerina loved to dance more than anything. She danced everywhere and often forgot to do other things. Her mother called her to tidy her room and get ready for school, but Angelina wanted only to dance. She danced in her dreams and hoped to be a real ballerina someday. At breakfast she stood on her bed doing curtsies. At school she tried on her mother’s hats, was late, and got scolded. On the playground she spun so fast that the other mouselings could not catch her. After school she danced in the kitchen and knocked over milk and cheddar cheese pies. Her mother was upset and sent her to her room. Then Mr. and Mrs. Mouseling bought Angelina a pink ballet dress and ballet slippers. The next day she went to Miss Lily’s ballet school, worked hard, and was told she might grow up to be a real ballerina. From then on, Angelina came when called, tidied her room, and went to school on time. She practiced every day and later became the famous ballerina Mademoiselle Angelina.

summary_text: The story begins with a child explaining many things Black people could not do, like play in white playgrounds, go to white schools, or drink from white water fountains. One spring night, the family goes to church to hear Dr. King. He tells everyone it is time to march for freedom, and he asks for peaceful protestors. The parents worry about jobs and safety, but the children say they can march. On May 2nd, many boys and girls meet at church and walk together, singing freedom songs. Police warn them to stop, spray them with water, and threaten dogs, but the children do not leave. Many are arrested and taken to jail. Inside the crowded jail, they sing “We shall overcome.” The marches continue for seven days. The jails fill up, President Kennedy notices, and leaders make a deal. Desegregation begins, and the child finally plays on a playground and eats in a diner that had once been closed to them.

summary_text: It was spring, Pinkalicious’s favorite season. She loved the cotton-candy sky at sunset and the garden full of blossoms. She believed fairies came to the yard and made the plants grow with fairy dust. One spring, she decided to build a house for the fairies so she could see them. Peter helped her gather twigs, leaves, and shells. Together they made a little house in the garden, added buttercups around the door, and made a shell path. Pinkalicious also made a pond, a boat, and a slide. She watched and waited, but the fairies did not come. Peter tried to cheer her up, but Pinkalicious still wanted to see them. Then she thought the fairies might come at night, so Mommy and Daddy let her and Peter camp outside. She left honeysuckle and berries for the fairies and stayed awake as long as she could, but she fell asleep. In the morning, the flowers were blooming and the snack was gone. Pinkalicious saw bright morning light and knew the fairies had come.

summary_text: Dusty is a crop-dusting plane who dreams of becoming a great racer. His friend Chug helps him, and Dottie fixes planes, but she tells Dusty that he is not meant to race. Dusty tries anyway and does well, so he joins the around-the-world race. During the race, flying high makes him sick, and flying low nearly sends him into an iceberg. When another plane gets oil in its eyes, Dusty slows down and helps it land safely. Dusty removes his heavy crop-dusting gear and flies faster, but Ripslinger wants to be the only winner. After Dusty’s antenna is broken, he gets lost, and the jets and pitties repair and refuel him. Dusty later crashes into the ocean during a storm. His friends share their parts, Dottie fixes him, and he returns to the race. Dusty flies high, passes Ripslinger, and wins. His friends cheer because his dream has come true.

summary_text: Nick enjoys playing on the playground until Ben tickles and pokes him too much. Nick does not like those touches, so he goes home and tells his parents how he feels. His mother explains that Nick owns his body and may say no to hugs, kisses, tickles, or any other touch he does not want. She teaches him that everyone has a personal space, like an invisible bubble, and that private parts must stay covered. Nick learns to tell his safety team if anyone makes him uncomfortable or offers treats for touching him. His safety team can include parents, teachers, grandparents, or an older brother. When Auntie visits, Nick asks for a high five instead of hugs and kisses, and she respects his choice. Nick also learns to ask permission before touching other people. He refuses unpleasant touches but enjoys his mother’s gentle caress and goodnight kiss.

summary_text: In a cave in the woods, a great brown bear sleeps through the cold winter. He sleeps all day and all night while the wind blows outside. A tiny mouse comes into the cave from the snow. It is dark and damp, so Mouse makes a small fire. The bear keeps snoring. Then Hair comes in, and Mouse asks who is there. Mouse and Hair pop corn and drink black tea. Badger comes next with honey nuts, and they share the food. Gopher, Mole, Ren, and Raven also come into the bear’s den. They talk, sing, and eat while the bear keeps sleeping. Hair stokes the fire, and Mouse cooks stew. A pepper flake makes the bear sneeze, and he wakes up very angry. Mouse tells Bear not to worry and offers more corn and tea. Bear eats and feels happy. When the sun comes up, the bear cannot sleep, but his friends are all snoring.

summary_text: Irie ran down the stairs wearing a winter hat even though it was a warm July day. Mama asked why she wanted to wear it. Irie said she did not like her hair because it was too poofy and did not move like other girls’ hair. Mama told Irie that she was not made to be like everyone else. She said that before Irie was born, she had talked with God and asked for a child with her favorite skin color, hair, eyes, nose, smile, and other special traits. She also asked for a big heart and kindness. Mama said Irie had grown up to be the most perfect her and was kind too. Irie ran to the mirror, took off her hat, and looked at herself. She saw her skin, hair, eyes, nose, and smile, and smiled. Mama told her again that she was the most perfect her and kind too.

summary_text: Mirha had waited a long time for her first day of school. Mama, Baba, and Nani said goodbye in the morning, and Mirha went to class feeling excited. But when she told the class her name, many children and even some teachers said it wrong. Some called her Mina, Miriam, Murha, Mero, Me, Mirha, Nera, or Yara. Hayden even asked if he could call her Mayo. Mirha wanted to say, “That’s not my name,” but she stayed quiet and felt sad. At home, she told Mama she wanted to change her name to something easier. Mama told her that Mirha was a beautiful name and that it meant happiness in Arabic. Mama said her name was special and should not be changed. The next day, Mirha told Hayden her real name and showed him how to say it. Hayden said sorry, and they played together. Mirha made her first friend.

summary_text: Gilbert the goblin says goblins are secretive, but he thinks yetis are even more mysterious. He talks about other puzzling things like the Tooth Fairy, gnomes, peanut butter and banana sandwiches, and goblins themselves. Gilbert decides to prove that yetis are not mysterious by finding one and taking its picture. He goes up a mountain and thinks he sees a yeti, but it is only shrubbery. He keeps searching and spots more things that are not yetis, like an ice carving bunny, a polar bear getting a makeover, a meditating mountain goat, and a snowboarding unicorn in a puffy coat. Gilbert gets tired and says he gives up. He wonders why it is so hard to find just one yeti. Then the mountain rumbles and an avalanche starts. Gilbert runs, and a secret yeti hideout called Flash is revealed. Gilbert says yetis are not so mysterious after all; they are just shy until they are not.

summary_text: Three pigs leave home to seek their fortunes. The first pig builds a straw house, but a wolf huffs and puffs it down and eats the pig. The second pig builds a house of sticks, and the wolf blows it down too. The two pigs escape from the story and meet their brother, the third pig. They explore a nursery rhyme and see a cat, a cow, a dog, a dish, and a spoon. Then they visit a story about a dragon guarding a golden rose. A brave prince defeats the dragon, and the pigs invite the dragon to come with them. The pigs return to their brick house and discover that the wolf cannot blow it down. The wolf comes inside, and everyone has soup. The pigs, the dragon, and their friends stay together and live happily ever after.

summary_text: Rabbit loved carrots. He picked up carrots wherever he went and hid them in his cozy hole. But Rabbit could not sleep because his home was too crowded. He asked Tortoise for a place to stay, and Tortoise offered to share his house. Rabbit said it was cozy, but then he brought his carrots inside too, and the house became too tight. Rabbit and Tortoise tried Bird’s nest next, but Rabbit carried the carrots up the tree. The branch wobbled, snapped, and Bird lost his nest. Then Squirrel let Rabbit stay in his house, but Rabbit brought more carrots, and the house could not fit them all. Last, Beaver offered his house. Rabbit wanted to bring even more carrots, but then rain came, Beaver’s house collapsed, and all the friends were left cold and tired on the riverbank. Rabbit saw that he had caused the trouble. He shared everything with his friends, and things got better.

summary_text: Morgan loved to share, and it made him happy to see other people smile. On the first day of kindergarten, he felt nervous, and Mommy told him school would be fun. Mommy gave the old man an apple from Morgan’s lunchbox, a bottle of water, and one dollar. The man said thank you, and Morgan felt happy. At school, Daddy was there to meet him after his night job. Morgan was excited and joined his class. In math, he shared a red pencil with Jacob, who had lost his. Later, Morgan shared a favorite book with Olivia. In art class, he shared art pencils and taught the class to draw smiling Hearts. His teacher gave him a star. When Mommy and Daddy picked him up, Miss Wilson said Morgan was a great friend. On the way home, Morgan saw the old man again and said he loved to share.

Nugget tells him not to worry, but Steve decides to try his own egg-growing method. He puts strange things into a pot, including chocolate chips, chilies, lemons, rocks, flowers, socks, and a jelly bean heart. At midnight, the egg grows very large, but then it cracks open and a huge hungry dragon appears. The dragon flies away into the real world and starts eating every chocolate egg in town. Steve and Nugget chase it, but they cannot stop it. When the dragon comes into a house, they learn it is Trevor, a friendly dragon whose sweetheart is a peach jelly bean. Trevor then burps out hundreds of chocolate eggs. Steve and Nugget hide the eggs around town, saving Easter. In the end, the Great Easter Bunny gives them the Golden Egg Cup, and Steve learns that Easter is about sharing joy and making a new friend.

One day he came to the Goodwin family’s home, where young Hannah Goodwin first saw him. He was thin, barefoot, and wore old clothes. The family invited him in, and he talked about the wide, wild land and the pioneers moving west. He said he could not stay because he had to keep planting apple trees across the Great Frontier. He carried a Bible and a sack of seeds, but no gun or knife, and he said he would harm no creature. Years passed, and Hannah heard stories of him walking through snow, rain, and dangerous land, sharing apple seeds and helping orchards grow. At the end of his life, old Hannah saw him again in her orchard. He thanked God for the trees, and later children were told to remember Johnny Appleseed and the apples he left behind.

At last old Mr. Bunny came, chased the cat into the greenhouse, and took Benjamin, Peter, and the onions home. Mr. McGregor later found the cat locked in the greenhouse. Peter got home safely, and his mother forgave him because he had his coat and shoes back.

summary_text: Greta lived in a beautiful forest. One morning she found many forest animals hiding in the garden. A wolf asked her for help because the giants were breaking the forest and ruining their home. The giants kept chopping down trees to build bigger houses, towns, cities, factories, shops, cars, and planes. Soon there was hardly any forest left, and the animals were scared and had nowhere to go. Greta wanted to help, so the next morning she went to the middle of the forest and held a sign that said, “stop!” At first the giants walked past her. On the fourth day, a little boy joined Greta, and then more people and animals came too. They made a huge crowd and stopped the giants. Greta told them the forest was being damaged and the animals were homeless. Everyone shouted for the giants to stop. The giants were sorry, and after that they slowed down, planted gardens, and helped care for the forest until it became beautiful again.

summary_text: There was a bear who was very easily scared. Each night he tied a bell to his door so he would hear if anyone came in. She read scary stories, slept with her door open, and brushed her teeth while hanging from a tree branch by her ears. One day Rabbit said they were going on an adventure. Bear wanted to read about adventures instead, but Rabbit asked if he was scared. Bear said no, and they set off together. They crossed a stream, went around a dark forest by bus, and traveled over a mountain by train and helicopter. At a rope bridge, Bear finally said he was scared and went home. Rabbit tried to cross the bridge, the board broke, and she fell. Bird got help, and Bear ran back, saved Rabbit, and learned it was okay to be scared.

summary_text: Mickey runs into the clubhouse and tells his friends that there is a Starlight concert in the park tonight. Minnie says they should load the tune car and get their instruments. Minnie calls for Toodles, and Toodles brings a wrench, a pump, and a paddle. Mickey uses the wrench to change the tire, and the friends drive on. They sing as the car rolls along. Then they reach the lake, but the bridge is closed. They get into a boat, count the paddles, and row across the water. After that, they find a mountain. The glove balloon has no air, so Toodles brings the pump. Goofy fills the balloon, and the friends fly over the mountain. The balloon lands in a forest with big bears. The friends play a lullaby with the flute and violin, and the bears fall asleep. Then Mickey and his pals reach the park in time for the concert and play their song.

Baba warned that a white mitten could get lost in the snow.
While Nikki played,
one mitten fell off
and stayed behind.
A mole found it
and crawled inside to be warm.
Then a rabbit, hedgehog, owl, badger, fox, bear, and tiny meadow mouse all climbed into the mitten.
The animals squeezed together
because the mitten was warm and cozy.
The mitten stretched bigger and bigger
but Baba’s knitting held it together.
The little mouse sat on the bear’s nose.
The bear’s nose tickled,
and he gave a huge sneeze.
The sneeze sent the mitten flying
and scattered all the animals.
Nikki saw the white mitten in the sky
and ran to get it.
When he came home,
Baba saw that Nikki was safe
and still had both mittens,
but one mitten was much bigger than the other.

summary_text: Adelita was the daughter of Francisco and Adelia, who lived in a village in Mexico. Adelita’s mother died soon after Adelita was born, so Esperanza helped care for the family. Francisco later married Dona Michaela, who had two daughters, Valentina and Dulce. After Francisco died, Dona Michaela treated Adelita cruelly. She sent Esperanza away and made Adelita work in the kitchen. When the family went to a fiesta for Javier, Adelita felt sad because she could not attend. Esperanza returned and helped her find her mother’s beautiful dress and rebozo. At the party, Adelita disguised herself as “Ciencienta.” Javier fell in love with her, but she ran away at midnight. The next day, Javier searched for her. He saw the rebozo at Adelita’s house and recognized her. He asked Adelita to marry him. Adelita invited Dona Michaela, her stepsisters, and Esperanza to the wedding. Adelita and Javier lived happily ever after.

summary_text: A unicorn says that it is moonlight white and has a magical horn. It looks a lot like a horse, but it is a unicorn. Its horn can make water clean or heal a hurt. summary_text: Three little bears go to a spooky old tree. One has a light, one has a stick, and one has a rope. They ask if they dare go into the tree, and they dare. They find a twisty old stare and go up it. Then they have a giant key and see a moving wall. They ask if they dare go through the wall and into the spooky old hall. They dare. They get out by going up a ladder, through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. They run fast home, safe at last.

summary_text: Queen Elsa was excited because it was Princess Anna’s birthday. She made Anna’s cake with ice and put a special ice decoration on top. summary_text: Many years ago, an emperor loved fine clothes more than anything else. He did not care about hunting, plays, food, or wine. One day, two swindlers came to town and said they were master weavers. They told the emperor they could make a magical cloth that only intelligent people could see. The emperor gave them gold and sent his prime minister to check on their work. The prime minister saw nothing, but he lied and said the cloth was beautiful. He even gave the swindlers more money. Then the emperor visited the room himself and also saw nothing. Afraid of seeming stupid, he praised the cloth and ordered a suit. Soon the swindlers pretended to dress him, and he marched through town while everyone pretended to admire his clothes. At last, a child shouted that the emperor had nothing on. The crowd agreed, and the emperor knew he had been tricked.

and likes to roar and drink.
The child looks in the sink
and outside the door
but no one has seen him.
Another person says dinosaurs do not exist anymore
and cannot be found anywhere
from the deepest deep to the highest ground.
The child explains that the dinosaur is not just any dinosaur.
He is very big
takes a nap at 4
and was not in the shower
the hair-combing place
or a big desk drawer.
The child keeps searching
and asks for help.
One person suggests getting a cat, dog, bird, or small white rat instead.
At tea time
many animals are listed
but still no dinosaur is found.
The child then goes to Professor Pew
who shows a museum room
and says dinosaurs are kept there
because they lived 200 million years ago.
The child says that is not the right dinosaur
because his dinosaur is five years old
just like him.

summary_text: Mr. Panda asks, “Would you like a donut?” One animal says, “Give me the pink one,” but Mr. Panda says no and changes his mind. Another asks for the blue one and the yellow one, but Mr. Panda says no again. A third says, “No, go away,” and Mr. Panda still does not give a donut. Then someone says, “Want them all, then bring me some more,” and Mr. Panda says no and changes his mind again. After that, Mr. Panda asks if anyone else would like a donut. A polite visitor says, “May I have a donut, please, Mr. Panda?” Mr. Panda gives all the donuts. The visitor says thank you, and Mr. Panda says, “You’re welcome.” Then Mr. Panda says, “I do not like donuts.”

summary_text: The Horace B. Smedley School was gloomy because its football team, the Smedley Tornadoes, had lost every game and had not scored a point. The players only horsed around, and Coach Armstrong became so upset that he had to rest at home with the measles. Everyone needed a real expert before the Thanksgiving game against the strong Werewolves. Miss Nelson heard that Viola Swamp was the meanest substitute teacher in the world, so she put on an ugly black sweatsuit and called for help. Coach Swamp quickly made the players work hard. They did leg raises, ran faster, and stopped horsing around. In a few days, the team looked much better. When Coach Armstrong came back, he was surprised to see the players working like a real team. On Thanksgiving Day, the Tornadoes beat the Werewolves, 77–3. Miss Nelson went home tired and happy after getting tough with the team.

summary_text: Kelp was born deep in the ocean. He was a narwhal, but he was different from the others. His tusk was shorter, he liked different food, and he was not a very good swimmer. His friends did not mind, so Kelp did not mind either. Then a strong current swept him away. He wished he could swim better and found himself near land. On a cliff, he saw a sparkling creature that looked like him. Kelp swam to shore and tried walking on land for the first time. It was hard, but he kept going until he reached the forest. There he met land narwhals, who were unicorns. They showed him that his tusk was called a horn, gave him unicorn delicacies in cones, and taught him to gallop. Kelp had fun, but he missed his ocean friends. He said goodbye and returned home. His narwhal friends welcomed him back and told him they already knew he was a unicorn. Kelp felt happy, but he still remembered the unicorns and wondered if he had to choose between them.

summary_text: Lightning McQueen was lost on a strange highway after something went wrong in his truck. He raced off an exit ramp, could not find his driver, and then heard sirens and saw flashing red lights. Sheriff chased him, and Lightning swerved, crashed through a fence, and got tangled in telephone wires. The next morning Mater brought him to traffic court. Doc, the judge, said Lightning must leave town, but Sally said he should fix the road he damaged. Doc made a deal: if Lightning won a race, he could go. If Doc won, Lightning would repair the road. Lightning agreed, but he lost control on a sharp turn and landed in a cactus patch. Later, he worked on the road, learned to turn left to go right, and had fun tractor-tipping with Mater. He found Doc’s old racing cups, learned Doc was the Hudson Hornet, and helped finish the road. Then Lightning went to California, raced again, and remembered his new friends. He stopped Chick Hicks, helped The King finish the race, and returned to Radiator Springs.

summary_text: A long time ago in Africa, Mufaro lived with his two daughters, Manyara and Nyasha. Both girls were beautiful, but Manyara was often mean and told Nyasha that one day she would be queen and Nyasha would be a servant. Nyasha stayed kind and worked in the garden. One day she found a small snake named Nyoka and welcomed it. Soon a messenger said the king wanted to see the most beautiful and worthy daughters in the land so he could choose a queen. Mufaro told both girls to get ready. That night Manyara left early, but she was rude to a hungry boy, an old woman, and laughing trees. In the morning she was missing, so the others followed her path. Nyasha gave food to the boy, seeds to the old woman, and the trees bowed to her. At the city gate, Manyara ran out in fear after seeing a monster. Nyasha went inside and found Nyoka, who changed into the king and chose her to be his wife. A great feast was held, and Mufaro was glad that Nyasha became queen.

summary_text: Lance Cottonwood is a bright leaf who does very well in school. He enjoys his classes about leaves, sunlight, and changing colors. But during the autumn semester, he learns that his final test is to let go of his tree and fall to the ground. Lance is afraid. He wishes he were like Doug Fir, an evergreen who can stay on his branch all winter. While the other leaves float down, Lance makes excuses and remains alone in the tree. His teacher tells him that it is okay to be scared and listens to his worries. Lance sees children making a leaf pile and collecting leaves for crafts. His friends are having fun below, so Lance decides to try. He takes a deep breath, lets go, and floats gently into the pile. Lance is the last leaf to finish, but he does not fail. His friends cheer because he did it.

Many sea creatures came to play, and Ariel was happy to be with her friends.

summary_text: A child gets ready for New Year's with Mom and Grandma. The child hears that a dragon can bring health and Fortune and hopes to find one. The child and friends decorate the street with red lanterns and look for a dragon trail. They see a real red dragon's tail. The friends try many traps. They offer noodles and sticky rice, but the dragon eats the food and comes back twice. A cozy place does not catch him. A loud beat only catches the wind. Gold does not work either, and the trap falls through. For the final try, the children do a mighty Dragon Dance. They have fun, but the dragon does not appear. They make a giant mess and clean it up. The child says sorry to Mom. Mom gives the child a hug and says she loves this dragon best. They watch fireworks with Grandma, and the child feels lucky with the loving family. Next year may bring better luck.

They snuggle together and sleep, dreaming about their wonderful night at the beach.

The boys ran downhill, used the slippy slide to escape, and the bees followed them home. The bees landed on the honey buns, and Mrs. Lamb Chop laughed and said it was too hot for warm buns anyway. She said they needed ice cream.

At home, her mother comforted her and told her no one could stop her. May kept dreaming, believing, and working hard, and in the end she went to space and waved to her parents.

The walrus asks Mortimer to notice the mountains, ocean, blue sky, warm sun, and penguin family around him. Mortimer still has difficult moments, but the walrus says he is exactly where he needs to be. Afterward, Mortimer thinks about the walrus’s words. He realizes that he loves the mountains, ocean, and sky, and that he has friends and family. The penguin world is his only home and life, so he feels that things may work out after all.

summary_text: A pretty princess had a gold chain that she liked very much. One day, she lost it and cried all day. The king sent his men to look everywhere, but they could not find the chain. Then a frog came to the princess. He said he would find the chain if she let him sleep on her bed. The princess promised that she would. The frog searched everywhere and found the gold chain. He brought it back, and the princess was happy. But when the frog asked to sleep on her bed, she said no because he was dirty and ugly. The sad frog said she had broken her promise and went away. The next day, the princess found him very ill in her garden. She said she was sorry, picked him up, and put him on her bed. The next morning, the frog became a handsome prince. He married the princess, and they lived happily ever after.

The storyteller began to worry that no more chances would come. Then they thought that maybe they only needed to be brave at the right time. They promised to be ready if another chance appeared. One day, they saw something shiny in the distance, ran toward it, and let go of their fear. This time, they caught the huge chance and held on tight. It felt wonderful to soar and fly. Now the storyteller knows that holding back means missing out, so when a chance comes, it should be taken.

The day before Christmas, Aunt Eliza, Uncle Peter, and cousins Peter, Alice, and Ella arrive in a bob sled. The children play in the snow and make pictures. At bedtime, they hang their stockings by the fireplace and go to sleep so Santa Claus will come. In the morning, everyone finds red mittens and peppermint candy. Laura is especially happy because she receives a rag doll and names her Charlotte. The children eat pancake men, play inside, admire their gifts, and look at Pa’s book. Then the cousins leave in the bob sled. Laura has had a very happy Christmas.

summary_text: Martin Luther King, Jr. tells about the fight for civil rights after the March on Washington. Even after new laws were passed, black people still could not vote in Alabama. In Selma, 600 activists began a 54-mile march to Montgomery to ask for voting rights. Police stopped them with billy clubs and tear gas, and many people were hurt, but the marchers stayed peaceful and got back up. Two days later, they tried again with 2,500 people, but they still did not reach Montgomery. On Sunday, March 21, 1965, they tried a third time with 8,000 people. Black and white people, Christians and Jewish people, marched together in rain and tiredness. The world watched, and President Johnson sent troops to protect them. At last, they reached Montgomery with tears of joy. Dr. King says people should answer hate with love, violence with kindness, and keep marching together for freedom.
