Black people were stopped from voting, so the marchers wanted to tell the governor that voting rights were needed. Police attacked them with billy clubs and tear gas, but the marchers stayed peaceful. Two days later, 2,500 people tried again, and then a third march began on Sunday, March 21, 1965, with 8,000 people. Black and white people, Christians and Jews, marched together and sang, “We shall overcome.” They marched for two days through rain and exhaustion while the world watched. President Johnson sent troops to protect them. When they reached Montgomery, people cried tears of joy. Dr. King said that people should answer hate with love, violence with kindness, and keep moving forward together.

summary_text: A rainbow has many colors. Red comes first. Red is seen in strawberries, stop signs, and Mickey’s night-light. Orange comes next. Orange is like tigers, sunsets, and fruit. Yellow is the third color and is bright like sunshine and ducklings. Green is next, like peas, pickles, and tree leaves. Blue comes after green, like the sky and bluebells. Violet is at the end, like grapes. The colors are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet. A rainbow is made from light. White light can split apart, and many colors appear. Some light waves are colors that eyes cannot see. The friends look for little rainbows near their toys and cars while they learn the colors in order. They discover that all these colors are part of light and that the colorful rainbow comes from light waves.

summary_text: Percy Penguin was not afraid of anything. He slid on his tummy, jumped into the water, and loved exploring. Posey Penguin was more careful because she feared snow storms, heights, loud noises, and especially the dark. One day, a huge iceberg came near their land. Percy played on its slides, but he went too fast, crashed into a dark cave, and bumped his head. When Percy did not return, Posey became worried. She bravely swam to the iceberg and followed his footprints. Posey slid down into the cave and found Percy with a big bump. She had been scared, but she still came to help him. Percy showed her that the sky was beautiful green and blue, not black and empty. They slept in the cave and swam home the next morning. Percy thanked Posey and said she was the bravest penguin because she helped him even while she was scared.

summary_text: A hen lays eggs, and after a rooster mates with her, one egg can grow into a chick. The hen sits on the eggs to keep them warm. Inside the egg, the chick has food in the yolk, water in the albumin, and air space for its first breath. Over many days, the chick grows. On day three it has a heart. On day five its head, eyes, tail, wings, and legs begin to form. On day seven it is small but already looks like a chicken. On day ten and day eleven it grows more and can open and close its beak. On day fourteen it gets an egg tooth. On day eighteen it is very big and covered with soft down. On day twenty it breathes and pecks a hole. The next day it hatches, rests, and then the hen covers her chicks. Later the fluffy chicks come out and follow their mother to search for food in the barnyard.

He got up early at sunrise, but he could not see any stars, so he waited and waited. He waited through lunch and dinner. At last, just before the sun went away, he saw a star. He tried to jump for it, then climbed the tallest tree, but it was still too far. He tried many ways to reach it, but none worked. Then he saw something in the water. It was a baby star. He could not hold it in his hands. Later, he found a starfish on the sand and brought it home as his new friend.

He waited all day, until at last he saw one just before sunset. He tried to jump for it, then climbed the tallest tree, but it was still too high. He thought about using his father’s life preserver, a paper spaceship, and even a seagull, but none of these worked. Then he saw something in the water. It looked like a baby star, but when he touched it, it slipped through his fingers. Sad, he walked home and found a starfish on the sand. He had finally caught a star of his very own.

summary_text: PJ Funny Bunny was sad because he did not like being a bunny. He had to eat cooked carrots, he had many brothers and sisters, and his ears were very big. PJ left home and tried living with bears, but he could not sleep during winter. He tried being a bird, but he could not fly. He lived with beavers, but he did not like working. He lived with pigs, but they only sat in mud. He tried being a moose, but he could not make good moose calls. He tried being a possum, but hanging upside down gave him a headache. Finally, he lived with skunks and did not like that either. PJ hurried home. His family was happy to see him. PJ ate his carrots, played with his brothers and sisters, and was happy to be a bunny. He learned that it was better to be himself.

summary_text: Dino Boy is left behind when summer camp ends, and he feels lonely in a box at Lost and Found. He decides to escape and look for a home. A unicorn mood ring named Moody and Hamburger Hippo join him. They also meet Tina, a ballerina who comes out of a music box. The four toys leave through a window. They feel sad until a bus brings new children. A twin girl and boy choose Dino, a girl chooses Tina, another child chooses Hippo, and a girl takes Moody. At last, all four toys have loving homes.

summary_text: Ted Trimble and Maggie have enough money to live comfortably, but Maggie keeps buying expensive things. After Maggie drinks too much, Ted pushes her from a bedroom window. She survives but must use a wheelchair. Maggie sells some things and uses the gold bracelet to get a Telemark Three television. The machine can create real objects from television advertisements, using materials stored in the basement. Maggie quickly orders drinks and many other products, spending more money. Ted returns home and finds the room filled with purchases. He tries to attack her, but Maggie calls Telemark’s emergency protection service. A security man appears through the television. He explains that he is a duplicate and will soon die because of a flaw in his blood. Ted offers money, but the duplicate says money is useless to him and shoots Ted.

summary_text: Leo could not read, write, draw, or eat neatly, and he did not speak. His father worried and asked what was wrong, but Leo’s mother said, “Leo is just a late bloomer.” Leo’s father watched Leo every day and every night, waiting for him to bloom. He asked if Leo was really a bloomer, and Leo’s mother told him to be patient. Then she said, “A watched bloomer doesn’t bloom,” so Leo’s father watched television instead. The snow came and the trees budded, but Leo still did not bloom. Then, one day, Leo bloomed in his own good time. He could read, write, and draw. He ate neatly. He also spoke, and he said a whole sentence: “I made it.”

summary_text: Snow White was a beautiful baby whose name came from the soft snow falling when she was born. After her mother died, her father married a queen who was vain and cruel. The queen asked her mirror who was fairest, but one day it answered, “Snow White.” Jealous, the queen told a huntsman to take Snow White away. The huntsman warned her to run, so she fled through the forest and found seven kind dwarfs. The queen tried to hurt Snow White with a tight sash and then a poisoned comb, but the dwarfs saved her both times. At last, the queen gave Snow White a poisoned apple. Snow White fell lifeless, and the dwarfs placed her in a glass coffin. A prince came by after a year and a day. When he lifted Snow White, the apple piece flew from her mouth, and she woke up. Later, Snow White and the prince married, while the seven dwarfs carried her train.

summary_text: One day, hearts began falling from the sky where Cornelia Augusta lived. She caught one, then another, and then many more. Cornelia thought Valentine’s Day must be near, so she decided to use the hearts to make cards. She noticed that every heart looked different. She studied them from the front, back, and side, choosing special hearts for her friends. She threaded seven hearts together for one person. For another card, she pasted a handsome heart onto paper and added a soft, white cotton ball. She had eight hearts left. She cut circles from the biggest heart and arranged the small hearts on paper. Then she painted colorful patterns around them and folded the paper. She stamped and mailed all her Valentines. The rain of hearts never came again, but Cornelia kept finding other ways to make Valentines in the years that followed.

Bear said the sun would stay away, but Brown Squirrel said the sun would rise. Many animals came to watch. At dawn, red light appeared, and soon the sun came up. Brown Squirrel was right, but he teased Bear. Bear became angry and pinned Squirrel under his paw. Brown Squirrel said he needed room to breathe and say sorry. When Bear lifted his paw, Squirrel ran home. Bear scratched his back, but Squirrel escaped into his burrow. He slept all winter. In spring, pale stripes covered his back, so he became Chipmunk. Chipmunk sings about the sunrise, while Bear remembers that nobody can do everything.

summary_text: An old lady swallowed a fly, but she would not say why. Then she swallowed a spider that wriggled, jiggled, and tickled inside her. She swallowed the spider to catch the fly. summary_text: When the fall wind blows and the cornfields become bare, a child gets ready for Thanksgiving in the woods. The child packs special treasures, including rocks, a rope, shells, a flashlight, and Brownie. Mama, Daddy, and Grandpa help everyone travel to a clearing beneath tall trees. The cousins build a fort, while the grown-ups make tables, seats, a fire, and a tarp. The next morning, neighbors help bring food such as turkey, potatoes, corn, apples, pickles, and pies. Everyone warms by the fire and roasts marshmallows. At the end, the family walks home along a candlelit path while singing. Grandma calls it a perfect ending.

summary_text: An apple begins as a flower on an apple tree. In winter, tiny leaf buds and flower buds wait under the cold snow. When spring brings warmer, longer days, the buds open. Green leaves and pink-and-white flowers appear. The flowers have male and female parts. Bees visit the flowers to collect nectar, and pollen sticks to their bodies. When bees fly to another apple tree, pollen reaches the flower's sticky tubes. The male cells travel to the ovary and join the female cells. Then the flower is fertilized, its petals fall, and an apple starts growing where the flower meets the stem. The ovary becomes the apple's core and seeds, while the white part swells around it. Leaves use sunlight, water, and air to make sugar for the fruit. Apples grow all summer, become sweet in fall, and are picked when ripe. Their seeds can grow into new trees.

summary_text: Charlie was the smallest child in Mr. Tiffen’s class, and he was always at the front or back when the children lined up. One fall day, the class saw a big, medium, and small pumpkin. The children guessed how many seeds were inside, but Charlie did not make a guess. They opened the pumpkins and scooped out the seeds. The children made groups so they could count faster. Some counted by twos, some by fives, and Charlie counted by tens. The big pumpkin had 340 seeds, and the medium pumpkin had 316. Charlie discovered that the little pumpkin had 350 seeds—the most of all! Mr. Tiffen explained that size does not always show how many seeds a pumpkin has. Lines on the outside can match rows of seeds inside. At the end, Charlie led the line because the class lined up from smallest to tallest.

summary_text: The fish in the ocean were decorating the reef and singing for the holiday. Mr. Fish felt gloomy because he wanted presents for all his friends. He thought every present had to be big, bright, perfect, meaningful, and shiny. He visited one store, then another, but nothing felt right. A special item was sold out, and the last store was closed. Mr. Fish had no presents and felt he had let his friends down. A gentle voice told him that the best gifts come from the heart and that he himself was enough. Mr. Fish felt peace, joy, and love. He learned that a gift made with care can be a very merry gift.

summary_text: Peppa and George went to bed while rain fell outside. Peppa hoped there would be muddy puddles in the morning. But it rained so much that the ground became covered with water. Daddy Pig could not jump in a puddle because he landed in a big pool. The Pig family’s house looked like a desert island, and they needed food. Granny Pig and Grandpa Pig came in a boat. Peppa, George, and Polly went with them to ask the neighbors what food they wanted. Polly copied everyone, but she forgot the list at the supermarket. Peppa remembered the orders, so Grandpa Pig brought cheese, newspapers, comics, and chocolate to the neighbors. In the evening, Peppa was happy she had helped, but there were no muddy puddles. The next morning, the sun came out and the water disappeared. A huge muddy puddle was left at the bottom of Peppa and George’s hill.

summary_text: Duck is tired of doing farm chores while Farmer Brown is in charge. He makes a sign asking for an election, and the farm animals vote. He leaves the Vice President in charge and returns to the farm, where Farmer Brown now does the hard chores while Duck works on his autobiography.

Cookie felt sad because he was not sweet, not fast, and did not know what he was good for. Fox took him to the dentist, then to the Christmastown Spa, where elves dipped him in eggnog, sprinkled him with powdered sugar, and sang Christmas carols. At last, Christmas tree ornaments told Cookie he was one of them. Cookie hung on the biggest Christmas tree and was happy to know what he was made for.

His sister Marisol found one of the crumpled pictures and took it to her room. Raman followed her and saw that she had made a gallery on her walls from his drawings. Marisol showed him the vase picture and said it looked “vaseish.” Raman looked at the pictures in a new way. He began drawing freely again, making treeish, houseish, and boatish pictures. He also drew feelings and wrote poemish poems. Later, he felt something wonderful that pictures and words could not capture, so he simply enjoyed it. Then he lived ishfully ever after.

summary_text: A new fifth grader feels lonely and unsure of herself after moving to a different neighborhood. Theresa, a small but loud bully, secretly kicks her legs whenever teachers are not watching. The girl hides the bruises from her mother and invents long routes around school to avoid Theresa. One day, Theresa catches her and kicks her until her knee bleeds. Mary Lou, the biggest and strongest girl at school, helps clean the wound, but she tells the girl to stand up for herself instead of promising to fight Theresa. When Theresa tries to kick again, the girl swings her arm and accidentally hits Theresa in the nose. They fight and are both sent to the principal. They spend a week together on the bad-kids’ bench. Theresa discovers that the girl loves books and invites her to the downtown library. Later, they become friends. The girl realizes that Mary Lou’s courage changed her life and helped her become braver and more connected to others.

summary_text: Mom is cooking in the kitchen, and Grandma is standing near her as the family gets ready for New Year’s. The child hears Mom say that a dragon would bring health and Fortune. Outside, the child and friends decorate the street with red lanterns and watch for a dragon’s tail. Soon they see a real red Dragon’s Tail. The dragon can control the water, and the children think he is very amazing. They try to catch him with tacos, then with noodles and sticky rice, but he comes back to eat more. They try to trap him with a cozy place to nap, but that does not work either. Next they try gold, and then they use the mighty Dragon Dance. The dance makes a big mess, but the dragon is still not caught. In the end, the child helps clean up. Mom hugs the child, and they watch fireworks with Grandma. The child feels lucky with family, and they say better luck next year.

summary_text: Sylvester Duncan loved collecting unusual pebbles. One rainy day, he found a shiny, round, red pebble that was magic. When he held it, he could make wishes come true. He wished for sunshine and made a wart disappear. Then he saw a hungry lion and became frightened. Without thinking, he wished to be a rock. The lion left, but the pebble was beside the rock, so Sylvester could not touch it or become himself again. His parents searched everywhere, but they could not find him. Seasons passed while Sylvester stayed a rock on Strawberry Hill. In spring, his parents came for a picnic and found the red pebble. Sylvester’s mother wished he were with them. Sylvester wished to be himself again, and the magic worked. He became a donkey once more and was reunited with his loving parents. They kept the pebble in a safe.

summary_text: Owl was the captain of the castle’s night watch. While the other knights slept, he lit torches, watched the walls, and kept the castle safe. One morning, Early Bird came to him. She wanted to be a night owl and asked many questions. Owl was tired, but she stayed busy and made lots of noise. She tried working at night, but she fell asleep before the sun went down. Later, Owl told her she was not an owl or a knight, so Early Bird went away. When she did not come back, Owl became worried and searched the cold, dark forest. He found wolves there, and Early Bird woke the knights to help. The knights chased the wolves away. Early Bird was a terrible owl, but Owl said she was a very brave knight. The next morning, she let Owl sleep, and they talked over pancakes.

summary_text: In a village in Africa, Mufaro lived with his two beautiful daughters, Manyara and Nyasha. Manyara was often rude and boasted that she would be queen while Nyasha would be her servant. Nyasha was kind, worked in her garden, and sang while she grew millet, sunflowers, yams, and vegetables. One day, a small garden snake named Nyoka stayed with Nyasha and helped make her garden even better. Later, a messenger announced that the king wanted a wife and invited the most worthy and beautiful daughters to come to the city. Mufaro told both daughters to go, but Manyara secretly left early. On the way, she ignored a hungry boy, insulted an old woman, laughed at laughing trees, and ran past a strange man with his head under his arm. When Nyasha traveled the same road, she shared food, gave seeds, and showed respect. At the palace, Manyara ran out in fear, saying a monster snake was inside. Nyasha entered and found Nyoka, who revealed he was the king and chose her as his wife. A great wedding followed, and Mufaro said he was happiest because Nyasha became queen and Manyara served in the queen’s household.

summary_text: Sometimes the child remembers things and sometimes the child forgets. In the morning, the child brushed teeth but forgot to make the bed. After breakfast, the child put dishes in the sink but forgot the milk. The child almost forgot to feed the puppy, but the puppy reminded them. The child watered the plants and fed the goldfish. Then the child got ready for school and reached the bus on time, but forgot the lunchbox. Mom brought it to school. After school, the child played in the rain and remembered the rain slicker but forgot the rubber boots. At snack time, the child had cookies and milk and forgot to count the cookies. Later, Dad came home, and the puppy got the paper first. At bedtime, the child washed up, picked up some things, and then noticed the toys were still not put away. One thing was never forgotten: Mom always read a bedtime story, and the child always kissed her good night.

summary_text: Pig was a pug who had done many naughty things, so it was time for obedience school. A strict trainer told Pig he would learn to behave. He told the other dogs to follow him and escape. Pig rode off, but his steed fell. Pig kept going fast downhill and knocked over a cake stall and a hot dog barbecue. Then Pig got too close to a gas tank, and there was a big explosion. After that, Pig was only a little burned, and his fur grew back. The blast made Pig change. He began sharing and giving, and he really did become better.

summary_text: Pig was a pug who loved Halloween treats. On Halloween night, he rushed through the streets and shouted, “Treats. Treats. Treats. Treats.” He grabbed whole baskets of candy and sometimes turned over pumpkins if people would not give him enough. If he felt shortchanged, he got angry and played mean tricks, like egging front doors. He wanted all the treats for himself and kept taking more and more. Then Pig ate too much candy without thinking. Trevor, a clever dog, warned that dogs cannot eat chocolate. Pig started to choke on the chocolate. Trevor quickly grabbed Pig by the ankles and spun him around. This made the chocolate come out like warm soup. After that, Halloween became different. Pig had a small buffet, respected people’s homes, and shared his treats. He was kinder now, and people saw that an old dog could learn new tricks.

As the seasons passed, he became big and strong. He hunted and fished for the old woman, and soon she had meat, fish, furs, and blubber. She shared the food with him and with the village. She told the bear to leave at once, and he went away sadly. Later, when she was lonely, she called for her son, and a big polar bear came to bring her food.

summary_text: Sid was a cat who lived in six houses on Aristotle Street. Each night he went from number one to number six to eat six dinners. Sid had to remember six names and act in six different ways. He was swanky as Scaramouche, had a job as Bob, was naughty as Satan, silly as Sally, smooched as sooty, and acted rough as Schwartz. One cold day, Sid got a cough and was taken to the vet six times. The vet gave him medicine and then noticed six sick cats in Aristotle Street. He called the owners, and they found out about Sid. The owners were angry and said he could only have one dinner a day. Sid then moved to Pythagoras Place, where everyone talked to each other, so everyone knew about his six dinners and nobody minded.

summary_text: Little Critter says, “I’m sorry” many times after he makes mistakes. Later, he takes apart his sister’s dollhouse and cannot put it back together. At the end, Mom says that sometimes saying “I’m sorry” is not enough, and Little Critter learns he must be more careful.

At the front door, they found Edgar’s last note and a huge Easter basket filled with chocolate eggs and jelly beans.

He kept trying and felt he might not be so bad after all.

summary_text: A child keeps doing small things that seem harmless. At the zoo, the child feeds popcorn to a bear. The child talks during story time, honks the car horn, splashes at the pool, stands on the bus, leaves a coat on the school floor, throws a snowball, shoots a straw wrapper at dinner, and runs onto a football field. Each time, an adult asks, “What if everybody did that?” At the end, the child comes home and gives Mom a hug. Then the child asks the same question and says, “Everybody should.” The story shows that some actions should not be copied, while kind actions should be shared by everyone.

When the busy day ends, they go home to rest and come back ready for a new day. Everyone has a place and is welcome.

summary_text: Monty the manatee felt shy on his first day at Sea school. He waved goodbye to his caring mommy and slowly paddled into school. A school of fish also teased Monty and said he was ugly, slow, and clumsy. Then a huge shark came toward all the sea creatures, ready to eat them. Clever Monty closed his eyes and looked like a rock. He tucked his friends under his tummy and stayed still. The shark swam away because he thought Monty was a rock. The sea creatures cheered for Monty and felt sorry for being unkind. They became friends and played nicely. Monty said that what is inside matters more than being fast, slow, thin, or fat, and that kindness makes the world better.

Young wayfinders learned from their mentors, and Mataivasa taught his protégé. Later, the protégé sailed beyond the reef with a crew. The villagers watched, knowing the winds would carry them home.

summary_text: After World War II, Ando walked through the damaged streets of Osaka and saw hungry people waiting in the cold for expensive bowls of ramen. He could not forget them. He decided to spend his life making food so people would have enough to eat. After several businesses, Ando lost his money and began dreaming of noodles that families could make quickly and affordably. He mixed flour, salt, water, eggs, powdered milk, and spinach, but many batches failed. He kept trying until he found the right balance. Then he worked to make noodles that could become soup with hot water. One night, he watched Masako fry tempura and noticed the tiny holes in the crispy batter. Ando fried his noodles, added hot water, and discovered that they became soft, tasty ramen in two minutes. His family helped demonstrate the invention. Soon, many kinds of people enjoyed the nutritious, convenient noodles. Ando said that peace follows from a full stomach.

summary_text: In Haiti, a mother kept many bees and made sweet honey for her children. One day, she carried a large pot of honey to the market. Papa God had helped him when he needed it.

summary_text: The punctuation marks worked every day in Mr. Wright’s classroom. On a very hot day, Mr. Wright said they should take a vacation. The punctuation marks left, but they soon learned that the class needed them. Without punctuation, Mr. Wright could not read the class’s book, and the words made little sense. The punctuation marks sent postcards from Take a Break Lake. The children guessed who had written them and tried to send a reply. Since they could not write properly without punctuation, they borrowed marks from the unruly classroom next door. They wrote that they missed punctuation and needed it to read and write. The punctuation marks came back and returned to their places. Then they explained how commas, periods, question marks, exclamation points, apostrophes, colons, and quotation marks help writing make sense. The class thanked them and promised not to take them for granted.

summary_text: An ugly pumpkin waits in a pumpkin patch to be picked, but no one chooses him. One day, a skeleton comes for pumpkins. The pumpkin finds shelter in a garden filled with squash. There, he notices something surprising. He discovers that he is a squash after all. When Thanksgiving comes, the pumpkin finally finds where he belongs. He is happy to tell his story and invites everyone to let the feast begin.

summary_text: Long ago, all the trees were green and happy except a weeping willow. He wanted his leaves to change colors. The angel of the trees asked God, but God said no because the willow had already received other wishes: he had grown big and his branches had curved down. The willow kept whining until Mr. Oak, Miss Sycamore, and all the trees moved away. At last, God said yes. The willow’s leaves became red, orange, yellow, and brown. He was very happy, but then he became sick and began to die. His old friends saw this and sent God a letter. They said the willow was their friend and they did not want him to die alone, so they would change colors and die with him. God agreed. He promised the trees would return each spring. The willow stopped complaining because he had friends.

At last Strega Nona returned, sang the song, blew the kisses, and stopped it. She made Big Anthony eat the pasta for his punishment.

It ate the fish and wanted the chickens and pigs the villagers gave it. The villagers were afraid the eel would eat them, too. Maui, a strong demigod, came to help. He rode with a villager to the eel’s cave. Maui hit the eel with his fish hook, but the eel attacked him. Maui changed into a little fish and then back into a man. The eel wrapped around him and opened its mouth. Maui pushed the eel’s coils up, so the eel bit itself. The eel fled, but Maui chased it and defeated it with his magical hook. He buried its head. A coconut tree grew there, giving the villagers a useful fruit.

After people stop admiring him, they begin teasing him, and Stanley feels unhappy about being flat. Arthur comforts him and has an idea. He uses a bicycle pump to fill Stanley with air. Stanley becomes round again, and the family celebrates Arthur’s clever idea.

A tiny sprout grew from the place where Jack had been. Tim watered and weeded it while vines and yellow flowers appeared. At last, a little green pumpkin grew. By August, many pumpkins were hiding among the leaves. In October, frost made the plant die, so Tim picked the green pumpkins and placed them on the porch. By Halloween, they were orange. Tim gave away all but one, carved its face, and welcomed Jack back from seed to pumpkin again.

summary_text: It is springtime, and Grandpa Pig hides many chocolate eggs in the garden for Peppa and her friends. He tells them to look carefully and not step on his plants. Peppa finds an egg in a plant pot. Rebecca Rabbit finds one under a bush, and Freddy Fox finds one in a wheelbarrow. Richard cannot find an egg, so Grandpa Pig puts his hat on Richard's head. When Grandpa lifts the hat, an egg is underneath. Now Richard has an egg, too. The friends eat all the chocolate eggs. Then Granny Pig takes them to see three chickens named Jamaima, Sarah, and Neville. Their eggs begin to hatch, and three baby chicks come out. Peppa and her friends pretend to be chicks and sing about pecking food, a fluffy yellow head, and a straw bed. Granny Pig says that now it really is Easter.

summary_text: A good egg lived in a carton with eleven other eggs. The other eggs ignored bedtime, ate sugary cereal, had tantrums, and broke things. The good egg tried to fix everyone’s behavior and keep peace. He worked so hard that he became exhausted, and cracks appeared in his shell. His doctor said the cracks came from putting too much pressure on himself. The good egg left the carton and traveled alone. He took walks, read books, floated in a river, wrote in his journal, breathed quietly, and painted. Little by little, his cracks healed, and his head no longer felt scrambled. He decided to return because he missed his friends. He promised to be good to the other eggs while also being good to himself. The carton came back together, and he understood that the other eggs did not have to be perfect, and neither did he.

summary_text: A little old lady lived alone in a small house. She felt there was not enough room, so she asked a wise old man for help. He told her to bring in a hen. Then she brought in a pig, which chased the hen and raved the ladder. Last came a cow, which charged at the pig and jumped on the table. The house felt smaller and smaller. The wise old man told her to take all the animals out. The hen flew out, and the lady shooed out the goat, pig, and cow. Suddenly, her house felt enormous. She stopped grumbling and enjoyed having plenty of room.

A bird eats one seed

birds fly,
the sun shines,
and rain falls.
The seeds begin to grow roots, stems, and leaves.
Some plants are hurt by weeds and children,
and one flower is picked.
The tiny plant keeps growing all summer
until it becomes a giant flower.
Birds, bees, and butterflies visit it.
In autumn again, the wind shakes the flower,
and many tiny seeds fly out
to begin the story again.

summary_text: One quiet night, Irene heard someone knocking on the door. She called Brody, and they found a duck outside. The duck came in and said his name was Max. Max told them he had been born in the spring. He had stayed behind when his flock flew south because he thought winter would be nice, but it was cold and lonely. Irene said winter was better with a warm home, so Max stayed. In January, Max learned how to use the remote control and liked watching Wild Kingdom, worldwide wrestling, and Gigi’s magic mailbox. In February, he learned to cook. By March, he felt at home. By April, he knew too much, and everyone got tired of his reruns and his many recipes. Then Max ran in and said his flock had returned. He said goodbye, gave Irene his chef’s hat, and gave Brody his rubber duckies. After hugs, Max left. Later, when October came, the house was quiet again, and everyone was happy to hear quacking. When Max came back with his flock, everyone welcomed him home.

When the parade begins, she wishes everyone a Happy Thanksgiving Day.

summary_text: Jasper Rabbit needed new underwear, so Mom took him to the store. He saw a pair of creepy underwear that looked cool and comfy, and he asked Mom to buy them. That night, Jasper wore them to bed, but they glowed a ghoulish greenish glow. He got scared, changed into plain white underwear, and hid the creepy pair in the laundry hamper. The next morning, the creepy underwear were on him again, so he threw them in the garbage. But they came back in his dresser drawer. Jasper mailed them to China, but they returned with chopsticks. Then he used Mom’s sewing scissors to cut them up. After that, he checked his drawer and found plain white underwear. He thought the creepy underwear were gone, but they still came back. Jasper finally took a shovel, dug a deep hole at Creek Hanger Hill, and buried them. When he got home, he found only plain white underwear in his drawer. Later, he bought more creepy underwear with his allowance and hung them up like string lights. That night, he was not scared and slept happily.

summary_text: It is a dark night, and St. Patrick’s Day is almost here. A leprechaun says he is coming to make a mess. At the end, he says only a brilliant child might build the perfect trap, so the people must try again next year.

summary_text: Millie makes mistakes in many everyday activities. She spills milk, uses too much toothpaste and glue, spells banana wrong, and runs too fast. Millie dreams of becoming a top athlete, so she enters a hurdle race. At first, she forgets to jump and breaks hurdles. Then she lands on her face and her bum. When she jumps very high, she crashes into a tree and breaks a tooth. Millie feels embarrassed, but she calms herself and says she is strong and can figure things out. She makes a long stick from branches and shoelaces, uses it to reach a kite, and gets down from the tree. Then she practices jumping carefully. In the next race, Millie jumps over the hurdles, reaches the finish line, and wins. She learns that practice can turn mistakes into lessons and make her tougher and more resilient.

summary_text: Pearl walks home from school and stops in a bright forest. There, she hears a small bone speak. The fox shrinks to the size of a mouse and runs away. Pearl brings the bone home. Her parents are amazed when it talks, and the bone becomes a happy part of the family.

He is a leprechaun best seen from far away.

summary_text: Rosa grew up near Montgomery, Alabama, with her mother, brother, and grandparents. summary_text:
Mila tells us about her family. She has a big brother named Luca and a little sister named Sophia. Mila has super ears because she uses implants that help her hear big sounds and tiny sounds. Mila thinks she can do many grown-up things by herself, like making her bed and opening snacks. But her mom and dad still help her and tell her to eat broccoli, wear the right clothes, and go to sleep.

Mila decides to prove she is a big kid and tries to do everything alone. She picks her own clothes, puts on a pink headband, and uses tape to fix her sneaker laces. After that, Mila tries to ride her bike without training wheels. She falls and learns it is okay to ask for help. Mommy and daddy help her, and soon Mila rides on her own. Everyone cheers for her.

summary_text: The Sun is unhappy because a total solar eclipse will happen tomorrow. During the eclipse, the Moon will move in front of the Sun and cover its light. The Sun worries because people on Earth must never look directly at it, and it is upset that its friend Moon will help hide it. The Sun writes to Earth and asks if people will be safe. Earth writes back and says that earthlings know the safety rule and will protect their eyes with eclipse glasses. Earth tells the Sun to ask Moon. The Sun sends Moon a note, and Moon replies that people on Earth will think both of them are amazing and should get ready for a spectacular show. On eclipse day, the Moon moves into place, people wear glasses, and the Sun sees that no one is hurt. The Sun watches the full shadow, sees the solar corona and a diamond ring, and learns that Sun and Moon can shine in different ways.

The Sun says it may forget things sometimes, but it was right from the start about one important thing: looking directly at its bright light is dangerous unless a person wears special solar eclipse glasses. The Sun explains that there is only one time when it is okay to look without the glasses. That time is totality, when the Sun’s disc is completely behind the Moon. At that moment, people can take off their eclipse glasses because they cannot see any part of the Sun through them. But when the Sun starts to show again, making the diamond ring trick, the glasses must go back on right away. The Sun ends by telling people to protect their eyes when they look at the sky. It also says a total eclipse happens in one place on Earth only about once every 375 years.

In the end, Nemo went back home and returned to school, and Marlin let him go with love.

summary_text: Rainbow Fish was the most beautiful fish in the deep blue sea. His blue, green, and purple scales had shiny silver scales among them. Rainbow Fish gave one small scale to the little blue fish. Then he gave scales to many other fish. The more scales he shared, the happier he became. Soon the water sparkled with scales, and Rainbow Fish felt at home. He had only one shining scale left, but he was happy to swim and play with his friends.

Katie then cleared the side streets so cars could move again. Finally, she went home and stopped to rest. Katie worked hard and helped everyone in the snowy city.

summary_text: Polly loved visiting her grandparents' farm because she could gather eggs, help with animals, ride Mustard, pick blueberries, and play with Rob and Paige. On her birthday, Aunt Patty gave her an iPad. Polly was excited and spent almost all her time downloading games, watching videos, and using the iPad. She stayed up late, missed gathering eggs, said no to feeding the pigs, and did not help build a barn fort. When the iPad went dark, Polly went outside and brushed Mustard. Gramps explained that an iPad is not wrong, but using it all day can make her miss other good things. Polly found Rob and Paige making a hay fort and had fun helping them. She decided to put the iPad away for the rest of her visit. Then she rode Mustard, gathered eggs, picked blueberries, and played with her cousins for the rest of the week. When she got home, her mother could help her make a plan for using the iPad sometimes, not all the time.

Tim asked for their treasure, and they gave him a little gray goose that laid golden eggs. On his way home, Tim stayed with the McGoons and told them about the goose. While he slept, they swapped it for an ordinary goose. Tim later got a magic tablecloth from the wee folk, but the McGoons stole that too. After Tim told the wee folk what happened, they gave him a green hat. Tiny men jumped out of the hat and beat the McGoons until they returned the goose and tablecloth. Tim and Kathleen used them to get food, and their home was comfortable again.

The next day, he gave his story to the teacher and said he had finished it. Bria the ladybug was happy, and the story said Ricky had found his hidden talent and was a good poet.

Then Mr. Stork came late and gave Mrs. Jumbo a bundle. Inside was a baby elephant with big blue eyes. Mrs. Jumbo named him Jumbo Jr. When the baby sneezed, his ears opened very wide. The other elephants laughed and called him Dumbo. Mrs. Jumbo loved her baby and held him close.

Later, some boys teased Dumbo in the tent. Mrs. Jumbo got angry and threw straw to make them leave. The ring master took Mrs. Jumbo away and locked her in a wagon. Dumbo cried for his mother. Then Timothy the mouse came and became his friend. Timothy made a plan to help Dumbo and his mother. Dumbo later flew through the air with a magic feather, then learned he did not need it. He could fly by himself. After that, Dumbo became famous, and Mrs. Jumbo was freed. Dumbo was happiest when he was back with his mother.

A little girl gave him her hat, and the children said he looked awesome. But Sneezy wanted more warmth, so he sat in a hot tub and melted again. The children rebuilt him once more. Then a little boy gave him a red and blue scarf, and a little girl gave him a bright orange coat. Sneezy felt too hot and wanted to take the clothes off. The children told him to get something cold from the ice cream store. Sneezy ate seven scoops of ice cream and felt just right at last.

summary_text: Nelson was a boy from South Africa whose family belonged to an old clan. His father died when Nelson was twelve, and he went to live with the chief’s family, who helped him continue learning. At the palace, Nelson heard stories about African history. He also learned that white people controlled the country and had better homes, schools, and pay, while other people were treated unfairly. Nelson went to college because he wanted to change this. He joined a group that worked for equal rights and protested against apartheid, a system that separated people by skin color. He was arrested, hid in disguise, and was finally sent to prison for twenty-seven years. Even in his cell, Nelson dreamed of equality. The president released him, and they worked together to change the laws. Nelson later became South Africa’s first black president. His life showed that hope and determination can help people keep working for a fairer country.

summary_text: One morning little Benjamin Bunny heard a pony and saw Mr. McGregor and Mrs. McGregor ride past in a gig. When they were gone, Benjamin hopped to the wood behind Mr. McGregor’s garden to visit his family. There he found his cousin Peter Rabbit, who looked poorly and wore only a red cotton pocket handkerchief. Peter said Mr. McGregor had chased him in the garden and taken his clothes. Benjamin told Peter that Mr. and Mrs. McGregor were away for the day. The two rabbits went to the wall and looked into the garden. Peter climbed down a pear tree, and Benjamin followed. They found Peter’s coat and shoes on the scarecrow. Benjamin tried on the tamashanter, and they filled the pocket handkerchief with onions. They walked on, but Peter heard noises and wanted to go home. Soon they hid under a basket when a cat came and sat on top of it for five hours. At last old Mr. Benjamin Bunny came, chased the cat away, took the rabbits out, and went home with them. Peter got his clothes back, and his mother forgave him.

The story ends with “That’s what we see.”

summary_text: Money explains that it does not grow on trees and can be used to buy basic needs and fun things, such as pizza, clothes, a houseboat, or a guinea pig. However, money cannot make someone truly happier, and a person’s value is not measured by how much they can buy. Money says children should learn four important things: how to earn, save, spend, and give it away. Children can earn money by selling lemonade, singing, or letting others use it. They should save some in a clear jar for unexpected rainy days. They can spend money on things they really want and on learning activities, such as music, art, or zoo school. Money warns against buying things they do not need or spending more than they have. At the end, money says that becoming good at something children love can help them earn more, and then they can share.

Everyone likes being looked after, even Dr. Brown Bear.

summary_text: A child on a snowy farm wonders if Christmas has arrived. Daddy wants to decorate quickly, but Mama says the family will keep Christmas simple and make their own presents. On Christmas Eve, they decorate a long table and go to church to hear about Jesus being born in a manger. On Christmas morning, the child receives thoughtful homemade gifts. Friends and neighbors bring food to the Little Red Barn. Everyone sings, eats, plays, and enjoys winter activities together. At the end of the happy day, the child wants another simple Christmas on the farm next year.

summary_text: Grandma Tala tells the children an old story about Maui, the Heart of te Fiti, and a darkness that spreads across the islands. She says someone will one day go beyond the reef, find Maui, and return the Heart to save everyone. Tui, the village chief and Moana’s father, stops the story and says no one should go outside the reef because it is safe inside. Deep in the lagoon, the ocean gives her a glowing green spiral stone. Tui finds her, takes her back to shore, and tells her she is the next great chief, but she must learn where she belongs. Grandma Tala later picks up the stone and keeps it. Moana then spends time with her parents, learns about sharing, and watches the village before hearing the waves call her again.

Ruby learned that worries do not have to stay forever, and talking to someone can make them shrink.

summary_text: For many years, children remembered the planets with the sentence “My very eager mother just served us nine pizzas,” which included Pluto. Scientists later learned more about Pluto and began to question its place among the planets. Pluto is rocky even though it is far from the sun, its orbit crosses Neptune’s orbit, its path is tilted and stretched out, and it is very small. In 1976, astronomers discovered that Pluto had a moon named Charon, making Pluto seem even smaller. In 1992, scientists found the Kuiper Belt, a region filled with icy objects like Pluto. Mike Brown and his team later discovered Eris, an object larger than Pluto, which caused a debate about what counts as a planet. In 2006, the IAU decided that planets must orbit the sun, be round, and clear their orbital neighborhoods. Pluto and Eris became dwarf planets. The story shows that scientific ideas can change when new information is discovered.

summary_text: Albert is a private investigator following a mysterious woman on a train. She wears a fur coat, a red scarf, dark glasses, and high heels, and she never seems to look back. She cries as they take him away, leaving a lonely trail of tears on her cheek.

summary_text: Ping is a way of sending something from yourself into the world. You can ping with your voice, fingers, brush, poem, or a small or big gesture. You can express feelings, say, “I love you,” and share your mind, heart, and dreams. You can ping to one person, a few people, everyone, or life itself. The other person gives the pong, and you cannot decide how that person will respond. The pong may smile, become scared, become angry, or not notice. After you ping, breathe deeply and keep your heart open. Then listen for the pong. It may give you something to learn, think about, be thankful for, keep, or let go. Sometimes you may need to pause. The story asks what your next ping will be.

McGee and D fixed it, went home, and decided to camp in their backyard instead.

summary_text: Harrison P. Spider loved life and wanted to share his joy with everyone. But he often sat too close, shook hands too hard, and gave very big high-fives. Teachers, coaches, and parents noticed that Harrison was not leaving enough personal space. His dad talked with him and taught him a space saver. Harrison stretched his arms out front and wide, then brought them back to his sides. If he could do this without touching anyone, he knew he had left enough room. Harrison practiced again and again, and soon his whole family practiced too. The next day, he used the space saver at school. Later, his dad explained that when a place was crowded, Harrison should simply put his arms down, be still, and stay in his own space. Harrison chose his own seat on the bus, kept space during baseball, and sat on his own mat at story time. He did not do it perfectly, but he got better most of the time.

Bugs, owls, teasing children, and the laughing shepherds made it difficult. One day many travelers passed by, and Benjamin began to wonder if the promise would ever happen. He looked away from the stump and watched the shepherds. Then a bright light filled the sky above them, and he heard singing. When he looked back, a small green shoot had appeared on the stump. Benjamin remembered the promise and ran into Bethlehem shouting that the king had come. A shepherd opened a door and invited him in to meet the king and join the watch.

summary_text: One Saturday morning in Manchester, a film crew came to Moss Row tip, a big broken piece of land near Aras. They brought lorries, cameras, lights, cabins, and many men dressed like old soldiers for a television film about the Battle of the Somme. They used fake gunfire, smoke, and explosions, and the actors kept charging up the ridge and falling down. The narrator watched all day. Then Grandad came home and stopped in shock when he saw the battle. He had been in the real war, and the noise and sights upset him. Mum explained that the war had been horrible and that Grandad had lost friends. That night, Grandad looked out at the tip again and heard a weak cry. He and the narrator went onto the tip, found a mud-covered man in a crater, and helped him back. Grandad carried him home. The next day, the tip was ordinary again, but the narrator never forgot how much the war had meant to Grandad.

a big broken piece of land near Aras.
They brought lorries, cameras, lights, cabins, and many men dressed like old soldiers
for a television film about the Battle of the Somme.
They used fake gunfire, smoke, and explosions,
and the actors kept charging up the ridge
and falling down.
The narrator watched all day.
Then Grandad came home
and stopped in shock
when he saw the battle.
He had been in the real war,
and the noise and sights upset him.
Mum explained that the war had been horrible
and that Grandad had lost friends.
That night, Grandad looked out at the tip again
and heard a weak cry.
He and the narrator went onto the tip,
found a mud-covered man in a crater,
and helped him back.
Grandad carried him home.
The next day, the tip was ordinary again,
but the narrator never forgot how much the war had meant to Grandad.

summary_text: Taylor decided to build something new, special, and amazing. Taylor felt proud, but then everything came crashing down. The chicken came first and said to talk about it, but Taylor did not want to talk, so the chicken left. Then the bear came and said to shout about it, but Taylor did not want to shout, so the bear left too. The elephant came and said to remember how things were, but Taylor did not want to remember, so the elephant left. The hyena wanted to laugh, the ostrich wanted to hide, the kangaroo wanted to throw it all away, and the snake wanted to knock down someone else’s stuff. Taylor did not want to do any of that. Soon Taylor was alone. Then the rabbit came close and sat quietly with Taylor. Taylor asked the rabbit to stay. The rabbit listened as Taylor talked, shouted, remembered, laughed, and made plans to build again.

summary_text: Mr Watson and Mrs Watson have a pig named Mercy. Every night they sing her a song about the bright morning sun and the dark night. The song makes Mercy feel warm, like she has eaten hot toast with lots of butter. But when the lights go out, Mercy feels afraid in the dark. One night Mercy decides she does not want to sleep alone. She gets out of her bed and climbs into bed with Mr and Mrs Watson. While they all sleep and dream, a hole opens under the bed. The bed falls into the hole, and everyone wakes up. Mr Watson says not to move, and Mrs Watson cries. Mercy is hungry and thinks about toast. She gets off the bed and walks to the kitchen, but there is no toast there. Then she remembers that Baby Lincoln next door has sugar cookies. Mercy goes outside and looks in Baby Lincoln's window. Baby wakes up and sees Mercy at the window. She thinks Mercy is a monster and calls for help. Eugenia Lincoln wakes up, calls the fire department, and rushes to Baby's room.

summary_text: Alex is a big polar bear who lives in the Arctic. Xena is a tiny penguin who lives in the Antarctic. They are called Polar Opposites because they live on opposite sides of the world and are very different. Alex is mostly white with some black, and Xena is mostly black with some white. Alex is shaggy, gets up late, likes sour things, and is messy and loud. Xena is smooth, rises early, likes sweet things, and is neat and quiet. Alex likes bright clothes, while Xena’s favorite clothes are not bright. Alex pushes things, but Xena pulls them. Alex travels fast, and Xena takes it slow. Even though Alex and Xena are different in many ways, they can always meet in the middle.

summary_text: Five little monkeys took a bath, put on their pajamas, brushed their teeth, and said goodnight to their mama. Then five little monkeys jumped on the bed. One monkey fell off and bumped his head, so mama called the doctor. The doctor said, “No more monkeys jumping on the bed.” Then four little monkeys jumped on the bed. One fell off and bumped his head, and mama called the doctor again. The doctor said the same thing. Next, three little monkeys jumped on the bed, and one fell off and bumped her head. Then two little monkeys jumped on the bed, and one fell off and bumped his head. After that, one little monkey jumped on the bed and fell off and bumped her head too. Mama called the doctor each time, and the doctor kept saying, “No more monkeys jumping on the bed.” In the end, five little monkeys fell fast asleep, and mama said, “Thank goodness. Now I can go to bed.”

summary_text: A bear left his den on a warm, bright morning. He smelled ripe berries, ate a feast, and fell asleep in the sunshine. While he slept, a great rumbling carried him far away to a new forest. The new forest had trees to climb, bark to scratch, soft mud, and many smells. Then the bear found a beautiful sandwich lying all alone. He waited quietly and ate it. Just before he finished, he heard a strange sniffing, snuffling, slobbering, and snorting sound. Someone had seen him, so the surprised bear ran away through the park and down the street. He climbed a tall tree and saw his own forest. Waves carried him home, where he heard familiar birds and bugs. The bear made it home safely. Only a little lettuce was left because the bear dropped it while running away.

summary_text: Finn the Frog talks to the reader and asks not to draw on his book pages, because only his illustrator, Mr. Arthur Lynn, is supposed to do that. Mr. Arthur appears and makes Finn normal again, with his sweet shoes. Finn thanks him and feels happy to be himself again. Then Finn gets hungry and asks for a big juicy fly, but when it is drawn too big, he gets scared. In the end, Finn says he will keep the fan pictures on the refrigerator and not let anyone draw in his book anymore.

summary_text: As the days grow short and cold, winter comes and many animals get ready in different ways. Birds like Bluebirds and Orioles fly south to warm places with food, and later they will return north in spring. Monarch butterflies also migrate south after gathering in trees by the hundreds. Some bats fly south, but others stay in caves and hibernate all winter. Woodchucks, also called groundhogs, eat a lot in fall, then crawl into their tunnels and sleep for up to four months. Pikas do not hibernate or migrate. They live in high mountains and gather grass in summer, dry it on rocks, and hide it under stones for winter food. Squirrels bury nuts and acorns and eat them later, though some forgotten nuts may grow into trees. Other animals, like mice, deer, rabbits, and foxes, must keep hunting for food all winter. People can help by putting out food, birdhouses, and other winter shelters. In the end, the days grow longer and warmer, and spring comes.

Pete thinks the next one will be better. When he shows Callie, she says her picture feels like something is missing. Pete feels sad and puts his crayons down. In art class, Pete is afraid to make a mistake, and his paper stays blank. Then Gus, Callie, and Grumpy Toad tell Pete that his art is cool because it is his. The teacher says art should be fun and is for everyone. Pete smiles, tries again, and draws the whole gang having fun together. His friends like the picture, and Pete makes a rocking masterpiece.

summary_text: Last Thanksgiving, Clifford stayed home while his family visited Grandma. His kind neighbors took care of him, but Clifford thought about his family and especially his mom, who lived in the city. He decided to visit her for Thanksgiving. The trip became difficult. Cars bumped into him, and a drawbridge opened beneath him, making him wet and cold. Clifford went through a dark tunnel, where a train surprised him. He pushed the train back to the station and reached the street. In a strange neighborhood, he climbed a tall building and saw his old neighborhood and his mom’s house. A parade blocked the way, so he used the park as a shortcut. He accidentally joined a football game before finally finding his mom. She was happy, and they had a nice Thanksgiving dinner. Emily thought about Clifford at Grandma’s house. Clifford hurried home, and Emily did too. They were thankful for each other.

Tacky showed them his funny march and a big cannonball. Then the other penguins sang Tacky’s silly song as loudly and badly as they could. The hunters covered their ears and ran away, leaving their things behind. The penguins hugged Tacky because his odd ways saved them all. Tacky was different, but he was very nice to have around.

They look at a map
and walk to the river shore.
Archie feels hot
and says his feet hurt.
Dad gives him binoculars,
and Archie can see past the dirt to the trees.
He spots a bright blue feather
and a bluebird building her nest.
They see a bunny,
then watch ants carry food and leaves home.
Archie sees a squirrel with a snack,
but he tries to chase it.
Mom points out a sign
that says to turn right,
and they soon reach the river.
There they see lily pads
and a green frog.
Archie finds flat rocks
and skips them in the water.
When it is time to go back,
the sun is orange and pink.
The family goes home
to get ready for bed.

When they reach the place, they use a map to explore and walk toward the river. Archie says he is hot and his feet hurt, so Dad gives him binoculars to help him look around. Archie sees a bright blue feather and a bluebird building a nest in a tree. They also see a bunny, but when they get too close, it gets scared away. Dad says they can count the tree rings to learn its age. Along the trail, they watch ants carrying food and leaves, and Archie sees a squirrel with a snack in its cheek. Mom points to a sign that says to turn right, and soon they reach the river. There they see lily pads, a green frog, and flat rocks that Archie skips across the water. At the end, they head home as the sun sets and get ready for bed.

summary_text: Alice says she is a fairy. She is a temporary fairy, not a permanent fairy yet, because fairies must pass many tests. She has wings, so she can fly fast, but not very high. Alice shows her magic wand, her blanket, and her magic mirror. She uses fairy dust and spells to do magic. She turns oatmeal into cake and makes her dog float on the ceiling. She also says she once changed her dad into a horse and then tried to make him new clothes and a crown. One time, she changed her white dress into a red one, and the duchess got very mad and locked her in the tower forever, but Alice got away. Alice says fairies must be careful with magic and go to advanced fairy school to learn more. She is still learning and thinks she may be a temporary fairy forever.

summary_text: Mayzie the bird was tired of sitting on her egg. When Horton the Elephant walked by, she asked him to sit on it for a little while. Horton said yes, and Mayzie flew away on vacation. Horton stayed with the egg day after day. He sat through rain, wind, snow, and ice, and he kept saying, “I meant what I said and I said what I meant. An elephant’s faithful 100%.” Hunters found Horton and pointed guns at him, but he would not leave the egg. They took Horton and the egg away and showed him in a circus. Horton still stayed faithful. Then one day the circus went by the tree where Mayzie was. The egg cracked open, and a tiny bird came out. Mayzie wanted her egg back, but the bird belonged with Horton. People saw the baby bird and were amazed. They sent Horton home happy.

summary_text: When bedtime comes and the house is quiet, a nice dream truck may come to visit. The truck floats and flies, and a girl with stars in her eyes drives it. She helps children get ready for bed by giving them dreams. The truck has many dream choices. Children can pick dreams about treasure, winning, magic, pirouettes, summer, snow, and puppies. They can also choose princess dreams, super speed, heroes, flying, whales, dragons with jelly bean scales, moon beams, astronauts, and a triple dip cone. There are even dreams about narwhals, birthdays, and sea mine monsters. Some dreams are about music, like drummers, guitar, standing ovation, and rock star. There are big dreams and small dreams, and kids can choose new ones or keep one they love. After choosing, children snuggle into bed with their nice dream and go to sleep.

summary_text: When summer ended, the bear family saw cool weather, birds flying south, and leaves changing colors. Brother bear was ready to go back to school, but sister bear felt unsure because she was starting kindergarten. Mama bear took sister to meet Miss Honey Bear and look at the kindergarten room. The room had yellow curtains, small tables, chairs, paint, blocks, books, and clay. Miss Honey Bear told sister that kindergarten had stories, songs, ABCs, pictures, games, and many things to make and build. Sister liked what she saw, but when the first school morning came, she worried again. Brother bear helped her get on the big yellow school bus. At bear country school, the kindergartners got noisy, so Miss Honey Bear called, “Story time!” This helped everyone settle down. Sister painted, built with blocks, made a clay donut, looked at books, ate snack, and slept at nap time. At the end of the day, she showed her painting to mama and papa and was excited about school.

summary_text: Snow falls, and the children come outside to play. They like snow, even though they do not like snow in their faces. They dig it, throw it, slide on it, make tracks, and make snow angels. They climb a steep hill with their dog, then race down quickly. They make snowballs and build a snow house. Inside, they eat bread and meat, and leave some bread for the birds. Next, they roll a very big snowball and make a huge snowman named Ned. Ned has a head and a hat. Then the sun comes out. The warm sun makes Ned smaller and melts the snow. The children save some snow before it is gone. They put the snow away so they can play with it another day.

summary_text: Mrs. Bulldog had four puppies: Rocky, Ricky, Bruno, and Antoinette. Rocky was clever, Ricky was fast, and Bruno was strong. Antoinette had not yet found the special thing she could do, but her mother told her to keep her chin up. At the park, the puppies played with Fifi, Fufu, Ooh La La, and Gaston. Then Ooh La La disappeared. Rocky looked for paw prints, Ricky searched around the lake, and Bruno looked everywhere, but they could not find her. Antoinette felt a tug in her heart and a twitch in her nose. She followed smells past sidewalks, street vendors, signposts, buggies, bicycles, and broomsticks. Even a garbage truck did not stop her. At the city museum, she ran past the guard and found Ooh La La just in time to save her from a fall. Mrs. Bulldog was proud because Antoinette had been brave. Later, Antoinette became a famous police dog in Paris.

summary_text: Three white mice hide on a white piece of paper because of the cat this morning. Then they find three cans of paint and begin to play. One mouse jumps into red paint and comes out red. Another mouse jumps into blue paint and comes out blue. The third mouse jumps into yellow paint and comes out yellow. Next, the yellow mouse jumps into the red paint and becomes orange. The red mouse and blue mouse mix their colors and make purple. The blue mouse and yellow mouse mix their colors and make green. Soon the paint gets sticky, so the mice wash themselves in the sea. After that, they paint the paper instead of their bodies. They make blue, yellow, red, purple, green, and orange colors on the paper. They leave some paper white so they can still hide from the cat.

summary_text: In the jungle of Newell, Horton the elephant heard a tiny cry while he was splashing in a pool. He looked around and found only a little speck of dust floating in the air. Horton believed someone small was on it, so he gently lifted the clover and carried it to safety. A sour kangaroo and her young kangaroo laughed at him and said there was no one there. Horton still protected the speck because he said, “A person’s a person, no matter how small.” The news spread, and the Wickersham brothers took the clover away and gave it to the eagle Vlad Vladikov. Horton chased the eagle all night until the clover was dropped in a huge field of clovers. Horton searched and searched until he found the Whos in Whoville. The mayor asked everyone to make noise, and after Jojo added one last “Yop,” the Whos were heard. Horton was saved, and the kangaroos finally agreed to protect the Whos too.

summary_text: Emily Elizabeth loves holidays, and her big red dog, Clifford, loves them too. Clifford can be Santa at Christmas, blow a horn on New Year's Eve, be Emily's Valentine, and dress as an Easter Bunny. On April Fool's Day, Clifford does not trick anyone, and no one tricks him. On Thanksgiving, he gets a very big turkey. Emily says Halloween is the best holiday. Last year, she dressed as a pirate, while Clifford chose to be a ghost. At the party, the children could not guess who was inside the big ghost costume. Emily and Clifford bobbed for apples, and Clifford won an apple game. Mommy told a ghost story, but nobody was afraid because Clifford was there. Afterward, they went trick-or-treating, had little luck, and went to bed. Now Halloween is here again, and Emily will be a fairy princess. She wonders whether Clifford should be an Indian or a knight.

One day, the howler monkey asked, “Why are you so slow?” The sloth did not answer. Then other animals came and asked why the sloth was so quiet and so boring. The anteater asked too, and the jaguar asked why the sloth was so lazy. The sloth thought and thought for a long, long time. At last, the sloth said it was true that it was slow and quiet, but it was not lazy. The sloth said it liked to live in peace and do things slowly, slowly. Then the sloth yawned and said, “That’s just how I am.”

Margaret helped her make a sign with paper, a yellow marker, and flower duct tape. JoJo wrote “no lines allowed” and taped it above her bed. The lion did not return. Then a bear came, so JoJo made a new sign that said “no bears allowed.” The bear left too. After that, a tiger came from her closet. JoJo made another sign that said “no Tigers allowed,” but the tiger stayed. JoJo and the tiger looked at each other. Then JoJo showed him her alphabet book and read to him. The next day, JoJo changed the sign above her bed and was glad she did.

summary_text: On a bright spring morning, Turkey read a sign for an Easter egg hunt with a special prize. Turkey, Cow, Pig, Sheep, and Rooster wanted the eggs, but animals were not allowed. Turkey said he would wear disguises so they could try anyway. On the day of the hunt, Turkey dressed like a rabbit and hopped around the park. He found a special egg behind a rock, but a child saw him and told him to leave. Turkey tried again as a daffodil near a bench, but Mabel Mayberry almost picked him for her bouquet. Then Turkey dressed like a bumblebee and flew toward an egg on a slide, but Farmer Jake said no turkeys were allowed. Finally, the animals decided Turkey should look like a special egg. He was rolled through the hunt, but Max found him and turned him in as a giant special egg. Farmer Jake and Edna laughed, and Max and Turkey each got a prize.

summary_text: The PAW Patrol gets ready for Halloween. Skye wears a princess costume. Zuma is a pirate. Rocky is a viking. Rubble is a rock star. Chase is a superhero. Marshall is a pumpkin. Captain Turbot falls into the water, and the sail goes up. The ship starts moving out to sea, and he calls Ryder for help. Ryder says there is a simple answer. He and the pups go to the ship. Ryder finds Chickaletta at the wheel, and she is steering the ship. Then Ryder hears the moaning sound. He finds Wally the walrus asleep behind barrels. Wally ate the cookies, and his snoring made the sound. The mystery is solved. Later, everyone sees a ghostly pirate ship in the moonlight. Happy Halloween.

summary_text: Ruby Bridges is almost six years old in 1960. She does not like her old-fashioned name, but she loves her grandmother, who chose it, so she decides to live with it. Ruby enjoys her first school, where she makes friends, likes her teacher, and earns many gold stars. Then her parents tell her she must change schools. She takes a test and passes. The next morning, four white federal marshals take her to William France Elementary School. Outside, angry white people scream, and Ruby does not understand why. Inside, she meets a white principal and, the next day, Mrs. Henry, her white teacher. Ruby discovers she is the only child and the only Black person in the school. Her mother explains that a court case changed the laws so Black children could attend white schools. Ruby learns that being first helps make school fairer for all children.

summary_text: It is the night before Easter at the Healer house. Bluey and Bingo get ready for bed, and Dad and Mom say the Easter Bunny will come and will not forget them. The girls have made Easter pictures, and they each have an egg pouch at the end of their bed. Bingo sees glitter spilled on the rug, and Bluey wakes up. In the morning, the pouches are empty, but Bluey and Bingo find a box and a letter. They think the clues will show where the chocolate eggs are hidden. The clues lead them to the letter box, the kitchen, the fridge, the playroom, the backyard, the sand pit, the upstairs bathroom, and then their room again. Bluey and Bingo keep searching and help each other when they feel sad. Then Bluey sees Easter Bunny footprints. The girls follow them to Dad’s study and find that the Easter Bunny did remember them after all. They are happy and say, “Happy Easter!”

Po says the family must sweep out bad luck before the new year, so the child sweeps dirt out the back door and cleans the windows very well. Po also says not to clean on New Year’s Day, because that could sweep away good luck. Next, Po gets a bath ready and tells the child to wash hair before New Year’s Day, because washing on the holiday is bad luck. The child washes three times and helps with the baby brother too. Mama makes a whole chicken and a fish with the head and tail still on, so the family will stay together and have a good beginning and ending. She also cooks long noodles, and the child eats them without breaking them. Red and gold banners, paper cuts, and a lucky sign are put on the door, and everyone stays awake to welcome Chinese New Year’s Day.

summary_text: Parrots are green, goldfish are red, elephants are gray, and pigs are pink. Most animals have their own color, but chameleons change color where they go. One chameleon sat on a tiger’s tail and thought he could stay on a green leaf and be green forever. He climbed onto the greenest leaf. In autumn, the leaf turned yellow, and the chameleon turned yellow too. Then the leaf turned red, and he turned red. When winter winds blew the leaf from the branch, the chameleon went with it and was black in the long winter night. When spring came, he walked into the green grass and met another chameleon. He told his sad story. The older chameleon said they could stay together. They would still change color, but they would always be alike. So they stayed side by side and were green, purple, yellow, and red with white polka dots together.

summary_text: A mother fox lived with her cubs in a cozy den. In the daytime they played, roamed, hunted, and explored. At night they curled up together, and the mother told them stories. The crow began to talk, and the cheese fell down. The little fox caught it and went home. That night, she told the story to the others.

summary_text: Every spring, Rebecca Estelle planted carrots, beans, tomatoes, peas, corn, and rudabagas, but never pumpkins. When she was a girl, her family had been very poor, and she had eaten pumpkins for a whole month. After that, she never wanted to see a pumpkin again. One autumn day, a pumpkin fell from a truck and smashed in her yard. Rebecca Estelle covered it with dirt and tried to forget it. But in spring, pumpkin vines grew at the edge of her yard. She ignored them, cut them down, and shut her curtains, but the vines kept growing back. She stopped using the front door and did not look at the vines all spring and summer. Then, one autumn day, she saw that pumpkins had covered her whole yard. Rebecca Estelle decided to give them away. She made pumpkin pies and many pumpkin treats, carved jack-o-lanterns, and called the town to come. Everyone came, ate pumpkin food, and left with pumpkin gifts. Rebecca Estelle kept only a few seeds for next spring.

All was quiet in the kangaroo house. Mommy was putting baby Wyatt down for a nap, and Cammy Kangaroo was supposed to have quiet time, but she kept thinking about treats. She went to the freezer drawer, took out the ice cream, and carried it to the playroom. She ate too much before Mommy found her. Mommy told Cammy not to sneak treats because sugar can cause cavities and she needed to ask first.

The next day, Cammy looked for more sweets again. She tried the freezer, the pantry, the top of the refrigerator, daddy’s chocolate bars, and even a brownie in the microwave. Mommy kept finding her sneaking treats and moved the lock from the playroom door to the pantry door. Soon Cammy went to the dentist and learned she had four cavities. The dentist gave her a new toothbrush and floss. When Cammy got home, she found Daddy and Wyatt eating ice cream, and Mommy said the family had too many sweets and should start with a healthy dinner.

summary_text: Ariel is a young mermaid who loves exploring shipwrecks and collecting human treasures. Her father, King Triton, warns her that humans are dangerous, but Ariel is curious about their world. One night, she sees fireworks and finds Prince Eric on a ship. A storm wrecks the ship, and Ariel saves Eric after he falls into the sea. Triton destroys Ariel’s collection when he learns about Eric. Then Ursula, the sea witch, offers Ariel legs in exchange for her voice. Ariel must kiss Eric in three days. Ariel and Eric become friends, but Ursula disguises herself as Vanessa and tries to marry him. Scuttle and the animals help stop the wedding. Ariel gets her voice back, but the sun sets before she can kiss Eric. Triton gives up his freedom to save Ariel. Ariel defeats Ursula with a wrecked ship. Triton then gives Ariel the choice to become human, and she and Eric unite their two kingdoms.

summary_text: Pete the Cat could not wait for Friday because his school was having a science fair. Pete had never been a scientist before, and now he could try. His teacher put the students into groups, and Pete worked with Cali, Gus, and Squirrel. They talked about many ideas, like a mini submarine, a giant tree, and an invisible guitar. Then Gus suggested making a volcano, and everyone liked that idea. At Pete’s house, they checked a big book of experiments and gathered glue, water, newspaper, paint, a plastic bottle, vinegar, baking soda, and dish soap. Pete and Gus mixed the glue and water, while Cali and Squirrel tore newspaper strips. They made a sticky volcano, but the brown paint was really blue. They decided to keep it blue and tested the lava. The volcano erupted and made a big mess. On Friday, their blue volcano amazed the class, and glitter lava burst out at the fair. Pete said science is hard work, but a good team makes it easier.

summary_text: One morning Paddington went into the Browns’ garden with paper and pencil and made a list of the nice things about being a bear and living with the Browns. He wrote about having his own room, a warm bed, and marmalade for breakfast. He soon remembered another very nice thing: the garden. The Browns’ garden was quiet and lovely, but it took hard work to keep it nice. Mr. Brown mowed the lawn, Mrs. Brown weeded the flower beds, and Mrs. Bird helped too. Mrs. Bird suggested that Jonathan, Judy, and Paddington each have a piece of the garden. Mr. Brown agreed, and the children began their work. Paddington bought a garden book, looked at the building site, and accidentally left his marmalade jar on a platform. Builders poured concrete over it, but when the jar came back, Paddington found a way to use the broken concrete. He made a rock garden, won praise, and later received a gold star from Mr. Lionel Trug on National Garden Day.

Next he met a bear and then a wolf, and he outran them too. At last he met a fox, who asked him to come closer. The gingerbread man did, and the fox snapped him up.

His farm grows, helps many people, and Cojo’s family becomes stronger too.

summary_text: Ernestine goes camping for the first time with her aunt Jackie and her cousin Samantha after her dad says yes. After lunch, they go hiking, and Ernestine’s pack feels heavy, so she stops for water and eats some food to make it lighter. Back at camp, they eat tofu hot dogs, broccoli salad, and s’mores. Ernestine says she wants to come back next year and asks her dad about s’mores.

After that, Mary Ellen liked reading very much.

summary_text: It was the night before Easter, just before dawn. Sister and I were in bed, and our Easter baskets were on the table. We waited and hoped the Easter Bunny would come. Then the hens in the barn made a loud clatter, and I got up to see what was happening. I saw a big fuzzy rabbit with a crook in his ear. He walked on two legs and came to the house with chocolates and striped lollipops. The bunny wore a checkered vest and a bow tie. He filled our baskets with chocolates, chicks, and lots of candy. Some sweets spilled onto the floor. Then he chose eggs and hid them around the house on couches, chairs, the mantle, the bookshelf, and under the stairs. When the rooster crowed, the bunny hurried away in his cart. I read his note: “Happy Easter to all, and to all a great day.”
