Snow covers the forest, and the acorn waits in the ground. When winter ends, the snow disappears, birds build nests, and green leaves appear. In spring, the acorn sends a root down and a shoot up. It becomes a seedling with small roots and leaves. During the warm summer, sunlight helps the little sapling grow taller. As the years pass, it becomes a small tree, then a tall, strong oak with long roots and wide branches. Animals use it for shelter. Buds open into flowers, and later the tree grows tiny acorns in round cups. When autumn returns, the leaves turn yellow, red, dry, and crinkly. The acorns grow bigger, turn brown, and fall to the ground. The cycle begins again.

They went home and bought Pluto a bone.

summary_text: When little box turtle Terence hatched, his parents saw that something was missing, but they were not upset. They gave him a name and a shell that fit him just right. Terence liked his shell because it kept him dry on wet days, safe from strangers, and warm on scary nights. Terence found his old shell again, but it had changed. He and the hermit crab fixed it together. They worked on it for a long time, and the shell was finished. It was still weird, but Terence was happy because he was more than just his shell.

summary_text: Winter came, and Anna needed a new coat because her old blue one was too small. Her mother had once hoped to buy one after the war, but the stores were still empty and there was no money. So Anna’s mother used family treasures to trade for what they needed. First, she and Anna visited a farmer and traded a gold watch for wool, but they had to wait until spring. Anna visited the sheep often, asked if their wool was growing, fed them hay, and gave them hugs and Christmas gifts. In spring, the farmer sheared the sheep and gave them wool. Next, Anna’s mother traded a lamp with an old woman for yarn. Later, they dyed the yarn red with lingonberries, traded a garnet necklace for cloth, and a porcelain teapot for tailoring. At last, Anna got a beautiful red coat. On Christmas Eve, the helpers came for cake, and on Christmas Day Anna thanked the sheep.

Her classmates asked to play in her band, and she felt brave enough to perform.

By the end of summer, Wesley had created his own civilization, and when he returned to school in September, he had many friends.

summary_text: Franklin the Turtle could do many things by himself, like slide down the riverbank and use buttons and zippers. But he was afraid of small dark places, so he would not crawl into his shell. Each night, Franklin’s mother shined a flashlight into his shell and told him there was nothing to be afraid of. Franklin still thought creepy slippery things and monsters lived inside. So Franklin went out to ask for help. He met a duck, a lion, a bird, and a polar bear, but each one was afraid of something different and had something they used to feel safe. Franklin did not need their things. At last, he met his mother again. They walked home beside the pond. His mother gave him supper and a warm hug, then sent him to bed. Franklin finally crawled into his shell and said good night. Then, when no one was looking, he turned on his nightlight.

They measured the canary’s beak, the heron’s legs, the pheasant’s tail, and even the whole hummingbird. One morning, the nightingale met the inchworm and told him to measure her song. The inchworm said he could measure things, not songs. The nightingale said she would eat him for breakfast if he did not try. So the inchworm began to measure while the nightingale sang. He counted and counted until the song was very, very long and hard to measure. At the end, the inchworm forgot what he was doing and thanked the nightingale.

Mommy and Daddy said Kami had to clean her room before they could leave.
Kami did not want to clean
because her room was full of rocks, shells, feathers, toys, and other treasures she liked to collect.
While she cleaned, Kami kept putting special things into her pouch.
Then she remembered that Savannah had asked her to bring back a stuffed puppy,
and she needed to find it.
Kami looked in the shells, the closet, and under blankets.
She found Wyatt hiding under the blankets,
and he helped too.
Daddy came in
and saw the room was still messy,
so he helped Kami clean one thing at a time.
Together they made the bed
and put things away.
Kami found Savannah’s puppy in a drawer.
Her room was clean,
and she was happy.
She almost lost something in her pouch,
but she found it,
and then the family left for the party.

summary_text: Grace Campbell learns that the United States has never had a woman president, so she decides to run for president in her school election. Her teacher lets the class hold an election, but another class chooses Thomas Cobb as its candidate. Thomas is good at spelling, science, and soccer, so Grace knows she must work hard. The children learn about electoral votes and that a candidate needs 270 votes to win. Grace promises a peaceful, clean school and better lunches, while Thomas promises tutoring, soccer lessons, and fish tacos. Grace makes posters, gives speeches, hands out cupcakes, and helps improve the school. On Election Day, the states cast their votes. Thomas and Grace are very close, and only Wyoming remains. Sam gives Wyoming’s three votes to Grace because he thinks she is the best person for the job. Grace wins with 270 votes and tells the class she will become president someday.

summary_text: One day, the narrator suddenly had a problem. The narrator did not want it, ask for it, or like it, and wondered why it was there. The narrator tried to make it go away by shooting it, scolding it, and ignoring it, but nothing worked. Then the narrator became very worried. The more the narrator worried, the bigger the problem seemed to become. Hiding and disguising did not help, because the problem kept appearing everywhere. Finally, the narrator could not take it anymore and decided to face the problem. Although the narrator was afraid, the narrator tackled it and looked closely. The problem was not what the narrator had imagined. Inside it was something beautiful: an opportunity to learn, grow, be brave, and do something. Now the narrator is not afraid of problems and knows that every problem has an opportunity for something good if it is carefully examined.

summary_text: Luca is a young sea monster who lives in the ocean but dreams of seeing the land. He meets Alberto, and they discover that sea monsters become humans when they come out of the water. The friends build pretend Vespas and dream of traveling. Luca's parents worry and want him to live with his uncle, so Luca runs away to find Alberto. In the town of Portorosso, they meet Julia and join a race to win money for a real Vespa. They practice swimming, eating pasta, and riding a bike. Alberto feels left out and reveals that they are sea monsters. During the race, rain changes Alberto, and Luca rescues him. Massimo accepts the boys, and they win because they cross the finish line. Alberto sells the Vespa so Luca can go to school. Alberto stays with Massimo, and the friends keep their happy memories and friendship.

summary_text: Look up at the sky at night and you may see the moon. Sometimes it is big and round, called a full moon. Sometimes only part of it shows, like a crescent moon or a quarter moon. The moon seems to change, but it really does not change shape. It changes because it goes around Earth. As it moves, we see more of the lighted half or less of it. This is called waxing when the moon grows bigger and waning when it gets smaller. Half of the moon is always lit by the sun. The moon goes through phases in the same order again and again: new moon, crescent, first quarter, full moon, third quarter, crescent, and back to new moon. A new moon means we cannot see it. A few nights later, a crescent appears, then the moon grows until it is full, and after that it gets smaller again.

summary_text: When summer began, Wallace went west because his parents wanted him to rest and calm his wild imagination. He rode a westbound train to visit Aunt Fern, but a group of Cowboys captured him and took him to their Cow Camp instead. The cattle boss said they needed a new Cowboy because the old one had quit, and Wallace agreed to help. He wrote Aunt Fern a note to tell her where he was. That night he got new clothes and looked like a Wrangler, but he learned that being a cowboy meant more than wearing boots and a hat. Over the next days, he learned roping, riding, and making fire with sticks. Soon everyone said Wallace was a first-rate cowhand. When the roundup was over, Aunt Fern invited him and the Cowboys to a barbecue. While they were eating, the cattle began to stamp and a stampede started. Wallace found a tablecloth on the ground and spun it like a lasso. The cattle ran away, and the Cowboys cheered and called him a true Buckaroo.

summary_text: The story begins with a pilot who, when he was six years old, drew his first picture: a snake with an elephant inside it. He showed it to grown-ups, but they thought it was a hat. He drew another picture, but the grown-ups did not care. So he stopped drawing and became a pilot. One day his plane crashed in the Sahara desert, and the next morning he heard a small voice asking, “Draw me a sheep, please.” It was the little prince, a boy with golden hair. The pilot first showed him the snake picture, then drew several sheep until the little prince liked one that was inside a box. Over the next days, the little prince told him about his tiny planet, the baobabs, his flower, and his journey through four small planets. He met a king, a man who counted stars, a lamplighter, and a writer. On Earth he met a snake, a rose garden, and a fox. The fox taught him that a tamed friend becomes special. At the end, the little prince went back to the snake and left his body behind so he could return home to his flower and star.

summary_text: Leonardo loves numbers and enjoys counting everything around him. At school, he solves a math problem quickly, but his teacher becomes angry when Leonardo daydreams about birds and calls him a blockhead. Leonardo feels hurt and leaves. His father sends him to Africa, where Alfredo tells him to study what makes him happy. Leonardo learns Hindu-Arabic numerals, fractions, geometry, division, and subtraction during his travels. He writes about a rabbit puzzle and discovers a pattern: each number comes from adding the two numbers before it. Later, people in Pisa still make fun of his ideas. Alfredo helps Leonardo notice the same numbers in flowers, starfish, apples, and square shapes. Leonardo draws a spiral using the pattern. He realizes that Mother Nature uses these numbers in many places, so he no longer feels ashamed of being called Blockhead.

Then Skippy John Jones went back to his room, wrapped in his blankie, talking to his bobble head and still thinking Chihuahua.

summary_text: After World War II, Momo fuku Ando walked home through the ruins of Osaka, Japan. He saw a long line of hungry people waiting in the cold for ramen soup, and he could not forget them. He decided that food would be his life’s work. Over the next years, he made salt, dried fish, and nutritious food for sick people. Then one business deal failed, and he became poor again. He dreamed of a new kind of ramen that would be tasty, healthy, and easy to make. In his backyard shed, he mixed and tested flour, salt, water, eggs, milk, spinach, soup, and many cooking methods, but the noodles kept failing. One night he watched his wife make tempura and saw how hot oil made tiny holes in batter. He fried his noodles, then added hot water. At last, instant ramen worked. Ando and his family made and sold it, and many people were able to eat it.

summary_text: After World War II ended, Momo fuku Ando walked home through the ruins of Osaka, Japan. He saw a long line of hungry people waiting in the cold for ramen soup. Food was scarce because of bad harvests, rationing, and war, and many poor people and orphans struggled to eat. Ando could not stop thinking about them. He decided to make food his life’s work and began creating salt, dried fish, and nutritious food for sick people. For more than 10 years, he kept working. After one business failed, he was poor again and thought about how families needed noodles that were cheap, filling, and easy to make. He experimented with ingredients and methods many times, but the noodles kept failing. Then, after watching his wife make tempura, he realized frying created tiny holes. He fried the noodles, dried them, and found that hot water made them soft and tasty. After a year, he invented instant Ramen and sold it to many people.

summary_text: At the end of a road by a glittering stream stood a house where 12 children were born and grew up. They learned to crawl in the front hall, stood on the wooden stairs for pictures, and had their heights marked on the wall. They played, lied about the cat, and were scolded. In the serious room, men were comforted and the organ was played. The children read books about planets and stars, dreamed of Mars, kept secrets, and collected toys, feathers, bones, and movie stars. They worked hard, too. They milked the cows in the barn, fed calves, cleaned stalls, fished in the stream, picked apples, and brought mud into the house. They helped their mother, set the table, cared for a sick younger child, and sewed and darned their clothes. Spring always came, and rain leaked through the roof. As the children grew up and left, the youngest one finally went away too. Then the house leaned, rotted, and slowly fell apart.

The pranksters agreed to slow down in town, and everyone enjoyed the day together.

Little Pumpkin used a flashlight trick to scare Gerard, but then she was alone. At Bat Belfry, she got scared by a vampire, bats, and spiders, so she hurried home through the oak tree door. Back on her porch, she hugged her parents, ate a maple chocolate cluster, and agreed to stay close to them while they read a spooky Halloween book together.

summary_text: One morning, Andy left for school, and the toys had the room to themselves. Woody said the coast was clear and asked about a game called sardines. He explained that one toy hides, and the others look for that toy. When they find the hider, they hide there too, until the last toy is still looking in the next game. The toys understood and began to play. They guessed a number, and Ham was chosen to be it. Woody told everyone to close their eyes and count to 25 while Ham hid. Ham looked in Andy’s toy chest and under the bed, but those places seemed too easy or too scary. At the last moment, he climbed into an old lunch box and shut the lid. Woody found him first and climbed in. Jesse found them next and squeezed in too. Then more and more toys came, and the lunch box got fuller and fuller until every toy was packed inside. Rex could not fit, so Woody ended the game and sent everyone out. After that, the toys played sardines with small hiding places.

summary_text: Moana of Montenui loved the ocean. She liked Grandma Tala’s stories, especially the one about Maui, who stole the heart of Teiti and upset nature. Moana’s father, Chief Tui, said the ocean was dangerous, so people could not sail past the reef. But Moana felt close to the ocean. The ocean gave her a special gift, and Grandma Tala picked it up and said it was the heart of Teiti. When Moana was 16, Grandma Tala showed her hidden canoes and told her it was time to learn who she was meant to be. Grandma Tala asked Moana to find Maui and restore the heart. Moana set sail with the heart in her necklace. A storm came, and she washed up on an island where she met Maui. Maui took her boat, but the ocean made sure Moana went with him. Maui said he would help if Moana helped him find his magic fish hook. They faced the Kakamura and went into Lowa Tha. Moana tricked Tola, the crab monster, and got the fish hook back. Maui taught Moana to wayfind by using the sun, stars, moon, and ocean current. Grandma Tala’s spirit came back and told Moana to know who she was meant to be. At Teiti, Moana gave the heart to Teay, who became Teiti again. The world was balanced, and Moana returned home as a daughter, a leader, and a wayfinder.

summary_text: Princess Merida is late, and the royal family waits. Her mother, the queen, teaches her to be a princess and shows her how to play the harp, but Merida is bored and wants to play with her sword. The queen says Merida must marry the son of a lord. Merida is upset when she gets ready to meet the lords’ sons in a fancy gown. The young lords shoot arrows at a target, and the best shooter will marry the princess. Merida joins the game and wins, so no one can marry her. The queen is angry, and Merida cuts the family tapestry and runs away. She meets a witch and asks for help. The witch makes a spell cake, and when the queen eats it, she turns into a bear. Merida and her mother look for the witch, go fishing, and meet a mean bear. They return to the castle, where Merida tries to help her mother and fix the torn tapestry. The queen protects Merida, they fight the bear, and the spell breaks. The queen becomes human again, and Merida and her mother hug.

summary_text: Sadie Sprocket wanted to travel far into space and go to Mars, so she read every book about space and learned all she could. She said no one had been to Mars and decided she would be the first. Sadie drew a map, planned a long trip, and interviewed a crew. Then she and her team searched a junkyard for parts and built a rocket ship that was sturdy, safe, and fast. After testing every switch, they launched with friends, family, and reporters watching. The trip took 100 days, and the crew spent the time reading, making food, and tracking the ship’s altitude. When they reached Mars, Sadie chose a place to land on level sand. Sadie and her crew dug it free, fixed the wires, restored power, and blasted off. They returned home, became famous, and Sadie said she might next travel to Neptune, but she would need a bigger rocket.

summary_text: Trev wants to protect his mom and sisters, especially from his stepdad. When the stepdad leaves, he threatens Trev’s mom, and Trev worries even more when he hears that the stepdad is coming back. Trev does not want to stay scared, so he decides to take action and learn how to box. He thinks that if he can throw hands and build himself up, nobody will be able to knock him down. Their advice does not feel useful to Trev, because he also feels threatened by his sister’s disrespectful boyfriend. Trev is left facing a hard choice about how to use his hands and what kind of future he wants.

summary_text: Katie Caboose rode at the very back of a long train. She did not like the smoke, bumps, loud noises, dark tunnels, high mountain tracks, or deep rocky places. Katie wished she could be a tree, a house, or a quiet little cabin. One night, a small switchman’s shack told Katie that it wished it could be a caboose because Katie had the best life. Katie began to feel happier about being herself. Soon, a train took her away again. On a hot mountain climb, the train gave a big jump, and Katie’s old coupling bolt broke. Katie flew loose down the track. She went faster and faster and flew over the treetops. Two tall spruce trees caught her and held her safely. A train came looking with a crane and a bright light, but it did not see Katie. She stayed in the trees with squirrels and birds. At last, Katie was free and loved her new home.

summary_text: Stellaluna was a baby fruit bat who lived with her mother in a warm forest. One night an owl attacked the bats. Mother bat was hurt, and baby Stellaluna fell into the dark forest. She held on to a twig, but by morning she fell again and landed in a bird nest. Three baby birds lived there: Flap, Flitter, and Pip. Their mama fed them bugs, and Stellaluna was very hungry, so she ate bugs too. She learned to stay awake in the day and sleep at night, but she still liked to hang by her feet. The bird mama was upset and told Stellaluna to obey the rules. Later, Stellaluna learned to fly with the birds, but she got lost in the dark. Then she met other bats and found her own mother. The bats showed her fruit, and Stellaluna was happy. At last, Stellaluna brought the birds to meet the bats, and they all stayed friends even though they were different.

summary_text: The story begins by showing how huge numbers can be hard to imagine. It explains that one million kids standing on each other’s shoulders would be taller than buildings and mountains, and that counting to one million would take about 23 days. Then it asks about a billion and a trillion, and the book gives more big comparisons, like a billion kids reaching past the moon and a trillion kids reaching far beyond the moon and close to Saturn’s rings. The story says that the easiest way to understand giant numbers is to start with ten. It uses apples to show how ten becomes one hundred, then one thousand, then ten thousand, then one hundred thousand, and finally one million apples in a truck. After that, the story moves to a Crayola crayon factory, where millions of crayons are made every year. Workers melt wax, add color, fill molds, wrap crayons, pack boxes, and send them to kids all over the world.

He began trying to be happy and kind. He still made mistakes, but he also said please and thank you, smiled, and held doors open. He learned that trying to change could make him feel good, and others began to see that he was not so bad anymore.

They danced until night came. Papa got tired. Then mama and papa kissed baby and put him to bed, with dance dreams in his head.

Bats went into a cave, caterpillars closed their cocoons, and Hedgehog said, “See you in Spring,” before going into his warm winter home. Then snow came and covered the forest. Mama said snow was like a special secret and told him to enjoy it while it was there. Little Owl listened to the quiet forest and heard a tiny drip from an icicle.

summary_text: One windy afternoon, a little old lady left her Cottage and walked into the forest to gather herbs, spices, nuts, and seeds. It grew dark on the way home. On the path, she met two big shoes that went “clump clump,” then a pair of pants that went “wiggle wiggle,” then a shirt that went “shake shake.” She kept walking and found two white gloves that went “clap clap” and a tall black hat that went “nod nod.” Near her Cottage, she saw a very big orange pumpkin head that went “boo boo.” The little old lady ran home and locked her door. Inside, she sat by the fire until there was a knock on the door. She opened it and saw all the things again, standing together. She was not afraid. She spoke to the pumpkin head, and it looked happier. The next morning, she saw the clothes and pumpkin head in her garden, and they scared the crows away.

summary_text: A little butterfly wants to reach a group of migrating butterflies and find the flowers, but the trip is 200 miles long. The butterfly worries about flying so far and asks if it can take a plane, a hot air balloon, or a blip, but the answer is no. It remembers life as a caterpillar, when it built a chrysalis, waited, and then started the journey with friends. Now it is lost and alone, and it fears storms and animals like snakes, birds, dragonflies, frogs, and spiders. A whale also appears, and the butterfly jokes about living in its stomach, but the whale spits it out. The butterfly keeps hearing, “Keep trying,” and starts flying again. It travels mile by mile, though wind blows it back and it feels discouraged. At last, after 200 miles, it reaches the flowers and says it can do many things when it believes in itself. Then it is told to eat up before going dormant for winter.

summary_text: A few days before Halloween, a shopkeeper put pumpkins on the shelves outside a little shop in a big city. A girl came to look at them. She picked up one pumpkin and carried it away. The other pumpkins worried about their friend, then saw him across the street, high up as a Jacko Lantern. He had triangle eyes, a nose, and a big smile. The pumpkins were happy for him and dreamed that they might become jackolanterns too. Then one pumpkin saw something sad. He had lost his stem and was now just stumpkin, a stemless pumpkin with a little stump. Still, stumpkin was a nice pumpkin, orange like a traffic cone and round like a basketball. More people came over the next days. Some pumpkins left and some stayed. Stumpkin waited for a home. A cat sat on his top, and then a baby chose him, but a bad dog ruined it. On Halloween night, the shop closed, and the shopkeeper carried stumpkin away. He did not get a window, but he did already have a home, and that made him very happy.

summary_text: In a warm forest, Mother Bat had a tiny baby bat named Stellaluna. One night, an owl attacked Mother Bat while she was flying for fruit. Stellaluna fell into the forest and then into a bird nest where three baby birds lived: Pip, Flitter, and Flap. Stellaluna was hungry, but she did not want the bugs Mama Bird brought. At last she ate a grasshopper. She tried to live like the birds. She stayed awake in the day, slept at night, and ate bugs. She still liked to hang by her feet. Mama Bird made her follow the nest rules. When the babies grew, they learned to fly. Stellaluna flew too, but she was clumsy and got lost after flying far away. In the dark, she met other bats and found her real mother. Mother Bat took her to eat fruit and fly at night. Later, Stellaluna visited the birds, and the birds and bats learned they were different, but still friends.

summary_text: Duck knocked on Hippo’s door and asked him to walk in the rain. Duck twirled her umbrella and said, “It’s spring, spring, spring!” Hippo was worried about the weather, but Duck said he could come if he shared her umbrella. Hippo put on his big rubber boots and went outside. At first, there was no room for Hippo. He tried walking in front of Duck, and then behind her, but that did not work. Then Duck stood on Hippo’s feet while Hippo held the umbrella, and that worked just fine. They jumped in puddles, splashed through mud, and dropped a stick into the creek. Duck wanted to sail down the creek, so Hippo helped her into the water. Again, there was no room for Hippo, so Duck sat on Hippo’s lap. They swirled around boulders and a crocodile, then twirled into a pond. Duck could not find Hippo, but Hippo was under her, and Duck was sitting on his head. At the end, they went home, shared the umbrella again, and Hippo invited Duck in for tea.

summary_text: Hercules Beal is starting seventh grade at a new environmental sciences academy. Hercules wants a dog, and he unexpectedly finds Mindy, a brave brown-and-white dog who protects him from Achilles. At school, a strict retired Marine lieutenant colonel assigns Hercules a project about the twelve labors of the mythical Hercules. Hercules researches the first labor, capturing the Nemean lion, and realizes that a dangerous problem near his home may be its modern equivalent. Eleven ugly cats are living in an abandoned summer house and threatening Mindy and local birds. With Ellie, Henry, and Ty, Hercules tries to drive the cats out and board up the house. He is injured but finishes the job. When he meets the scarred one-eyed cat afterward, she unexpectedly shows affection, and Hercules feels some of his deep sadness begin to loosen.

summary_text: The story tells about being new. When someone is new, they can look, see, peer, touch, taste, and hear. They may doze, nap, and snooze because being new can make them sleepy. A new baby can fit in tiny spots, get carried a lot, wear little baby shoes, and open wide to yell. Sometimes new babies make funny smells and feel mad, scared, or blue. Then they take baths, wash off the grime, and get cuddled. They also play games like peekaboo. Every day they stretch and grow and learn new things. Soon they are not new anymore, but later they can be new again in new places, with new games, new friends, and new family members. They try new things, meet new folks, and pick new favorites. The story ends by saying it is okay not to know what to do, because being new can be exciting and loved.

She runs out the back door. Then the three dinosaurs rush back, but Goldilocks is already gone. The story ends with the dinosaurs disappointed and the house still needing the back door locked.

He moved to a quieter place, but Rabbit soon asked him to make ice sculptures. Tortoise said no again and packed up. Then Squirrel invited him to a snowball fight, and Tortoise got angry because he still wanted to sleep. He moved higher and higher to find a quiet place, but winter kept following him. At last, Tortoise found a flat piece of wood behind a small tree. When he sat down, he was sent sliding on a sled and then across the ice. He smiled, giggled, and joined his friends skating, sliding, and spinning all night. By the end, Tortoise saw that winter could be fun too.

summary_text: Every year, Santa prepared for his Christmas ride, but he often worked slowly and caused a last-minute rush. Muckle, an elf, believed Santa was too old-fashioned and wasted time. Afterward, the elves accepted Santa’s delays because they understood that his careful way was normal and important.

The child gave him a stuffed monster, and Gabe snuffled it. The child laughed, yawned, and fell asleep.

Then he heard his parents calling. They found him, hugged him, and took him home. Franklin said he was sorry and promised never to go into the woods alone again.

summary_text: Audrey Fay Hendrix lived in Birmingham with her Mama C, Daddy, and family. When Mike, also called Martin or Dr. King, visited, the family served him a big meal, and the grown-ups talked about segregation laws that kept black and white people apart. Audrey spoke up because she wanted to eat inside Newberries, sit downstairs at the Alabama, and use the same schools and stores as white children. Mama told her to hush, but Audrey kept listening to meetings at Fred’s church, where people sang, shared stories, and heard Mike say segregation was wrong. Mike asked people to protest and fill the jails, but many adults were afraid. Then Jim said children should go instead. Audrey said she wanted to go to jail, and her parents let her join the protest. She marched from 16th Street Baptist Church, was arrested, and spent days in juvenile hall with hard beds, little food, and strict guards. After more children were arrested, the jails filled up, the protests worked, and Birmingham later ended segregation laws.

summary_text: Leila was happy that Ramadan was starting, because for the first time her mom said she could fast all month. The next morning, she woke up before sunrise, ate pancakes, and prayed with her mom before school. Her mom gave her a note for Mrs. Penworth, but Leila forgot to hand it over. On the bus and in class, she worried that no one knew about Ramadan. At lunchtime, she did not eat and felt hungry while other children shared food. She left the cafeteria and went to the library, where Mrs. Carmen listened to her. Leila explained that she was fasting and missed her friends, Hen and Ishrat. Mrs. Carmen told her to write her thoughts down, so Leila wrote a note and a poem about Ramadan for Mrs. Penworth and gave them to her. The next day, Mrs. Penworth praised her poem, said fasting was special, and invited her to share it with the class and spend lunch in the library.

summary_text: At night, fireflies danced in the dark. In the morning, the Sun came up, and a friendly ladybug found some aphids for breakfast. Then a grouchy ladybug flew in and wanted the aphids too. The two ladybugs argued, and the grouchy one said it would fight anyone. So the grouchy ladybug went off to look for bigger and bigger animals. At 6 o'clock it met a yellowjacket. At 7 o'clock it met a stag beetle. At 8 o'clock it met a praying mantis. At 9 o'clock it met a sparrow. At 10 o'clock it met a lobster. Then it met a skunk, a bull, a snake, a hyena, a gorilla, and an elephant. Each time, the other animal was bigger or stronger, and the grouchy ladybug flew away. At 5:15 it met a whale and held on to its tail. The whale slapped it across the sea and land. At 6 o'clock the grouchy ladybug came back home. The friendly ladybug still had aphids left, and the tired grouchy ladybug thanked it. Then the fireflies woke up and danced around the moon.

The next day, Josh has a big store tantrum, but Mum helps him breathe and throw away his anger. She says it is fine to be angry, but anger should not ruin the day.

summary_text: Old man Winter saw his big bear friend in the countryside and softly said, “Sleep big bear sleep.” But big bear did not hear well. He thought he heard, “Drive a jeep, big bear drive a jeep,” so he drove a jeep on a road south of town. Then old man Winter said it again, but bear thought he heard, “Sweep big bear sweep.” He swept a house down the street. Next he thought he heard, “Leap big bear leap,” and he played leapfrog with a frog. After that, he thought he heard, “Dive deep big bear dive deep,” so he swam in a clear blue lake and got very tired. Then he thought he heard, “Climb a mountain steep big bear steep,” and he climbed to the top of a mountain. At last old man Winter told him it was winter time and to go to bed. Big bear went to his cozy den, put on his pjs, blew out the light, and said, “Good night.”

summary_text: Ping was a boy in China who loved flowers. Whatever he planted grew into beautiful flowers, bushes, or trees. The old emperor loved flowers, too, and needed to choose the next emperor. He gave every child a special seed and said the child with the best plant after one year would become the successor. Ping carefully planted his seed, watered it every day, and moved it to a bigger pot with better soil. Still, nothing grew. When spring came, the other children brought big, beautiful plants to the palace. Ping felt ashamed, but his father told him that doing his best was good enough. Ping brought his empty pot. The emperor asked what happened, and Ping told the truth. Then the emperor smiled. He had cooked all the seeds, so none could grow. Ping was the only child who brought the truth. Because Ping was brave and honest, the emperor gave him the kingdom and made him emperor.

In the kitchen, there were five more wacky things. The child was late for school and saw six more wrong things, then seven more. At school, the child saw eight wrong things and told the others. The child ran to Miss Bass and said there were nine things wrong in her class. Everyone said nothing was wrong, but the child kept seeing more wacky things. At the end, the child counted all the wacky things and got rid of the shoe on the wall.

summary_text: At sunrise in the Bayou, Tiana was a frog and had finished building a raft to take herself and Prince Naveen back to New Orleans. Naveen sat in the back and played his ukulele. A big alligator came near them, and Tiana and Naveen were scared. The alligator was friendly. His name was Louis, and he loved jazz and played trumpet. Louis told Tiana and Naveen that Mama Odie knew magic and could help them become human again. He took them to see her. On the way, a fly came by, and Tiana and Naveen got tangled while trying to catch it. The fly was Ray, a kind firefly, and he helped free them. Ray led them through the Misty Bayou with light from his firefly family. Then frog hunters caught Tiana and Naveen. Ray flew into a hunter’s nose, and Naveen got away. Naveen saw Tiana in a cage, grabbed the boat with his tongue, and rescued her. Afterward, Tiana cooked swamp gumbo, and Naveen learned to mince mushrooms. Later, Louis played trumpet, Naveen asked Tiana to dance, and they twirled under the light of Evangeline, the evening star.

counted down from 10,

Everyone cheers and all the monsters do the Halloween Hustle together.

The child tried to scrub the dye off, but then woke up. It was Easter morning, and Clifford looked normal again. summary_text: Valuable things disappeared from homes in Gotham City. Batman found a bird feather at every crime scene, so he studied the clues with Bruce Wayne. Alfred showed him a report saying that birds were acting strangely, and some were missing. Then Batman and Alfred saw a vulture flying away with an umbrella full of valuables, including Batman's cell phone. The phone had a tracker, so Batman followed the birds to a skyscraper. The birds carried stolen things into the Penguin's Iceberg Lounge. The Penguin had trained them to steal and made them attack Batman. Batman turned on a fire alarm, and cold sprinklers freed the birds from the Penguin's control. The birds flew away. The Penguin tried to escape in a rocket umbrella, but Batman threw a freeze capsule and covered him with frost. Commissioner Gordon and the police arrested the Penguin because Batman had found evidence.

summary_text: In November, the Earth grows quiet and makes a white, silent winter bed for flowers and small creatures. summary_text: Jangles is a giant trout who lives in Big Lake. His crooked jaw is covered with shiny lures and rusty hooks, so they clink when he swims. On the way back, the child tricks Jangles and ties him upside down. Jangles asks to be freed and says he is more than a fish—he is a storyteller. The child realizes doing what is right matters more than proving the catch, so he lets Jangles go. Later, Dad gives him a tackle box full of hooks and lures as proof of the amazing adventure.

summary_text: Mr. Kean was the principal of a school he loved very much. Every morning he walked through the halls and watched the children learn shapes, colors, numbers, and letters. He saw them read, write, draw, paint, and make things like dinosaurs, forts, and pyramids. Tilly lived nearby with her parents, her brother, and her dog Beans. On school days, she went to school, and on weekends she climbed her tree, walked Beans, and played with her brother. Mr. Kean kept saying it was a fine fine school, so he asked for school on Saturdays, then Sundays, then holidays, and then all summer too. Tilly finally told him that Beans, her brother, and even she had not learned some important things at home. Mr. Kean understood. He said school would not happen on weekends, holidays, or in summer. Everyone cheered, and the town said learning is important, but time with family is important too.

Then his mom takes him to a cooking contest, where Judge Gustaf tastes Milo’s cookies and names him the winner. Milo learns that never giving up is the secret ingredient.

Charlie Brown chooses a tiny green tree for the play, but the children laugh at it. Linus then tells everyone about the shepherds, the angel, and the birth of Christ. Charlie Brown understands that Christmas is not about greed. He takes the tree outside and tries to decorate it, but a heavy ornament makes it fall over. After Charlie Brown leaves, Linus and the other children decorate the little tree. When Charlie Brown returns, the tree is beautiful. His friends wish him Merry Christmas and sing carols with him. Charlie Brown feels happy and expects the best Christmas ever.

In the kitchen, a space-age robotic machine cooks the meals and washes the dishes. In the living room, the chairs, table, and sofa spin, and trampolines lead to a big ball pit. In the bathroom, a scrub-a-dub-dub belt washes him clean. In the bedroom, he sleeps high in a tower with glass all around. Then he adds more special rooms: an art room with a giant roll of paper, a flying room that lets him float and fly, a racetrack room with go-karts, a fish tank room for swimming, and a plexiglass playroom that can detach and fly with jets. He says his house will stand out as the best on the street.

summary_text: Sally and the narrator had a big job to do. The snow was deep, and their mother went to town for the day, saying someone had to clean it away. While they worked, the Cat in the Hat came to the house. Sally warned the narrator not to trust him because he had played bad tricks before. The cat said he only wanted to get out of the snow, but he went inside and started making trouble. The narrator found him eating cake in the tub, with the water running. The narrator told the cat to leave because there was work to do. When the water was shut off, a pink ring was left in the tub, and then Mother’s white dress was spotted. The cat used a wall to clean the dress, but the wall got dirty too. Then he used shoes, a rug, and a bed to clean more spots, but each thing became messy. Finally, the cat called in more help from his hat, and many little cats came to clean the snow. At last, the house and yard were clean again.

summary_text: Old Man Winter sat on a storm cloud in the countryside and whispered to Big Bear, “Sleep, Big Bear, sleep.” But Big Bear did not hear well. In his den in the Dell, he thought he heard, “Drive a Jeep!” So Big Bear drove a Jeep south of town. After that, Old Man Winter whispered again, but Big Bear thought he heard, “Sweep Big Bear sweep.” Big Bear swept a house room by room. Then he heard, “Leap Big Bear leap,” and he played leapfrog with a frog. Next, he heard, “Dive deep Big Bear dive deep,” so he dove into Clear Blue Lake and swam to shore, very tired. Finally, he heard, “Climb a mountain steep Big Bear steep,” and he trudged to the mountaintop. At last Old Man Winter told him it was winter time and he should go to bed. Big Bear went back to his cozy den, put on his PJs, blew out the light, and said, “good night.”

summary_text: On January 1st, Squirrel hangs up her new nut calendar and hears on the radio that it is a good day to make a resolution. He says he resolved to teach others how to read, and he will teach Skunk when she is well. Squirrel runs to visit Skunk, who is sick in bed and wishes she could learn to read. To cheer Skunk up, Squirrel plays “Hide and Skunk,” and Skunk laughs until Dr. Owl says she is feeling better. On the way to the Hidey Hole Diner, Squirrel helps Mole and Turtle find a good place for their garden by Wild Cat Creek. At the diner, she helps Porcupine laugh. Finally, Rabbit tells Squirrel that her actions show her resolution: she has been helping others every day. Squirrel is happy because she has made her first resolution.

summary_text: A little girl and her dog, Pancho, live in a city that sings with music and many sounds. They dance past the café, bakery, bookstore, market, and park, moving with the rhythm of radios, cars, bicycles, carts, drums, and barking dogs. One day, the city suddenly sounds wrong and then becomes silent. The girl feels her heart beating fast, but she calms Pancho and says they need to go to Mom. Soon the city has a new rhythm, with sirens, helicopters, and people rushing to help. The girl and Pancho find Pelusa, the baker’s dog, crying alone. They want to reunite Pelusa with her family. At the flower shop, Mom is not there at first, but then she hugs them. Together they join firefighters, rescuers, neighbors, and expert dogs to find Don Polo, the baker. Everyone sings, and the city’s hopeful music grows. In the end, Mom tucks them in, and the next morning the city sings and they dance again.

summary_text: Hank was a cactus living in a pot by a window that looked out at the hot desert. He liked quiet and wanted to be left alone. Rosie the Tumbleweed came by and said hello, but Hank ignored her. A tortoise, a jack rabbit, a coyote, a cowboy, a lizard, and an owl all passed by too. Hank yelled at each one and told them to go away. The owl would not give him a hug, and Hank began to feel lonely. The next morning, he felt sad inside. Then the wind blew an old cup onto Hank’s face, and he could not get it off by himself. Rosie came back and knocked the cup off for him. Hank felt sorry for being rude, so he grew a flower for Rosie. When Rosie returned, Hank gave her the flower. Rosie was so happy that she hugged him. Hank and Rosie got stuck together, but they did not mind, because it was better than being alone.

summary_text: Little Nick went to the zoo with his parents and saw a koala. He wanted to take the koala home, but his mother said no because the koala had a mother and father who would be sad. Nick stomped, shouted, and felt very angry. A monkey told him to take deep breaths and blow slowly. Nick tried, but he still felt upset. The monkey suggested counting to ten, and a kangaroo suggested exercising by jumping, doing sit-ups, or squats. Then Nick met a parrot who explained that people can handle anger by counting, talking, or writing an apology letter. Nick thought carefully and understood that the koala was wild and should stay with its family. He breathed, counted, and exercised again. Then he apologized to his mother. She was proud, hugged him, and offered to buy him a new toy. The story says to express anger safely so it does not hurt others or ruin their day.

summary_text: William lived in a small village in Malawi where there were no lights and very little money. Later, he found a library with science books and learned how engines and radios worked. One picture showed a windmill that could make electricity and pump water. William decided to build his own “electric wind.” He collected parts from a junkyard and built a machine with help from his cousin Jeffrey and his friend Gilbert. When the wind blew, the blades turned and a bulb lit up. Later, he used his windmill to power lights and pump water for his family.

summary_text:
Henry Brown was a slave, so he did not know his birthday. He worked with his brothers and sisters in the master’s house. One day, the master called Henry and his mother upstairs. Henry hoped he might be freed, but instead the master gave Henry to his son and told him to obey and never lie. Henry then watched a bird fly freely and said goodbye to his family.

Henry went to work in a factory for his new master. There he met Nancy, and they later married when both masters agreed. They had children, but Nancy worried their master might sell them. Soon Henry learned that Nancy and the children had been sold at the slave market. He searched for them and saw them taken away. After that, Henry was lonely and stopped singing. Many weeks later, Henry decided to escape. With help from James and Dr. Smith, he had himself mailed in a crate to Philadelphia. After a hard trip, the box was opened, and Henry was welcomed to freedom on March 30, 1849.

summary_text: The story is about a cheese who calls himself The Big Cheese. He says he is the biggest and most impressive cheddar around, and he likes being loud, noticed, and praised. He was not always famous. He grew up on a crowded platter in a tiny kitchen as a small, plain kurd. He wanted to become important, so he worked hard to get attention and stayed only with things he already did well. Then Wedge came to town. Wedge was quiet, shy, and very different from him. One summer, the Tiny Village held an all-day cheese cathlon. The Big Cheese won the foot race many times before, but this year Wedge beat him. Wedge also won chess, hat making, sheep hurting, bread buttering, and bird calling. At the end, Wedge was named first place winner. After losing, The Big Cheese felt calm and went home. He later talked with Wedge and learned that losing can teach empathy, humility, and perspective.

When people got closer, they saw the tiny kakamura jumping around on decks made from many found objects. The creatures wore coconut shells on their bodies and painted faces on the shells. Their boat split into many boats and surrounded the voyagers. Spears fell on the men’s canoe, drums sounded loudly, and kakamura warriors jumped aboard with sharp claws and scary faces. They took the treasures and left the boat broken. The voyagers went home shaken and warned others, but later travelers were also attacked.

summary_text: On a sunny weekend, Otto the bulldog wanted to play tag with his friend Dennis, but Dennis was busy researching the Statue of Liberty for a family road trip. Dennis needed pictures and facts for his report. Otto found Smidge, a tiny kitten, and they decided to help. They took Dennis’s notes and camera and rode a train to New York City. On the way, they learned that the Statue of Liberty was a gift from France, was made of copper, and turned green over time. In New York, they rode a ferry to Liberty Island and took many pictures. Mr. Ratton and Mrs. Heights showed them the broken chain, the tablet with July 4, 1776, the seven rays on the crown, and the gold torch. Otto and Smidge rushed home with the pictures. A few days later, Dennis said the report helped his parents add the Statue of Liberty to the summer road trip.

Before he flew away, he thanked Rudolph, Dasher, Dancer, Prancer, Vixen, Comet, Cupid, Donner, and Blitzen, and wished everyone Merry Christmas.

summary_text: Miss Frizzle showed the class a film strip about the human body, and the children knew another strange adventure was coming. The next day, she made them do an experiment and then took them on a class trip to the Science Museum to see how food gives the body energy. They rode in the old school bus and stopped at a park for lunch. When it was time to leave, Arnold was still at the picnic table eating cheesy wheezys, so he stayed behind. Miss Frizzle pressed a strange button, and the bus began shrinking and spinning. The class landed inside a human body and traveled down the esophagus into the stomach, then into the small intestine. Miss Frizzle showed them how food moves into the blood through tiny villi. The children rode red blood cells through the blood, into the heart, up to the brain, and along the nerves and muscles. At the end, they were blown back to school through Arnold’s nose.

summary_text: Kevin was a koala who liked to stay high in his tree. He liked to cling, nap, and eat leaves. He thought the ground below was too fast, too loud, and too strange, so he did not want to try new things. One day Wombat called up to him and asked him to come down and play. Then Ruse and the dingos also invited him. Kevin said no and stayed in his tree. Days and weeks passed, and Kevin kept still while the others played below. Then one day he heard a tapping sound and saw a crowd under the tree. They told him to jump and said they would catch him. Kevin was scared and said he could not let go. But then the tree came down with a crash. Kevin loosened his paws one by one and found that he felt light, safe, and happy. Wombat held out a paw, Dingo asked him to play, and Kevin said yes. After that, Kevin was ready to try something new.

summary_text: Deep in a birch forest lived the terrible Baba Yaga, who was always hungry and lived in a hut made of bones. Far away, Vasilisa lived with her mean stepmother and two cruel stepsisters after her father died. Vasilisa worked hard, but her mother had left her a doll that could talk and give advice, and it comforted her. When the stepmother used magic to put out the house light, she sent Vasilisa to Baba Yaga to borrow a flame. Vasilisa walked through the forest and reached Baba Yaga’s bone fence and hut. Baba Yaga made her stay and do many hard jobs. Each day Vasilisa’s doll helped her finish the work, while Vasilisa cooked big meals for Baba Yaga. At last Baba Yaga asked how she had done everything, and Vasilisa said it was by her mother’s love. Baba Yaga sent her home with a burning skull. The skull burned up the stepmother and stepsisters, and Vasilisa went to live with a kind old woman. Later her beautiful cloth reached the tzar, who married Vasilisa.

summary_text: The story asks what it would be like to wake up with animal hair instead of human hair. It first talks about polar bear hair, which has two layers and keeps the bear warm in cold, wet weather. Then it describes reindeer hair, which is thick, hollow, and helps the animal stay warm and float in water. Musk ox hair is very long and shaggy, and it protects the animal in winter and summer. Oryx hair is short and pale, so it helps the animal stay cool in the desert. Lion hair is a big mane that makes a male lion stand out. Zebra hair has black and white stripes that help confuse hunters. The story also explains sloth hair, arctic fox hair, giant pangolin scales, porcupine quills, and mole hair. At the end, it says wild animal hair might be fun, but people do not need hair like animals do, so they do not have to choose.

summary_text: Little Red Riding Hood lived with her mother, and her grandmother loved her very much. Her grandmother made her a red velvet cloak, so everyone called her Little Red Riding Hood. Then a huntsman heard loud snoring, came in, killed the wolf, and cut open his belly. Out came Little Red Riding Hood and her grandmother, safe and alive. They thanked the huntsman and ate together.

summary_text: Deep in the forest, a large crocodile lived in a river. He was selfish and shouted at all the other creatures to stay away. He said the river was his and that he would eat anyone who came near. Because of this, no fish, frogs, crabs, or other animals came to the river. The forest creatures were afraid and went far away to drink and bathe. One morning, the forest heard a loud groaning sound. The crocodile was lying on his back with a swollen jaw and tears in his eyes. The animals watched, but no one helped. Then a little mouse came. He ran along the crocodile’s body, went into his mouth, and pulled out a bad tooth. The crocodile’s pain stopped. He thanked the mouse, gave him a nut, and later became his friend. After that, the crocodile invited all the animals to the river, and they came back safely.

summary_text: When superheroes have a bad day, they may feel sad or angry. They could kick, punch, shout, crush crates, bend gates, throw trucks, knock down buildings, start forest fires, or flatten the town’s tires. But they have other choices. They can hike or go mountain biking to let their angry steam out. They can rescue people, do good deeds, build fun theme parks, catch bad guys, and tame scary beasts. Even when they feel upset again, they could make blizzards, twisters, sticky webs, or trouble for the whole world. Real superheroes do not choose to rampage. They look into their strong hearts and fight the urge to hurt others. They notice their sorrow, anger, and pain while they wait for those feelings to pass. They may frown, sigh, slump, or cry. Then they get up and continue saving the world in their own super way.

Witch made spells, Frank danced, Dracula flew like a bat, Werewolf howled at the moon, and Mummy walked in bandages. Buu went home smiling because his friends helped him feel better. He decided to thank them with a party. He closed the drapes, made the house dark, and got ready all day. When his friends came, they stayed up late, made potions, flew, howled, and danced. Buu danced too, glowed in the dark, and had fun until morning.

summary_text: Temple Grandin was a girl who experienced the world differently. Loud sounds, crowded places, tags on clothes, and hugs upset her. She did not speak until she was three, and some people wrongly thought she should be sent away. Her mother believed in her and found teachers who helped her. Temple was teased at school and was eventually sent to stay with her aunt on a ranch. There, she felt comfortable around cows and realized that she thought in pictures, just as she imagined the cows did. A teacher helped her discover her love of science. Temple built a machine that used boards to give a comforting squeeze. Later, she studied animals and designed better, kinder farm equipment. Her ideas changed many farms. Temple became a speaker who told people that every person is special and that being different can help someone do important things.

summary_text: On October 14th, Mrs. Bear and Mr. Bear settled into their den for winter. Mrs. Bear set her alarm for February 14th, because she had a special plan for Valentine's Day. Four months later, she woke up while Mr. Bear kept sleeping. She made a sign that said, “It’s nice to share Valentine’s Day with someone you love,” and hung it on the wall. She brushed out leaves, dug up a pot of summer honey, and put out crispy critters for Mr. Bear. She also got two valentine poems she had written in summer. Then she went outside, broke ice on the pond, and filled a berry can with cold water. Mrs. Bear tried again and again to wake Mr. Bear, but he kept sleeping. At last she shouted, “One, two, three. Surprise!” Mr. Bear woke up, hugged her, and showed her chocolate covered ants. They shared their treats, read the poems, and ate together until the den was empty. Then they went back to sleep until spring.

summary_text: One duck gets stuck in the muck down by the Deep green Marsh. The duck calls for help. Each time, the duck stays stuck deep in the muck. Next, eight possums nibbling on blossoms, nine snakes leaving little wakes, and ten dragonflies zooming through the skies come to help. At last, all of them work together. Splish bump bleep plop plunk slush swash link zing. The duck gets out of the muck and says, Thank you!

The answer is no, and the bus driver thanks them and leaves. At the end, the pigeon sees a truck coming and thinks about driving it.

summary_text: A few days before Christmas, snow fell in Tidmouth. Everyone got ready for the Christmas party. Sir Topham Hat gave Thomas an important job. Thomas had to pick up the Christmas tree. Thomas said, “You can count on me,” and he puffed away. But the next morning, Thomas had not come back. Sir Topham Hat said Thomas was stuck in the snow. He sent Donald and Douglas to help find him. The twins went out, but they could not find Thomas. Then Harold flew over and saw Thomas covered in snow. Donald, Douglas, and workers helped dig Thomas out. James came and gave Thomas a push. Soon Thomas was free. The engines worked together to bring the Christmas tree back to Tidmouth station. People waved and cheered as they went. The tree was decorated just in time. Then everyone in Tidmouth came to give gifts and sing carols at the Christmas party.

summary_text: Docks was always busy, and Cranky the crane worked there day and night. He never got a nap, so he was always cranky. The shed fell down, and Bill, Ben, and Salty were trapped. The Fat Controller came to the docks and saw the mess. He told Cranky he had made a terrible mess and must wait until Harvey could clear it up. All night, Salty told stories. In the morning Harvey came and cleared the mess. Cranky felt better and promised to be kind. He worked carefully and said please and thank you, but later he became cranky again.

summary_text: One morning Sir Topham Hat spoke to James and said that if he could not behave, his red coat would be taken away and he would be painted blue. James felt cross. He bumped the coaches hard onto the train and made them groan. Then he had to take them to a different platform where people stayed far away. James felt lonely and wanted to show that he could pull the coaches well. When the guard blew his whistle, James started off with a big jerk. He went too fast, and then the train began to slow down because the brake pipe was leaking. The driver and guard found a hole. They fixed it with newspapers and a leather bootlace from Jeremiah Jobling. After that, James pulled the train safely and was careful never to bump coaches again.

After that, James pulled the train safely, and he became sadder and wiser and never bumped coaches again.

summary_text: Harry was a white dog with black spots, and he liked almost everything except baths. One day he heard water running in the tub, so he buried the scrubbing brush in the backyard and ran away from home. He played in the street where they were fixing it, then at the railroad, and then with other dogs. Each time he got dirtier and dirtier. He even slid down a coal shoot and became so dirty that he looked like a black dog with white spots. Soon Harry felt tired and hungry, and he wondered if his family thought he had really run away. So he hurried back home. At the house, his family did not know him at first. Harry tried his old tricks, but they still said he was not Harry. Then he dug up the scrubbing brush and showed it to them. The family gave him a bath, and when they scrubbed him, they finally knew it was Harry. Afterward, he was white again with black spots, and he went to sleep happily.

If you do not catch Santa, there is always next year.

summary_text: Deep in the woods, an old white cabin stands with pumpkins in the garden. Inside live a cat, a squirrel, and a duck. They make pumpkin soup together: the cat slices the pumpkin, the squirrel stirs, and the duck adds the salt. They eat the soup, play music, and sleep in a quilt made by all three. One morning, the duck wants to be the head cook. He takes the special spoon and says it is his turn to stir. The squirrel and the cat say no, and they fight. The duck is upset and leaves in a wheelbarrow. The cat and squirrel look for him, but they cannot find him. They feel sad and make the soup too salty. Then they search in the dark woods and near a steep cliff. At last they see light in the cabin and find the duck home. They cook soup again, and this time the duck stirs while they stay quiet. The duck teaches the squirrel to measure the salt, and the soup is good again.

summary_text: The feast to welcome spring was about to begin, and Moana and Grandma Tala were gathering shells. Moana was making a surprise anklet for her father, Chief Tui. Kevin tried to call 911, but the phone did not work because the wires were damaged in a snowstorm. On Christmas Eve, Kevin acted like a grownup. Pooh found several eggs, but his basket had a hole, so the eggs kept falling out. Piglet, Rue, Tigger, Eeyore, and Kanga each found some of Pooh’s eggs and brought them back. At the end, Pooh’s basket was empty, but his friends gave him the eggs they had found. Rabbit counted the eggs and said Pooh was the winner. Pooh then shared the feast with his friends, and Rabbit had lots of honey for everyone.

summary_text: Max is a lucky dog who lives in New York City in an apartment building with many animal pals. He loves his owner, Katie, and waits for her to come home. Then Duke comes to live there too. Duke was adopted from the pound and is excited, but Max does not want to share. Max also has many friends in the building, like G, a sweet Pomeranian, Chloe the fussy cat, Mel the pug who chases squirrels, Buddy, Norman the lost guinea pig, Leonard the poodle who likes loud music, and Pops, an old bassad hound in a doggy wheelchair. One day, Max goes missing. Pops leads the search, and Max’s friends help look for him. Below the city, Snowball the bunny leads the flushed pets in the sewers. They include Tattoo the pig, Ripper, Derek, and a bearded dragon who likes to drive cars. Max and all his friends are special and need lots of love.

summary_text: This story says that every child is different. Some children like swimming, hiking, dancing, or riding bikes. Some like blue, yellow, or pink. Some are good at science and math, while others enjoy sports, music, instruments, or singing. Some children wear glasses, speak with an accent, or use a chair, ramp, crutches, a wheelchair, or a sling. The story says that these differences are part of each person. It is never okay to make fun of someone because of how they look, act, or sound. Every child is an individual, just like you. The story reminds children to be kind to people who are different, because everyone is different from someone else. It is okay to be different, and it is okay to be yourself.

summary_text: Frosty the Snowman was a happy snowman with a corncob pipe, a button nose, and two eyes made of coal. The children found an old silk hat and put it on his head. Then something magical happened, and Frosty came to life. He began to dance and laugh and play with the children. Frosty saw that the sun was hot, so he said they should run and have fun before he melted away. He went down to the village with a broomstick in his hand and ran all around the square, saying, "Catch Me If You Can." He went down the streets of town to the traffic cop and stopped for a moment when the cop shouted, "Stop!" Then Frosty hurried on his way, waved goodbye, and said, "Don't you cry. I'll be back again someday."

summary_text: Taylor Allison Swift was born on December 13, 1989, in West Reading, Pennsylvania. She grew up with her mom, dad, and little brother Austin. The family loved to read, visit new places, and play outside. Taylor especially loved Christmas because her family lived on a Christmas tree farm. At Christmas, her dad mowed the fields on a tractor, and Taylor picked praying mantis egg pods off the trees so no bugs would surprise people. As a child, Taylor tried many things like riding horses, acting, and writing poetry. Then she learned to play guitar and found what she loved most. Taylor wanted to go to Nashville, Tennessee, because she liked country singers Faith Hill and Shania Twain. When she was 11, her mom took her and Austin there. Taylor visited music offices and gave out CDs. Later, RCA Records wanted to work with her, and her family moved to Nashville. Taylor made albums, sang her own songs, and became a big music star.

summary_text: An old lady swallowed a daisy. She was not lazy. She swallowed the daisy to brighten the clover. Then she swallowed a butterfly. She did not sigh. She swallowed the butterfly to rest on the daisy. The daisy stayed to brighten the clover. After that, she swallowed a bird. It was not absurd. She swallowed the bird to glide with the butterfly. The butterfly rested on the daisy, and the daisy brightened the clover. Then she swallowed a pot. Believe it or not, she swallowed the pot to carry the bird. Next she swallowed some gold. It was shiny gold, and she swallowed it to fill up the pot. The bird, butterfly, daisy, and clover were all part of the chain. At the end, she swallowed a fiddle. The old lady started to dance, a wee little leprechaun joined her, and she giggled so much that out popped a rainbow. Happy St Patrick's Day!

summary_text: Brian was a leprechaun who liked to be alone. He lived under the ground in a quiet place. Then a man named Shawn McDonald built a stone cottage right over Brian’s home. Brian used magic to scare Shawn, but it did not work. So Brian made a door under Shawn’s bed and came out at night when it rained. Shawn could not sleep, and Brian whispered, “It’s only the cat under the bed.” Shawn soon guessed there was a leprechaun there. He put food under the bed, and Brian ate it. Later, Shawn got poor, and Brian left gold coins on the kitchen table. People in the village heard stories and thought Shawn had a chest of gold. Two robbers came to steal it. They tied Shawn up and looked under the bed. There they saw a wild cat, and they ran away. Shawn was free, and Brian and Shawn lived well and happily.

summary_text: Oi was a leprechaun who lived in the basement of a house in Chicago. He sat by his pot of gold and sometimes sang and read newspapers. Michael McKeever lived in the house with his mother and father. On St Patrick’s Day, Michael found that his old baseball shoes were too small and broken. He could not ask for new shoes because his family had little money. His mother asked him to get a big pot from the basement. There Michael saw Oi in the recycling bin beside the gold. Michael and Oi talked. Michael told Oi that his dad had lost his job, the hot water tank was broken, his mother’s bike was broken, and he needed new shoes. Oi would not give him any gold, and they argued. Later Michael’s father said he believed their luck would change, and Michael felt better. That night Oi remembered that he had been a cobbler in Ireland. The next morning, Michael found a new pair of green baseball shoes with gold shamrocks and strong spikes. They were very lucky shoes.

summary_text: It is March 17, and the leprechaun family wears green for St Patrick's parade. The wee ones march, and everyone joins in. Bedelia leads the clan with granddaddy Dan. Timothy Shaunessy marches with a big pot of gold. Aunt Rose taps her toes with a shamrock in her hand. Johnny and Jack play the fiddle and the drum, and everyone dances, even the pig. After the parade, the family goes home for lunch. They eat mulligan stew and green apple punch. Kate cuts the cabbage, and Pat shells the peas. Before they eat, they say, “May the luck of the Irish be with you today!”

summary_text: High up in the mountains, little Yak looked at the sky. Mom said, “The snow is coming.” Little Yak said he had never seen snow before, so he ran to his friends. Pika said he was gathering grass to eat in winter. Blue thrush said she was flying to a warm winter home. Brown bear said he was eating all summer so he could sleep a long winter. He watched the snow all around him and said yaks are lucky when the snow comes because they get to see the beautiful snow while other animals sleep, hide, or go away.

summary_text: St Patrick’s Day is celebrated on March 17th. It honors St Patrick, who lived many years ago. He was born in Britain and was raised in a Christian family. When he was a boy, people took him to Ireland and made him a slave. He had to herd sheep, and he prayed for help. Six years later, he escaped and went back to Britain. There he thought and prayed and decided he wanted to return to Ireland to teach people about God. He studied religion in France. In 432, the pope gave him the name Patricius, and he became a priest and then a bishop. Bishop Patrick went back to Ireland, preached, and built churches and schools. People trusted him and loved him. He died on March 17th in 461, and later he was called Saint Patrick. Today people celebrate with church, green clothes, shamrocks, cards, songs, dances, parades, and food.

Then she swallowed some gold to fill up the pot. Each time, the story repeats the chain: gold, pot, bird, butterfly, daisy, and clover. At the end, the old lady swallowed a fiddle. The story says it is a riddle why she swallowed the fiddle. She started to dance, a wee little leprechaun joined her, and they twirled high and low. She giggled so much that out popped a rainbow, and everyone wished Happy St Patrick's Day!

summary_text: Brian was a leprechaun who liked living alone under the ground. One day, a man named Shawn McDonald built a stone cottage right over Brian’s home. Brian tried to scare Shawn away with leprechaun magic by making him see headless ghosts and a banshee, but Shawn only thought Ireland was full of magic. Brian then built a door under Shawn’s bed and worked there at night, tapping and disturbing Shawn’s sleep. When Shawn heard Brian say, “It’s only the cat under the bed,” he thought a cat must be in the house and decided to feed it. Soon Shawn’s food ran low, and Brian’s help with gold coins kept him going. But people gossiped that Shawn had hidden treasure, and two robbers came to steal it. They tied Shawn up, but when they looked under the bed, they found a wild cat. The robbers ran away, Shawn was freed, and Brian and Shawn lived happily together.

summary_text: It is March 17, and the leprechaun family is dressed in green for St Patrick’s parade. The wee ones march along, and everyone joins in. Bedelia leads the clan with granddaddy Dan, and they walk and talk as they go. Timothy Shaunessy marches with a big pot of gold. Aunt Rose comes next, tapping her toes and carrying a shamrock. Johnny and Jack play the fiddle and the drum, and the whole crowd dances an Irish jig, even the pig. After the march, the family goes home for lunch. They eat mulligan stew and green apple punch while Kate cuts the cabbage and Pat shells the peas. Friends and family keep arriving, including the Casys, McGregors, and Ogrady family. The house fills up, everyone is welcomed inside, and the leprechauns pile their plates high. Before they eat, they all say, “May the luck of the Irish be with you today!”

summary_text: Audrey Fay Hendrick lived in Birmingham with her mama and daddy. When Mike, also called Martin or Dr. King, visited their home, they cooked him a big supper. Audrey listened when the grown-ups talked about segregation, the laws that kept black and white people apart. She wanted to go places and do things like everybody else. She heard Mike preach at Fred’s church that unfair laws should be disobeyed and that people should fill the jails. Most grown-ups were afraid to go, but one night Jim said, “If grown-ups won't do it, fill the jails with children.” Audrey stood up and said she wanted to go to jail. Her mama agreed. Audrey joined the children at 16th Street Baptist Church, marched out singing, and was arrested. In jail, she was lonely and scared, but she stayed there. After seven days she went home. Two months later, Birmingham removed the segregation laws, and Audrey ate at Newberries like everyone else.

summary_text: High up in the mountains, little Yak looked at the sky while his mom said, “The snow is coming.” Little Yak had never seen snow before, so he ran to tell his friend Pika. Pika said he had been gathering grass to eat through the cold winter. Then little Yak asked if yaks do that too, but Pika said he did not think so. Little Yak told blue thrush the snow was coming, and blue thrush said that was why he was flying to a warm winter home. Brown bear also explained that he had been eating all summer to build up fat for his long winter sleep. Little Yak went back to his mom and asked what yaks do in winter. Mom said yaks stay right where they are. When the snow started falling, little Yak snuggled close to his mom. He said yaks are lucky because while other animals are away, sleeping, or hiding, yaks get to see the beautiful snow.

summary_text: St Patrick's Day is celebrated on March 17th in Ireland and in many other places. The holiday honors St Patrick, who was born in Britain around the year 380. As a boy, he was kidnapped and taken to Ireland, where he had to herd sheep. He prayed for help and escaped six years later. After he returned to Britain, he thought and prayed about his life. He went to France to study religion, and in the year 432 the pope named him Patricius. He became a priest and then a bishop. Bishop Patrick sailed back to Ireland and preached there. He built churches and schools, and people trusted him. He cared for the Irish people for the rest of his life. He died on March 17th in the year 461. Later, the Catholic Church made him Saint Patrick. Today people celebrate with church, green clothes, shamrocks, decorations, songs, dances, parades, food, and cards.

summary_text: At bedtime, a child thinks there is an alligator under the bed. He is careful when he walks and looks, but the alligator is never there when he checks. He calls his mom and dad, and they look too, but they do not see it. The child decides he must do something himself. He goes to the kitchen and gets alligator bait. He fills a paper bag with food alligators might like, such as fruit, vegetables, a sandwich, cookies, candy, and pie. He puts the food in different places around the house to make the alligator come out. The alligator comes for the food and crawls through the hall. The child follows it to the garage, shuts the door, and locks it. Then he goes to bed. In the morning, he leaves dad a note to warn him that the alligator is in the garage.

summary_text: There are four eggs: one, two, three, four. Three eggs crack open, and three little birdies hatch out. They say goodbye and wave to the last egg, but it does not hatch. The birdies wait and wait. Then they come back. They listen and peck, peck, peck at the egg to help it open. At last, the egg cracks. A surprise comes out. It is not a bird. It is an alligator. They stay with the alligator, and they look like friends. In the end, they go for a little ride in the water at sunset, and the sun in the sky looks like another egg.

summary_text: Sophia Valdez was a baby who liked to help. Her Abuelo also helped people in Blue River Creek by doing chores, walking pets, and visiting lonely friends. Each morning, Abuelo walked Sophia to class, and they went home together on Blue River Pass. One day, a pup chased a squirrel and ran away. Sophia and Abuelo followed it up a hill made of trash. The hill broke, and they fell into mud. Abuelo got hurt, and the next day Sophia walked to school alone. She did not like that the hill of trash was still there. Sophia decided to fix it and make a new park. She asked neighbors for ideas and drew a map. Then she learned the town thought she would build it alone. Sophia felt scared and went to city hall. At first, the clerk said she was only a kid and could not build a park. Sophia spoke up, and the mayor let her start a petition. With help from family, neighbors, and school friends, the town built the park together.

summary_text: Old man Bookwire lived by a beautiful forest, but he was a grump. He scolded fireflies, clouds, and lilacs. In summer, he painted the colorful birds in his yard, and sometimes he painted squirrels by accident. Then fall came, and the birds flew south for the winter. Bookwire thought he would be alone, but the squirrels had built flying machines and followed the birds. They flew in gyrocopters, gliders, and a zeppelin. The birds waved goodbye, and the squirrels flew after them. They traveled through night, rain, and turbulence until they reached a warm beach in Santa Vaca. There they had a fiesta, swam, ate mangoes, and danced. Later, Bookwire got a phone call from Santa Vaca. He missed the birds and squirrels, so he drove his old car to the beach. The squirrels hugged him, and he laughed for the first time in a long time. He painted the birds there, but the hot sun made him too tired. The squirrels gave him water, and everyone drove home together.

summary_text: Lucy, Tom, Bob, and M were spending a weekend with their granddad on a gray, drizzly day when everyone felt bored and grumpy. Grand Dude tried to cheer them up by showing postcards and using a shiny magic compass. When Lucy picked a postcard of a sandy beach, he waved the compass over it and the children were suddenly on the beach. They rode flying fish, built sandcastles, and ate ice cream, but then crabs pinched Bob and more crabs came from the sea, so Grand Dude used the compass again. The next postcard took them to a desert valley, where they met a cowboy and rode horses. A herd of wild buffalo rushed toward them, Tom fell, and Grand Dude lassoed him back onto his horse just in time. After Tom asked for somewhere less stampy, they were taken to a hill with flowers and cows, but an avalanche came down the mountain. The cows flew them away safely. At last, Grand Dude used a photo of his house, and the compass sent them home for bed, where they brushed their teeth, washed, and fell asleep.

summary_text: Old Bear woke from his winter sleep because he smelled food. He followed the smell to Bubba Braa’s house by the forest. He got full and sleepy. Before he left, Bubba Braa gave him a red scarf she had made. After he went away, Bubba Braa’s friends arrived. They saw the bear tracks and knew the “rabbi” was really a bear. Everyone laughed, and they worked together to make more lotas for everyone.

She made them run, jump, and practice. After many days, the Tornadoes got much better. When Coach Armstrong came back, he was surprised. On Thanksgiving Day, the Tornadoes beat the Werewolves 77 to 3, and everyone celebrated with hot dogs.
