summary_text: Owl took a kettle from the cupboard and said he would make tear water tea. He put the kettle on his lap and sat very still. Then Owl thought of sad things, like chairs with broken legs, songs with forgotten words, spoons lost behind the stove, books with torn pages, stopped clocks, mornings nobody saw, mashed potatoes left on a plate, and pencils that were too short to use. As he thought about these things, he began to cry. His tears dropped into the kettle. He cried and cried until the kettle was full. Then Owl said, “That does it.” He stopped crying and put the kettle on the stove to boil. At last he filled his cup and drank the tea. He said it tasted a little salty, but tear water tea was always very good.

and sings about lobsters crawling on rocks and crabs crawling on rocks.
Then the speaker talks about a song called “Slippery Fish,”
where a slippery fish slides through the water
and gets chomped by a great white shark.
After that, a humongous whale appears in the water.
The speaker also tells the children to put on their glasses,
open their book,
and look inside.
The book is called I Am the Biggest Thing in the Ocean by Kevin Sherry.
In the story, a giant squid says it is bigger than shrimp, clams, crabs, jellyfish, sea turtles, an octopus, a shark, many fish, and even a whale.
The story ends with the giant squid saying it is the biggest thing in the ocean.

summary_text: Three little bears go to a spooky old tree. One bear has a light, one has a stick, and one has a rope. They ask if they dare go in, and they do. Then they climb a twisty old stair. Next they find a giant key and a moving wall, and they go through it into a spooky old hall. There they see a great sleeping bear. The three little bears go over the sleeping bear. After that, they have no light, no stick, and no rope, and they all have the shivers. To get out, they go up a ladder through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. Then they run fast home again, safe at last.

His feet stick out, and he cannot see well. Duck calls for Pig and Mouse. Pig and Mouse see him and think he is a pumpkin monster. Duck starts chasing them without knowing why they are running. They hide behind the barn. Duck cannot see them, and then he bumps into things. Duck battles the pumpkin monster and wins, and everyone cheers for Duck. After that, Duck makes another jack-o'-lantern to celebrate and wishes Duck were there to see it. Then Duck is still inside the pumpkin again, and the story starts over in a circle.

summary_text: The kids talk to Mama and Papa about food. They say the grown-ups should stop eating ice cream sundaes for breakfast, mayonnaise for lunch, and French fries for dinner. The kids say bodies need vegetables, whole foods, and slow foods, not fast food. They ask the parents to try one bite of healthy food. Mama and Papa make funny faces and do not want to try it. The kids keep offering kale, broccoli, quinoa, spinach, and cauliflower. They use silly ideas like an airplane coming in for a landing and special rewards if the parents eat their vegetables. At first, the parents still refuse. Then they finally take a teeny bite. They discover they like the food. The kids are happy, and everyone sits down for dinner with yams and linguini with clams. The story ends by saying that one bite can lead to big surprises.

summary_text: In New York City, tourists go to an arcade on M Street to see Lily, a real chicken who seems to play tic-tac-toe. Lily sits under bright lights and always wins, so people keep coming back to play. But Beatatrice worries about Lily. When she visits her cousins in the city, she asks many questions about where Lily lives, whether she goes outside, and how she eats. Her dad tells her that a computer helps Lily look like she is playing. Beatatrice decides to try the game herself. She ties with Lily twice, and the big boss gives her prizes. Then Beatatrice asks to play against the big boss. If she wins, she will take Lily home. The big boss agrees, and Beatatrice wins. Lily is taken to Beatatrice’s backyard coop upstate, where she can scratch in the ground, see other chickens, and warm herself in the sun.

summary_text: Gilbert had 15 blank Valentine cards to fill for his classmates. Mrs. Bird said Valentine’s Day was about liking each other. Gilbert wrote kind poems for Patty and Frank first. Patty had smiley eyes and a silly laugh, and Frank once let Gilbert use his baseball mitt. Then Gilbert had two cards left, for Lewis and Margaret. He did not want to be kind to them because Lewis had tweaked his nose and Margaret had made fun of his glasses. So Gilbert wrote mean poems and signed the wrong names. On Valentine’s Day, the class opened their cards. Patty and the others had friendly notes, but Lewis and Margaret found the bad ones and got mad. Mrs. Bird said Valentine’s Day was not for fighting. Gilbert was left out at lunch and recess, and he felt sorry. Later, Lewis and Margaret said they were sorry too, and Gilbert made new cards and kind poems for them.

summary_text: Mr. Willoughby got a big Christmas tree by special delivery. He was very glad at first, but when the tree was put in the parlor corner, it touched the ceiling and bent over. Mr. Willoughby said something must go, so Baxter the butler cut off the top. The top was given to Miss Adelaide, but it was still too big for her room, so she cut off the top again and put it outside. Tim the gardener found it and took it home, but Mrs. Tim said their house was too small and cut off the top. Barnaby bear then found the tree top and took it to his mother. Mama Bear wanted a Christmas party, but little bear said it would not hold a star, so Mama Bear cut off the top again. Frisky fox took the tree top, then Benjamin rabbit found it and brought it to his family. Mrs. Rabbit said it was too tall, so she cut off the top. At last Mistletoe mouse found the tiny tip and took it home. Mrs. Mouse said it was the right size, and they put a cheese star on top.

summary_text: In the wild wild west, a Rancher and his wife lived on a ranch. Every morning, the Rancher fed the cattle and saddled his horses, while his wife baked breakfast biscuits. One day, she got tired of biscuits and made gingerbread dough instead. She cut out a gingerbread Cowboy with boots, a hat, and a big belt buckle, then gave him raisins, candies, and nuts for eyes, mouth, and vest. She put him in the oven to bake. When the Rancher peeked inside because he was hungry, the gingerbread Cowboy jumped out and ran away. He laughed, “Giddy up giddy up as fast as you can. You can't catch me. I'm the gingerbread man.” He ran past a Road Runner, havelinas, longhorn cattle, and Cowboys, and each one wanted to catch him or eat him. At the river, a coyote offered help. The coyote carried him across, then tricked him, tossed him up, and swallowed him. That was the end of the gingerbread Cowboy.

summary_text: Anansi, his wife Asu, and their children had very little food because the rains did not come and the harvest failed. Anansi went to the farm with his hoe and dug in the dry ground for root vegetables. Instead of vegetables, he found a buried pot. The pot spoke to him and sang, “Do not wash me” and “Wrap me, tap me, and I will cook.” Anansi asked for chicken stew, and the pot filled with stew. summary_text: Sigfreed was a serious fart who lived alone in a busy neighborhood. He wore monogram towels, carried a briefcase, and listened to Beethoven. Unlike the other farts, who liked jokes and messy fun, Sigfreed felt that farts should be treated with respect. At the yearly board meeting, he brought four ideas. He said a fart should come from a higher place, should make a nicer sound like Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony, should smell like lemongrass or mint toothpaste, and should have a better name. The board could not agree, so the town farts were asked to decide. Sigfreed spoke proudly, but the elder fart told him to be proud of who he was and not take himself so seriously. Sigfreed thought about this, withdrew his debate, and joined the others at the fall party. In the end, he kept liking Beethoven and tea and scones, but now he had friends and smiled more.

At the Christmas program, Ruthie was the Heavenly Angel. At the end, Papa returned in an army uniform and hugged Ruthie, Mama, and the tiny angel.

Stella's hiccups and toe-tickling scared Emma, so Stella became Emma's monster. The child happily returned to bed with Gabe back under his bed, and everyone was ready to sleep.

On the third day, she learned his name was Rumpelstiltskin. When she said it, he was angry and disappeared into the ground.

summary_text: Babushka lived alone in Adasha and was famous for the beautiful eggs she painted. Every day through the long winter, she decorated eggs with stars, flowers, triangles, and circles. After a snowstorm, she went outside and saw caribou coming to eat because the snow covered their grass. Then a goose fell from the sky. Babushka found that a hunter had hurt the goose, so she carried it home, fed it, and kept it warm in her best basket. She named the goose Rashinka. As Rashinka grew stronger, she laid eggs and explored the house. One day she knocked over Babushka’s paint jars and then the basket of painted eggs, and all the eggs broke. Babushka and Rashinka were sad. The next morning, Babushka found a new, brightly colored egg in Rashinka’s basket. For 12 mornings, more beautiful eggs appeared. Babushka took them to the festival in Moscow, won first prize, and came home. That night she found one last egg hatch, and the little goose stayed with her always.

In the end, the alligator ate everything and stayed in the garage, and the child wondered if Dad would have trouble getting into the car the next morning.

summary_text: Maddie loves glue at home with her dad, where they make glue glasses, mustaches, and bouncy balls. But at school her art teacher warns, “Too much glue never dries” and tells the class to use glue carefully. Maddie ignores the warning and pours out the fullest bottles, making a huge sticky mess on her art project. She even lies on the table and rolls around, covering herself in glue and decorations. When she tries to get up, she cannot move. Her teacher says there is too much glue, and Maddie calls for help. Noah, Izzy, Owen, Luke, and Grace all try different ways to free her, including lassos and a tow truck, but everything only breaks or spreads the glue more. The school nurse and principal also come, but nothing works. At the end of the day, Maddie whispers a plan, and when the glue finally dries, her dad arrives, peels her off the table, and calls her a masterpiece. At home, he finishes the project, hangs it on the fridge, and the principal sends a note asking Maddie to use tape instead of glue.

So he used his trident to break down the wall. The mother joined her baby, and the dolphins splashed Ariel and Erik. Ariel laughed because they were forgiven.

summary_text: One fine morning, a young click beetle went for a walk. At noon it climbed up and down a flower. In the afternoon it rummaged through pebbles. In the evening it crawled among tall grass. At night it climbed a tree, got tired, and fell to the ground on its back. It tried to turn over, but it could not, so it cried, “HELP.” A wise old click beetle had been watching. The old beetle said it would teach the young beetle how to click, flip through the air, and land on its feet the next morning. The young beetle slept. The next day the old beetle showed how to do it. Then the young beetle tried many times, but it kept landing on its back. Earthworm, turtle, snail, and mouse all passed by and spoke to it. Then something very big appeared, and the young beetle was scared. The old beetle called, “QUICK, CLICK and FLIP!” The young beetle clicked, flipped, did three somersaults, and landed on its feet.

summary_text: Little Nick was very happy when summer vacation began. He went to his grandparents’ farm and hugged Grandma and Grandpa. After breakfast, Nick asked to go outside to play. Soon he saw Duck, Sheep, Cow, and Pig having a loud argument. They were upset because they would not share toys, a ball, or mud, and they were saying unkind things to each other. Nick asked them to stop and said it was rude. He told them that kindness means doing nice things, helping others, respecting older and younger people, waiting your turn, and not mocking others. He gave examples from his own life, like helping his sister, giving up a seat, and helping a boy get his ball. The animals listened, apologized, and promised to be kind and polite. They said hello, smiled, and said sorry when needed. By the end of the day, everyone was happier, and Duck thanked Nick for being a good friend.

summary_text: Kamala and her sister Maya looked at their building courtyard and imagined a playground there. They told Mommy, and she agreed that it would be nice. Kamala wrote a letter and Maya drew a picture, then they went to ask the landlord. He said no. That night, the sisters asked the other children in the building, and the children also wanted a playground. They wrote to the landlord again, but he said the project would cost too much. He said they could do it themselves if they wanted. The children talked to their parents, but most answers were no. Then Mr. Green offered to help by getting scrap lumber and sand. Soon the children measured, cut, sanded, hammered, and filled a sandbox. Miss Lopez offered old tires for a teeter-totter. More people helped, and the empty courtyard slowly became a playground. Later, Miss Flores found a way to buy an old slide from a school. The children held a potluck and a bake sale to help pay. At last the slide arrived, Kamala and Maya rode it first, and the landlord praised everyone for their work.

After many tries, he bakes his 11th batch. Then his mom takes him to a surprise cooking contest. The judge tastes Milo’s cookies and says they are the winner. Milo learns that the secret ingredient is never giving up.

summary_text:
Sneezy the Snowman stood out in the cold winter air and shivered. He said he needed a drink to warm up, so he drank cocoa from a cup and smiled, but the hot drink made him melt into a puddle. The children were upset and asked what to do. A voice from the puddle said, “Make me brand new,” so they rebuilt Sneezy from snowflakes. Soon a cold wind blew, and Sneezy sneezed a giant sneeze. A little girl shared her hat, and then Sneezy felt better for a moment.

But Sneezy kept getting too cold or too hot. He sat in a hot tub and melted again, then the children rebuilt him again. A little boy gave him a red and blue scarf, and later a little girl gave him a bright orange coat. When Sneezy got too warm, the children stopped him from taking off all the clothes and took him to an ice cream store. He ate seven scoops and finally said he felt just right.

His dad told him that feeling scared was okay and that a deep breath could help. Jabari took a deep breath, climbed back up, walked to the end, and jumped into the water. He splashed down and came back up. His dad said he did it, and Jabari said, “Surprise! Double backflip is next.”

summary_text: In Spain, there was a little bull named Ferdinand. While the other young bulls ran, jumped, and butted heads, Ferdinand preferred to sit quietly and smell the flowers. She saw that he was happy and let him stay. As Ferdinand grew up, the other bulls became strong and fought each other, hoping to be chosen for the bull fights in Madrid. Ferdinand still liked his quiet place best. One day, five men came to choose the biggest and fiercest bull. Ferdinand was not trying to impress them, but when a bee stung him, he jumped up, snorted, and acted wild. The men thought he was fierce and took him to Madrid. In the bull ring, Ferdinand would not fight. He sat down, smelled the flowers, and was sent home.

Rain falls, and Nana sprays the child with the hose. Later, they pick tomatoes, beans, cucumbers, and zucchini. Bats, skunks, spiders, snakes, and other animals work in the garden and dirt. In the fall, the plants dry, the leaves fall, and Nana and the child harvest food before frost comes. At the end, winter arrives, and the garden sleeps down in the dirt.

Candy fell everywhere, but children picked it up, and the cat ran home with a sore tail. Mouse found one lemon drop hidden in the ivy. He carried it home for one last treat and felt very happy.

summary_text: Freckleface Strawberry is a seven-year-old girl with red hair and many freckles. When she grows up, her freckles do not disappear, but she does not care as much. She lives happily ever after, and a speck of dirt is mistaken for a freckle.

summary_text: Mary Anning searched the beaches and cliffs near her home in England for seashells and fossils. She wanted to understand the bones she found, so she read books, copied papers, drew pictures, and wrote many notes. One day, Mary and her brother found a huge head in the rock. Mary then searched for the rest of the creature. After a storm caused landslides, she found its ribs, backbone, and flippers. The skeleton was named ichthyosaurus, and people learned that it was millions of years old and belonged to a creature that had become extinct. Mary later discovered fossilized poop and fossils that held ink. When she was twenty-four, she found a flying reptile called a pterosaur. Women could not join scientific societies, but scientists came to Mary for help. Her discoveries helped create paleontology, the study of prehistoric life through fossils. Mary kept exploring and learning with her simple tools and great determination.

summary_text: On Christmas Eve, a boy lay in bed and listened for Santa’s sleigh bells. He thought Santa was real, even though a friend said there was no Santa. Then he heard steam and saw a train outside his house. A conductor invited him aboard the Polar Express and took him to the North Pole. Many children in pajamas rode with him, sang Christmas carols, and ate candy. The train raced through dark forests, high mountains, icy plains, and a frozen desert until it reached the North Pole, a city full of toy factories and elves. At the center, Santa chose the boy for the first gift of Christmas. The boy asked for a silver bell from Santa’s sleigh. Santa gave him the bell, but it fell through a hole in the boy’s pocket on the way home. On Christmas morning, his sister Sarah found the bell in a box with a note from Mr. C. The boy could hear the bell, but others could not. As years passed, only he could still hear it.

summary_text: A long time ago in China, there was a boy named Ping who loved flowers. He could make plants grow very well. The Emperor also loved flowers, and when he needed a new ruler, he gave all the children special seeds. He said the child who showed the best flower in one year would become Emperor. Ping planted his seed and cared for it every day, but nothing grew. He changed the pot and soil, but still there was no sprout. When the year was over, all the children went to the palace with their flowers, but Ping brought only an empty pot. He was ashamed, but his father told him to bring the truth to the Emperor. At the palace, Ping told the Emperor what had happened. The Emperor smiled and said the seeds had been cooked and could not grow. He chose Ping because Ping was honest and brave, and he made Ping the new Emperor.

summary_text: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta, Georgia, on January 15, 1929. He grew up with his father, who was a pastor, his mother, who had been a teacher, and his sister Willie Christine and brother Alfred Daniel. As a boy, Martin liked baseball, football, basketball, riding his bicycle, and singing in his father’s church. One day, two friends said they could not play with him anymore because they were white and he was black. Martin cried and did not understand why skin color mattered. His mother explained that black people had been treated unfairly for a long time. Martin learned to read at home and read books about black leaders. He finished high school early, went to Morehouse College, studied in Boston, and married Ketta Scott. Later, as a pastor in Montgomery, he led peaceful protests after Rosa Parks was arrested. He helped lead the bus boycott, the March on Washington, and other peaceful protests. In 1964 he won the Nobel Peace Prize. In 1968 he went to Memphis to march for fair pay, and there he was killed.

summary_text: On hot summer days at Grandma’s farm in Michigan, the sky grew dark and thunder scared the child, who hid under the bed. Grandma, called babushka, told the child it was “thunder cake-baking weather” and said they must make a Thunder cake before the storm came. She explained that the child should count the seconds between lightning and thunder to know how far away the storm was. They found the recipe, wrote down the ingredients, and hurried outside. As the storm moved closer, they gathered eggs from Nellie Peck hen, milk from the kick cow, chocolate, sugar, flour, three overripe tomatoes, and strawberries. Grandma stayed calm and helped the child keep going. They mixed the batter, put the cake in the oven, and finished just as the storm reached the house. They ate the cake together, and after that, the child was no longer afraid of thunder.

summary_text: Everyone loves Clifford because he has good manners. He says “please” when he asks for something and “thank you” when he gets it. He visits his sister in the country by calling ahead, arriving on time, knocking, and wiping his feet. He washes his hands, eats with his mouth closed, helps clean up, and says “thank you” and “goodbye.”

Sister and Lizzy then decided to take turns being teacher and ran back to play together again.

The wolf jumped at her, but Granny and a woodcutter burst in and chased him away. Little Red gave Granny the fruit, and they all had breakfast.

In first grade, the other children sounded out words easily, while Trisha saw only wiggly shapes and stayed in the same reader for a long time. She felt different and dumb, so she drew pictures and dreamed instead. Her grandma told her that being different was part of life and that Trisha was smart and dear. Later, after her grandma and grandpa died, school still felt very hard. Then her family moved to California. In fifth grade, Mr. Falker helped her, stopped the other children from laughing, and taught her with Miss Plessy. At last Trisha read a whole paragraph, ran home, and held the honey book close because she was happy.

Hector told Miguel about the song “Remember Me.” Miguel returned home with Mama Imelda’s blessing and sang to Mama Coco. Mama Coco remembered her papa, and the family saw that music could bring them together.

summary_text: A cookie tells about living in a bakery on a street corner near a river. When the cookie was younger, school in a gingerbread house was hard. Miss Biscotti was kind, but the cookie did not raise a hand, finished tests last, and often made mistakes. The cookie felt lost, like a raft at sea, and worried at night in a cookie jar with many roommates. One day Miss Biscotti gave the class a homework task to make something completely original. The cookie tried a cooking project, hammering and nailing, and a sculpture, but each one failed. Then the cookie watched the rain and river and got an idea to write a poem called My Crummy Days. The next day the cookie read the poem to the class. Everyone clapped and cheered, and Miss Biscotti said no one else could have written it. After that, the cookie felt more confident, kept writing, and learned that people can be smart in different ways.

summary_text: Amelia Bedelia visited her grandparents on a sunny autumn day. Amelia Bedelia also made a tiny pie of her own. When the family’s pie cooled outside, birds ate it. Later, the tiny pie in the oven was done, and everyone shared it happily.

summary_text: Bruce was a bear who lived by himself. He was grumpy and did not like sunny days, rain, or cute little animals. He liked only eggs, and he collected them from the forest. Bruce did not eat eggs raw. He liked to cook them into fancy recipes from the internet. One day he found a recipe for hardboiled goose eggs with honey salmon sauce. He got salmon, honey, and eggs, and he went home to cook. But the fire in his stove went out, so he went to get more wood. When he came back, he found that the eggs had turned into goslings. Bruce did not want goslings. He took them back to their nest, but Mrs. Goose was away. The goslings followed him home, and Bruce could not make them leave. As time passed, the goslings grew up. In winter, Bruce and the geese packed bags, took a bus, and migrated to Miami together. Now they spend winter at the beach.

summary_text: Germs are very tiny, so people cannot see them. They can be in the air, in food and water, on the body, and on things people touch. Germs are not for sharing because they can make people sick. When a person coughs or sneezes, the germs can come out. The story says to cover the nose with a tissue and cover the mouth too. If germs get on hands, they can spread when people hold hands, play games, or give high fives. Germs can stay on doorknobs, coins, phones, keyboards, shoes, pets, toys, poles, sponges, and the toilet. They can stay there for up to two hours. To wash germs away, use warm water and lots of soap. Scrub the hands, rinse them, and dry them with a clean towel. Wash hands before eating and after many dirty things.

He always did what God said and never sinned. Jesus said he would open the way back to God. People put Jesus on a cross, and he died, taking our sin. Then the curtain tore. After Jesus was put in a tomb, he became alive again. Jesus now invites people to come and live with God forever.

summary_text: It was race day in Umi City, and Milly, Geo, and Bot were happy because UmiCar was going to race. A mean dump truck laughed at UmiCar and said he was too small. Milly told UmiCar he was small but very fast. The race started, and UmiCar zoomed down the streets, passed a tractor and then a taxi. He flew over a ramp and landed in a park. Soon he reached a drawbridge, but it was up because the dump truck had made it rise. Beach balls were in the water below, and Milly saw a pattern: small, small, big. When one big ball was missing, Milly made a new big ball so UmiCar could bounce across. UmiCar lowered the bridge for the other racers. Later, the dump truck spilled soapy water on the road, and UmiCar skidded. Geo fixed his broken steering wheel with shapes. Near the end, the team counted to ten, UmiCar went faster, passed the dump truck, and won the race. He shared his balloons, and the dump truck said sorry.

summary_text: Jeremy wants black high-top shoes with two white stripes, just like the other kids at school. Grandma tells him he needs new winter boots instead. Soon Jeremy’s own shoe comes apart during kickball, and Mr. Alfrey, the guidance counselor, gives him a pair of donated shoes that are too small and have Velcro and a cartoon animal on them. The other kids laugh, but Antonio does not. At home, Grandma is kind about the shoes, and later she saves money so they can look for the wanted shoes. They go to stores and thrift shops, but most shoes are wrong or too expensive. At the third thrift shop, Jeremy finds the black high tops he wants and buys them with his own money, even though they are too tight. He tries to wear them, but they never stretch. Later he sees Antonio’s taped-up shoes and thinks about him. Jeremy leaves the shoes at Antonio’s door, and Antonio gets them. After that, when snow comes, Jeremy remembers his new boots and smiles as he and Antonio get ready to race.

Her teacher told her to make a mark and see where it takes her. Vosi made a strong dot on the paper. Her teacher looked closely and told her to sign it. Vosi said that maybe she could not draw, but she could sign her name. The next week, Vosi saw her dot hanging above her teacher’s desk in a gold frame. Vosi wanted to make a better dot, so she used watercolors to paint yellow, green, red, and blue dots. Red and blue made purple. She kept making more dots, big and small, and even made a dot by not painting one. At the school art show, a little boy said he could not draw. Vosi gave him a blank paper and told him to show her. When he drew a shaky line, Vosi asked him to sign it.

summary_text: When Abraham Lincoln was a boy, he lived on a farm and worked, but he liked to read more than anything. He loved animals too. One day, when he was 10, he saw boys hurting turtles with hot coals. Abraham told them to stop and let the turtle go, and they did. After that, he wrote one of his first essays about why hurting animals is wrong. He had almost no school, so he practiced writing on trees and in the dirt. He read many books, even walking six miles to get one. He copied words about George Washington on pieces of wood. Later, in Illinois, he met the Clary's Grove boys, who were bullies. They challenged him to a wrestling match, and Jack Armstrong cheated and won. Abraham did not get angry, but he said the fight had not been fair. The boys saw his courage and backed down.

summary_text:
One hot day in the jungle of Nool, Horton the Elephant was splashing in a pool when he heard a tiny yelp from a speck of dust. Horton looked closely and guessed that a very small person must be on the speck. He gently lifted the dust speck onto a clover and said, “A person’s a person, no matter how small.” The sour Kangaroo and her young one laughed at him and said no one could live there. Horton kept the clover safe and walked with it, even when the news spread and the jungle animals made fun of him.

Later, the Wickersham brothers grabbed the clover and gave it to a black-bottomed eagle named Vlad Vladikoff. Horton chased after it all night. By morning, the clover had fallen into a huge field of clovers, and Horton searched and searched until he found it. The mayor of Whoville told Horton that all the Whos were safe but needed help after the fall. When the Kangaroos and Wickershams tried to take Horton away, the Whos made a loud noise, and Horton’s friends heard them. Their voices proved they were real, and Horton saved them.

summary_text: Apples grow on apple trees, and apple trees grow in many places around the world. Long ago, colonists brought apple seeds and small trees from England to America. As people moved west, they carried apple seeds too. In the early 1800s, John Chapman traveled through Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Indiana planting apple seeds and giving seeds and seedlings to settlers. People called him Johnny Appleseed. In spring, apple blossoms bloom on the trees. Insects or wind carry pollen from one blossom to another so apples can grow. The blossoms die, the apples grow through summer, and then they ripen in fall. Workers pick ripe apples by hand during harvest time. Some apples go to stores, and some are made into juice, cider, jelly, and applesauce. In winter, the trees become bare and dormant until spring comes again.

Frida became a famous artist and showed that being different can be beautiful and strong.

She kept swallowing bigger animals to catch the ones before them. After the dog, she swallowed a horse to catch the dog, and then a cow to catch the horse. The story repeats that she swallowed each animal to catch the one before it, all the way back to the fly. At the end, the story asks if she died, but says she did not. Instead, she had a terrible stomachache that night, threw up, and everything came back out, even the spider and the horse. After that, she felt much better.

The house stays quiet while all these creatures sleep in a tall stack. Then the flea bites the mouse. The mouse squeaks, which scares the cat. The cat claws the dog, the dog bumps the child, and the child bumps the granny. At last, the granny bumps the bed and breaks it. After that, the napping house is no longer quiet, and no one is sleeping.

summary_text: One bright fall day, Sophie picked a squash at the farmer’s market and decided it was her friend. She named it Bernice, drew a face on it with markers, wrapped it in a blanket, and rocked it to sleep. When her parents wanted to cook it, Sophie said Bernice was not for supper. Bernice went everywhere with Sophie, including the library and the garden, and Sophie treated her like a pet. Her parents tried to explain that Bernice was a squash and would get mushy if they did not eat her, but Sophie would not agree. As winter came, Bernice became softer. Sophie learned from a farmer that squash need fresh air, good dirt, and a little love, so she planted Bernice in the garden and covered her with soft soil. After winter, a green sprout appeared. In summer, Bernice grew into two tiny squash named Bonnie and Baxter, and Sophie loved them too.

summary_text: Jeremy Jacob was at the beach building a sand castle when a pirate ship sailed by. He saw the skull and crossbones flag and heard the pirates sing. He tried to tell Dad and Mom, but they were busy with the beach umbrella and baby sister sunblock. The pirates rowed to shore, and their leader, Braid Beard, talked to Jeremy and looked at his sand castle. Braid Beard said Jeremy was a good digger and invited him to help bury a treasure chest. Jeremy went with them and became a pirate. On the ship, he learned pirate songs, pirate words, and pirate manners. He played soccer with the crew, but the ball rolled off the deck and a shark ate it. Later a storm came, the mast was hit by lightning, and Jeremy helped find a place to bury the treasure. After the storm, the pirates gave him a flag and sailed away, and Jeremy went to soccer practice.

summary_text: In a meadow near an old stone wall, a family of field mice lived in a home by the barn and granary. The farmers had moved away, so the barn was empty and winter was coming. The mice worked day and night to gather corn, nuts, wheat, and straw. Frederick did not carry food like the others. When they asked why, he said he was gathering sun rays for the cold winter days. When they asked again, he said he was gathering colors because winter is gray. When they thought he was dreaming, he said he was gathering words because winter days are long. Then Frederick shared his sun rays, colors, and words. His story made the mice feel warm and happy. They clapped and said, “You are Frederick!”

summary_text: In the morning, the big trucks got ready to work. Crane said, “Let’s hoist.” Doza said, “Let’s push.” Digger said, “Let’s dig.” They built tall buildings, roads, and bridges. When the loud whistle blew, the trucks took a break because they were tired. Digger did not rest. In the rubble, he found a tiny flower. Every day, while the other trucks built, Digger visited the flower. He watered it when it looked dry, shielded it on windy days, and sang it a bedtime song at night. The flower grew, but the city grew too. Soon there was only one open space left. Crane said they needed a building there. Dozer blew smoke and cut the flower down. Digger saw little seeds in the rubble. He took the seeds and drove far away to a place no big truck had been. There he dug them into warm earth and cared for them every day.

summary_text: In India, on a big river island, a boy loved trees. He saw that the floods were taking away the land and leaving sandbars. Animals lost their homes, and the boy worried that people and animals would be in danger. He told the village, and the elders gave him 20 bamboo saplings. The boy went by canoe to a sandbar and planted them one by one. Every day he brought water, carried buckets, and cared for the young plants. He worked hard until the bamboo grew into a thick patch. Then he brought cow dung, earthworms, termites, ants, and seeds from other villages to make the soil better. He kept planting as he grew up. Soon the small patch became a big forest. Buffalo, rhinos, snakes, gibbons, birds, and elephants came back. The man kept planting more grass and fruit trees, and he protected the forest so it could stay alive.

summary_text: In India, on a big river island, a boy loved trees because they gave shade, food, and shelter. Every rainy season, floodwaters washed away more land, and the island became smaller. The boy saw animals left on sandbars with no homes, and he worried that animals and people would suffer without trees. He told the village, and the elders gave him 20 bamboo saplings. He took them by canoe to a sandy sandbar and planted them one by one. Each day he carried water from the river, built a watering system, and kept caring for the plants even when he was tired and sore. The bamboo grew into a thick patch. The boy then brought cow dung, earthworms, termites, ants, and seeds from other villages to make richer soil. Over many years, the bamboo patch grew into a large forest, and wildlife returned. Later, the man kept planting, protecting, and pruning the forest, which became known as Malai.

Then friendly birds came and put the leaves back on the tree. Later, the wind blew again and the last leaf flew away. Fletcher kept it safe in the den overnight. In the morning, the wind stopped, and the tree was covered in shining icicles. Fletcher hugged the tree and went to breakfast.

She did not listen. The plant grew from there everywhere, going two and fro, hi and low, through rain or snow, with a bow. When it was time to go, she returned there again. In the end, Little Miss learned from one little kiss endless Bliss.

summary_text: On a quiet rainy afternoon, the Octonauts were busy at the bottom of the ocean. Then Dashy Dog sounded the octo-alert. Nothing changed. Then the fish flew off the merry-go-round and landed upside down. The Octonauts saw him smiling and learned he was not a frown fish at all. He was an upside down fish, a catfish that swims upside down.

summary_text: Birds make many different kinds of nests. A woodpecker taps a hole inside a tree, while a hummingbird makes a tiny cup with spider webs. Some birds do not build nests at all. They use nests made by other birds. An emperor penguin father keeps an egg warm on his feet for about 60 days. Falcons scrape a small nest on a cliff, and cactus wrens build several dome-shaped nests. Weaver birds weave grass, while burrowing owls live underground. Some birds make nests that float on water, and shorebirds lay eggs on pebbly ground where the colors help hide them. Swiftlets make nests from saliva, and hornbills seal the mother inside a tree with a small food hole. Bald eagles build huge nests from sticks. Flamingos make muddy nests. At the end, a child’s nest is a cozy bed for resting and dreaming.

summary_text: Once there were three little wolves who lived with their mother: one black, one gray, and one white. Their mother told them to go into the world and build houses for themselves, but to beware of the big bad pig. They met a kangaroo, a beaver, a rhinoceros, and a flamingo, and each one gave them building materials. First they built a house of bricks, then a house of concrete, then a very strong house with metal and locks. Each time, the pig came, asked to be let in, and said he would huff and puff and blow the house down. The pig could not blow the houses down, so he used bigger tools and destroyed them. The wolves escaped each time and built again. At last they built a house of flowers. When the pig came again, he smelled the flowers, stopped huffing, and began to sniff. He became a big good pig, and the wolves played games with him and invited him in for tea and fruit. They all lived happily together ever after.

When old bear came to the door, Bubba Brana thought he was the rabbi and invited him in. She lit the menorah, said the blessings, and then played dreidel with him. Old bear ate nuts, but Bubba Brana won the game and saved the rest. Then she brought out the latkes, and old bear ate them all. After dinner, Bubba Brana gave him a red scarf. Later, her friends arrived and said the rabbi was already at the synagogue. Bubba Brana and the others saw bear tracks and knew a bear had come. Bubba Brana laughed and asked everyone to help make more latkes for all.

Then the bell rings a third time, and Milo races downstairs to answer it.

summary_text: At the edge of the woods, a minnow and a tadpole lived in a pond and were inseparable friends. One morning, the tadpole found that he had grown two little legs. He proudly said he was a frog, but the minnow argued that he could not be a frog because he had been a little fish the night before. They argued until the tadpole said, “Frogs are frogs and fish is fish and that's that.” Over the next weeks, the tadpole grew front legs and his tail became smaller. He became a real frog and climbed onto the grassy bank. The minnow grew into a full-fledged fish and kept wondering what had happened to his friend. Later, the frog returned and told the fish about birds, cows, and people he had seen while hopping around the world. The fish imagined these things and longed to see them too.

summary_text: Johnny Orchard lived on a farm at the top of a valley near the woods. His grandfather had planted a few apple trees, and they were the only apple trees in the valley. Johnny felt embarrassed because the other barns had bear skins hanging up, but his barn did not. After hearing about the bears other men had shot, Johnny said that if he ever saw one, he would shoot it quickly and get the biggest bear skin in the valley. Instead, when he went into the woods, he found a bear near a stump and gave it maple sugar. The bear followed him home and ate the sugar. Johnny’s parents were surprised, but the bear stayed and ate milk, chicken mash, apples, pancakes, and more maple sugar. He also got into neighbors’ cornfields, smokehouses, maple buckets, and sheds, and he grew very large. Soon the neighbors complained, and Johnny’s father said the bear had to go back to the woods. Johnny tried taking him west, then east, then south on Galls Island, but the bear always returned. Finally, Johnny and his father took him north into the woods, where men from the city zoo caught the bear in a trap and said he would have a fine place to live.

summary_text: One morning in Maine, Sal woke up thinking about her trip with her father to Bucks Harbor. While getting ready with her little sister Jane, Sal found that one of her teeth was loose. She ran to her mother, who told her that this was a sign she was growing into a big girl and that a new tooth would grow in later. Her mother also said that when the tooth came out, Sal could put it under her pillow and make a secret wish. Sal went outside to help her father dig clams and asked several sea animals if they had teeth. She watched fishhawks, loons, seals, and seagulls, then the tooth fell out while she was working in the mud. Sal was sad because she could not save it for her wish, and she and her father looked for it but could not find it. On the way home, Sal picked up a gold feather and wished on that instead. The family then went to Bucks Harbor by boat, where the motor had to be fixed, and Sal’s father bought milk and groceries. Sal later shared ice cream with Jane and said their wishes were used up, and the family headed home for clam chowder.

Anna saw Elsa in danger and blocked Hans’s sword. Anna turned to ice, then melted when Elsa hugged her. Summer returned, and the sisters went home together.

summary_text: A happy gray stone lived in a pile with many other stones. He waited to learn his purpose and hoped it would make someone happy. One by one, the other stones were picked, and Stone became worried when he was the last one left. At last, he was taken away and placed on a desk beside a large cup. He thought he had found his job, but he was only a paperweight. Then bright scribbles came to make art on the paper. Soon the paper pile grew and grew, and the scribbles cried because they had used all the paper. Stone did not want them to be sad, so he rolled down and asked for red, yellow, and blue. The scribbles made art on Stone, and he became a small gift. More stones joined in, and scribble stones began traveling everywhere, bringing happiness and art to many people.

summary_text: One day, a hungry fox was getting ready to hunt when he heard a knock at his door. A piglet was outside. The fox opened the door, grabbed the piglet, and said it was his lucky day. He wanted to make a pig roast for dinner. The piglet asked to be washed first because he was dirty. The fox agreed and gave him a bath. Then the piglet said he was too small and should be fed first so he would make more meat. The fox agreed again and cooked him a nice dinner. After that, the piglet said his meat was tough and needed a massage to become tender. The fox worked very hard, pushing and squeezing the piglet. The piglet kept asking for more, and the fox grew tired and passed out. The piglet then picked up the rest of the cookies and went home. He relaxed by a warm fire and looked in his address book to see who to visit next.

summary_text: Kevin put on his Spiderman t-shirt, Batman underpants, and jeans with horseshoes on the pockets. He did not feel very brave or lucky. Kevin went home and talked with his father, who asked what Kevin could do if Sammy dug a hole. Kevin said he could kick dirt back in. Kevin and his father laughed, and Kevin said they could walk out the other door. The next morning Kevin returned to the playground and went to the sandbox. Sammy shouted threats, but Kevin answered back. They both dug tunnels until their heads bumped. Then they started planning a fort together.

summary_text: Percy was a humble pencil in a small town. He lived in a cozy stationery shop with pens, markers, and glittery gel pens, but he felt ordinary. Percy watched children come in for school supplies and heard them talk about dreams. One day, he heard a little girl named Lily wish for a special pencil that could help her write the best story ever. Soon after, Lily came to the shop with her mom, saw Percy, and picked him. Percy was very happy. At home, Lily used Percy every day to write stories about magical lands, brave knights, and talking animals. Percy felt alive as Lily wrote, laughed, and sometimes cried. Later, Percy wore down and felt discouraged. Then Lily sharpened him and said, “I can't write Without You Percy.” Percy became sharp again and helped Lily finish her biggest story. She entered it in a school contest, read it to her class, and won first place. Lily hugged Percy and said, “We did it together!”

summary_text: During a dark, rainy night, two boys are in bed when the power suddenly goes out. They hear a creek, a crack, stomping, clanging, and loud bangs. They become frightened and hide under their blankets because they think a monster is coming to eat them. The sounds move toward the kitchen, and the boys become curious as well as scared. They go to the door with blankets over their heads. First they hear slurping and crunching, while the dog whimpers and barks. After a strange silence, the boys hear a shriek and a splatter. They leave their room and creep down the hall. When they enter the kitchen, they discover that the frightening intruder is not a monster. It is their dad, holding a spoon and eating. Their fear turns into laughter when Dad says he is sorry and explains that everything was for a bowl of delicious ice cream.

summary_text: In Spain, there was a little bull named Ferdinand. While the other young bulls ran, jumped, and played, Ferdinand liked to sit quietly under his favorite cork tree and smell the flowers. His mother worried that he might be lonely, but Ferdinand was happy where he was, so she let him stay. As Ferdinand grew bigger and stronger, the other bulls fought each other and wanted to go to the bullfights in Madrid. Ferdinand did not want to fight. One day, five men came to choose a bull. Ferdinand sat on a bumblebee by mistake, and the bee stung him. Ferdinand jumped, snorted, and ran around, so the men thought he was fierce and took him to Madrid. At the bullring, Ferdinand saw the flowers and sat down to smell them. He would not fight, so the men had to take him home.

The story ends with the children saying, “That’s what I hear.”

summary_text: Chicken Little thought there were only chickens nearby, but then something big, furry, and gray appeared. She believed it was the Big Bad Wolf and warned everyone to run. The chickens welcomed him into their flock, and they became better together.

summary_text: Elephant woke up grumpy. When the doorbell rang, he stomped downstairs and said, “Go away! I’m grumpy.” On the doorstep was a present. Elephant opened the box and found hats. He liked the hats and felt a little happier. Zebra was not happy at first and said, “Go away! I’m grumpy.” Elephant gave zebra a smooth hat, and zebra smiled. They cheered, “Hooray for a hat!” Then they went to turtle, who stayed in his shell, and gave turtle a hat too. Turtle cheered. Next they showed owl. Owl did not want to look, but elephant gave owl a hat, and owl smiled. Elephant, zebra, turtle, and owl marched to lion. Lion did not want visitors, but elephant gave lion his last hat. Lion was still sad because a friend was not feeling well. So elephant, zebra, turtle, owl, and lion made a surprise for giraffe and gave giraffe all the hats. Giraffe felt better, and everyone cheered and said to be a good friend.

summary_text: Anansi the spider was walking through the forest when he saw a strange moss-covered rock. He said the magic words, “Isn't this a strange moss-covered rock?” and fell down senseless. When he woke up, he remembered what had happened and learned that the rock was magic. Anansi decided to use the rock to trick other animals. First he visited Lion, who had a pile of yams on his porch. Anansi invited Lion for a walk, led him to the rock, and Lion said the magic words and fell down. Anansi hurried back and took all of Lion’s yams. He did the same thing to Elephant and stole all the bananas from his porch. Then he tricked more animals, including rhinoceros, hippopotamus, giraffe, and zebra, and kept stealing their food. Little Bush deer watched him from the leaves and planned a way to stop him. She tricked Anansi with coconuts, then called the other animals. Together they went to Anansi’s house and took back everything he had stolen.

Then she showed him how to float, put his face in the water, kick like a frog, and say, “bubble bubble” and “chicken airplane soldier.” Froggy tried, but he still had trouble. He went home for his flippers, then for his mask and snorkel, and kept trying again. At last, he began to swim. When it got cold and his mother said it was time to get out, Froggy did not want to leave. He put on his bathing suit and flippers again and went back into the pond, swimming and saying the words all night long.

summary_text: The Little Red Hen lived in a barnyard with her three chicks, a duck, a pig, and a cat. She found some grains of wheat and asked who would help her plant them. The duck said, “Not I.” The pig said, “Not I.” The cat said, “Not I.” So the Little Red Hen planted the wheat herself. When the wheat grew tall and golden, she asked who would help cut it. The Little Red Hen made the flour into dough and baked the bread herself. When the bread was ready, the duck, pig, and cat wanted to eat it. But the Little Red Hen said no, because they had not helped. She and her three chicks ate the warm bread.

summary_text: Jerome collected words. While other people collected stamps, rocks, coins, art, bugs, baseball cards, or comic books, Jerome listened for special words everywhere he went. He wrote down words like Peru, Willow, Emerald, Cage, Drift, Bloom, Geometry, Kaleidoscope, Symphony, Aromatic, Vociferous, Effervescent, Molasses, Bellow, and Rex. He kept his favorite words in scrapbooks and sorted them into groups like dreaming, science, sad, action, and poetic. One day, while carrying his words, Jerome slipped and the words flew everywhere. As he picked them up, he saw new and surprising word pairs, and he began making poems and songs from them. He used simple words too, like “I understand,” “I’m sorry,” “Thank you,” and “You matter.” The more words he collected, the better he could share his thoughts and feelings. At the end, Jerome poured his words into the wind from a hill, and children below began to catch words too.

summary_text: I am not a unicorn. I am not a fish. I am a narwhal, and I am a kind of whale. My family includes the beluga whale, the dolphin, and the porpoise. I live in the cold Arctic waters with my pod, which means my family. I can dive very deep and hold my breath under the ice for a long time. In spring, narwhals swim to warmer bays. This is called migration. When we get there, we lie on the water and rest. This is called logging. Long ago, people found narwhal horns on the beach and thought they were unicorn horns. My horn is really a big front tooth called a tusk. It grows in a spiral through my upper lip. It helps me taste salt and find food. I can stun cod fish or squid with my tusk and then eat them. I make clicking and knocking sounds, and my family knows what I mean.

In the end, he says only a brilliant child may make the perfect trap, and maybe next year someone will catch him.

summary_text: The girl in the story loved watching a TV show about a boy with a magic pencil. He could draw food when he was hungry and draw a police officer when people were in danger. She wished for a magic pencil too. She wanted to draw a lock for her door, stop time so she could sleep longer, erase the smell from the garbage dump, and make her family happy. She wanted beautiful dresses for her mother, schools for her father to build, and a proper ball for her brothers and herself. Every night she hoped for the pencil, but it never came. One day at the dump, she saw a girl her age sorting trash and boys collecting metal scraps. Her father explained that some children had to work and some girls did not go to school. This made her think about unfairness. Later, when girls were told they could not go to school, she began to write and speak out for them. Her voice grew strong, and people around the world listened.

Then he found a recipe for make a witch stew and used dog drool instead of frog spit. After the dog drank it, she turned into a witch again. In the end, the potions wore off, and the witch became normal. The cat was never allowed to make lunch again.

summary_text: Just me and my mom went to the city. Mom gave me money to buy train tickets, and I wanted to help her get on the train, but the steps were too high. Mom helped me instead. Then the conductor came, and the tickets were gone, so Mom paid him more money. The city was busy, and I held Mom’s hand. We went to the Museum of Natural History and saw rooms full of old dinosaur bones. I picked up a little dinosaur egg to show Mom, but someone took it away. I tried on costumes for Mom, and a museum guard did not like that. Next we went to the aquarium and saw fish and seals. Mom got mad because she could not find me. I ran to the front to see the seals better. We also went to an art museum, had lunch, bought a hot dog, and went to a store where I tried on clothes. We took a taxi back to the train station, and Mom bought the tickets this time. We went home, and I stayed awake almost all the way.

After that, the family ate broccoli, corn, and salad instead of green beans.

summary_text: Wilma Rudolph lived in Clarksville, Tennessee, with her large family. She loved to run, laugh, and play, but before she was five, she became very sick. Doctors found that she had scarlet fever and polio, and people said she might never walk again. Wilma could only move by hopping on one foot. Her mother took her by bus to a hospital in Nashville, where doctors and nurses helped her do exercises. At home, Wilma kept practicing, even when it hurt. She was sad when her school would not let her attend because she could not walk. Later, she got a steel brace and returned to school, where other children made fun of her. Wilma kept working hard. One Sunday at church, she took off her brace and walked down the aisle by herself. After that, she practiced more, and when she was 12, she no longer needed the brace. She then played basketball, won many games, and later went to the Olympics in Rome. There she won three gold medals and became known as the fastest woman in the world.

summary_text: On his twelfth birthday in August 1999, Michael Rosario worries that the Y2K computer problem will cause disasters when the year changes to 2000. At the Super Saver, he secretly takes a can of peaches for his mother, but Billy Gibson notices him. Jamar Prince interrupts and walks Michael home, protecting him from Billy. At Fox Run, Mr. Mosley gives Michael twenty dollars and introduces him to Ridge, a strange teenager in shiny eggshell-colored clothes. Ridge does not know the date or the year and quickly disappears. Later, Michael’s babysitter, Gibby, gives him a Red Hot Chili Peppers CD for his birthday. That afternoon, Michael and Gibby secretly feed the neighborhood cats. They find Ridge studying a dumpster as if he has never seen one before. Ridge asks unusual questions, uses slang awkwardly, and refuses to say where he lives. Michael becomes convinced that Ridge is hiding something, while Gibby follows Michael away from the strange encounter.

summary_text: In Santa Cecilia, Miguel Rivera lived with his big family, including Mama Coco. Every Día de los Muertos, the Rivera family remembered relatives who had died, and Abuelita always said no music because of Mama Imelda’s sad past. Miguel loved music anyway. He learned guitar from videos of Ernesto de la Cruz and sneaked out with his dog Dante to enter a talent show. When he fell onto the family ofrenda, he found a photo that showed Ernesto with Mama Coco’s family. Abuelita broke Miguel’s guitar, so Miguel went to Ernesto’s tomb and took a guitar from the wall. When he played it, he was sent to the land of the dead. There he needed a blessing to go home. Mama Imelda would not bless him, so Miguel searched for Ernesto with Héctor, a skeleton who helped him. Miguel learned the truth: Ernesto had stolen Héctor’s songs and tried to keep the secret. In the end, Miguel returned home, helped Mama Coco remember her papa with the song “Remember Me,” and the Rivera family allowed music again.

summary_text: Miguel Rivera was excited for school because Senora Senna said the class would do a special paper mache project. summary_text: Molly Lou Melon was a tiny girl with a big heart. Her mom told her to be true to herself, take responsibility, accept others, and use her strong voice to help people. Molly Lou tried to do these things. At school, she sat with Ronald Durkin and Gertie. Tina Bonkel snickered at them, but Molly Lou stood up and said they were friends. In winter, Molly Lou and Bettina Bonklehead painted on their desks by mistake. Molly Lou said, “me,” and cleaned the desks during recess. In spring, a new boy, Garvin Grape, came to school and talked about gravity. Bettina made fun of him, but Molly Lou said gravity was a big deal and gave Garvin a note inviting him to recess. On the first day of summer, Bettina tripped Garvin, and his glasses flew away. Molly Lou caught the glasses and told Bettina to never do that again. Ronald and Gertie helped Garvin up, and the friends shouted together.

summary_text: Hui is a book-reading parrot who says the words in the book are tricky and make tongues slip. He talks about fresh fish at Finney’s diner, where Finney has fresh fish, fresher fish, and his best fish, the freshest fish. Finney proudly says his finest fish is his freshest fish, and it is french fried. If someone orders the wrong way, the bones can fall out, so Pinnerblin comes with his shin pin bin and puts the bones back in place. Hui also tells about Spreader bread and bread spreaders, who spread butter and must be careful with beds and bedding. Then he speaks of ape cakes and grape cakes, where a greedy ape gobbles green grape cakes. Hui says he makes the words easy by looking in a mirror and saying what he sees. He ends by talking about a storm: when the drops start dropping, the storm starts, and when the drops stop dropping, the storm starts stopping.

The fairies told her she was Princess Aurora and took her home. Maleficent made Aurora touch a spindle, and she fell asleep. Prince Philip fought Maleficent, killed the dragon, and kissed Aurora. She woke up, and everyone was happy.

At the feast, the good fairies Flora, Fauna, and Meriwether came to give gifts. Flora gave beauty and Fauna gave song, but before Meriwether could speak, the evil witch Maleficent arrived in anger because she had not been invited. She cursed Aurora to prick her finger on a spinning wheel and die before her 16th birthday. Meriwether changed the curse so Aurora would only sleep until true love’s kiss woke her. The king burned all spinning wheels, and the fairies hid Aurora in the woods as Briar Rose. On her 16th birthday, Briar Rose met Prince Philip and fell in love. The fairies then told her she was a princess and took her home, where Maleficent tricked her into touching a spindle. Aurora fell asleep, and Philip fought Maleficent, killed the dragon she turned into, and woke Aurora with a kiss. They were reunited, and everyone was happy.

summary_text: Catherine Olivia Sessions, called Kate, grew up in the woods of Northern California. She liked gathering leaves, pine needles, and flowers to make necklaces and bracelets. At school, she learned to read, write, and count, but she loved science most of all, especially trees. Kate felt the trees were her friends. She studied them in college and learned about soil, insects, plants, and how trees grow. In 1881, she became the first woman to graduate from the University of California with a science degree. After college, Kate moved to San Diego and saw that it was a dry desert town with very few trees. She worked as a teacher and vice principal for two years, then left to become a gardener. Kate searched for trees that could live in hot, dry places. She found many kinds and planted them all over San Diego.

summary_text: Little penguin wanted to fly like the other birds. He asked why he could not fly. A gull told him that penguins cannot fly, but little penguin still thought he had wings. He flapped his wings, flapped harder, waddled fast, and jumped. He landed with a splat in front of his dad. Dad asked what he was doing. Little penguin said he wanted to fly like other birds. Dad said penguins cannot fly. Penguins swim. Little penguin tried again. He flipped and flapped his little wings until he was tired. He said he knew he could do better. Then he slipped, bumped, and tripped, and fell splash into the sea. Dad came close and took little penguin by the wing. They swam under the sea, leapt above the sea, and moved through the water again and again. Little penguin thought this was just like flying. He asked if swimming was like flying, and dad said it was almost the same.

summary_text: Subway was born the color of midnight, while her mama was the color of dawn, her baba was the color of dusk, and her sister Mitch was the color of high noon. At school, Mitch got kind names, but Subway was called Blackie and Night. This hurt Subway, so she hid away and wished she looked like Mitch. The next morning, she was still dark. Mama asked her name and told her that brightness is not in skin, and beauty comes from the mind and heart. That night, a shooting star came and took Subway away. The star showed her a story about Night and Day, who were both needed. When Subway woke up, she felt beautiful inside and out and went back into the world.

summary_text: The story asks, “Who am I?” for many dinosaurs. First, it describes a brachiosaurus with back legs shorter than its front legs, a long neck, and a long tail. At the end, the story names a tyrannosaurus rex with big teeth, a short tail, long back legs, and short arms. It eats meat and is the fiercest dinosaur.

summary_text: Turk lived on Wishbone Farm, and his parents were very proud of him because he was the biggest, strongest, and most graceful bird there. Every November, the family worried about turkey time, when farm turkeys were chosen for Thanksgiving dinners. Turk practiced dancing and football moves each day, while his brother Runt warned that turkeys were in danger. Two days before Thanksgiving, Madame Waddell came to pick a turkey for ballet. Turk danced beautifully, but Runt acted wild and chased her away, so she left without choosing anyone. The day before Thanksgiving, Coach Giblet came to choose a turkey for his football team. Turk showed off again, but Runt got sick and sneezed all over, and the coach drove away. On Thanksgiving morning, a little old lady came by and pointed at Runt, but Turk and Runt worked together to scare her off. The family was thankful they were safe and together, and by December they were still watching out for holiday danger, with Runt ready with a new plan.

Christopher Robin took Pooh’s present to Rabbit’s house, and all the friends shouted, “Happy birthday!” Pooh saw the cake, balloons, streamers, honey pots, and presents. He hugged Piglet and Christopher Robin and said waiting had been fun too.

After Fly Guy caused trouble in the lunchroom, the boss fired Miss Muzzle. Roz came back, called Fly Guy a Super Fly Guy, and made him special garbage soup. Everyone was happy again.

summary_text: One bright morning in the city of Chapur, Uncle Rafi drove his otter rickshaw with Avy and his cat Chutki riding along. The streets were busy and loud. Then a little frog hopped in front of the rickshaw. Uncle Rafi stopped fast, and the frog moved safely to the side. Avy said it was close, and Uncle Rafi said every life matters and people must be kind. Soon a woman on a bicycle called for help because her chain was broken and she would be late for her daughter’s school play. Uncle Rafi said they would help, so Avy and Chutki rode with her to the school. After that, they saw a man whose vegetable cart had tipped over. Avy and Uncle Rafi helped pick up the cart and the vegetables. The man gave them cucumbers. At last, they went home. Avy told his mother about the adventure and said kindness was the best thing to carry.

The ducks now want a diving board for the pond.

Stacy loved words. She liked reading, writing, spelling, and learning unusual words from the dictionary. She kept a special notebook for extraordinary words and practiced them carefully. Words made her feel understood, especially when she felt quiet, clumsy, grumpy, or anxious. One day her teacher, Mrs. Blakesly, asked her to stay after class and gave her a spelling test with a big red 100. Then Mrs. Blakesly told Stacy that she would be in the spelling bee with Jake. Stacy knew Jake was a bully who used words to hurt other students, and she hoped she could be braver at the contest.

Stacy studied all week. At the county library, she took her place onstage and spelled word after word correctly. Soon only Stacy, Jake, and one other girl were left. The other girl missed her word, and then Jake kept spelling correctly too. Stacy finally misspelled instantaneous and lost. Jake won first place, and Stacy got second. Jake was rude, but Stacy told him he should be courteous. Her mother reminded her, "Only fail if you stop," and Stacy remembered perseverance. She decided she would keep learning words and try again tomorrow.

summary_text: Mortimer was a wee mouse who lived in a big house in a dark hole under the stairs. He liked being unnoticed, but he did not like his hole because it was cold, cramped, and creepy. Each day he sneaked out to look for crumbs and tidbits. One day he saw a Christmas tree with twinkling lights and a bright star. Next to it was a little house and a bed that looked just right for him. Mortimer climbed the tree, reached the table, and found small statues. He moved the statues away and crawled into the baby’s wooden bed. Every day he found food like cookie crumbs, fruitcake morsels, and peppermint candy, but the statues were always put back. Then, on Christmas Eve, Mortimer heard a man tell the Christmas story about Joseph, Mary, Bethlehem, shepherds, wise men, and a baby born in a stable with no room in the inn. Mortimer saw that the baby statue was Jesus. He put all the statues back, laid the baby in the manger, prayed, and later found a new house just his size. He thanked Jesus for making room for him.

summary_text: On a bright Christmas Eve, Fletcher the rabbit saw that the rabbits had moved to a new burrow. He worried that Father Christmas would not find the new home. Fletcher began to collect sticks and make a trail of arrows through the wood. Squirrel saw him and helped. Soon birds came down from the trees, and then the mice joined in too. Together, they finished the trail to the rabbit’s new burrow. The rabbits’ home was warm and smelled like blackberry pie. The friends sat by the fire, ate pie, and sang Christmas songs. Then snow fell softly, and the arrows disappeared. Fletcher became worried again. He asked everyone to stay awake and help Father Christmas find the burrow. But one by one, the animals fell asleep. Father Christmas came anyway. The next morning, the rabbits were happy because Father Christmas had found them, and all their friends came to share the bright, warm burrow.

She got a new idea, went back to work, and soon students came to listen. In the end, Penelope smiled and invited everyone to come back for Penelope story time the next day.

summary_text: There was a house on a hill, and the house felt worried because no one lived in it. It saw cobwebs, dust, squeaky doors, rattling pipes, and stairs that creaked. The house thought it might be haunted and tried very hard to stay still, quiet, and calm so no one would notice how spooky it was. Then the wind came. It made the house rustle, scratch, flicker, and howl through the roof. When the wind stopped, the house was quiet again, but it still felt lonely. The house decided it needed people who would like a spooky house. Soon, a family came up the hill and went inside. They made themselves at home, and the house was happy to be haunted.

summary_text: Sophie was having tea with her mummy in the kitchen when someone rang the door. Sophie opened the door and found a big furry stripy tiger. The tiger said he was very hungry and asked to have tea. Sophie's mummy said he could come in. The tiger sat at the table and ate all the sandwiches, buns, biscuits, and cake. Then he drank all the milk and tea. After that, he looked around and ate the supper in the saucepans, the food in the fridge, and the packets and tins in the cupboard. He also drank all the orange juice, daddy's beer, and the water in the tap. Sophie could not have her bath because there was no water. When daddy came home, Sophie and her mummy told him what had happened. Daddy said they should go to a cafe. They put on their coats, walked out in the dark, and ate supper with sausages, chips, and ice cream. They also bought a big tin of Tiger food, but the tiger never came back.

The little hedgehog, Hedgie, saw what was happening and offered to help. The next mornings, Penny and Hedgie gave Tompton an acorn, a strawberry, a mushroom, and a potato instead of an egg. Each time he cooked the food and ate it, but he woke up hungry again. At last Hedgie hid in a straw nest. Tompton grabbed him, got stuck on his prickles, and ran home. After that, Penny’s eggs hatched into five baby chicks, and Tompton went back to eating porridge.

summary_text: Poppy Caldwell lived at Thursday’s Hope, a group home, and every time she looked in a mirror she saw a smiling girl standing behind her. The girl wore a white pinafore and dark dress, and Poppy believed she might be a ghost or angel. When Poppy asked her bunkmate Ashley about it, Ashley laughed and told others, and soon Poppy was called “crazy poppy.” The teasing got worse, but the mirror girl became Poppy’s comfort. The girl sometimes took strange objects from her pockets, and the next morning Poppy found them under her pillow. Poppy hid these treasures, but Ashley stole and destroyed some of them. After Ashley found a charcoal sketch Poppy had hidden, Poppy smashed Ashley’s favorite mirror in anger. She was sent to Miss Tate’s office, where she found her own file and a letter from Great-Aunt Delfina at Larkspur House. Miss Tate said the letter looked like a joke. That night the mirror girl was gone for the first time, and Poppy later thought she did not need her anymore, but she was wrong.

summary_text: Marcus Geller could hear music that no one else seemed to notice, and he often tried to play along with it. At home, practicing the cello was hard because he lived with three older siblings and had little privacy. It was even harder because his mother became upset when he played. Marcus knew his mother was worried about her younger brother Shane, who had also been a very talented cellist and had died at age 12, the same age Marcus was now. Marcus could not stop playing, because the music in his head would become too strong. When he was younger, he had talked about the music all the time, but after a doctor suggested medicine, he kept it secret and began copying the melodies on any instrument he could find. This made his parents less worried and brought attention from teachers. Later, his mother brought him a letter from Larkspur Academy in New York State, inviting him to study there for free after a scout heard his recital in Ohio. Marcus was amazed, and then he heard an even louder, stranger burst of music that his mother could not hear.

Max gets into the car and says, "Bye bye, Grandpa! Bye bye, moon!" As the car drives away, Max keeps watching Grandpa until he is gone and only the moon is left. On the ride home, the road turns and curves, but the moon seems to follow Max. It peeks through trees, goes over a bridge, past cows, through a town, and even at a tunnel. Then dark clouds cover the sky, and Max cannot see the moon. When he gets home, he thinks the moon will not shine for him all the way home. In bed, he feels lonely and misses Grandpa. Then the clouds move away, the moon comes back, and soft yellow light fills his room. Max remembers Grandpa's words and falls asleep peacefully.

summary_text: The story explains that there is a peaceful spot and an anxiety spot. The anxiety spot shows up when a person feels worried, nervous, anxious, or scared. It can appear when trying new things, like playing soccer or taking a test, and it often asks, “What if?” The story says you can answer, “I can do this,” to help turn the anxiety spot into a peaceful spot. Small anxiety spots can help sometimes, but big worries can make a person miss fun things. The story also says anxiety can cause a tummy ache or sweating. Eating healthy food, getting enough rest, and using music, drawing, or writing can help keep anxiety small. When worries grow fast, a child can use a hand trick, say the calming words, and take deep breaths to blow the worry away.

summary_text: When the Berlin Wall rises suddenly, 12-year-old Gera’s family is split apart overnight. Gera, her mother, and her brother Fritz stay on the Eastern side, which is controlled by the Soviets. Her father and middle brother are on the western side after going there to look for work, and they cannot come back home. Gera knows it is dangerous to watch the wall and to think about Freedom, but she still looks. She sees East German soldiers with guns guarding their own people and watching for any attempt to escape. Gera, her family, and their neighbors feel trapped in their own city. One day, Gera sees her father on a viewing platform on the western side. He makes a strange, phantom-like dance, and Gera believes he is telling her and Fritz to tunnel under the wall to escape East Berlin. She knows being caught could mean death, but she must decide whether to trust the message.

At the end, they look at another animal and argue again, saying it is an ant eater or a brachiosaurus.

summary_text: A prince wanted to marry a real princess. He traveled all over the world, but he could not find one he knew was real. He came home feeling unhappy. One night, a terrible storm came. A girl knocked at the city gate and said she was a princess. She was soaked from the rain, with water in her hair, clothes, and shoes. The old queen wanted to find out if the girl was truly a princess. She put one pea on a bed, covered it with 20 mattresses, and placed 20 feather beds on top. The girl slept there. In the morning, she said she had hardly slept because something hard had made her black and blue. The family knew she was a real princess. The prince asked her to marry him, and the pea was placed in the royal museum.

summary_text: Mr. Haktak and Mrs. Hacktack are an old, poor couple who live in a small hut and grow food in a tiny garden. One day, Mr. Haktak finds a heavy brass pot. When Mrs. Hacktack drops her hairpin into it, the pot makes two hairpins and two purses. The purses each contain five gold coins. The couple tests the pot with a coat and gets two coats. Then they put ten coins into one purse and receive two purses with ten coins each. They work all night and become rich. But trouble begins when Mrs. Hacktack falls into the pot and a second Mrs. Hacktack appears. Mr. Haktak falls in too, and another Mr. Haktak comes out. Mrs. Hacktack decides the extra people can become family. The couples build two homes and become good friends, while carefully avoiding the brass pot.

summary_text: There were three bears: papa bear, mama bear, and baby bear. They lived in a little house in the forest. They had three chairs, three bowls, and three beds. summary_text: Mila lives with her big brother, Luca, and her little sister, Sophia. At the end, Daddy brings out Mila’s bike without training wheels. Mila falls, tries again, and then asks for help. Mommy and Daddy help her learn, and she rides on her own while everyone cheers.

summary_text: The story asks what makes a house special and shows that home is more than a building. Two cats live there, and home is a place where each one can be themselves. The story says that home is a special place held in the heart, so the cats stay close even when they must be apart. In the end, home is where they know they will see each other’s smiling faces, and the message is that home is where the heart is.

summary_text: Gritsch the witch woke up hungry and wanted piggy pie. She looked in her old hag cookbook and found the secret recipe. It needed many things, but the last ingredient was eight plump piggies. Gritsch did not have any piggies, so she tried to think of where to find some. She guessed the circus and the zoo, but those were wrong. Then she remembered the farm and found an ad for Old McDonald’s farm. She flew there on her broomstick. At the farm, she saw ducks, cows, and chickens, but no pigs. She asked each animal about the piggies, but each one said there were no piggies. Gritsch got more and more upset because she still wanted piggy pie. Then a wolf came along and said he was hungry too. He told Gritsch to forget the pigs. Gritsch invited the wolf home for lunch instead, and they walked away together, each thinking about eating the other.
