summary_text: The Little Red Hen lived on a farm with duck, cat, and pig. She worked hard every day, but the other animals were lazy and did not help her. One day, she found grains of wheat. She asked who would help plant them, but duck said, “Not I,” cat said, “Not I,” and pig said, “Not I.” So the Little Red Hen planted the wheat by herself. She watched it grow, pulled weeds, and waited until the wheat was tall and ripe. Then she asked who would help cut it, grind it into flour, make dough, and bake bread. Each time, the other animals said, “Not I,” and she did it all by herself. At last, when the bread was ready, the animals wanted to eat it. But the Little Red Hen said no. She had done all the work, so she ate the bread all by herself.

summary_text: On Halloween night, children dressed in costumes and walked outside to trick-or-treat. They saw pumpkins glowing and many ghosts, ghouls, and goblins all around town. Then they looked up and saw a magic witch in the sky on her broom. She waved her wand, and music started, so the spooky creatures began to dance. The children learned that the witch had brought the creatures, so they made traps to catch her and send the ghouls back. The witch was very clever and brought even more monsters, like zombies, dinos, ghosts, and wolves. The children tried to make better traps before time ran out. The witch explored their dad’s toolbox, but she knew it was a trap and sent a bat in first. In the end, the dance party ended, the witch opened a portal, and all the monsters left in a flash. The children said happy Halloween and goodbye until next year.

summary_text: Deep in the woods, an old white cabin held three friends: a cat, a squirrel, and a duck. The cat sliced the pumpkin, the squirrel stirred the water, and the duck added the salt to make pumpkin soup. They ate the soup, played music, and slept in a quilt made by all three. One morning, the duck woke early and wanted to be the head cook. He took the squirrel’s spoon and said he should stir the soup. The squirrel and cat said no, and they all had a big fight. The duck packed a wheelbarrow and left. The cat and squirrel looked for him in the pumpkin patch and in the dark woods, but they could not find him. Their soup became too salty, and they cried. At last they found the duck back at the cabin. They cooked together again, and the duck stirred while the others let him help. The soup was good, and peace returned to the cabin.

In the end, everyone lived happily ever after.

summary_text: When spring winds warm the earth, a farmer plants hundreds of pumpkin seeds in dark, moist soil. The seeds crack open underground, and roots grow down while stems send green shoots up through the earth. In less than two weeks, tiny seedlings appear. Two seed leaves open and reach toward the sun. The leaves use sunlight, water from the soil, and air to make sugar, which feeds the plant. Soon the seed leaves dry up, and broad prickly leaves unfold. The farmer keeps weeds out because weeds take water from the soil that pumpkin plants need. The stems do not stand tall; they spread across the ground and form tangled vines. Flower buds appear, and bright orange flowers open. Bees carry pollen from male flowers to female flowers, and then tiny hard fruits begin to grow. All summer, warm sun and rain help the fruits grow bigger. By autumn, the green pumpkins turn yellow and then orange. After about four months, the patch is full of ripe pumpkins.

Mr. Ray explained how Eddie glowed. Then Eddie showed everyone his family in the cave. Nemo did not find a shell, but Mr. Ray said he still got an A in exploring.

summary_text: The story teaches that monsters can be noisy, messy, hungry, selfish, mean, wild, tired, or grumpy, and children can help them behave. If a monster is noisy, whisper, “Be quiet.” If it is hungry, give it a fork and a spoon and say, “Chew your food.” If it is selfish, say, “Take turns.” If it is mean, walk away and say, “Good bye.” If it scares you, scare it back and say, “Boo.” If it makes a mess, say, “Clean up.” If it is wild, give it a timeout and say, “Sit still.” If it is tired and grumpy, send it to bed and say, “Go to sleep.” If it asks nicely, kiss it and say, “Good night.” The story says that next time you catch a monster running wild, you will know what to do.

At last, she swallowed a cow. But then she coughed and coughed, and all her new friends flew out.

summary_text: The story explains that mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment, both inside our bodies and around us. It says breathing is the main tool for practicing mindfulness. First, it shows how mindfulness can help with focus, stress, and calm. Then it teaches a game called Rainstorm. Children rub their hands for wind, tap slowly for rain, clap for lightning, stomp for thunder, and then slow down until everything is quiet. After that, it shows Funny Breath, where children sit tall, make bunny paws, and take quick bunny breaths. Next comes Scrunch and Let Go, where children squeeze their toes, legs, belly, arms, hands, and face, then breathe out and relax. It also teaches Hot Chocolate, where children blow on an imaginary cup, and Bear Breath, where children breathe slowly like a bear in a cave. At the end, it asks children to think of kind things they have done and kind things they can do next time.

summary_text: The story explains that mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment, including what is happening in our bodies and around us right now. It says that breathing is the main tool for practicing mindfulness. The book Breathe Like a Bear shows simple exercises that can help children focus in school, let go of stress, and calm down when they feel hyper or fidgety. The first exercise is Rainstorm. Children rub their hands for wind, tap slowly for rain, clap for lightning, and stomp for thunder. Then they slow down until everything is still and quiet, and they take a long breath in and out. The next exercise is Funny Breath, where children sit up tall, make bunny paws, take quick little breaths, and then let the air out. They can also feel their belly move. The third exercise is Scrunch and Let Go, where children tighten their toes, legs, belly, arms, hands, and face, then breathe out and relax. These exercises help prepare them for calm breathing activities like Hot Chocolate and Bear Breath.

summary_text: A young man walked all day and all night until he was tired and hungry. He came to a big house and knocked on the door. A little old lady opened it, but she said she had no food to give him. The young man asked for something to do and said he could make soup from a stone. The old lady was surprised, but she let him use a pot. She filled it with water and put it on the fire. The young man dropped a round gray stone into the pot and asked for more things to make the soup better. One by one, the old lady added onions, carrots, beef bones, pepper, salt, butter, and barley. The soup bubbled and grew thicker and better. At last they ate it together. Before he left, the young man took the stone from the pot, put it in his pocket, and said he would cook it more tomorrow.

summary_text: Mera rode in Granddad’s car to his home beside Larima, a lake with a little island and his pet otter, Cara. The lake was usually normal, but sometimes it disappeared completely, and then rain filled it up again. Mera asked Granddad where the water went, and he gave funny answers about sheep, mermaids, narwhals, and Giants from Over the Mountain. Mera looked for clues on the dry lake bed and stayed awake to catch the lake vanishing, but she never did. At last, she said it was a mystery and did not care anymore. Granddad took her up the mountain and gave her binoculars. They waited until Mera saw a huge herd of mammoths drinking at the lake. The mammoths made the whole lake dry up and then left. Granddad told Mera to keep it a secret, and as they walked home, it began to rain.

summary_text: A group of pencils talked about their hard life at school. They said students often tossed them, rolled them, snapped them, chewed on them, bent them, and left them in bins. The pencils said they were important because they help students write, fix mistakes, and work on paper, but they still did not get kind treatment. While the students were at lunch, the pencils got together and wrote a letter with their complaints. They said they would go on strike and not take the rough treatment anymore. When the students came back, a young girl read the letter first. Her eyes filled with tears, and she said the pencils were right. She told the others to treat the pencils better and practice using them carefully. One by one, the students began to handle the pencils with more care. The story ends by reminding readers to use school supplies gently so they will last and be ready when needed.

At last, zero jumped up and landed on top of the tree, and when zero joined with ten, there was 100. Then all the numbers came back out and shouted happily.

The next January, hermit crab leaves and finds another big empty shell.

summary_text: Chester liked doing things the same way every day. He cut sandwiches diagonally, got out of bed on the same side, tied his shoes in double knots, ate toast with jam and peanut butter, and carried a tiny first-aid kit. His best friend Wilson was just like him, and they did many things together. They played baseball, rode bikes with hand signals, dressed alike for Halloween, and shared picnics in every season. Then Lilly moved into the neighborhood. Lilly did things her own way, too. She wore band-aids, talked backwards, used disguises, waved at cars, and carried a squirt gun. At first, Chester and Wilson hid from her. One day, older boys bothered them, and a fierce cat scared the boys away. The cat was Lilly in disguise. After that, Chester, Wilson, and Lilly became friends. They shared lunch, sleepovers, and new ideas. They taught each other hand signals, wheelies, backwards talk, and double-knotting shoes.

summary_text: Mr. Spivy was angry and scared when he saw the broom acting in strange ways. He called it wicked and told others it was dangerous. But the broom kept working hard on the widow Mina Shaw’s farm. It swept the road and even played the piano with one note at a time. One day, two of the Spivy boys and their dog bothered the broom on the dirt road. The boys kicked stones into its path, called it names, and tapped it with sticks. The broom finally turned and knocked both boys down. When the dog chased and bit at it, the broom was still not harmed. That evening, Mr. Spivy and three other men came to the widow’s house with rope and a stake. Mina said they should take the broom away. The men tied it up, burned it, and turned it to ashes. After that, people found the dog safe in a tree, and life seemed normal again.

summary_text: Fletcher the fox went out every day to visit his favorite tree. One morning he saw that the green forest was changing and the tree’s leaves were turning brown. Fletcher worried and told Mummy that his tree was ill. Mummy said it was only autumn. Fletcher tried to help by tying a leaf back on with grass and then pushing it onto a twig, but the leaf still fell. The next day, a strong wind blew. Fletcher chased leaves as the squirrel took some for a nest and the hedgehog took some to keep warm. Fletcher cried out that they were stealing the leaves. Then friendly birds came and put the leaves back on the branches. Fletcher thanked them and fell asleep under the tree. Later, the wind blew all the leaves away again. Fletcher found one last leaf, held it through the wind, and carried it home when it came off. In the cold morning, he saw the tree covered with shining icicles and knew it was beautiful in winter too.

Dad reminds her that she kindly cared for Stella and that Stella will not forget her. The name Stella means star, so Olive can remember her by looking at the sky each night.

summary_text: Many years ago, there was a small boy in a tribe who was called Little Gopher. He could not ride and shoot like the other boys, but he loved to decorate stones with berry juice. The wise shaman saw that Little Gopher had a special gift and told him his path would be different from the warriors. When Little Gopher went to the hills alone, he had a dream vision. A young Indian maiden and an old grandfather came to him and gave him tools for painting. The maiden showed him a pure white buckskin and told him to find one like it. After the dream ended, Little Gopher made brushes and paints and began painting hunts and visions. He found a white buckskin, but he could not make the colors of the sunset. One evening, a voice said he would find the colors because he had been faithful. The next night, sunset-colored brushes appeared, and he painted quickly. In the morning, the brushes had grown into bright flowers, and the people gave him a new name: He who brought the sunset to the earth.

but he had a special gift for decorating stones with berry juice.
The tribe’s shaman saw this gift
and told him not to follow the same path as the warriors.
When Little Gopher went alone into the hills to think about becoming a man,
he had a dream vision.
A maiden and an old grandfather appeared
and told him he would become great by painting the deeds of warriors and the visions of the shaman.
The maiden showed him a pure white buckskin
and said to find one like it.
Later, Little Gopher made brushes and paints,
but his work was not complete until a voice told him he would find the colors he sought.
One evening he found sunset-colored brushes on the hill,
painted the buckskin,
and left the brushes behind.
The next day, the brushes had grown into bright flowers.
After that, the people called him “He who brought the sunset to the earth.”

summary_text: Three baby owls, Sarah, Percy, and Bill, lived with their owl mother in a hole in a tree. One night they woke up and found that their mother was gone. Sarah said she was hunting for food, Percy agreed, and Bill said, “I want my mummy!” The baby owls came out of their home and waited on the tree. Sarah sat on a big branch, Percy on a small branch, and Bill on an old bit of ivy. It was dark in the wood, and they stayed brave while they waited. They moved together onto one branch and thought about where their mother might be. Sarah worried she could be lost, and Percy wondered if a fox got her. Bill still said, “I want my mummy!” Then they closed their eyes and wished for her return. Soon their mother came softly through the trees. The baby owls cried “Mummy!” and flapped and danced. Their mother was back, and Bill said, “I love my mummy!”

But Adella says the bubbles went away on their own. Ariel keeps the pearl in her treasure grotto.

In the next spring, everyone in the neighborhood planted Chinese vegetables, and the whole street smelled like soup.

summary_text: It was his first year on the island, and everything was fine until the first leaf fell. He asked, “Are you okay?” Then a red leaf fell and a yellow leaf fell all over the island. He tried to catch the leaves and put them back on the tree, but it did not work. He sat under the tree and watched the leaves blow around. Soon he grew sleepy. He found a hole, filled it with leaves, and went to sleep just as the wind began to blow. Winter came, and he slept snug in the ground while snow piled up thick above him. In spring, he woke with wide eyes. He felt the sun and saw little buds on the bare trees and tiny leaves opening. He cried, “Welcome!” and thought the leaves welcomed him.

summary_text: Miss Spider wanted friends, so she made tea and set out chairs, cakes, cups, and plates. Beetles, fireflies, bumblebees, rubber bugs, ants, butterflies, and moths saw her web or her many legs and hurried away. Miss Spider felt sad because no bug would stay. Then a little moth came in from the rain. The moth was wet, and his wings were too damp to fly. Miss Spider gently covered him with a checkered cloth. They talked and ate tea and pie until his wings were dry. Miss Spider carefully tossed him into the air. The moth told Ike, and Ike told May, that Miss Spider had never meant to hurt anyone. Soon, eleven insects came to Miss Spider’s tea party. They saw her drink tea and eat flowers. Before long, Miss Spider knew all the bugs and their children, and she had the friends she wanted.

summary_text: At the zoo, Chip worked every night to stop the usual chaos. The mice often escaped first, which scared the elephants, then the birds flew out, and the tigers tried to break free. Chip had a plan for all of it. He fed the tigers, guided the birds back to their aviary, calmed the elephants with a pillow, and lured the mice back with cheese. But one night, the trouble was worse than ever. It came from Pete, a grumpy pirate penguin with an eye patch and an army of alligators. Pete wanted to escape the zoo by causing enough trouble to make the animals crash through the gates. His plan used snakes, flamingos, and a giant snowball. Chip stopped him by calling in air support, sending fish to distract the alligators, and placing bananas so the snowball missed the hippo pool. Pete failed, and the next morning the zoo opened safely.

summary_text: Elmer was a special elephant covered in many bright colors. He made the other elephants happy with games and jokes, but Elmer was not happy because he thought they might laugh at his patchwork body. One morning, he left the herd and found a bush full of berries the color of elephants. He shook the bush, rolled in the berries, and rubbed berry juice all over himself. Soon he looked like an ordinary elephant. When he returned, the elephants stood very still and serious. Elmer wanted to make them laugh, so he shouted, “Boo!” Everyone jumped, and then everyone laughed. Rain fell and washed away the berry juice, showing Elmer’s bright colors again. The elephants said his joke was the biggest laugh of all. They decided to celebrate Elmer every year with a colorful parade.

Mouse said he would help Bear find a book about pickles,

summary_text: A brave Knight wanted Glory and Treasure, so he went on a quest with a fierce and friendly detective. At first, they lost the treasure map and searched for it. They found it folded in the Knight’s pocket, and then the Knight led the way. They rode on his Noble rocket and went into space, but they did not find any treasure. On the way back to Earth, the rocket spun and crashed into the ocean. The Knight and the detective stayed safe, climbed onto a pirate ship, and met Pirates who were ready to Dance. The Knight used a pillow to distract it, and the detective tickled it. The Beast moved away, and they opened the chest. Inside, they found more treasure maps and started a new quest.

summary_text: An old woman lives in a small house with her very big family. Winter is coming, and she needs to knit, but her grandchildren keep asking questions about her yarn. She becomes very tired of the interruptions, packs her things in a big sack, and calls, “Leave me alone!” She goes into a dark forest, but a bear family comes near her fire. She leaves and climbs a mountain. Mountain goats visit her and fight over snacks, so she leaves again. The woman climbs all the way to the moon. Little green moon men examine her, but they cannot hear her because they have no ears. She travels through a wormhole to a dark, quiet void. There, she knits 30 little sweaters without anyone disturbing her. She puts the sweaters in her sack, drinks tea, and returns through another wormhole. Everything is where she left it, and she says nothing.

summary_text: Tai Singh was born in the mountains near Virginia City, Nevada, and grew up speaking and writing in both English and Chinese. In America, many Chinese people were treated unfairly, but Tai Singh wanted a bigger life. He became a trail cook for map makers and earned a name as the best trail cook in California. In 1915, Stephen Mather hired him for a special camping trip with writers, business leaders, congress members, and a movie star. Mather wanted them to see the beauty of wild places and support a national park service. Tai Singh planned meals for 30 people for 10 days and cooked breakfast, lunch, and dinner while traveling from campsite to campsite. He and Eugene packed, unpacked, washed dishes, and kept the food fresh. When a mule once wandered off with fancy food, Tai Singh made new plans and served a simpler meal. After other accidents, he still fed everyone well. At the end, he gave each camper a fortune cookie with a message about the mountains. Later, Congress created the national park service, and Sing Peak was named for him.

summary_text: On a fine spring day in Bear Country, Mama Bear noticed that Brother Bear and Sister Bear came home from school and went straight to the TV with their milk and cookies. Papa Bear joined them later, and Mama saw that the whole family was watching too much television. The bears used to talk at dinner and play outside, but now they sat and watched shows all the time. That night, Mama said there would be no TV for a whole week. The cubs were upset, and Papa first tried to argue, but Mama said he had to stop too. The next day, Mama sent Brother and Sister outside to ride their bikes and trikes. At night, the family sat under the stars, watched bats fly, and saw the sky fill with stars. During the week, they also went on a nature walk, watched tadpoles hatch, saw an orb spider spin a web, and visited the Bear Country Mall. When the week ended, the family talked happily at dinner. Brother asked about TV, and Mama said the problem was the TV habit. The next day, the others found other things to do, and Papa finally went fishing.

summary_text: Rabbit loved carrots very much. He picked up carrots everywhere he went and filled his cozy burrow with them. Soon there were so many carrots that Rabbit could not sleep in his hole. Rabbit wanted to bring more carrots again, but the rain started, Beaver’s house collapsed, and everyone ended up on the riverbank. Rabbit saw that his friends were cold, tired, and without homes, and he still had all the carrots.

summary_text: Mickey Mouse loves animals, so he agrees to watch Mr. Palmer’s pet shop for one night. Mr. Palmer leaves and says he will be back tomorrow afternoon. Mickey looks at the animals, but one little puppy keeps whimpering. Mickey takes the puppy out, but the puppy runs to the fishbowl, knocks it over, and sends the fish flying. Mickey catches the fish and puts it in a new bowl. Then a customer comes in, and Mickey forgets to lock the kennel door. The puppy gets out again and frees the mice, so the customer runs away. Mickey puts the pets back and locks the kennel this time. That night the puppy howls, so Mickey lets him sleep under the covers. In the morning the shop is messy, and Mickey finds the puppy in the basement. Mickey cleans up, and the puppy helps him sweep and dust. Mr. Palmer returns, gives Mickey his paycheck, and thanks him. Mickey takes the puppy instead of the money and names him Pluto.

and wants to leave his snowy home
because a huge snowbank blocks the front door.
Escaro digs through the snow
and asks about jokes and facts
while he searches for spring.
Soon he sees that the snowbank is not a snowbank at all.
It is a bunny rabbit.
Escaro does not want the bunny in his book
and says he will go on alone.
The bunny stays,
so Escaro goes into his shell
and then agrees to have a hopping contest.
He hops very high,
all the way to the Moon,
and wins.
After that, Escaro realizes he may not have unwe after all.
He may just be hungry.
Then the sun shines,
the birds sing,
the snow melts,
and flowers appear.
Escaro invites the bunny to eat the flowers with him.

summary_text: Escargo is a very beautiful French snail who is going to the library to check out a French cookbook. While he travels, he talks about books, stories, and how there are many books about other animals, but none about a brave snail hero. Escargo decides to write a story with the reader’s help, just like cooking from a recipe. He says the main character should be a French snail hero with a shiny brown shell and translucent tentacles. In the end, Escargo is not eaten, and he says he has saved the day.

summary_text: Cookie is an elf who makes toys, but she wants to invent toys instead. She thinks of a flying race car, a tidy-up robot, and a safe jetpack. The Chief Elf Officer tells her that inventing is not her job. Then, just before Christmas, the sleigh-loading machine breaks. The elves cannot fix it, and Christmas is very close. Cookie has an idea, but the others do not listen at first. She works all night and makes a plan. Pudding secretly gives the plan to Santa. The CEO learns that Santa likes the plan and lets Cookie try. Cookie makes Lifter Gifts that carry presents to the sleigh. She also makes robots to clean the workshop. The elves work very fast, and Santa is ready on time. Cookie becomes the Chief Inventor, and every elf may choose the job that brings the most joy.

summary_text: Every summer, children came to Camp Horizon on Lake oh my gosh in New Hampshire. Felix and Harry had gone there for many years and liked swimming, diving, horseback riding, horseshoes, and board games. One day after lunch, they decided to take a rowboat out on the lake. The camp rules said to wear life preservers, stay where the camp could still be seen, and never go out in bad weather. Felix and Harry were in a hurry, so they forgot the life preservers and rowed away from shore. Soon the wind pushed them farther out, and they could not get back. It got dark, cold, and rainy, and the boat rocked hard. Then the boat broke apart, and the boys fell into the water. They were tired and could not see the shore. Just when they were sinking, something lifted them up and carried them back to land. When they looked back at the lake, they thought they saw a huge turtle with a long neck diving under the water.

summary_text: The story says many kinds of living things have teeth, like uncles, policemen, zebras, unicycle riders, and little girls named Ruthie. Teeth are found in many places, even underground, and in all directions. Mr. Donald Driscoll Drew says teeth help people chew. Smiling Sam the Crocodile says teeth help him smile. Hi Trapezer Mike Macabre says teeth help him with his job. Quincy Quick says teeth help him speak, and without them he would sound like ducks. Simon Snead the snail has no teeth, and Pam the Clam says she cannot eat many foods without teeth. Jimbo Jones says teeth are needed to play trombones. Hilda Hen says both women and men have teeth, and children grow two sets. They lose the first set and then grow 32 new teeth. The story ends by warning not to ruin teeth by chewing trees, breaking them on knots, or biting bottle tops. It says to keep teeth safe and be kind to the dentist.

summary_text: A scout finds a beautiful sparkling crystal and brings it to the ant queen. She loves its taste, so many ants travel through the dark woods and climb a huge mountain to find more. They reach a strange place filled with crystals. Most ants take one crystal and go home, but two ants stay because they want to eat crystals forever. Soon, a giant scoop lifts them into the air and drops them into a boiling brown lake. The ants struggle through waves, a whirlpool, heat, rushing water, spinning food, and a strange force in narrow holes. Exhausted, they sleep. At night, their fellow ants return. The two ants join the line, each take only one crystal, and follow their friends home. They hear their family below and feel happy because they understand that their true home is with their ant family and queen.

summary_text: Little Mae loved to dream. For a school assignment, she said she wanted to see earth from out there in space. Her mother told her that to do that, she would need to become an astronaut. Mae asked if she could do that, and her mother and father told her that if she could dream it, believe it, and work hard for it, anything was possible. Mae went to the library, looked at books about space, drew pictures, and made an astronaut costume from orange curtains and cardboard boxes. That night she dreamed of dancing in space and seeing earth like a shining ball. The next day at school, Mae shared her dream, but the other children laughed. Miss Bell told her she could be a nurse instead. Mae felt sad and cried at home. Her mother comforted her and told her to keep following her dream. Mae kept dreaming, believing, and working hard, and in the end she went to space and waved to her mom and dad from the spaceship.

summary_text: Officer Buckle knew more safety tips than anyone in Naville, and he kept each new one on his bulletin board. He gave safety speeches at Naville School, but the students never listened, and sometimes they even snored. That changed when the police department bought a police dog named Gloria. Gloria went with Officer Buckle to the school, and when he said, “Gloria sit!” she sat down. The children became interested as Officer Buckle shared tips like keeping shoelaces tied, wiping up spills, and never leaving a thumbtack where someone might sit on it. They laughed, clapped, and cheered, and there were no accidents after the speech. The next day the police station received many thank-you letters, including one from Claire. Soon other schools asked Officer Buckle and Gloria to come speak, and they visited 313 schools. Later, after a television appearance, Officer Buckle stopped giving speeches when he thought no one listened to him. When Gloria came alone to Naville School, everyone fell asleep. Afterward, the school had a terrible accident with banana pudding, and the students sent more letters. Claire wrote again, saying Gloria missed him. Officer Buckle then learned his best safety tip: always stick with your buddy.

segments.text: Officer Buckle knew more safety tips than anyone in Naville,
and he kept each new one on his bulletin board.
He gave safety speeches at Naville School,
but the students never listened,
and sometimes they even snored.
That changed when the police department bought a police dog named Gloria.
Gloria went with Officer Buckle to the school,
and when he said, “Gloria sit!”
she sat down.
The children became interested
as Officer Buckle shared tips like keeping shoelaces tied,
wiping up spills,
and never leaving a thumbtack where someone might sit on it.
They laughed,
clapped,
and cheered,
and there were no accidents after the speech.
The next day the police station received many thank-you letters,
including one from Claire.
Soon other schools asked Officer Buckle and Gloria to come speak,
and they visited 313 schools.
Later, after a television appearance,
Officer Buckle stopped giving speeches
when he thought no one listened to him.
When Gloria came alone to Naville School,
everyone fell asleep.
Afterward, the school had a terrible accident with banana pudding,
and the students sent more letters.
Claire wrote again,
saying Gloria missed him.
Officer Buckle then learned his best safety tip:
always stick with your buddy.

summary_text: This story tells about little presidents who lead the country and help people. George Washington was the first president of the United States. John Adams was the first one to live in the White House. Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence and liked books, art, and inventions. Abraham Lincoln kept the states together and set people free. Ulysses S. Grant rode horses well and made Christmas a federal holiday. Theodore Roosevelt made national parks and saved forest land. Franklin D. Roosevelt gave jobs to Americans and was the first president in a wheelchair. John F. Kennedy sent the first astronaut into outer space. Ronald Reagan was a movie star and helped bring people together. Barack Obama was the first African American president, and the story says anything can happen in the USA.

summary_text: The dinos love donuts. They dip them in jelly, add sprinkles, and eat the glazed and cake-crumb ones. They eat donuts because they are good for prey and help dinos see danger far away while they eat sweet dough all day. The dinos also like the holes, because the holes fit on horns and spikes, and a stick can help reach them. But the dinos love dancing even more than donuts. They dance from dawn to dusk and all through the night. Triceratops, raptors, Stegosaurus, Brontosaurus, and Pterodactyl all dance in different ways. Their dancing makes the palm trees shake, their footprints make pools, and dust floats like wigs around their heads. The dinos wait in line for donuts because they need a lot of food. A child makes a giant donut for the dino dance. The dinos love it, but they do not like the center hole, because they fear rocks. If a rock gets on the dance floor, a dino can step on it and get hurt.

summary_text: Nimbus was born high in the sky. She had wide feathered wings and loved the clouds, but sometimes the sky felt empty. When that happened, she traced pictures in the stars and dreamed of having company. One night, a wishing star shot across the sky, but Nimbus did not have time to make her wish. She flew down to the place where the star had fallen. On the ground, she met a sparkling creature named Kelp. Nimbus told Kelp about her search, and Kelp wanted to help. Nimbus looked high, and Kelp looked low, but they did not find the star. Then Kelp asked his friends for help. His pointy friends searched everywhere, but the star was still missing. Nimbus thanked them and flew back to the sky. There, she saw that her new memories and new constellations made the sky feel less empty. She thought her wish may have already come true.

Then Mr. Gramzy brings them a real egg that needs care. Roy and Silo take turns keeping it warm, turning it, and sitting with it day and night. After a while, the egg cracks open, and a baby penguin comes out. They name her Tango. Roy and Silo feed her, sing to her, and snuggle her. Tango grows strong, swims with them, and the children at the zoo cheer for the family.

One day he met a parrot, who asked why he was shaking the jungle and what kind of animal he was. The elephant said he lived alone and called himself Suki. Then a tiger came by and said exercise might help, so Suki ran, rolled, and walked in different ways. After that, the parrot told him to soak in the river like a crocodile. They told Suki he was a perfectly dandy little elephant, and Suki danced happily with them while the parrot watched.

Mama put medicine on the sore fingers and tape on all of them. The tape helped Sister remember, but it also made things hard. Other cubs teased her, so Sister pulled off the tape and started nibbling again. Mama explained that a habit is something you do so often you do it בלי thinking. Papa first wanted to scold her, then he and Mama tried giving her pennies for each day she did not nibble. That did not work well. Then Gran suggested giving Sister 10 pennies at the start of each day. This plan worked better. Sister still had to give back some pennies, but after 10 days she had many pennies and all 10 fingernails back.

summary_text: Mr. Hatch was a tall, thin man who did not smile. Every day he went to the shoelace Factory, ate lunch alone, bought a newspaper and a turkey wing, then read and went to bed early. One Saturday, he found a brown package on his porch from Mr. Goober the postman. Inside was a heart-shaped red box of candy and a card that said, “Somebody loves you. You only.” Mr. Hatch was amazed because he thought he had no friends. He laughed, dressed up, and started acting in new ways. He helped Mr. Smith at the newsstand, found little Melanie Todd for Mr. Todd, and baked brownies for the neighborhood. Soon children and parents came to his house for brownies, lemonade, and music. Later, Mr. Goober returned and said the Valentine had been delivered to the wrong house. Mr. Hatch felt sad and stopped smiling. But his neighbors remembered how kind he had been. They filled his porch with hearts, candy, streamers, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.” Then Mr. Hatch smiled and laughed and joined his friends.

and found no crumbs left.

summary_text: People make quick guesses about others. They think a small boy cannot play basketball, but he gets the ball in the hoop and everyone cheers. The child does robotics and is called brilliant. Another person says a girl cannot join a relay race because she is a special kid, but she runs and people cheer. Finally, people think a boy cannot sing, but he surprises them. The story shows that people may be wrong when they judge others. Everyone is fantastic, so we should think carefully and be thoughtful.

summary_text: Marisol was an artist who loved to draw and paint. She had her own art gallery, made posters, and believed everybody was an artist. When her teacher said the class would paint a mural for the library, Marisol was excited. The children talked, sketched, and made a big drawing before they went to the library. Marisol said she would paint the ocean, and other children said they would paint fish and the sky. But when Marisol looked for blue paint, she could not find any. She wondered how she could paint the sky without blue. The bell rang, and she had to stop for the day. On the bus ride home, she kept thinking about the missing blue paint. That night, she dreamed of a sky full of many colors. The next morning, it was raining, and the sky was not blue. Marisol went to school, mixed colors in a dish, made a new color called maricel, and painted the wall. When a boy asked what color it was, she said it was sky color.

summary_text: Ruth’s mother taught her to love books, to be kind, and to know that she was important just like a boy. Ruth grew up in a Jewish family that had come to the United States to be safe and free, but she still saw unfair treatment. Jewish people were not allowed in some places, and girls could not do the same things as boys. Ruth wanted to help change this. She studied hard, went to college, and learned about lawyers, who speak for people’s rights in court. After college, Ruth became a wife, a mother, and a law student. Many people did not want women at law school, but she worked very hard and did well. After law school, she could not find a job in New York City because she was a mother and Jewish, but she did not give up. She taught law, worked as a volunteer lawyer, and argued before the Supreme Court to help make laws fairer for women and men.

summary_text: On the far away island of Salamasand, Yertle the Turtle was king of a small, clean pond where the turtles had plenty to eat and were happy. But Yertle wanted to see more and be higher than everyone else. He ordered nine turtles to swim to his stone and stand one on top of another, making a nine-turtle stack for his throne. Yertle climbed up and bragged that he could now rule cows, mules, a house, a blueberry bush, and a cat. Then Mac, the turtle at the bottom, said his back, shoulders, and knees hurt. Yertle did not listen and ordered many more turtles to pile up. Mac and the others obeyed, and Yertle rose even higher. Mac asked for rights and food, but Yertle shouted back. When the moon rose, Yertle wanted to go higher still. Then Mac burped, the throne shook, and Yertle fell into the pond. Yertle became king of the mud, and all the turtles were free.

The pets stay at home, and everyone hopes there will be no more storms.

summary_text: Long ago, before the Civil War, an old sailor named Peg Leg Joe worked on a cotton plantation and helped enslaved people escape. At night, after work, he taught them a song called “Follow the Drinking Gourd,” which was really a secret map to freedom. One day, Molly saw that her husband James had been sold to another master. That night, Molly, James, their son Isaiah, old Hattie, and Hattie’s grandson George sang Joe’s song and followed the stars. They ran through fields, crossed a stream, and hid from the master’s hounds. For many nights and days, they traveled by the signs in the song, sometimes hungry and sometimes in danger. A farm boy once brought them food, and later they reached the Ohio River, where Peg Leg Joe was waiting. He carried them across and sent them to safe houses on the Underground Railroad. In the end, they reached Lake Erie, boarded a steamship, crossed to Canada, and were safe at last.

Otto the otter has visited the small pond near the grey house for a long time. The people there named him Otto and like to watch him swim, play, and eat. He comes often, but not every day, and after a few hours he leaves through a creek to another pond. At night he goes away, and the people do not know where he sleeps. One winter he stayed away for a long time, and when he came back in spring, he arrived with two babies. Then the people saw that Otto was really a girl, and they changed her name to Opal.

Opal’s babies are called pups. She kept them safe in a den when they were tiny. Later she brought them to the pond, taught them to swim, and showed them how to find food under the water. The pups played on the grass and on the turtle islands, while Opal watched them closely. As they grew, they traveled more and stayed less. The people hoped to see Opal and her pups for a long time.

then brought them to the pond.
She taught them to swim,
find food,
and stay close.
The pups grew,
played on turtle islands,
and began traveling with Opal to other ponds.

summary_text: Clark the Shark went to Theodore Roosterfish Elementary and loved school, lunch, and recess. He was the biggest and strongest fish, but he was also too loud and too wild. He shouted, munched too much lunch, and played too rough, so the other fish stopped sitting with him, eating with him, and playing with him. Clark asked Mrs. Inkydink what was wrong. She told him he needed to stay cool and remember that there is a time and a place for everything. Clark tried, but he kept forgetting. Then he made rhymes to help himself remember. He said, “When teacher’s talking, don’t go walking,” “Only munch your own lunch,” and “Easy does it, that’s the way.” These helped him behave better. Later, a scary new kid, Sid the Squid, came to school and made a mess. Clark helped him play safely and taught him to stay cool. Everyone cheered for Clark, and he told his mother what he learned.

summary_text: Bear was an easily scared bear. At night, he tied a bell to his door because he was afraid someone might sneak in, and he was even afraid of his own reflection. Because he could not see himself well, he did not brush his teeth well, and food stayed in his teeth. His only friend was Rabbit. Rabbit was not scared of anything. Bear wanted to read about adventures instead, but Rabbit kept asking if he was scared. Bear said no and went with her. They crossed a stream, went around a dark forest by bus, rode a train and helicopter over a mountain, and came to a rope bridge. Bear finally said he was scared of the bridge and went home. Then Rabbit fell through the bridge, and Bird woke Bear. Bear rushed out, crossed the stream, forest, and mountain quickly, and saved Rabbit. After that, Bear admitted he was scared, Rabbit said she was too, and Bear learned that sometimes it is okay to be scared.

summary_text: Snow falls from the winter night sky and drifts down through the sycamore branches. It lands on a husky’s tail, on a frozen pond, and near sleeping fish. The snow covers footprints, rocks, sticks, and the banks of a winter brook. Trees shake in the rising snowstorm, and an empty nest holds tight as the wind blows. The snow says hello to the storm and howls. Then morning comes. The orange hills glow, and the early light shines on everything. The snow begins to melt in the sun and turn to slush. Soon the winter thaw brings new leaves, waking animals, bright flowers, blue water, running brooks, and green grass. Robins come back, the petals bloom, the fish wake up, and streams run down the hills. In the end, winter is gone, and spring arrives.

summary_text: Trevor and his brother Sammy go with their neighbor to choose a Christmas tree. On the way home through the forest, their dog Tuffy barks and sniffs as if someone is watching them. Inside, two trolls are grabbing all the Christmas things and shouting, “Mine!” Trevor tells them the items belong to his family. The trolls want Christmas, so Trevor helps them clean their house, decorate it, and learn to share. He gives them his red horse, and they play together. The hedgehog returns the family’s gifts, and Trevor goes home. On Christmas morning, Trevor and Sammy find their tree lit with candles and their stockings full. Later, Trevor finds a present with a troll horse inside from Tig and Mig.

summary_text: Early one morning, Petunia the silly goose walked in the meadow and found a Book. She had seen a Book before under Bill’s arm, and she remembered hearing that Books are precious and that the one who loves Books is wise. Petunia thought that if she carried the Book and loved it, she would become wise too, and no one would call her silly again. So she took the Book and went off with it. She slept with it and swam with it, and soon she became proud. Her neck stretched longer and longer. The other animals saw her with the Book and believed she was wise. They asked her for advice, and Petunia liked giving it, even when no one asked. She gave wrong advice to King, Ida, Noisy, Straw, and Cotton, and each one had trouble because of what she said. At last, the animals opened a box of candies, and it exploded. Then Petunia saw the Book open and noticed she could not read the words. She understood she must learn to read to be truly wise.

The mechanic filled the tank, and the next day the boys wrote about Uncle Mickey’s car.

summary_text: Scaredy squirrel lives in his nut tree and never wants to leave. He likes his safe home, his nuts, and his familiar view. He is afraid of many things outside, like tarantulas, poison ivy, green martians, killer bees, germs, and sharks. Every day he follows the same routine: wake up, eat a nut, look at the view, eat more nuts, look again, and go to sleep. He also keeps an emergency kit ready with things like a parachute, bug spray, gloves, a hard hat, soap, and sardines. He has a plan for danger: panic, run, get kicked, put on the kit, and leave only if he must. He watches and waits, but one day a bee appears. When he jumps, his kit falls, and he grabs it. Then his parachute makes him glide, and he discovers he is a flying squirrel. After landing in a bush and playing dead, he waits, then returns home and changes his daily routine.

summary_text: One evening, Harold decided to go for a walk in the moonlight. There was no moon, so he drew one with his big purple crayon. He also drew a long straight path and a field, then a small forest with one tree. The tree was an apple tree, and Harold drew a scary dragon to guard the apples. The dragon frightened Harold, and he soon found himself over his head in an ocean. Harold made a trim little balloon, and the moon went with him as he sailed away. After landing on a beach, he made a picnic with nine kinds of pie. He shared the leftover pie with a hungry moose and a porcupine. Then he made a hill into a mountain, fell, and made another balloon and basket. He made a house, then a city of windows, and asked a policeman for help. At last he remembered his bedroom window was always around the moon. He made his bed and fell asleep.

summary_text: Goldie Luck was born in the year of the golden dragon, and her parents said she would have good luck and great wealth. But Goldie often had trouble keeping money and broke things. One Chinese New Year, her mother sent her next door to visit the Chans and bring turnip cakes. Goldie was sleepy and hungry, and she did not want to go. At the Chans’ apartment, no one answered the door, so she pushed it open and dropped the plate. The turnip cakes fell on the floor. In the kitchen, Goldie tasted three bowls of congee and ate the one that was just right. Then she tried three chairs and broke little Chan’s rocking chair. In the bedroom, she tried three beds and fell asleep on little Chan’s futon. When the Chans came home, they found the mess and Goldie sleeping. Goldie woke up, went home, and then came back to say sorry. She helped fix the chair and beds, and she and little Chan made more turnip cakes together. Mrs. Chan gave Goldie a red envelope, and Goldie ate turnip cakes with little Chan.

At the end, Taylor says many people have these toots, so they are tooting turkeys too, and he says toots are healthy.

summary_text: One cold morning, Dragon went into the crunchy snow to find the perfect Christmas tree. He looked at many trees, big and small, crooked and straight, until he found one that was just right. The tree had a strong brown trunk and green branches that waved in the cold December wind. Dragon could not cut down such a lovely tree, so he came back with colored lights and Silver Bells to make it even prettier. That night, he looked at his shining tree and thought it was perfect. Later, Dragon made a candy wreath from Old Wire and chocolate candy, but he kept eating the candy when pieces fell off. Soon he shook the wreath until every piece fell off, and he got a tummy ache. Dragon also bought clip-on mittens so he would not lose them, but then he lost his coat. At Christmas, Dragon bought gifts for himself, but he gave them away to hungry raccoons, a cold Rhino, and two sad birds. When he got home, his sack was empty, and he slept under his warm quilt.

summary_text: The tub people were seven wooden figures who stood in a line on the edge of the bathtub: father, mother, grandmother, doctor, policeman, child, and dog. Later, a big man fixed the drain and pulled the child back out. The tub people smiled, but the child was put into a tool box. After that, they waited until they were moved to a new room and placed on a soft bed, where they became seven again and played new games together.

summary_text: Ruby loved swinging high and exploring the garden. She was happy until she found a tiny worry. At first, she hardly noticed it, but it grew bigger every day. The worry followed Ruby at breakfast, while she brushed her teeth, on the school bus, and at the movie theater. No one else could see it, so Ruby tried to pretend it was not there. Soon, worrying about the worry made it enormous, and Ruby could think of almost nothing else. One day at the park, Ruby saw a sad boy sitting alone. A worry was hovering beside him too. Ruby learned that other people had worries. She asked the boy what was on his mind, and his worry became smaller while he talked. Ruby talked about her own worry as well. Both worries disappeared, and Ruby felt like herself again. Worries came back sometimes, but they did not stay long when she talked about them.

At first this was not fun, but worms wiggled by and tickled him. In the dark, Acorn changed and grew. He pushed up through the ground and became an oak tree. He kept growing for many years and stayed a little wild inside.

summary_text: A bright yellow bus spent her days driving and carrying people from one important place to another. Every morning, children climbed in with pitter patter, giggle giggle, and patter sounds, and the bus felt happy. Then a new driver came and took the bus on unfamiliar roads. The children still climbed in with shuffle, clunk, and creak sounds, and the bus still carried them and felt joy. After a long time, another new person drove the yellow bus into the city, parked her in a quiet spot, and walked away. No one came for a while, and the bus stayed empty and still. One cold night, people climbed in and huddled together, making rustle and bump sounds. Later, the bus was taken by a truck across a bridge, through the country, and to a farm in a valley. There, more animals came in with clip clop and maaah sounds. Then the farmer gathered them and took them away. The farm became quiet. Soon the river rose, and then swimmers came in with swish and swoosh sounds, and they filled the yellow bus with joy.

summary_text: On a snow-cold day, a round old couple made Easter eggs in their snug little house. The round old man blew out the insides of the eggs. The round old woman painted some eggs and dyed others in glass cups. Their little rabbit watched. Later, when the winter wind blew, they made straw baskets. They twisted and braided the straw while the rabbit watched. On an early spring day, they made chocolate eggs too. The round old woman melted the chocolate, sugar, and butter, and the round old man poured the chocolate into tiny molds. On Easter, when the church bells rang, the couple gave every child in the village a straw basket filled with Easter eggs. The rabbit watched again. After a year, the rabbit began to help. He put the eggs into the baskets and took the baskets down the lane. Then, each year, he made more eggs, baskets, and chocolate, and the children learned that the Easter Bunny came.

summary_text: Little Morer Mouse looked outside and saw only brown. He wanted to see green. He ate the shells off his sunflower seeds and listened when the big people said it was springtime and “Garden time!” They explained that seeds could be planted in dirt with water and sunshine and grow into many more seeds or vegetables. Morer was unsure, but he decided to plant his last sunflower seed. He found a sunny place, dug a hole, dropped in the seed, covered it with dirt, and watered it from an acorn cap. The next day it rained, and Morer found soggy dirt. He wanted to dig up the seed, but he waited after a quiet voice said, “Wait.” He waited through more rain. On the third day, sunshine came, and two green leaves appeared. Morer cared for the plant, pulled weeds, and watered it until it grew into a giant sunflower full of seeds. He thanked God, saved the seeds, and fell asleep beside a spider friend.

summary_text: The people in Squawk Valley were sad because Thanksgiving was coming, but they had no turkey for their feast. They read in the newspapers that all the turkeys were gone. A wagon even came down the street selling shredded wheat, but no one wanted that for Thanksgiving. Then Ebeneezer Beezer had an idea. He said they should hold an arts-and-crafts fair and offer one big turkey prize. The townspeople made many turkey pictures and models from spuds, clay, rope, oatmeal, paper, and soap. They put up signs in the forest that said Model Wanted, and a real turkey named Pete came to pose. Pete was clever and liked to eat. He judged the turkey art on Thanksgiving Day, but then he disappeared. He had blended in with the other turkey art, found his fee, and left a note. The townspeople still had no turkey, but they were thankful for their shredded wheat. They learned that a plump and perky turkey can be very clever.

and told him to get a good suit for the show.

and ended up at the Youth Seminar
where new souls get their personalities
and find their spark.

a new soul who did not want to go to earth.

helped 22 understand life
and learned that being inspired by life was more important than just a single purpose.
In the end, 22 went to earth
and Joe received a special portal back to life.

summary_text: Duncan the dragon loved reading, but whenever he opened a book, the story came alive and his imagination caught fire. Sadly, the book caught fire too, so Duncan could not discover how the story ended. He wondered whether pirates would find treasure, a captain would save a ship, or aliens would conquer Earth. Duncan tried to stay calm and decided to find a friend who could read the book to him. He asked a raccoon, a possum, and a bull, but none of them read it. Duncan returned home crying. A mouse saw his sadness and offered to help. The mouse loved books and read to Duncan. Together they battled sea monsters, dodged icebergs, discovered new lands, ate hot dogs and marshmallows, and sailed home. Then the mouse read, “the end.” But for Duncan, it was only the beginning of a wonderful book adventure.

Boo found a photo of himself and P, and both felt sad and cried because they missed their friend. Ellie saw this and pushed the wall Far Far Away. summary_text: A gingerbread man began as batter in a bowl. Children in a classroom mixed ginger, cinnamon, molasses, butter, and eggs, then rolled and shaped him like a man and added sweets. The art teacher sent him to the principal. Principal Peacock showed him a missing poster from room 23. At last, the class came back, cheered, and made him a gingerbread desk, chair, and house. He stayed with them and looked happy.

summary_text: The Cat in the Hat takes Sally on a trip to the rain forest. He says the rain forest is steamy and wet because lots of rain falls there near the equator. He also tells about other kinds of rain forests, like seasonal rain forests, cloud rain forests, and mangrove rain forests. Then he explains that rain comes from transpiration, when plants give off water and warm air makes clouds. The Cat says the rain forest has four floors. On the top floor, very tall emergent trees grow, with buttress roots to hold them up. Harpy eagles and macaws live there. On the next floor, the green canopy is full of animals like howler monkeys, sloths, toucans, orchids, and tree frogs. Hummingbirds help flowers by carrying pollen. The understory is dark and has spider monkeys and ocelots. The forest floor is full of leaves, insects, snakes, jaguars, and people who have lived there for many years. In the end, the Cat says many trees are being cut down and asks people to save the rain forest.

summary_text: Two older people talk about their families, their pasts, and how they met. One person says his son disowned him and used a hurtful word, and he worries he may never get to talk to his grandchild. The other person says her daughter also disowned her. They talk about growing up feeling different from other children. One liked playing a girl’s part in pretend games, but had to act like someone else to survive. He spent 15 years in the Army as a paratrooper in the 82nd Airborne Division and says soldiers had to seem very tough. After leaving the military, he finally began wearing women’s clothes because he had been afraid to before. Later, they met at a transgender support group at the VA. They joked with each other, and people started saying they were really sisters. They often sit together at Denny’s for coffee for many hours. At the end, they say that losing their children hurts, but they are always there for each other and are glad to be sisters.

summary_text: Once there was a peddler who sold caps. He carried many caps on his head: his checked cap, then gray caps, brown caps, blue caps, and red caps on top. He walked through town calling, “Caps! Caps for sale!” One morning, nobody wanted to buy any caps. The peddler grew hungry, so he went for a walk in the country and came to a big tree. He sat down, leaned back, and fell asleep. When he woke up, his caps were gone. He looked all around, then looked up into the tree. Monkeys were sitting in the branches, and each monkey wore a cap. The peddler shook his finger and stamped his feet, but the monkeys copied him. At last he threw down his own cap. Then all the monkeys threw down the caps too. The peddler put them back on his head and walked back to town calling, “Caps! Caps for sale!”

summary_text: Alexander was a little mouse who lived in a house. People often chased him with a broom, even though he only wanted a few crumbs. Instead of changing himself, Alexander asked the lizard to change Willie into a real mouse. The lizard did so. Alexander and Willie hugged and danced together until dawn.

summary_text: Little Yoshio ran out into Tokyo and listened to many sounds. He heard his boots splash in puddles, rain on his umbrella, and a koto player tuning her instrument. The koto player played beautiful music and told Yoshio that the most beautiful sound was ma, or silence. Yoshio went to school wondering where silence could be. He listened all day, but there was always noise. At recess he sat in the bamboo grove, but the wind and bamboo still made sound. On the way home he heard buses, trains, and traffic lights. At home he heard chopsticks, slurping, and bathwater dripping. That night he tried to stay awake to find silence, but he fell asleep. The next morning, he got up early and went to school before anyone else. In the empty classroom, while reading a book, he suddenly found silence. He learned that silence was there between sounds all along.

At the treasure chest, they meet a fierce fire-breathing armadillo. The Knight uses a pillow to distract it, and the detective tickles it. The beast curls into a ball and falls down. The heroes move it away, open the chest, and find treasure maps inside. They take the new map and begin another Quest.

summary_text: It was the night before the child’s birthday, and the house was ready. The invites were out, streamers were hung, presents were wrapped, and a banner was up. The child blew up balloons, especially the ones with stars. Mom said it was time for bed, so the child put on jammies and went to sleep, thinking about birthday gifts. In the morning, the child woke up very happy because it was birthday time. Mom said the child was a year older, and the child said a new age meant growing taller and running faster. Mom and Dad set the table with napkins, plates, hats, horns, and party favors. Dad got out three flavors of ice cream. Then there was a loud crash in the kitchen. The balloons popped, Mom screamed, and the kitty was laughing near melted ice cream. Dad and the child went to the store to buy more ice cream. When they came back, friends were hiding inside and shouted surprise. The child got gifts, cards, books, games, and money from Grandma. Then the lights went out, the cake came in, and everyone sang happy birthday as the child got ready to make a wish.

After that, the world went back to normal, but people noticed small kind acts more, like opening doors and making room. Everyone remembered that Sally had paid super extra special attention.

Later, five eggs are hidden nearby, and Scarecrow guards them as he waits for more baby crows.

Amanita pulled them up and rode off to find Florian, but she got lost in a dark forest. The noses pointed her toward his castle by following the smell of roses. She found Florian, gave him the noses, and they planted them in his garden. Amanita took home nine thorny rose bushes and was pleased because they were dangerous and smelled nice.

summary_text: Early one morning, Mr. MaGee and his little dog, Dee, packed the camper and drove to the mountains for camping. Mr. MaGee told Dee the views were nice and the air was sweet. They found a camp spot on a hill with a view of Mount Adams, Mount Lincoln, and Jefferson, and a brook with a waterfall. Dee gathered sticks and logs while Mr. MaGee made a fire and cooked hot dogs. They roasted marshmallows and then went to sleep in their bunk beds. During the night, a bear came smelling the marshmallows. The bear pushed under the hitch, and the camper and car came loose. The camper rolled down the hill with MaGee and Dee asleep inside, splashed into the stream, and went toward the waterfall. It stopped on a rock. The bear later took the hitch, but when he saw it was not food, he left. The camper rolled back to the car, and MaGee and Dee went home and decided to camp in the backyard.

Kelp came up near the surface and saw a sparkling creature on a cliff that looked just like him. He swam to land and tried to walk, but it was hard. Kelp then wondered if he had to choose between the sea and land.

summary_text: In 1855, William Covington Hanover follows Ava O’Neill through snowy New York. He wants to learn the secrets of Teresa and Theodore Morningstar, famous inventors who have disappeared after creating a mysterious treasure hunt called the Old York Cipher. William pretends to be a gentleman, but Ava knows he is a thief. When he threatens her and knocks away her book, Ava breaks his finger, hurts his knee, and calls the police. The coppers arrest William while Ava safely enters the Morningstar building. In the present day, Tess Biederman lives in that same building with her twin brother, Theo, and her unusual hybrid cat, Nine. Tess worries that developer Darnell Slant will buy their home and replace old buildings with new ones. She visits the post office for her grandfather and finds a strange letter sealed with gold wax and marked “Trust no one.” Although Tess tries not to worry, the Old York Cipher seems to be waking up and choosing her and other children for a new adventure.

She went to the baker’s, and the three good bunnies went to pick blackberries. Naughty Peter went into Mr. McGregor’s garden instead. He ate lettuces, beans, radishes, and parsley. Then Mr. McGregor saw him and chased him. Peter ran all around the garden, lost his shoes, and got caught in a gooseberry net. He escaped, but left his blue jacket behind. He hid in a shed, jumped into a can, sneezed, and ran out a window. At last he found the gate and got back to the wood. He rushed home tired and wet. His mother put him to bed and gave him camomile tea. Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread, milk, and blackberries for supper.

summary_text: A long time ago in Lime, an English town, a girl and her mother picked wild blackberries. The mother skimmed cream from the morning and evening milk, then beat it with clean twigs until it became whipped cream. The girl washed the berries from a well, strained out the seeds, and mixed the fruit with sugar and cream. Her mother let her lick the spoon. They took the bowl to an ice pit in the hillside to chill. After supper, they served the blackberry fool in blue dishes to father, the older brothers, and even the baby. Later, the girl licked the bowl clean in the kitchen. A bit more than 200 years ago near Charleston, South Carolina, another girl and her mother made the same dessert with blackberries, cream, sugar, and ice, and the girl also licked the spoon and the bowl clean.

Then there is a bright flash of lightning that lights up the sky, followed by a big crash and boom. Baby Goofy is told again not to be scared. After the storm, the sun comes out and the storm is over. Then a beautiful rainbow appears in the sky with red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. The rainbow is there for Baby Goofy to see.

summary_text: Pete was playing on his bedroom floor when a monster appeared at his window. Pete said hello and asked the monster to play cars. The monster wanted to eat Pete, but he played cars with him anyway. They made races, parking lots, and crashes. Then Pete asked to play pirates. The monster still wanted to eat Pete, but he had never played pirates before, so they dug for treasure, walked the plank, and acted like scallywags. Next, Pete wanted to play blocks. The monster liked building, so they made a castle, built towers, and knocked them down. After that, Pete said they should play superheroes. The monster wanted to eat Pete and did eat him, but playing alone was no fun. He missed Pete and spat him out. Pete said sorry, and the monster asked to play superheroes again.

summary_text: The story says, “I am enough.” It tells about a child who is like many things in nature and life. The child is like the sun, and shines. The child is like a voice and sings, like a bird and flies, like trees and grows, and like mountains and stands strong. The child also fights like a champ, loves like a heart, climbs like a ladder, and rises like the air and wind. The child pushes, pulls, pours, and falls like rain. The child dreams like the moon, learns like a student, swells like water, and burns like fire. Even in winter, the child keeps trying. Sometimes the child cries, but still tries again. The story says people do not have to be the same. They may look different and sometimes disagree, but they all have worth. In the end, they should live with love, help each other, stay together, and remember: “I am enough.”

summary_text: There was an alligator under the child’s bed at night. The child looked for it, but it hid, and Mom and Dad did not see it. So the child went to the kitchen and made alligator bait. The child put a peanut butter sandwich, fruit, pie, cookies, vegetables, soda, and candy in different places from the garage to the bed. Then the child watched and waited. Addie came to eat the food, and the child followed him from the hall closet, down the stairs, and down the hall. When Addie crawled into the garage, the child shut the door and locked it. Then the child went to bed. In the morning, there was no mess to clean up. The child left Dad a note to say there was an alligator in the garage and to be careful.

Then, one day in the cafeteria, the narrator dropped lunch on their loafers. A cool bean helped clean it up. Later on the playground, another cool bean helped after the narrator tripped and scraped a knee. In class, a cool bean quietly helped the narrator answer the teacher. After that, the narrator felt more confident and started spending time with the cool beans again.

summary_text: The story is about a grape who calls himself a sour grape G because he holds grudges easily. He remembers small slights from a banana, an orange, and a lime, and says nobody steps on him. But he was not always like this. As a young grape, he lived with about 3,000 other grapes in a close-knit community on a vine. His grandparents visited on weekends and taught the family to be kind, forgiving, considerate, and grateful, and to stay sweet no matter what life brings. For a while, he followed that advice. Then his birthday party changed everything. He planned a big celebration with rides, snacks, a magician, and fireworks, but nobody came because he had written the wrong date on the invitations. After that, he became bitter and began collecting grudges. Later, after a series of bad delays on the way to see Lenny, he realized he had acted the same way as Lenny. He learned to let go of grudges, talk things out, and be grateful.

summary_text: In a small village near the Moroccan desert lived a young potter named Amir. His father made famous pots, but Amir wanted to make the most beautiful pot of all. He worked hard, used gold dust, and put his shiny pot in the town square. People admired it for a while, but an old herb seller said beauty alone would not last. A desert fox and a bird found that the pot was empty, and soon the wind made it tip over and crack. Amir made another pot with jewels and silver, but it was empty too. A sandstorm blew it away. Then the old herb woman told Amir that a pot must have a purpose. Amir made a simple clay pot, filled it with water, and left it for travelers. People came to drink, and his father said the pot now shone from the inside out. Amir understood that kindness mattered more than glitter.

The child climbs, slides, and sees more signs of life below the snow. A snowshoe hare rests in spruce, bullfrogs sleep under the snow, and beavers chew aspen bark. Then a fox hears a mouse and leaps to hunt. Later, by moonlight, the child sees a chipmunk waking for supper. At the hilltop, there is a fire, cocoa, hot dogs, and a sleeping black bear below. The child goes home, snuggles under the covers, and dreams of the animals in the secret kingdom under the snow.

summary_text: One day, when Mama was away, Mel decided it was time to learn to fly. She had stayed in the nest long enough. Her sister Pim asked if she was scared, and Mel said yes, but she would not let that stop her. Her brother Pip said the drop was very long, but Mel said she had wings. Mel said goodbye to her siblings, then jumped from the nest. She flipped, spread her wings, and fell and fell. The squirrels tried to catch her, and the bees tried too. A spider even offered to help, but Mel still fell. Then she splashed into the water, caught a fish, kicked her legs, wiggled her tail feathers, and spread her wings again. This time, she flew. The spider clapped, the bees cheered, and the squirrels raced her back to the top. Mama was waiting there, and Mel said, “I flew! I flew!” Mama said she knew Mel could do it.

summary_text: A weasel caught a mouse and brought him home to make mouse soup. The mouse said the soup would not taste good unless it had stories in it. The hungry weasel agreed, and the mouse told four stories. First, bees landed on his head, and he led them through mud until they flew away. Then two large stones wondered about the other side of a hill, but a mouse showed them it was like their own side. Next, a mouse could not sleep because ten crickets chirped too loudly, so he told them to go away. Last, an old lady found a thorn bush in her chair, and a policeman helped her water it until it grew leaves and roses. After the stories, the weasel ran outside to find bees, mud, stones, crickets, and a thorn bush for the soup. He was stung, scratched, and tired, and when he returned, the pot was empty. The mouse had escaped home, lit a fire, eaten supper, and finished his book.

summary_text: Little Red Riding Hood lived with her family near the Woods. Her grandmother loved her and gave her a red cape with a hood. One day Grandma became ill, and Little Red’s mother packed a basket of food and asked Little Red to take it to Grandma’s house. Little Red started out, but she soon forgot her task and talked about playing instead. She also borrowed a blue cape and hood before continuing. Halfway through the Woods, she met the big bad wolf, who was really Captain Hook filling in. He asked where she was going and then told her to pick flowers so he could go to Grandma’s house first. The wolf knocked on Grandma’s door and pretended to be Little Red. When Little Red arrived, she noticed something was wrong and asked strange questions about Grandma’s ears, eyes, and teeth. A Woodsman came, and the story turned into a loud mix-up with no one getting eaten. In the end, Grandma was well and opened an ice cream shop, and everyone enjoyed ice cream sundaes.

summary_text: Mr. McGrey wanted a garden with lettuce, carrots, peas, and tomatoes. He planted the seeds and watched the vegetables grow. Then three hungry bunnies came at night and munched on the garden. Mr. McGrey was angry. First, he made a small wire fence. The bunnies still ate the plants. Next, he built a tall wall, but the bunnies still got into the garden. Then he made a deep, wet trench. The bunnies kept coming. Finally, Mr. McGrey built a huge thing around the garden. The bunnies looked, smelled, and touched it, but then they hopped away. In the morning, Mr. McGrey saw that his vegetables were untouched. He danced because he thought he had won. Then he climbed over, jumped across, squeezed between, and crawled under his garden defenses. He picked his vegetables and reached for something yummy.

summary_text: It was Christmas Eve, and Mickey sat by the warm fire while snow fell outside. Then he heard a loud clatter on the lawn and ran to the door. A sleigh came into view, pulled by reindeer, and Uncle Scrooge arrived with many wrapped presents. Daisy, Huey, Dewey, Louie, Donald, Minnie, Morty, Murdy, Grandma Duck, Goofy, and Pluto all came to join the Christmas fun. Donald and Daisy trimmed the tree while Scrooge sorted the gifts, but he could not find Pluto’s present. Soon everyone sat down for a big dinner with turkey, stuffing, mashed potatoes, gravy, ham, vegetables, pie, and eggnog. After dinner, they all took short naps. While they slept, St. Nick came down the chimney, gave Pluto a hug, and left a sack by the tree. At midnight, they woke up, opened the sack, and found Pluto’s bones and dog toys. Then everyone cheered, “Merry Christmas to all and a happy new year.”

Bird shows the squirrel what is happening. The wind shakes the trees, rustles the leaves, and even takes the squirrel’s hat. Bird explains that the leaves change colors and the wind blows them away every autumn. They will grow back in spring. The squirrel understands that there is no leaf thief and goes to sleep. The next morning, the squirrel says someone has stolen the grass too.

summary_text: Ronan was a mighty barbarian leader who invaded, raided, and traded for gold, jewelry, weapons, and tools. One raid went wrong when he found a book and first thought it was useless. He tried to get rid of it, but after seeing a picture, he began reading. He read the first sentence, then more and more until late at night. The next day, his friends Krom, Gunner, and Helgi found him reading instead of raiding. Ronan went raiding with them, but he could not stop thinking about the book. After the raid, he hurried home and read to the end. Soon he wanted more books, so he raided and read again and again until books piled up on his boat. To solve the problem, he built a library and opened it with a celebration. At first his friends mocked books, but Ronan read aloud to them, gave out library cards, recommended books, and started a book club. In the end, the barbarians read books too.

summary_text: Andy loved his toys, especially Woody, but he did not know that the toys came alive when people were not watching. On Andy’s birthday, he got a new toy named Buzz Lightyear. Buzz thought he was a real Space Ranger and would not listen when Woody tried to explain that he was a toy. Andy liked Buzz best, and Woody felt sad. When Andy went to Pizza Planet, his mom said he could bring only one toy. Woody tried to move Buzz aside, but Buzz fell out the bedroom window. Later, Buzz joined them in the car, and he and Woody fought. At a gas station they fell out and were left behind. The two toys followed a Pizza Planet truck, got trapped at Pizza Planet, and were captured by Sid, Andy’s mean neighbor. Sid planned to blow Buzz up with a rocket, but Woody and the mutant toys scared Sid away. In the end, Buzz learned he was a toy, he and Woody became friends, and they flew back to Andy’s car just as the moving van was leaving.

summary_text: In the deep blue sea lived a fish called Rainbow Fish. He had beautiful blue, green, purple, and silver scales. The little fish told the others, and soon no fish wanted to be with Rainbow Fish. He felt very lonely. Rainbow Fish asked a starfish why nobody liked him. Rainbow Fish gave one small scale to the little blue fish, then shared more scales with the others. The fish came back to him, and at the end he had one shining scale left and was happy with his friends.

summary_text: Calvin was a starling born in a very big family under an old barn. While his brothers, sisters, and cousins found worms, grass, dirt, and water, Calvin found a book. He learned to read and spent his days in the library, where he read about pirates, dinosaurs, planets, wind, and butterflies. The other starlings called him names, and Calvin felt sad. When fall came, it was time to fly south, but Calvin could not fly. His family left, then came back and tied him with string and scraps of cloth so they could carry him along. While they flew, Calvin saw places he had read about. Later, Calvin heard bad weather coming and warned everyone about a hurricane. His family listened and hid in a cave. The storm passed, and the starlings were safe. They celebrated Calvin, and then Calvin discovered he could fly too. Together, they flew south.
