summary_text: On Thanksgiving Day, a turkey tells how his big story began one year earlier at school. He heard children talking about a play and saying there would even be a turkey on stage. When he understood that he might be part of the show, he panicked and ran away from his pen. He dashed into the science room, knocked over flasks and beakers, and heard the loudspeaker call, “Catch that turkey!” More children chased him with catapults, food, and other tricks, but he escaped through a maze of books, past chairs and desks, and out to the Jungle Gym. He then ran into the coach’s room, got tangled in jerseys, and finally ended up at the curtain. There, he could not get away from the principal, so he went through the curtain and onto the stage. A child pointed at him and said he was cute, and a parent agreed. The turkey smiled, danced, and became the school mascot.

Annie was upset, but the case was solved.

summary_text: Bo was a small blue fish who lived alone in a cave. One night, he woke up frightened and traveled to a place filled with colorful fish and bright lights. Some fish told him that he could not be alone and tried to cover his blue color. Bo felt nervous, homesick, and unseen, but he kept exploring. In a beautiful cove, the Creator told Bo that every fish was a work of art and that all colors were reflections of the Creator. Bo saw his own portrait and learned that every fish had a special light to share. When the fish joined together, their lights grew brighter. Bo then helped the fish listen to one another and work together. Fish of many colors gathered, placed rocks carefully, and made a stunning rainbow. They learned that love and teamwork can make the world more beautiful, and Bo understood that every color matters.

In the end, Cora saw that the house and the memories in it were wonderful just as they were.

summary_text: Over the lake and past the bay was a green grassy hill where the Rocks played. They raced to the top and rolled down again. The Rocks included Kip, Chester, Marvin the boulder, Ignatius, the Pebbles, Kai, Maya, Stu, Parker, Grumpy Old Albert, Gabby, Lisi, and Emma. All of them were round and could roll, except Ricky. Ricky was flat on one side, so he could not roll like the others. His friends asked him to come roll, but Ricky said he could not. Marvin carried Ricky to the top of the hill and pushed him down, but Ricky only slid. Then the Rocks glued rubber balls onto Ricky, but he only bounced. They kept trying, but nothing worked, and Ricky felt sad and sat aside. His friends did not give up. Stu saw the rain and had an idea. They carried Ricky to the lake, covered his flat side with mud, shaped it into a round mound, let it dry in the sun, and wrapped vines around him. After that, Ricky tried again and finally rolled down the hill with his friends.

Some undies landed on animals and in different places, and the repeated line said that someone was wearing them or getting covered by them. The king of crowing flew up when undies hit the roof, and the billly goat caught a pair in his jaw. In the end, the farmer came outside and asked for his underwear back. After the wind settled down, he had to pick the undies off the animals and the ground, and something hit his hiney before the story ended.

summary_text: In the kingdom of Grimm, an old king is dying. He asks his faithful servant, Johannes, to care for his young son and show him everything he inherits except one locked room. The room contains a portrait of the Golden Princess, and the old king warns that seeing it will make his son fall in love and may cost him his life. After becoming king, the young prince insists on entering the room. He sees the beautiful princess and immediately wants to marry and save her, even after learning that she is cursed and that her husbands have died. Johannes gathers gold, disguises himself and the king as merchants, and visits the princess. She follows them to the ship because she loves the golden treasures. When she discovers she has been taken away, she protests, but learns that the merchant is a king who loves her. Johannes says she may return without the gold, so she chooses to marry the young king, and they live happily ever after.

summary_text: On a beautiful spring morning, the animals in the forest came to see a new baby deer. Thumper called for friend owl, and everyone gathered around Bambi and his mother. Bambi’s mother said she would call him Bambi. As Bambi grew, he explored the forest with Thumper and learned new words like bird, butterfly, and flower. He also met Flower the skunk, and the three became good friends. Later, Bambi’s mother took him to the meadow and warned him not to rush out because it could be dangerous. There, Bambi met Faline and played with her until a loud noise scared the deer away. Bambi got lost, but the Great Prince of the forest helped him return to his mother. After that, the forest became peaceful again. Bambi later learned about winter, the loss of his mother, love for Faline, the forest fire, and the birth of his twins with Faline.

summary_text: Susie’s mother and father go away, and Miss Mugs comes to stay with Susie. Miss Mugs is nice, but she is always in a hurry. She tells Susie to hurry up and get ready for school. On the way, Miss Mugs hurries past the milkman and makes a mess with milk. Then she hurries past a lady with three little cats and one big dog and makes another mess. The milkman and the lady both tell her not to hurry so much. Miss Mugs keeps rushing and falls into a hole by a sign that says, “Danger Men At Work.” Susie gets a policeman to pull her out with a rope. Miss Mugs hurries again, gets lifted by a steam shovel, and then walks under a ladder and gets glue all over her. Susie helps, but Miss Mugs keeps saying “hurry,” so Susie stops helping. At last, everyone helps pull her free. Miss Mugs learns to walk slowly and goes home slowly.

summary_text: Dasher lived with her reindeer family in a traveling circus. The animals stayed in a hot, crowded pen, but Mama told Dasher about a wonderful home with cold air, white snow, and the North Star shining above. Dasher wished to see that place. One windy night, the gate opened, so Dasher ran away. She followed the North Star but could not reach it. Then she heard bells and found Santa and his tired horse, Silverbell. Dasher offered to help pull the heavy sleigh. She flew through the sky, delivered toys, and discovered the North Star above the North Pole. Dasher loved her new home, but she missed her family. Santa helped her bring them to the North Pole. The whole family joined Santa's team, and Dasher finally had the snowy home she had always wished for.

summary_text: Amari Peters is sent to the principal after shoving Emily Grant, who has bullied her and made cruel jokes about Amari’s missing brother, Quinton. The police believe he may have been involved in something illegal, but Amari does not believe them. At home, Amari uses Quinton’s old laptop to post his missing-person notice online. She then sees hurtful comments about him and opens a surprising new email from Quinton’s delivery service. The message says a package has arrived and will disappear. Just then, someone knocks at the apartment door, leaving Amari wondering what Quinton has sent and whether it can help her find him.

This hurts his feelings, and it hurts Daisy’s feelings too. When this happens, the child and Daisy put on their helmets and blast off up through the clouds and across the galaxy to Pluto. They say hello to old friends and to the martians. From far away, the child sees that Earth is small, but he knows it is full of billions of different people. He realizes the Earth is big enough for everyone. He cannot change how he looks, but he hopes people will change how they see him. Then they may see that he is a wonder, and that they are wonders too. The story ends by saying, "We’re all wonders. Look with kindness and you will always find wonder."

He writes Mom and Dad a song and sings it to them. The song says he loves them with all his heart, and it is the best surprise ever.

summary_text: Owl was at home on a cold, snowy night. He sat by the fire and ate buttered toast and hot pea soup for supper. Then he heard loud banging at his door. summary_text: Alexander Hamilton was born in 1755 on Nevice in the Caribbean. His father left, and later his mother died, so Alexander was alone. He found work as a clerk and learned about money and business. When he was only 14, he ran the company for six months. In 1772, a hurricane hit the islands, and Alexander wrote about it in a newspaper. Rich businessmen read his writing and sent him to college in America. In America, he saw that England ruled the colonies and taxed many things. He became a patriot and gave speeches against British rule. When British soldiers marched into Lexington in 1775, the American Revolution began. Alexander joined the army, drilled his troops, and later fought at Yorktown in 1781. He led a charge against a weak British barrier and helped win the battle. After the war, he worked to build the new nation, helped write the Federalist Papers, and became Secretary of the Treasury. He later died in a duel with Aaron Burr.

summary_text: There was once a peddler who sold caps. He wore many caps on his head: his own checked cap, then gray caps, brown caps, blue caps, and red caps on top. He walked through the streets calling, “Caps, caps for sale. 50 cents a cap.” One morning nobody bought any caps, so the peddler became hungry. He left town and walked into the country. He came to a big tree and sat down to rest. He leaned back carefully and then fell asleep. When he woke up, he felt his head and found only his checked cap. He looked everywhere, but the other caps were gone. Then he looked up and saw monkeys in the tree wearing his caps. The peddler asked for his caps back, but the monkeys copied him and said, “tus, tus, tous,” and other sounds. Finally, he threw down his own cap. Then the monkeys threw down all the caps. He put them back on his head and walked back to town, calling, “Caps, caps for sale. 50 cents a cap.”

summary_text: Elizabeth was a princess who lived in a castle and was going to marry Prince Ronald. Then a dragon smashed the castle, burned her clothes, and carried Ronald away. Elizabeth could not find any clothes left, so she put on a paper bag and followed the dragon. She found his cave and knocked on the big door. The dragon said he was busy and told her to come back tomorrow. Elizabeth kept talking to him and asked if he was the smartest and fiercest dragon. The dragon breathed fire again and again, then flew around the world for her. He got so tired that he fell asleep. Elizabeth quietly walked past him, opened the cave door, and found Ronald. Ronald said she looked messy and was wearing a dirty paper bag. Elizabeth said Ronald looked like a bum. They did not get married.

summary_text: One morning, a rooster wanted to travel and see the world. He met two cats, three frogs, four turtles, and five fish, and each group happily joined him. They walked together down the road. When night came, the animals needed dinner, a place to sleep, and warmth. The rooster had not made plans for food or shelter, so he did not know how to help. The fish swam home, the turtles crawled home, the frogs jumped away, and the cats went home for an unfinished meal. Soon the rooster was alone. He had not seen the world, and he was hungry, cold, and homesick. He told the moon how he felt, but the moon disappeared. Then the rooster turned around and went home. He ate grain, sat on his own perch, and dreamed a happy dream about traveling around the world.

Brother Bear told her to wiggle it with her tongue and put it under her pillow when it came out, so the tooth fairy could take it and leave a coin. At breakfast, Mama heard about the loose tooth. Sister watched Dr. Barrison check Brother’s teeth with a little mirror and special tools. She saw a cavity get cleaned and filled. Then it was Sister’s turn. She still thought the tooth would stay in, but Dr. Barrison gently pulled it out with gauze. He gave Sister her tiny tooth to keep. The next morning, Sister looked under her pillow and found a shiny dime. She ran to show Mama and told Brother the tooth fairy had come.

Watson’s family wants to buy the house sooner than expected, so the wedding must happen at the end of the month. Kristy realizes she has only two and a half weeks to help plan everything. She and her mother make lists of guests, supplies, food, and decorations. Kristy also worries about leaving Brantford Court, her friends, and the Babysitters’ Club. At a club meeting, she tells the others the wedding will be soon and the move will happen in July. The club starts talking about dresses, the final fling dance, and all the changes ahead. Kristy begins to understand that the wedding will affect everyone, not just her and her mother.

summary_text: Gerald the elephant is missing one day, and his friend asks what happened to his trunk. Gerald says he broke it. He begins a long, crazy story. First, he was playing with a hippo and had an idea. He lifted the hippo onto his trunk, but the hippo was heavy. Then Rhino came and wanted a turn, so Gerald lifted both the hippo and Rhino onto his trunk. They were very heavy too, but that was not when he broke it. After that, hippo’s big sister came and wanted to play her piano. Gerald lifted two hippos, one Rhino, and a piano onto his trunk, but that still was not the cause. At last, Gerald ran to tell his very best friend what he had done. He tripped and fell, and that is how he broke his trunk. His friend says it is a crazy and funny story, and then Piggy begins to tell a long, crazy story about his snout.

summary_text: George lives on a farm and feels lonely because there are no other children nearby. On Saturday, his mother goes shopping and tells him to give Grandma her medicine. Grandma is tiny, grumpy, and mean to George. She frightens him by talking about magic powers, strange creatures, and scary secrets. George runs to the kitchen, where he decides to make a new medicine to shock her. He gathers almost everything runny, powdery, or gooey that he can find, including shampoo, toothpaste, shaving foam, face cream, nail varnish, cleaning products, spices, gin, and shoe polish. He also takes animal medicines from the shed, even though the labels warn that they are for animals and must be used carefully. George stirs the mixture, then boils it. Blue smoke, strong smells, foam, and sparks appear. Finally, he adds brown paint so it looks like Grandma's real medicine, fills her bottle, and carries it toward her at medicine time.

summary_text: Ariel was a young mermaid who loved the ocean. She played hide and seek with her sisters, then swam past the coral reef to look for more places. Soon a storm came, so Ariel and her father hurried back to the castle. After the storm, Ariel saw a ship sink in the water. The next day, she swam to the shipwreck with Flounder. She found treasures like a glove, a brush, a mirror, earrings, and a music box. The music box played a song. Sharks came, and Ariel used a rope and life preserver to lift them away. Ariel used her mirror to stop Ursula, and Koba broke the box. Ariel returned the Trident, and peace came back.

summary_text: Ancient Egypt was a long country with the Nile River running through it. The people buried their dead and hoped to live forever. They believed that after death, a new life would begin, and they would live in their tombs as they had on earth. To do this, the body had to be preserved. A body that was dried so it would not decay was called a mummy. At first, the hot, dry sand of Egypt dried bodies naturally. Later, embalmers learned to mummify bodies in a careful process that took 70 days. They removed the organs, covered the body with Natron, and let it dry. Then they cleaned it, added oils and spices, wrapped it in linen strips, and placed a portrait mask on the head. Artists and carpenters made coffins and sarcophagi, and the tomb walls were painted with scenes from Egyptian life. Finally, a funeral procession carried the mummy to the tomb, where it was sealed inside forever.

summary_text: Pete the Cat was happy and ready for a fun day with his sunglasses, surfboard, skateboard, guitar, and crayons. But when he looked outside, he saw dark clouds and pouring rain. Pete did not complain. He decided to find something fun to do. He drew a cool picture and played music. Then he found a big brown box. He looked at it, turned it, and thought, “This box rocks.” Pete used his imagination and painted the box. First, the box became a rocket ship, and Pete flew to space and saw the moon, stars, and planets. Then it became a yellow submarine, and Pete went under the sea with fish, coral, an octopus, and a whale. After that, the box turned into a race car, and Pete won the race. When the race car went flat, the box became a stage for Pete’s rock band. Pete learned that when plans do not go right, imagination can still make the day groovy.

summary_text: Ramadan begins when the crescent moon first appears in the sky. It lasts for one whole month. During Ramadan, Muslims think about what is important, feel thankful, and help other people. They eat and drink only when it is dark outside before the sun comes up. Each day they have a big meal called sahoor to get energy. In the evening, when the sun goes down, family and friends gather to break the fast. They eat a date first, then share a meal called iftar. People still go to work, school, and play, but they also spend time with family, pray, and do good deeds. When the crescent moon appears again, Ramadan ends. Then people celebrate for three days with a feast called idolfitter, also called the sweet festival. They eat, pray, and give gifts.

summary_text: Mary was a little girl who loved collecting colors instead of marbles or dolls. When her family moved out west, she said goodbye to her yellow house and kept her friend lemon with her. On the trip through the desert and into California, she noticed many new colors, like rust, Sienna, Azure, golden fruit, and steel gray buildings. She saved these shades in her sketchbook for later. Mary went to art school and met Lee, who showed her rosy pink and blushing red. Later, Mary worked at Walt Disney Studios, where the men in charge wanted only black and white. They changed or rejected many of her colorful ideas. Walt Disney liked her work and took her to South America, where Mary found even more colors. After she returned, she made new art for Disney films, but most of it was still turned down. Then Mary left and worked on other art jobs. Later, Walt asked her to help create a colorful ride about cultures from around the world. Mary agreed and became the leader of the project. The ride, It’s a Small World, was a great success.

summary_text: A boy found an egg lying in the path. He looked around and saw flamingos, frogs, turtles, and alligators, but no one answered when he asked whose egg it was. He saw an egg without a nest and a nest without an egg, so he climbed the tree and put the egg in the nest. Later Mr. and Mrs. Bird came home and found the egg there. They were surprised because it was very big, but they sat on it to keep it warm. They took turns sitting on the egg until they heard a squeaking sound. The egg cracked, and Junior came out. Junior had a big mouth full of teeth. Mr. and Mrs. Bird fed him worms, berries, cherries, bugs, crickets, spiders, grasshoppers, snails, ants, and centipedes. Junior ate and grew bigger and bigger. At last he was too big for the nest, so they tried to help him fly. He jumped, but he had no wings and fell into the water. Junior liked the water and swam well.

Olaf thought this looked fun and watched the snowgies go down again and again. When night came, the snowgies grew tired and went back inside. They piled up and fell asleep, and Olaf smiled at his sleeping little brothers.

On the way, Gramps told them about leprechauns, small magical beings who make shoes and hide gold in pots at the end of rainbows. At the parade route, the Cubs dozed off and dreamed they followed a rainbow to a leprechaun with a pot of gold. Then they woke up and found the real parade beginning, with marching bands, dancers, pipers, the mayor, police, fire fighters, and bears dressed as leprechauns.

summary_text: In Ridgeville, a boy named Leo loved building things. He worked hard on a go-kart called the Comet for the annual Ridgeville Derby. Leo was sure his design was perfect, but the steering kept getting loose after every turn. He tried many times to fix it with bolts and new parts, but nothing worked. Leo’s father saw his frustration and told him to visit Mr. Pinto, an old man who knew a lot from experience. In Mr. Pinto’s small garage, Leo showed his blueprints and used big words, but Mr. Pinto looked at the kart, wiggled the wheel, and found the problem. He gave Leo a small rubber washer and told him to place it in the right spot. Leo did, and the steering became strong and steady. At the Derby, the Comet raced fast and won. Leo learned that talent helped build the kart, but experience helped it succeed.

summary_text: One bright day, Jim pansy woke up and thought everything was wrong. The sun was too bright, the sky was too blue, and the bananas were too sweet. Norman, who lived next door, told Jim he might be grumpy. Jim said he was not grumpy. He shouted that it was a wonderful day and stormed off. Later, Jim felt sorry and said, “I guess I am grumpy.” Then he met Norman again. Norman had danced with the porcupine and was slumped and frowning. Jim asked if Norman was okay. Norman said he would feel better soon. Jim said he was still grumpy too. Norman said it was a wonderful day to be grumpy, and Jim felt a little better.

summary_text: The story is about a grape girl who calls herself sour because she keeps grudges when people upset her. She says she remembers every wrong, like when a banana bumped into her, an orange did not call her back, and a lime never returned her scarf. But she was not always like that. She grew up in a close-knit bunch of about 3,000 grapes living on a vine. Her family was kind and funny, and her grandparents visited on weekends to teach them to be kind, forgiving, considerate, and grateful, or “grapeful.” For a while, she stayed sweet and polite. Then her birthday party changed everything. She planned a big celebration with a ferris wheel, a magician, hay rides, snacks, and fireworks, but nobody came. She waited until sunset and felt upset. After that, she became bitter and started holding grudges. Later, when she was late meeting Lenny, he acted just like she did. Seeing the sky and park made her think differently, and she later found out she had written the wrong birthday date on the invitation. She realized the party had been her mistake. After that, she began talking things out, letting go of grudges, and being kinder again.

summary_text:
Once on a mountaintop, three little trees dreamed about what they would become. The first tree wanted to be a treasure chest full of gold and jewels. The second tree wanted to be a strong sailing ship for kings. The third tree wanted to stay on the mountain and grow so tall that people would think of God when they looked at her. Years passed, and the trees grew tall.

Then three woodcutters came. They cut down the first tree, the second tree, and the third tree. The first tree was made into a manger in a carpenter’s shop, not a treasure chest. The second tree was made into a small fishing boat and carried smelly fish, not kings. The third tree was cut into beams and left in a woodpile.

Later, the first tree held baby Jesus in a manger. The second tree carried Jesus on a lake, and he stopped the storm with one word. The third tree became the cross for Jesus, and on Sunday morning people remembered God’s love. The trees learned that God used them in ways better than they had dreamed.

summary_text: Nikolai was a boy who wanted to be a good person, but he did not always know what to do. He asked his friends three questions: when is the best time to do things, who is the most important one, and what is the right thing to do? Sonya, Gogol, and Pushkin each gave answers, but Nikolai was not sure they were right. So he went to see Leo, an old turtle living high in the mountains. Leo was digging a garden, and Nikolai helped him finish the work. Then a storm came. Nikolai heard a panda calling for help, carried her to Leo’s house, and made a splint for her hurt leg. He then found the panda’s baby in the forest and brought the little one back safe and warm. The next morning, Leo explained that the answers were in Nikolai’s actions: the right time was the time he was helping, the important ones were the people with him, and the right thing was to do good for them.

summary_text: On a farm lived a fat red hen, a duck in a pond, a goose in a pen, a sheep, a hog, a horse, a dog, a prize cow, two cats, and a ladybug. The animals made their sounds, but the ladybug never said a word. Then the ladybug saw two men in a big black van. She heard them whisper a plan to steal the fine prize cow. They wanted to open the gate at night, go past the horse, turn by the duck pond, pass the hog, not wake the dog, go past the sheep, and get to the cow shed. The ladybug spoke for the first time and told all the animals. She said the thieves were coming and explained their route. The animals listened, and the ladybug told them not to fear. She whispered a plan to each one. In the dead of night, the two men came onto the farm. The animals made noise and confused them. The men fell into the duck pond. The farmer woke up, called the police, and the men were caught. After that, the farm animals were safe, and the ladybug still never said a word again.

summary_text: Cassidy Blake can see ghosts and sense them even though most people cannot. During the last week of school, a tapping feeling draws her away from lunch and into the auditorium. Her best friend Jacob, who is dead but still spends time with her, follows. Cassidy discovers that the tapping comes from the veil, a boundary between the living world and the dead. She and Jacob cross into a ghostly version of the theater. There, Cassidy witnesses the memory of a boy performing in A Midsummer Night’s Dream. A loose sandbag causes a spark, and the stage quickly catches fire. The boy escapes beneath a trapdoor, but burning scenery seals him inside. Cassidy becomes trapped in the memory until Jacob pushes her back through the veil. She returns safely, though she understands that staying too long makes escaping harder. Jacob reminds her that friends do not leave each other behind.

At the end, they shared sweet treats together in the tower.

In the end, Grandma felt better, and everyone shared ice cream sundaes at Grandma’s shop.

summary_text: In January, Hermit Crab said his shell was too small. He stepped out into the ocean and felt afraid without a house to hide in. In February, he found a big, strong shell and moved in. It fit him well, but it looked plain. In March, he met a small sea anemone and asked it to live on his shell, and it agreed. In April, he found a little sea star and put it on his house. In May, a crusty coral came to live on the shell too. In June, a snail helped clean the house. In July, a sea urchin came to protect it. In August, they all went into dark seaweed and could not see well. In September, a lanternfish came to light the way. In October, Hermit Crab added smooth pebbles around his shell. In November, his shell felt small again, and he missed his friends. In December, a smaller hermit crab moved into the shell. The next January, Hermit Crab left and found another big shell to fill with new friends.

She led Olaf to Elsa’s office and told Elsa that Olaf wanted to learn about ghosts. Anna suggested an indoor campout and a ghost hunt. Elsa agreed. Olaf thought he had found a ghost, but it was only him. Anna and Elsa laughed and said Olaf made the best ghost hunt ever.

summary_text: Thanksgiving was fading away in the United States. People in New England still celebrated it, but many other regions did not, and the holiday was in danger of being forgotten. Sarah Hale became the person who fought to save it. She was a magazine editor, writer, and mother of five, and she used her pen as her main tool. Sarah wrote thousands of letters and articles to push for Thanksgiving to become a national holiday. Women across America also wrote letters after reading her work, and many states began to recognize Thanksgiving. Sarah then wrote to several presidents, including Zachary Taylor, Millard Fillmore, Franklin Pierce, and James Buchanan, but they all refused or did not act. During the Civil War, Sarah wrote to Abraham Lincoln and explained that a holiday could help bring the country together. Lincoln finally agreed. In 1863, he made Thanksgiving a national holiday for all Americans.

summary_text: Babushka lived alone in a little house in the country and was known for painting beautiful eggs. Every year, her eggs won first prize at the Easter Festival in Moscow. One day after a snowstorm, she went outside to feed the wild caribou and saw a goose fall from the sky. She put the goose in a basket lined with a warm quilt and named her Rashenka. Babushka cared for Rashenka, and the goose grew strong. Rashenka laid an egg each morning, but one day she jumped on Babushka’s work table and knocked over the basket of painted eggs. The eggs broke, and both Babushka and Rashenka felt sad. The next morning, Babushka found a shining egg in Rashenka’s basket. She cooked the egg for breakfast and admired its beauty. Soon she had enough eggs for the festival, where the judges chose her eggs as the most beautiful. Babushka won first prize, a feather bed quilt, and went home happy. Later, she found a new egg in Rashenka’s basket and saw that it was hatching. A special gosling came out, and Rashenka stayed with Babushka.

summary_text: Monkeys live in many places, like mountains, jungles, grasslands, rain forests, and cities. Some monkeys live in trees, and others live mostly on the ground. Snow monkeys, also called macaques, live in the mountains of Japan. In winter, they stay warm by bathing in hot mountain water that comes from inside the Earth. New World monkeys live in Central and South America. They are small, have flat noses, and live in trees. Capuchin monkeys are one kind of New World monkey. Old World monkeys live in Africa and Asia. They are bigger and have noses that are not flat. Vervet monkeys are one kind of Old World monkey. Monkey mothers stay close to their babies, and the babies learn from them. Young monkeys play, wrestle, and tumble. Boys often leave to join another troop, while girls usually stay with their moms. Monkeys also groom each other to show care.

summary_text: Goldilocks was a little girl who went into the forest to play and pick flowers. She saw a pretty little house and walked inside because she was thirsty and wanted water. In the kitchen, she found three bowls of soup. The first soup was too hot, the second soup was too cold, and the third soup was just right. Then she felt tired and sat in three chairs. The first two chairs were too big, and the last chair was just right, but it broke. Goldilocks went upstairs and tried three beds. The first bed was too hard, the second bed was too soft, and the third bed was just right. She fell asleep in that bed. Then the three bears came home. They saw that someone had eaten their soup, sat in their chair, and slept in their bed. Goldilocks woke up, saw the bears, ran down the stairs, and hurried back into the forest.

In the end, the dog snuggles in their bed and decides the children can stay. summary_text: A man lived alone in a little house on the edge of town. He cooked his own supper, cleaned his own house, and made his own bed. One night he came home very hungry and made a big supper. summary_text: When Baby Billy was born, his family saw that he had a mustache. His mother asked what it meant, and the nurse said they would have to wait and see if it was a good guy mustache or a bad guy mustache. At first, Billy’s mustache was good. He became a cowboy, tamed a bronco, protected cattle, cared for hurt animals, fixed fences, and later became a painter, a ringleader, a sword fighter, and a police officer. People liked Officer Billy. But as Billy grew, his mustache grew and curled up at the ends. Then it became a bad guy mustache. Billy turned to crime and became a cat burglar, a criminal, and a train robber. He even stole the tracks. When he planned to rob a bank, his getaway car was too slow, and his mother caught him. Billy was sent to jail. After a long time, he felt sorry for his thievery and wished his bad mustache would go away. Then his mother got him out of jail, and his father said the new neighbors had a baby coming to play.

summary_text: Eli sat on a park bench at Sakura Park and watched skateboarders glide under the cherry blossoms. He wished he could move like them. For his birthday, his grandmother gave him a skateboard with a dark blue deck and bright orange wheels. At first, it felt wobbly and hard to control. During his first week, he fell many times and got scrapes and bruises. One day, he sat on the curb and said he might not be meant to skateboard. Then an older boy named Ren stopped beside him. Ren said everyone falls and that the secret is getting up one more time than you fall. He told Eli to bend his knees and not stand so stiff. Eli tried again and rolled for a few seconds before falling into the grass. It was a small start, but he kept practicing every day after school.

summary_text: Anansi was a spider in Ashanti land. He had six sons: See Trouble, Road Builder, River Drinker, Game Skinner, Stone Thrower, and Cushion. One day Anansi went far from home and got lost. Back home, See Trouble saw that his father was in danger and told his brothers. Road Builder made a road, and the six brothers hurried to help. They found that a fish had swallowed Anansi. River Drinker drank all the river water, and Game Skinner split open the fish so Anansi could come out. Then a falcon carried Anansi high in the sky. Stone Thrower hit the falcon with a stone, and Anansi fell down safely. Cushion came next and helped him land softly. The spider family was happy to be together again. Later, Anansi found a beautiful globe of light in the forest. He wanted to give it to the son who saved him, but he could not choose. He asked Nyame to hold it, and because the sons argued all night, Nyame took the light into the sky, where it still shines.

A storm comes, the ship breaks, and Eric falls into the sea. Ariel saves him and carries him to shore. She sings to him, then leaves before the crew sees her. Ariel goes back to her cave and thinks about seeing Eric again.

summary_text: It was very late in Cutesville, and everyone was asleep except Love Monster. He had his hot milk with chocolate sprinkles, walked up the stairs, read bedtime stories, and snuggled with teddy. But that night, he could not fall asleep. He listened to the dark night and heard tick tock sounds, wind in the leaves, and owls. Then he heard something in the yard, and then downstairs. He hid under the covers because he thought something had come inside. The sound went bump, shuffle, crunch, crunch up the stairs, and Love Monster thought it had big teeth and was hungry. At last, he could not stay hiding. He got up, turned on his flashlight, and went to see. He found a tiny fluffy bunny, and the bunny was not alone either. They laughed together, and Love Monster saw that the dark was not so spooky after all.

At last they reach a clearing and see the bright northern lights. The creatures gather together, watch the colors in the sky, and then settle down peacefully to sleep under the stars.

summary_text: George, a curious little monkey, went to the aquarium with the man with the yellow hat. The man told George to wait while he bought the tickets, but George wanted to see inside. He heard a splash and a whoosh, then he hopped over the gate and went in. George saw two beluga whales, sea lions, and many fish. He followed people into a darker room and saw piranhas, seahorses, and a big red octopus. Then he reached into a touch tank, and a crab snapped at his finger. George did not like that exhibit, so he went outside into the sunlight. There he saw penguins swimming and flying through the water. George went into the penguin exhibit and copied the penguins. The penguins ran out, and one baby penguin fell into the water. George climbed the rope and swung over the beluga tank to save the chick. The director thanked George and made him an honorary staff member.

summary_text: Dusty is a crop duster who dreams of racing fast planes. He practices with his friend Chug, but Dottie warns that Dusty may break down. Dusty asks the old warplane Skipper to coach him. His dream comes true.

summary_text: Pret Hemman lives in a village on stilts with his family. Before school, he helps his father load the Longboat with nets while his mother makes coffee and cuts jack fruit. Pret suggests building a field, so the boys collect wood, barrels, styrofoam, old boat parts, and dock pieces. They build a floating field at the pier, even when villagers say it cannot be done. After weeks of work, the field is finished. The boys play there every day, and more villagers come to watch and cheer.

At auditions on Monday, Grace acted like Peter Pan very well. The class chose her for the part, and the play was a big success.

summary_text: In the grand city of Lu Yang, a boy named Chen Yu worked in Master Lao’s pottery shop. Master Lao made beautiful porcelain vases for the emperor. One day, Master Lao was asked to make a vase for the emperor’s spring festival and told Chen Yu that patience and honesty were important. That night, Chen Yu secretly tried to finish the vase. He painted on it, but he made a mistake and damaged it. He hid the vase and ran away. In the morning, Master Lao found the damage, and Chen Yu said nothing. Later, Chen Yu tried to fix the ruined vase by himself, hoping to show his skill. The repaired vase looked nice, but he used the wrong gold paint. At the spring festival, the vase cracked and the dragon paint peeled. The emperor was upset, and Master Lao’s shop was sealed. Chen Yu went to the emperor and told the truth. The emperor spared him and made him work in the palace store room for a year. After that, Chen Yu returned to Master Lao, learned to be honest, and later became a famous craftsman.

summary_text: A man and his wife wished for a baby, and one day they learned their wish would come true. Later, the king’s son heard Rapunzel singing, climbed up the same way, and fell in love with her. Rapunzel planned a way to escape with silk, but she accidentally revealed the secret to the witch. The witch cut off her hair, took her away, and trapped the prince's plan. The prince fell, became blind, wandered for years, and finally found Rapunzel again. Her tears healed his eyes, and they married and lived happily ever after.

She showed her loose tooth to fish hawks, a loon, a seal, and seagulls. While she was helping dig, her tooth dropped out in the mud and she could not find it. Later, she found a gull feather, made her secret wish on it, and went with her family to Buck's Harbor. There, a spark plug came out of the boat motor, and Sal gave her wish to Jane. After errands and ice-cream cones, Sal went home happy and said they would have clam chowder for lunch.

summary_text: Forever Green Forest was peaceful until Bruce, a big shaggy bear, came out of a canyon and stayed there. When he felt playful, he liked to tumble rocks down the hills. The rocks smashed logs and bushes and scared the rabbits and quail away. One day Bruce pushed a huge boulder off a bluff. It rolled fast and crashed near Roxy, a witch, and her cat, Clinker. Roxy was angry and ran to her cabin. There she baked a blueberry and honey pie and added a magic shrinking spell. She set the pie on a stump and waited. Bruce followed the smell, ate the pie, and laughed. Soon he became sleepy and fell asleep against a tree. While he slept, he shrank smaller and smaller until he was tiny. When he woke, rabbits and quail chased him, and he ran into the creek. Later, Roxy and Clinker found him, took him home, and kept him as a small pet bear.

Later, the child wakes at home and sees the sun on the snow and the first buds opening. Spring has come.

summary_text: In November, the Earth grows quiet and makes a white winter bed for flowers and small creatures. The trees stand bare like sticks and bones, with no leaves, and they stay still. On a special November day, they travel far to share a meal and give thanks. At Winter’s Gate, the stars are sharp, the sun appears only sometimes, and the world waits quietly for spring.

summary_text: Once there was a lazy Bear who had lots of money and land, but he only wanted to sleep. Nearby lived Hair and Mrs. Hair, who had lost their land after a bad bet with a tortoise. Their children were hungry, so Hair made a plan. He went to Bear and said they could be partners and share a field. Bear would sleep while Hair and his family did all the work. Bear agreed and chose the top half of the first crops. Hair and his family planted, watered, and weeded. At harvest time, Hair gave Bear the tops and kept the bottoms. Then Bear wanted the bottoms next time, so they planted again. This time Hair gave Bear the bottoms and kept the tops. For the third crop, Bear asked for both tops and bottoms, but Hair gave him the tops and bottoms and kept the middle. After that, Bear woke up and said he would farm for himself. Hair later bought back his land and opened a vegetable stand.

They cheered, used horns and poppers, and then the puppy and the children got very busy in the house. Soon the children went upstairs for a short nap. In the morning, the child saw that they had missed the new year and decided to stay awake next New Year’s Eve.

summary_text: In a beautiful Bamboo Grove, a panda and a narrator try to make a story. The narrator says every story needs a main character and a problem, but the panda says he has no problem. The narrator asks many questions, like whether the panda wants to go somewhere, is afraid of spiders, or wants to fly, but the panda says no each time. Then the panda starts acting silly by playing a banjo badly, hanging upside down, and singing the bamboo Burp song. The narrator decides the panda is a problem. The panda then says jelly beans are raining, aliens might land, and a boat could sail to Antarctica. Soon a second panda appears, and both pandas feel very hungry. They discover the real problem: they are in Antarctica and there is no bamboo. The alien helps them, and together they spell help with jelly beans. The alien ship takes everyone back to the Bamboo Grove, where they eat a bamboo and jelly bean feast.

summary_text: Simba is a little lion whose father, Mufasa, is king. Mufasa shows Simba the kingdom and tells him not to visit the shadowy elephant graveyard. Scar, Simba’s uncle, wants to be king, so he tricks Simba into going there. Simba and Nala meet hyenas, but Mufasa saves them. Later, Scar causes a wildebeest stampede. Mufasa saves Simba, but Scar pushes Mufasa from a rock. Simba thinks his father is dead because of him and runs away. Timon and Pumbaa care for him and teach him “Hakuna Matata,” which means no worries. When Simba grows up, Nala tells him the pride lands are hungry. Rafiki helps Simba remember Mufasa’s words. Simba returns, fights Scar, and wins. Scar falls to the hyenas. Simba becomes king, and he and Nala have a cub who is welcomed into the circle of life.

summary_text: Hansel and Gretel lived with their poor father, a Woodcutter, and their stepmother in a little house near a wood. Because there was no food or money left, the stepmother insisted that the children be left in the forest. The first time, Hansel dropped Pebbles along the path, so he and Gretel followed them home after their father left them to collect wood. The stepmother then took them deeper into the wood and locked Hansel inside so he could not collect Pebbles. Hansel dropped breadcrumbs instead, but birds ate them. Lost, the children found a house made of sweets and cakes. A Witch lived there and locked Hansel in a cage, planning to cook him when he became fat. When the Witch opened the oven, Gretel pushed her inside and locked the door. Gretel freed Hansel, and they took the Witch’s money. After a long walk, they reached home. Their father welcomed them and said their stepmother was gone, so they lived happily together.

summary_text: Rosie was a small girl with a big imagination. Every night, she dreamed of having superpowers to save the world. Her beloved soft toy, meow, was always with her. One night, a mysterious Force carried Rosie and meow to a secret garden. The garden had beautiful plants and flowers, but pretend monsters had been damaging it at night with big footprints and swinging tails. Mia told Rosie that they had been chosen to help save the garden. Rosie worried because she had no special powers, but Mia said she only needed courage and faith in herself. Rosie agreed, and she and meow began their mission. They met many obstacles, but Rosie stayed courageous. At last, they reached the monster’s lair. The monster was huge and ugly, but Rosie was not afraid. She squeezed meow tightly, and a bright light appeared as her superpowers awakened. Together, Rosie and meow defeated the monster. At sunrise, the garden was normal again, and Rosie learned that her true superpower was courage and faith in herself.

summary_text: A family can be people who are related, such as parents, children, cousins, or grandparents. It can also be a special group that loves and cares for one another. They support one another as a team. Together, they are a classroom family.

summary_text: Turk was the biggest, strongest, and most graceful bird on Wishbone Farm. His mother called him a dancer, and his father called him an athlete. His brother Runt warned that Turk might be eaten, but nobody listened. In November, Turk practiced ballet and football because his family thought he would be chosen for Swan Lake or a football team. A ballet teacher came, but Runt acted wild and scared her away. The next day, a football coach arrived. Turk played strongly, but Runt pretended to be very sick, so the coach left too. On Thanksgiving morning, a little old lady chose Runt because he was the right size. Turk saw her fork and roasting pan and understood that Runt had been right. The brothers worked together until the lady drove away. The family celebrated being safe and thanked one another. In December, Runt warned that holiday dinners were coming and said he had a plan. This time, everyone listened to him.

Covered in dust and webs, the pale man appears dead, but he opens his eyes and asks, “What do you want?” Michael quickly leaves when his family calls him.

summary_text: The children learn about leaves and talk about how leaves can make people and animals happy. Then they show how to make a leaf painting. First, they go outside and gather leaves of many shapes and sizes from yards and the park. Next, they put blue, red, and yellow paint on separate paper plates. These primary colors can be mixed to make new colors, such as green, orange, and purple. They place the leaves on paper with spaces between them. Then they dip a sponge in paint and dab it around the leaves. They hold the leaves so they do not slide and mix different colors. When they finish painting, they carefully peel the leaves off the paper. The paper has a pretty leaf pattern. Finally, they get ready to watch leaves on books with hot cider and invite others to ask a grown-up to explore more story books.

summary_text: Tony Sar loved making things move. At six, he used pulleys and rope to open the chicken coop from his bed, so the chickens ate while he stayed warm. When he grew up, he moved to London and made lifelike marionettes from wood, cloth, and strings. In New York, Macy’s hired him to create moving storybook puppets for its holiday windows. Later, Tony helped make Macy’s first Thanksgiving parade in 1924 for immigrant workers. He built floats and costumes, and animals from the Central Park Zoo joined the parade. The parade became a yearly event, but lions and tigers frightened children. Macy’s asked Tony to replace the animals. His small puppets were too little, so he designed huge balloon puppets. First, rubber balloons on wooden sticks appeared, but crowds needed taller puppets and the sticks were heavy. Tony then used lighter rubberized silk, helium, and controls below the balloons. On Thanksgiving, the giant puppets rose, waved, and danced through New York City before ending at Macy’s. This began the famous balloon parade.

summary_text: In Brooklyn, little Jean-Michel dreams of becoming a famous artist. He draws from morning until night, using pencils and papers. His pictures are messy, strange, and beautiful. His mother, Matilde, draws with him and teaches him that art is in books, museums, music, street games, clothing, and city life. Jean-Michel loves Picasso’s work. After a car accident, Matilde gives him a book about bones and body parts. He draws from it until he understands his body and feels less afraid. Later, Matilde becomes sick, and the family separates. Jean-Michel feels sad, but he keeps drawing and visits her with his artwork. As a teenager, he leaves Brooklyn for New York City. He sleeps on couches, makes collages, and paints poems and pictures on walls. He signs them “Samo,” and many people wonder who Samo is. His art moves from street walls to galleries. As a grown man, Jean-Michel becomes a famous artist and honors Matilde at his important shows.

summary_text: Mr Watson and Mrs Watson lived with their pig, Mercy, at 54 Deu Drive. Before Halloween, they decided Mercy should dress as a princess and go trick-or-treating. Mrs Watson made a pink dress, and Mr Watson found a tiara. Mercy did not want to wear the dress, but she agreed when Mr Watson promised her treats. At the Lincoln sisters’ house, Eugina said Mercy looked like a pig in a cheap dress and shut the door. Baby Lincoln gave Mercy candy. Mercy ate some candy, including butter barrels, but Eugina became angry. When General Washington, the cat, swatted at Mercy’s dress and tiara, Mercy chased him. Everyone chased Mercy and the cat to an old oak tree. General Washington climbed up and became stuck. Ned and Lorenzo from the fire department came and rescued him with a ladder. Then everyone had a party. Mercy smelled toast and melting butter, so wearing the snug princess dress was worth it.

In 1789, George became the first president of the United States and was elected again in 1792. He made treaties, kept the country out of a European war, and enforced the law during the whiskey attacks. In 1797, he returned to Mount Vernon. He died there in 1799.

The child has no souvenir and remembers staying home, caring for a little sister, reading books, and laughing with her. At lunch, Nadja does not understand the child’s rice, meat, and kimchi. The child is also left out of games because the climbing bars and running are too hard. Then the child shares the summer story with the class. The child says that staying on the block with a little sister felt like going everywhere. Rigoberto says Angelina is also his sister’s name. The class begins to make room for friendship and shared stories.

summary_text: At the start of the school day, pencils are ready, bells ring, and children hurry to class. The classroom welcomes everyone, no matter how they begin the day, what they wear, or where they come from. Inside, children feel safe, raise their hands, and take turns speaking. They play music, make art, and share stories. At lunchtime, they pass around many kinds of bread so everyone can eat. After lunch, they go outside to swing, slide, and play together. The children are part of a community, and their different strengths help make it strong. They learn from one another and discover the wide world. When school ends, they go home to rest and return ready for a new day. The classroom tells each child, “All are welcome here,” and says everyone has a place and space. Children can welcome someone different by playing, sharing food, or asking about special talents, and that person may become a new best friend.

summary_text: At school, Llama llama learns counting, writing, reading, and rules. He learns that letters make the alphabet, each letter has a name, and letters join together to make words. He says the alphabet, writes his name, and learns that the letters in “love” make a special present. Words can make rhymes, songs, sentences, books, and stories. When some words are hard, Llama does not need to cry or pout. He tries his best and sounds them out. With his teacher, he walks in line and learns that g and o spell “go.” He reads stories about fairies, princesses, pirate kings, knights, and dragons. Then, outside, he sees a sign with s, t, o, and p. He puts the letters together and reads “stop,” so he stops skipping and hopping. At the end of the school day, Llama feels proud and happy. He cannot wait to read to Mama and loves reading.

summary_text: On her first day of school, Milk felt scared. Her dad gave her a new backpack and called her “la creme de la creme,” meaning the best of the best. Milk tried to be friendly, but Waffle called her “spoiled.” She invited Cupcake to sit with her, shared crayons with Carrot, and proudly showed her family picture. Milk said she might become a queen, became upset when Soup splattered her spelling paper, and argued with Cheese, Beans, Waffle, and Egg. At recess, she wanted to play but was not invited. She found Celery’s lost raisin and had thrown it away, then promised to get a new one. Sadly, Milk slipped on Banana’s peel and spilled onto the floor. Her classmates remembered her kindness and helped her. After Milk returned to her carton, Cupcake sneezed frosting and sprinkles onto everyone. Milk stayed calm and forgave her. Waffle said Milk was not too spoiled, and Milk said Waffle seemed sweet. The class laughed and got along.

summary_text: The night before kindergarten, the children felt excited and a little scared. They packed backpacks with erasers, crayons, and pencils, then put them by the door. In the morning, they got ready, took pictures, and rode to school with their parents. Some children brought blankets or stuffed bears because they thought they might nap. Their parents worried the children would cry, so they offered to stay. Miss Sunrise greeted each child with a smile and invited everyone inside. The classroom had toys, books, and maps, but it had no beds for naps. The children colored, painted, played Simon Says, sang songs, skipped, and played together. Soon, every child had a friend, and they were happy with Miss Sunrise. Then the parents began to cry as they said goodbye. Miss Sunrise gave the grown-ups one last hug and sent them away. The children waved and called, “Don’t cry, Mom and Dad. Kindergarten is cool.”

summary_text: Turk is the biggest, strongest, and most graceful turkey on Wishbone Farm. His parents think he will dance in Swan Lake or play football, but his brother Runt keeps warning that Turk may be chosen for dinner. In November, Madame Waddell comes to choose a turkey. Turk dances beautifully, but Runt acts wild and scares her away. The next day, Coach Giblet visits to choose a football player. Turk shows his strength, but Runt pretends to be very sick, so the coach leaves too. On Thanksgiving morning, a little old lady comes to the farm. She ignores Turk and chooses Runt because he is the right size. Runt runs for help, and Turk finally understands that Runt was right. Together, they dance, sneeze, gobble, and tackle the lady’s shoes until she leaves. The family eats Korn and Alfalfa and gives thanks. Runt then says they must make another plan for December dinners, and everyone listens.

summary_text: Parley Elementary had a very noisy, crowded lunchroom. Students could not eat or hear one another, so they wrote Mrs. Mench asking for help. She put science projects on tables in the lunchroom, making less room. Students wrote again after food spilled and projects were knocked over. Then Mrs. Mench moved classroom pets there for a learning zoo. A snake escaped, hamsters squeaked, and tarantulas molted. The students sent many unhappy notes. During a heat wave, Mrs. Mench let all sports teams practice in the lunchroom. Balls flew, whistles blew, science projects exploded, and the room smelled bad. The students wrote that it was worse than ever. Finally, when the heat wave ended, Mrs. Mench moved sports outside, returned pets to classrooms, and put science projects in the hallways. The lunchroom became quiet, calm, and roomy. Students ate, laughed, and did not fight. The next day, they sent chocolate and thank-you notes, saying the lunchroom was peaceful and the best room in school.

Master Woo and Cole were impressed, and Kai and Ry promised to train as much as they played.

summary_text: In the morning, Mommy tells the child that he will be the king of kindergarten. He washes his face, dresses neatly, eats pancakes, and tells Daddy that he will grow taller. The children at his Round Table wave and say hello, so he waves back. In class, they learn about rules, shapes, the alphabet, and numbers. The teacher also reads about trucks, trains, and tractors. At recess, the child asks Marie to play, and together they battle a fire-breathing dragon in the cafeteria. At lunch, he shares an extra cup of chocolate pudding with Howie, who has no dessert. After resting, the children sing, dance, and move to music. At the end of the day, his teacher says goodbye. Going home, he plans to tell his parents about his new friends, kind teacher, and fun recess.

summary_text: The narrator is a potato who calls himself a couch potato. He spends all his free time on his comfy couch, using gadgets to get snacks, watch shows, play video games, read messages, and talk with his best Spud friends on screens. He thinks comfort is the most important thing. One day, a new video camera arrives, but the power suddenly goes out. With nothing to watch, he takes his dog, Tater, outside. He walks through the neighborhood and finds a park with a hill and a large tree. Sitting there, he notices the fresh air, birds, sky, clouds, and beautiful sunset. When he returns home, the power is back. After seeing his reflection in a screen, he wonders how much of his life he has spent on the couch. He decides to spend more time outside with his friends, biking, hiking, swimming, playing, and talking. He still enjoys the couch after a busy day, but now balances it with the world outside.

summary_text: An old mermaid swallowed a great white shark, but no one knew why. Then she swallowed a squid so it could float with the shark. The squid moved with a mighty jet blast. Next, she swallowed a tropical fish so it could dance with the squid. The story says sharks have many teeth, but they swallow food whole. The mermaid swallowed an eel to brighten the fish. She let out a squirrel and swallowed the eel. The eel’s body makes fluorescent light. Then she swallowed a crab to tickle the eel. The crab was hard to grab, but it can grow a spare claw. After that, she swallowed a sea star to play with the crab. The sea star did not swim away because it has no brain. At the end, the mermaid swallowed a clam and filled her mouth with it. Each new sea creature joined the others inside the mermaid.

summary_text: Carla brings unusual sandwiches to school because she likes to be different. On Monday, Buster sees her olive pickle and green bean sandwich and moves away. On Tuesday, Lesie rejects Carla’s banana cottage cheese Delight. On Wednesday, Na rejects her peanut butter, crackers, cheddar cheese, and pea bread sandwich. Carla brings even more unusual sandwiches on Thursday and Friday. Soon, no one will sit with her. During a class picnic, Buster forgets his lunch. Carla offers him her lettuce, tomato, raisin, bean sprout, pretzel, and mayonnaise sandwich, called the combo Deluxe. He refuses at first, but hunger makes him ask for one. After tasting it, Buster says it is the best sandwich he has ever eaten. Lesie, Na, and the other children try it too and enjoy it. The next day, everyone brings a creative sandwich. Carla brings peanut butter and jelly and says she still likes to be different.

summary_text: Cassie Louise Lightfoot is eight years old and lives with her family in New York. One night, she lies on the rooftop called Tar Beach with her baby brother, Bibi. Mommy cooks, Daddy brings a watermelon, and their neighbors, Mr. and Mrs. Honey, play cards. Cassie remembers seeing the stars fall around her and lift her above the George Washington Bridge. Her father helped build the bridge, which opened on the day Cassie was born, so she calls it her most prized possession. Cassie says she can fly and claims the bridge by flying over it. She also plans to fly over the Union building where Daddy works on high steel girders. She wants the building to belong to him so he will not have to search for work or face unfair treatment because he is not in the union and is part Indian. Cassie tells Bibi that anyone can fly if they have somewhere to go that they cannot reach another way.

summary_text: Zoom Squirrel says, “I lost my tooth.” The other squirrels keep saying his name wrong, calling him Zip, Zap, and Zooie. They worry about the lost baby tooth and decide to find it. They look near and far and ask for clues, but Zoom Squirrel cannot describe what the tooth looks like. The squirrels say the tooth may be lonely, hungry, or upset. They search while Zoom Squirrel checks under his pillow, but the tooth is not there. Then the squirrels lose Zoom Squirrel too. They are surprised because they thought the story would be happy. Soon, Zoom Squirrel comes back, holding the baby tooth. The squirrels cheer and wonder whether Zoom Squirrel found the tooth or the tooth found him. They call the tooth brave and put it in a baby buggy. They tell the tooth to rest, and the buggy wiggles. At the end, the squirrels learn that they do not know much about teeth.

summary_text: A pig parade sounds fun, but the story explains why it would be terrible. Pigs do not march. They like to snuffle, walking with their noses to find leftover apple skin and acrin around the Barnyard. They also refuse to wear majorette uniforms, even if someone finds hundreds of them. Pigs do not care about parade floats, including floats about the Three Little Pigs or Wilbur from Charlotte's Web. They only like root beer floats. Pigs also play sad country songs instead of cheerful marching music, with titles such as "My Tears Are Wet 'Cuz My Mud's Gone Dry." Finally, pigs cannot hold giant balloons. Their pigo are good for digging wild mushrooms, but balloons may hit buildings or float into outer space. Because of their snuffling, uniforms, floats, music, and balloons, a pig parade would fail. The story ends by saying a panda bear parade would be fantastic.

summary_text: Joe writes to Grandpa about his busy summer. He reads every day, writes a book, and practices math. He solves ice cream word problems about scoops, cones, prices, and days of summer. Joe and his friends learn cartography, make maps, and go on field trips. He also reads Grandpa’s encyclopedias and studies history. He learns that ice cream began in ancient China. Marco Polo carried recipes along the Silk Road to Italy. Queen Katherine Deichi married King Henry II of France, and ice cream spread through Europe. Quakers brought ice cream recipes to America. George Washington and Thomas Jefferson enjoyed ice cream, and Jefferson added vanilla. President James Madison served ice cream with strawberries. Joe studies inventions, too. At the 1904 World’s Fair, Arnold ran out of cups, so Ernest used waffles to hold ice cream. This made the first ice cream cones. In 1920, Harry Bird made chocolate-covered ice cream. Joe rests on Sundays and looks forward to his special trip to ice cream Peak.

On Yavin IV, Luke, Han, and Leia hugged because they had defeated the Empire.

summary_text: Beatrice lives with her mother and five younger brothers and sisters in Kiss Inga, a village in western Uganda. She learns that selling the second kid may also help her family build a new house with a steel roof.

Tama writes that the miracle is in people who keep believing in change, beauty, and hope.

summary_text: A grape used to be sweet and kind. He lived with about 3,000 grapes on a vine. His grandparents taught him to be kind, forgiving, considerate, and grateful, and to stay sweet. One year, he planned a big birthday party with rides, snacks, a magician, and fireworks. Nobody came, so he became angry and started holding grudges against everyone. He grew into a sour grape. Later, he tried to meet his friend Lenny at the park, but many problems made him three hours late. Lenny became very angry, just as the grape often did. While waiting, the grape noticed the pretty evening and felt calm. At home, he found his old birthday invitation and saw that he had written May 31 instead of May 21. He learned that the party mistake was his fault. He began talking, listening, and forgiving. He stopped holding grudges, became less sour, and made peace with Lenny. Life became sweet again.

summary_text: Martin Luther King Jr. dreamed that Black and white children could join hands as brothers and sisters and that freedom would ring. After the March on Washington, the president and Congress passed civil rights laws, but the work was not finished. In Selma, Alabama, 600 activists began walking fifty-four miles to Montgomery to demand voting rights because rules stopped Black people from voting. Police used billy clubs and tear gas and stopped the peaceful marchers. The group tried again with 2,500 people, but they were stopped again. On March 21, 1965, 8,000 people marched. Black and white Christians and Jewish people joined them. They marched for two days through rain and exhaustion. President Johnson sent troops to protect them, and they reached Montgomery with tears of joy. King said to answer hate with love and violence with kindness. Funtown later opened to Black people. King won the Nobel Peace Prize, fought poverty, and is remembered on a national holiday. He stood for peace, justice, and helping others.

Principal Crossly said the event was “way cool,” and everyone agreed.

summary_text: In a village in Ghana, an old man lived with his seven Ashanti sons. The brothers argued every day about work, weather, food, and when to go home. After their father died, the village chief told them that their inheritance would be shared equally. First, they had to turn seven spools of colored thread into gold before moonrise. If they fought, they would lose their home and possessions. The brothers went home and made peace. They decided to work together. Using blue, red, yellow, orange, green, black, and white thread, they built a loom and wove beautiful cloth with stripes and bird-like shapes. They carried the cloth to the marketplace, where the king’s treasurer bought all of it for a bag of gold. The brothers showed the gold to the chief. Since they had worked peacefully, he gave them their father’s property. They taught the villagers to make the cloth, and the village prospered.

summary_text: After World War II, Momo fuku Ando walked through ruined Osaka and saw hungry people waiting in the cold for expensive bowls of ramen. He decided to spend his life making food so people would have enough to eat. Ando made salt, dried fish, and food for sick people, but he still remembered the starving families. After losing his business, he began creating a nutritious ramen that could be cooked quickly. He tried many mixtures of flour, salt, eggs, milk, spinach, and water, but the noodles often broke, stuck, or became lumpy. He learned that balance was important. Ando also tried many ways to add chicken soup flavor. One night, he watched his wife Masako fry tempura. This gave him an idea. He fried the noodles in hot oil, making tiny holes in them. When hot water was added, the noodles became soft and the water became soup. After a year, Ando invented instant Ramen. His family helped make and sell it. People everywhere ate it and felt better.

summary_text: The Big Cheese is a loud, proud piece of cheddar. He likes being noticed and winning. He grew up as a small piece of cheese, but he worked hard to become famous. He talked with Wedge by a stream and learned about his life. The Big Cheese realized that losing could teach him humility and empathy. Now he enjoys trying new things, sharing attention, and praising his friends.

summary_text: Audrey Fay Hendrix lived in Birmingham, where segregation laws kept Black and white people apart. She wanted to eat inside Newberry’s, sit downstairs at the Alabama Theater, and use the same schools and stores as white children. At church meetings, Audrey heard Mike, also called Dr. King, speak against segregation. He asked people to march, break unfair laws, and fill the jails, but many adults were afraid of losing their jobs or homes. Jim Bevel then suggested that children protest. Audrey’s parents allowed her to join. She marched from 16th Street Baptist Church, singing and carrying a sign, and was arrested. In juvenile hall, she was lonely, hungry, and uncomfortable. She also heard that children were being knocked down by fire hoses before being jailed. By Audrey’s fifth day, the jails were full. After seven days, she went home. Two months later, Birmingham ended its segregation laws, and Audrey ate at Newberry’s counter with Black and white people.

summary_text: Big Cheese loved having huge Christmas parties. His parties had shiny decorations, a very tall tree, tasty snacks, funny jokes, loud laughter, surprise gifts, and many guests. He wanted every Christmas to be bigger than the last. One year, while he prepared his special party outfit, the washing machine broke. Water and soapy sludge flooded his house. Wedge invited everyone to his small, cozy home. At Wedge’s party, there were no giant decorations or loud shows. The friends simply talked, laughed, ate, and took a group photo. Wedge gave each guest a handwritten Christmas card. Big Cheese said the party was wonderful and thanked Wedge. On his walk home, Big Cheese realized Christmas could be about enjoying time with friends, not winning or having the biggest party.

summary_text: William lived in a poor village in Malawi, where darkness came early and there was little food or money. He loved taking apart radios and building toy trucks. When drought ruined the fields, William had to leave school. He began visiting a library and used science books and an English dictionary to learn how engines and radios worked. He read that windmills could make electricity and pump water, so he decided to build “electric wind.” William collected junk, including a tractor fan, pipes, bolts, and a bicycle generator. People called him crazy, but his cousin Jeffrey and friend Gilbert helped him build a tall windmill from tree trunks. When the wind came, its blades spun, and William connected wires to a bulb. The bulb lit up, and the villagers cheered. Later, his windmill charged a battery and lit his house. Years afterward, he built a pump that watered his mother’s garden. William received help to return to school and study engineering, hoping to bring renewable energy to Malawi.

The big boss gives Lily to Beatatrice. Lily now lives in Beatatrice’s backyard coop, where she eats, scratches the ground, and enjoys sunshine with other chickens. Each summer, Lily and Beatatrice visit Chinatown.

summary_text: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1929. He liked sports, riding his bicycle, and singing. When he learned that white friends could not play with him because he was black, he felt sad. His mother explained that black people had once been slaves and were still treated unfairly. Martin read about black leaders and became a minister. He married Ketta Scott in 1954 and became a pastor in Montgomery, Alabama. After Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her bus seat, Martin led a peaceful bus protest. He told people to meet hate with love. The protest lasted almost a year, and buses no longer had white-only sections. Martin later led protests in Atlanta and the 1963 March on Washington, where he said, “I have a dream.” New laws gave black people equal rights. In 1968, James Earl Ray shot Martin in Memphis. Martin’s dream was a world without hate, prejudice, and violence.

summary_text: A cookie lived in a bakery near a river. When he was young, he went to school in a gingerbread house with Miss Biscotti. He tried hard, but he often got low grades, finished last, and felt lost when lessons were hard. He worried because he could not answer quickly or raise his hand. One day, Miss Biscotti gave the class a homework task: make anything original. The cookie tried cooking, building, and sculpting, but each project failed. Then he watched the rain fall into the river and got an idea. He wrote a poem called “My Crummy Days.” The next day, he read it to the class. The children laughed, nodded, clapped, and cheered. Miss Biscotti said that only he could have written it. She gave him a note telling him to keep writing. After that, he was less afraid to speak and learned that people can be smart in many different ways.

People now simply called her Beatrice.

summary_text: Wilma Rudolph grew up in Clarksville, Tennessee, as one of 22 children. Although she loved running and playing, she was often sick. Before she turned five, she caught scarlet fever and polio, which left her left leg twisted and unable to move. Doctors said she might never walk again. Wilma and her mother traveled 50 miles to a hospital twice each week, where Wilma exercised her legs. She practiced at home too, eventually learning to walk with a steel brace. At church, she bravely removed the brace and walked alone down the aisle. By age 12, she no longer needed it. Wilma joined her high school basketball team and led it to the Tennessee State championships. A coach noticed her running and helped her receive a scholarship to Tennessee State University. At the 1960 Olympics in Rome, Wilma won gold medals in the 100-meter dash, 200-meter dash, and 400-meter relay, becoming the fastest woman in the world.

summary_text: A boy named Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy, who could say “Buzz.” Fly Guy went to school with Buzz. He learned reading, phonics, and art. She swung her swatter but missed many times. The boss fired her, and Roz returned. She made garbage soup for Super Fly Guy, and everyone was happy.

summary_text: Twinkie was a small dog, but he believed he was big. His owner carried him, dressed him in sweaters, sent him to charm school, and made him use a wee wee pad. Twinkie growled, barked, and roared until the robber ran away. After that, everyone knew Twinkie was brave. His owner stopped treating him like a tiny dog, and he ran happily with the big dogs.

summary_text: On Monday, Mr. Park chose Penelope to be the new student librarian. She had practiced alphabetizing books, pushing the book cart, and adding due-date stickers all year. Penelope was friendly and helpful, but she had a very loud voice. At the library, she pushed the cart, returned books, and filled in the computer sign-in sheet. She also loudly asked questions about flamingos, snowballs, dinosaurs, and other things. Mrs. Barry reminded her to use a quiet library voice. Penelope’s loud talking caused crashes and a messy library. She felt sad and thought she was not right for the job. Then Penelope remembered that not all library voices had to be quiet. She gathered students for story time. She read about an astronaut telling a farmer that he would plan the pig’s birthday party. Everyone laughed, including Mrs. Barry. Penelope was happy and invited them to come back the next day.

summary_text: Long ago, a village stood beside Lake Ontario. In a large painted wigwam lived an invisible being and his sister. A woman could marry him only if she could see him. A poor man had three daughters. The two older girls were cruel to their youngest sister, who sat by the fire until her skin was scarred and her hair was burned. The older girls dressed well and claimed they had seen the invisible being, but they could not answer questions about his bow or sled. They went home ashamed. The youngest girl had only broken shells, birch bark, and her father’s old moccasins. She made clothes and walked to the wigwam while people laughed at her. She told the sister that his bow was the rainbow and his sled runner was the Milky Way. The sister knew she had truly seen him. The invisible being called her beautiful. She bathed, her scars disappeared, and her hair grew long. They married and lived happily together.

summary_text: Little Gopher was smaller than the other boys in his tribe. He could not ride or shoot a bow as well as they could, but he loved painting stones with berry juices. The shaman told him that he had a special gift. When Little Gopher went into the hills to become a man, he dreamed of a young maiden and an old grandfather. They gave him paint, brushes, and a white buckskin. They told him to paint the deeds of warriors and the shaman’s visions so people would remember them. Little Gopher made brushes from animal hair and paints from berries, flowers, and rocks. He painted many pictures, but he could not copy the sunset’s colors. Each evening, he watched the sky from a hill. At last, magical brushes filled with sunset colors appeared. He painted the white buckskin and took it home. The brushes grew into bright flowers, so people called him “He who brought the sunset to the earth.”

summary_text: The boy thought his summer was perfect because Dad built him a tree house and he played on a great baseball team. Then Jeremy Ross moved nearby. The boy learned that getting to know someone can show that a person is not really an enemy. Different people can become friends.

summary_text: The boys go camping with Dad, as they do every year. At night, while they plan the next day, Dad hears something outside the tent. A phone light shows nothing, but the family hears moans, panting, growls, howls, rustling leaves, and loud footsteps. The creature comes closer and shakes the tent. In the moonlight, the boys see a huge beast with long claws, fangs, and a mouth covered in slime. Dad blows his whistle, but the creature becomes angry. Then it suddenly stops. Dad tells the boys to face their fears, and they look outside. They see a giant Sasquatch. It rushes toward them, so the three of them close their eyes and cry. Suddenly, the creature laughs. It is Mom wearing a Bigfoot costume and mask. She used her checklist to make scary noises, stomp, shake the tent, and take a picture. The frightening camping night was her prank.
